am1a.topicTitle: Order notation, gauge functions & asymptotic sequences 21

Show that \( \dfrac{1}{f(z)} \sim \dfrac{1}{a_0}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} d_n z^{-n} \), where \( d_0 = 1 \) and \( \sum_{k=0}^{n} d_{n-k} a_k = 0 \) for \( n \ge 1 \). Show that \( f(z)g(z) \sim \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} c_n z^{-n} \) with \( c_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} a_{n-k} b_k \), justifying carefully why the cross terms beyond order \( N \) are negligible.

am1b.questionText: Two functions have the asymptotic expansions \( f(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{2}{z} \) and \( g(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{1}{z} \) as \( z \to \infty \). Using the Cauchy product \( c_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} a_{n-k} b_k \), find the coefficients \( c_0, c_1, c_2 \) of \( f(z)g(z) \sim \sum c_n z^{-n} \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 02
am1b.questionText: Let \( f(z) \sim 2 + \dfrac{1}{z} \) and \( g(z) \sim 3 - \dfrac{1}{z} \) as \( z \to \infty \). Find the coefficients \( c_0, c_1, c_2 \) in \( f(z)g(z) \sim \sum c_n z^{-n} \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 03
am1b.questionText: Given \( f(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{1}{z} \) as \( z \to \infty \), use the reciprocal recurrence \( d_0 = 1,\ \sum_{k=0}^{n} d_{n-k} a_k = 0\ (n\ge 1) \) to find \( d_1, d_2, d_3 \) in \( \dfrac{1}{f(z)} \sim \sum d_n z^{-n} \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 04
am1b.questionText: Given \( f(z) \sim 2 + \dfrac{4}{z} \) as \( z \to \infty \), find \( d_1 \) and \( d_2 \) so that \( \dfrac{1}{f(z)} \sim \dfrac{1}{2}\left(d_0 + \dfrac{d_1}{z} + \dfrac{d_2}{z^2} + \cdots\right) \), where \( d_0 = 1 \) and \( \sum_{k=0}^{n} d_{n-k} a_k = 0 \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 05
am1b.questionText: Two expansions as \( x \to 0 \) are \( f(x) \sim 1 + x + x^2 \) and \( g(x) \sim 1 - x \). Find the coefficients of \( 1, x, x^2 \) in the product \( f(x)g(x) \) using the Cauchy product on ascending powers.

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 06
am1b.questionText: Given \( f(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{1}{z} + \dfrac{1}{z^2} + \dfrac{1}{z^3} + \cdots \) as \( z \to \infty \) (all \( a_n = 1 \)), use the reciprocal recurrence to find \( d_1, d_2, d_3 \) in \( 1/f \sim \sum d_n z^{-n} \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 07
am1b.questionText: Let \( f(z) \sim \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} (n+1) z^{-n} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{z} + \dfrac{3}{z^2} + \cdots \) and \( g(z) \sim \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} z^{-n} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{z} + \dfrac{1}{z^2} + \cdots \) as \( z \to \infty \). Find the first four coefficients \( c_0,\dots,c_3 \) of \( f(z)g(z) \sim \sum c_n z^{-n} \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 08
am1b.questionText: As \( z \to \infty \), \( f(z) \sim 1 - \dfrac{1}{z} + \dfrac{1}{z^2} - \dfrac{1}{z^3} + \cdots \) (so \( a_n = (-1)^n \)) and \( g(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{1}{z} + \dfrac{1}{z^2} + \cdots \) (so \( b_n = 1 \)). Find \( c_0,\dots,c_3 \) of \( f(z)g(z) \) and identify the closed form.

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 09
am1b.questionText: Let \( f(z) \sim 2 + \dfrac{3}{z} + \dfrac{4}{z^2} + \dfrac{5}{z^3} + \cdots \) as \( z \to \infty \) (so \( a_n = n+2 \)). Find \( d_1, d_2, d_3 \) so that \( \dfrac{1}{f(z)} \sim \dfrac{1}{2}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} d_n z^{-n} \), with \( d_0 = 1 \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 10
am1b.questionText: Given \( f(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{2}{z} + \dfrac{3}{z^2} + \dfrac{4}{z^3} + \cdots \) as \( z \to \infty \) (so \( a_n = n+1 \)), find the reciprocal coefficients \( d_1, d_2, d_3 \) of \( 1/f \sim \sum d_n z^{-n} \) and identify the closed form.

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 11
Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 12
am1b.questionText: As \( x \to 0 \), \( f(x) \sim 1 + x + \dfrac{x^2}{2} + \dfrac{x^3}{6} \) and \( g(x) \sim 1 - x + \dfrac{x^2}{2} - \dfrac{x^3}{6} \). Find the coefficients of \( x^0, x^1, x^2, x^3 \) in the product \( f(x)g(x) \), and comment on the result.

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 13
am1b.questionText: Let \( f(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{1}{z} + \dfrac{1}{2z^2} + \dfrac{1}{6z^3} + \cdots \) as \( z \to \infty \) (so \( a_n = 1/n! \)). Find the reciprocal coefficients \( d_1, d_2, d_3 \) of \( 1/f \sim \sum d_n z^{-n} \) and identify the function.

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 14
am1b.questionText: As \( x \to 0 \), \( \cos x \sim 1 - \dfrac{x^2}{2} + \dfrac{x^4}{24} \). Using the reciprocal recurrence on this series, find the expansion of \( \sec x = 1/\cos x \) up to and including the \( x^4 \) term.

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 15
am1b.questionText: Let \( f(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{a}{z} \) as \( z \to \infty \), where \( a \) is a constant. Using the reciprocal recurrence, show that \( \dfrac{1}{f(z)} \sim \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} (-a)^n z^{-n} \), and verify by summing the geometric series.

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 16
am1b.questionText: As \( z \to \infty \), \( f(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{1}{z} + \dfrac{1}{z^2} \) and \( g(z) \sim 1 - \dfrac{1}{z} \). Find the first four coefficients of \( f(z)g(z) \sim \sum c_n z^{-n} \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 17
am1b.questionText: Given the asymptotic expansion \( f(z) \sim 1 - \dfrac{1}{z} - \dfrac{1}{z^2} \) as \( z \to \infty \) (so \( a_0=1,\ a_1=-1,\ a_2=-1 \), higher zero), find the reciprocal coefficients \( d_1,\dots,d_5 \) of \( 1/f \sim \sum d_n z^{-n} \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 18
am1b.questionText: As \( z \to \infty \), \( f(z) \sim 4 + \dfrac{2}{z} + \dfrac{1}{z^2} \). Find the first three coefficients (the constant, \( z^{-1} \) and \( z^{-2} \)) of \( 1/f(z) \), giving each in fully simplified form.

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 19
am1b.questionText: Suppose \( f(z) \sim \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n z^{-n} \) and \( g(z) \sim \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} b_n z^{-n} \) as \( z \to \infty \). Show that \( f(z)g(z) \sim \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} c_n z^{-n} \) with \( c_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} a_{n-k} b_k \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 20
am1b.questionText: Suppose \( f(z) \sim a_0 + \dfrac{a_1}{z} + \dfrac{a_2}{z^2} + \cdots \) as \( z \to \infty \) with \( a_0 \neq 0 \). Show by induction (or otherwise) that \( \dfrac{1}{f(z)} \sim \dfrac{1}{a_0}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} d_n z^{-n} \), where \( d_0 = 1 \) and \( \sum_{k=0}^{n} d_{n-k} a_k = 0 \) for \( n \ge 1 \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 21
am1b.questionText: As \( z \to \infty \), \( f(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{1}{z} + \dfrac{1}{2z^2} + \dfrac{1}{6z^3} + \cdots = e^{1/z} \) and \( g(z) \sim 1 - \dfrac{1}{z} + \dfrac{1}{2z^2} - \dfrac{1}{6z^3} + \cdots = e^{-1/z} \). (a) Compute the first four Cauchy coefficients \( c_0,\dots,c_3 \) of \( fg \). (b) Verify they are consistent with \( fg = 1 \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 22
am1b.questionText: Let \( h(z) = \sqrt{1 + 1/z} \), which as \( z \to \infty \) has the binomial expansion \( h(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{1}{2z} - \dfrac{1}{8z^2} + \dfrac{1}{16z^3} - \cdots \). Using the Cauchy product, compute the coefficients of \( h(z)^2 \) up to \( z^{-3} \) and confirm they reproduce \( 1 + 1/z \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 23
am1b.questionText: As \( z \to \infty \), \( f(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{1}{z} + \dfrac{1}{2z^2} + \dfrac{1}{6z^3} \) (the series of \( e^{1/z} \)). Using the reciprocal recurrence, find the coefficients of \( 1/f \) up to \( z^{-3} \); then, separately, obtain the same coefficients via the Cauchy-product identity and confirm they agree.

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 24
am1b.questionText: As \( z \to \infty \), \( \sinh(1/z) \sim \dfrac{1}{z} + \dfrac{1}{6z^3} + \dfrac{1}{120 z^5} \) and \( \cosh(1/z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{1}{2z^2} + \dfrac{1}{24 z^4} \). Find the asymptotic expansion of \( \tanh(1/z) = \sinh(1/z)/\cosh(1/z) \) up to and including \( z^{-5} \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 25
am1b.questionText: Suppose \( f(z) \sim \sum a_n z^{-n} \) with \( a_0 \neq 0 \), and let \( \{d_n\} \) be its reciprocal coefficients (\( d_0 = 1,\ \sum_{k=0}^{n} d_{n-k} a_k = 0 \)). Show that the leading reciprocal coefficients are \( d_1 = -a_1/a_0 \) and \( d_2 = (a_1^2 - a_0 a_2)/a_0^2 \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 26
am1b.questionText: As \( z \to \infty \), \( f(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{1}{z} + \dfrac{1}{z^2} + \cdots \) (all \( a_n = 1 \)) and \( g(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{2}{z} + \dfrac{3}{z^2} + \cdots \) (all \( b_n = n+1 \)). (a) Find the Cauchy product \( c_n \) in closed form. (b) Identify the closed-form function \( fg \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 27
am1b.questionText: As \( z \to \infty \), \( f(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{1}{z} + \dfrac{1}{2z^2} + \dfrac{1}{6z^3} \) (series of \( e^{1/z} \)). Using the reciprocal recurrence, find the coefficients of \( 1/f^2 \) up to \( z^{-3} \) (i.e. expand \( e^{-2/z} \)) by first squaring \( f \) via the Cauchy product and then reciprocating.

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 28
am1b.questionText: As \( z \to \infty \), the function \( \coth(z) = \cosh z/\sinh z \) satisfies \( \coth z = 1 + 2e^{-2z} + 2e^{-4z} + \cdots \). Writing \( u = e^{-2z} \) (an exponentially small gauge as \( z \to \infty \)), find the reciprocal expansion of \( \coth z \) (i.e. \( \tanh z \)) as a series in \( u \) up to \( u^3 \).

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 29
am1b.questionText: Let \( f(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{2}{z} + \dfrac{3}{z^2} + \dfrac{4}{z^3} + \cdots \) (so \( a_n = n+1 \)) as \( z \to \infty \). Find the reciprocal coefficients \( d_n \) for all \( n \), and hence find the coefficients of \( 1/f^2 \) up to \( z^{-3} \) using the Cauchy product.

am1b.topicTitle: Algebra of asymptotic expansions: products & reciprocals 30
am1b.questionText: As \( z \to \infty \), \( \dfrac{\sin(1/z)}{1/z} \sim 1 - \dfrac{1}{6z^2} + \dfrac{1}{120 z^4} \). Find the asymptotic expansion of its reciprocal \( \dfrac{1/z}{\sin(1/z)} \) up to and including \( z^{-4} \).

am1c.questionText: Suppose \( f(x) \sim a_0 + a_1 x + a_2 x^2 + \cdots \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \). By taking a limit, write down a formula for the leading coefficient \( a_0 \) in terms of \( f \).
Let \( e(x) = \exp(-1/x) \) for \( x > 0 \). Evaluate \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \to 0^{+}} \frac{e(x)}{x^{3}} \).
Show that \( e(x) = \exp(-1/x) = o(x^{n}) \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \) for every fixed non-negative integer \( n \).
Two functions satisfy \( f(x) \sim 1 + 2x + 3x^2 + \cdots \) and \( g(x) = f(x) + \exp(-1/x) \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \). State the first three coefficients of the asymptotic power series of \( g \).
For \( e(x) = \exp(-1/x) \) with \( x > 0 \), find the location \( x_\star \) of the maximum of \( e(x)/x \) on \( x > 0 \).

Define \( f(x) = 0 \) for \( x \le 0 \) and \( f(x) = \exp(-1/x) \) for \( x > 0 \). Write down the asymptotic power series of \( f \) about \( x = 0^{+} \), and state in one sentence what this shows.
Show that if \( f(x) \sim \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n x^n \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \), then the coefficients \( a_n \) are determined uniquely by \( f \). [Give the recursive limit formula.]
Let \( e(x) = \exp(-1/x) \) for \( x > 0 \). Show that in any expansion \( e(x) \sim \beta_0 + \beta_1 x + \beta_2 x^2 + \cdots \) valid as \( x \to 0^{+} \), every \( \beta_n = 0 \).

Deduce from the result of the previous question that the coefficients of an asymptotic power series do not determine the function. Illustrate with \( f(x) = \dfrac{1}{1-x} \) and \( g(x) = \dfrac{1}{1-x} + \exp(-1/x) \).
Show that every derivative of \( e(x) = \exp(-1/x) \) (extended by \( e(0)=0 \)) vanishes at \( x = 0 \). In particular, compute \( e'(0) \).
For fixed integer \( n \ge 1 \), find the maximum value of \( g_n(x) = \dfrac{\exp(-1/x)}{x^{n}} \) on \( x > 0 \), and the point at which it occurs.
Show that \( \exp(-2/x) = o\bigl( \exp(-1/x) \bigr) \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \). What does this say about distinguishing exponentially small terms?

Suppose \( f(z) \sim a_0 + \dfrac{a_1}{z} + \dfrac{a_2}{z^{2}} + \cdots \) as \( z \to \infty \). Show that the coefficient \( a_1 \) is determined uniquely by \( f \), giving an explicit limit for it.

Let \( f(z) \sim 1 + \dfrac{1}{z} + \dfrac{1}{z^{2}} + \cdots \) as \( z \to \infty \). Using the reciprocal recurrence \( \sum_{k=0}^{n} d_{n-k} a_k = 0 \ (n \ge 1),\ d_0 = 1 \), find \( d_0, d_1, d_2 \) so that \( 1/f(z) \sim \sum d_n z^{-n} \).
Give an explicit example, with brief justification, of two distinct smooth functions on \( (0,\infty) \) having the same asymptotic power series as \( x \to 0^{+} \).

Let \( s(x) = \exp(-1/x^{2}) \) (extended by \( s(0)=0 \)), a function of a real variable \( x \). Evaluate \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{s(x)}{x^{4}} \) and state its Taylor series at \( 0 \).

Explain why an asymptotic series, even when its coefficients are uniquely determined, generally cannot be summed to recover the function. Use the divergent series \( \sum (-1)^n n!\, x^{n} \) of the Stieltjes-type integral as the illustration.
Determine whether \( \phi_n(x) = \exp(-n/x) \), \( n = 1, 2, 3, \dots \), is an asymptotic sequence as \( x \to 0^{+} \), and relate this to the hierarchy of exponentially small terms.

Consider \( F(x) = \dfrac{1}{1+x} + \exp(-1/x) \) and \( G(x) = \dfrac{1}{1+x} \) on \( x > 0 \). Show they have the same asymptotic series to all orders as \( x \to 0^{+} \), and find the smallest \( x \) at which they differ by more than \( 10^{-3} \). (Solve the resulting transcendental condition.)

Prove that the difference of two functions sharing the same asymptotic power series as \( x \to 0^{+} \) is \( o(x^{n}) \) for every \( n \). Hence characterise the equivalence classes of the relation 'has the same asymptotic series'.

State Borel's theorem (Ritt's theorem) that any sequence \( \{a_n\} \) is the asymptotic-coefficient sequence of some smooth function as \( x \to 0^{+} \), and explain how, together with uniqueness of coefficients, it makes precise the failure of injectivity of the map (function) \( \mapsto \) (series).
Show that \( \sin\!\bigl( e^{1/x} \bigr) \) has the asymptotic power series \( 0 \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \)? Investigate carefully, and decide whether it possesses an asymptotic power series at all.

The exponential integral has the divergent expansion \( E_1(x) = \int_x^{\infty} \frac{e^{-t}}{t}\,dt \sim e^{-x}\bigl( x^{-1} - x^{-2} + 2!\,x^{-3} - \cdots \bigr) \) as \( x \to \infty \). For \( x = 5 \), find the index \( n \) of the smallest term and hence state the order of the optimal-truncation error.

Suppose \( f \) and \( g \) both have asymptotic expansions \( \sum a_n z^{-n} \) and \( \sum b_n z^{-n} \) as \( z \to \infty \). Prove the product \( fg \) has the expansion \( \sum c_n z^{-n} \) with \( c_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} a_{n-k} b_k \), and explain why the \( c_n \) are then uniquely determined.
Let \( h(x) = \exp(-1/x) \sin(1/x) \) for \( x > 0 \). Determine its asymptotic power series as \( x \to 0^{+} \), and evaluate \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \to 0^{+}} h(x)/x^{10} \).

Consider \( \cosh z \) as \( |z| \to \infty \). In the sector \( |\arg z| < \pi/2 \) it behaves like \( \tfrac12 e^{z} \). Explain how the subdominant term \( \tfrac12 e^{-z} \) is exponentially small there, and why this hidden term is exactly the kind of contribution an asymptotic expansion in that sector omits.

Define \( \Phi(x) = \exp(-a/x) \) for constants \( a > 0 \). Two such bumps, with \( a = 1 \) and \( a = 2 \), are added to a common base \( B(x) \). Show all three of \( B \), \( B + e^{-1/x} \), \( B + e^{-1/x} + e^{-2/x} \) share the same power series, and find \( \lim_{x\to 0^+} (e^{-1/x} + e^{-2/x})/x^N \) for arbitrary fixed \( N \).

Let \( h(x) = e^{-1/x} \) extended by \( h(0) = 0 \). Its series is \( 0 \). Show that term-by-term differentiation of this zero series gives the (correct) zero series for \( h' \) on \( x > 0 \), and discuss why differentiation can nevertheless fail for general asymptotic series.

Using \( \Gamma(1/2) = \sqrt{\pi} \), consider \( f(x) = \Gamma\!\left(\tfrac12\right) + \exp(-1/x) \) on \( x > 0 \). State the asymptotic series of \( f \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \), and give \( \lim_{x\to 0^+} f(x) \) in exact form.

An asymptotic series for a function \( G \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \) has terms \( T_n = (-1)^n (n+1)!\, x^{n} \). The optimal-truncation error is known to be of order \( \exp(-1/x) \). For \( x = 0.1 \), find the index \( N+1 = [x^{-1}] \) used to truncate, and state the order of the resulting error.

am1d.questionText: Suppose \( f(x) = o(1) \) as \( x \to \infty \). Integrate this estimate to give the sharpest bound you can on \( \displaystyle \int_a^x f(t)\,dt \) of the form \( o(g(x)) \).
Given that the integrable function \( f \) satisfies \( f(t) = o(t^{2}) \) as \( t \to \infty \), find the sharpest bound of the form \( o(g(x)) \) on \( \displaystyle\int_1^x f(t)\,dt \).

An asymptotic power series as \( x \to 0^{+} \) is \( H(x) \sim 3 + 2x + 5x^{2} + 7x^{3} + \cdots \) with \( H'(x) \) continuous up to \( x=0 \) and itself possessing an asymptotic power series. Write down the term-by-term differentiated series for \( H'(x) \).

Integrate the asymptotic series \( g(t) \sim 1 - t + t^{2} - t^{3} + \cdots \) (valid as \( t \to 0^{+} \)) term by term to obtain the leading three non-zero terms of an asymptotic series for \( \displaystyle F(x)=\int_0^x g(t)\,dt \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \).

The function \( G(x) \) has the asymptotic series \( G(x) \sim a_0 + a_1 x + a_2 x^{2} + \cdots \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \), and it is known that \( G = F' \) for some \( F \) with \( F(0)=0 \). Assuming term-by-term integration is valid, write the leading three terms of the series for \( F \) in terms of the \( a_n \).

Consider \( h(x) = \exp(-1/x) \) for \( x>0 \). By comparing \( h(x) \) with \( x^{N} \), explain why \( h \) has the asymptotic power series \( h(x) \sim 0 + 0\cdot x + 0\cdot x^{2} + \cdots \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \), and state the value of every coefficient.

Let \( f \) be continuous with \( f(x)=o(\varphi(x)) \) as \( x\to\infty \), where \( \varphi \) is continuous, positive and non-decreasing. Show that \( \displaystyle\int_a^x f(t)\,dt = o\big(x\,\varphi(x)\big) \) as \( x\to+\infty \).

For the Stieltjes integral \( \displaystyle F(x)=\int_0^{\infty}\frac{e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \), it is given that \( F(x)\sim\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(-1)^n n!\,x^{n} \) as \( x\to 0^{+} \). By differentiating under the integral sign, find \( F'(x) \) as an integral and hence its asymptotic series.

Let \( e(x)=\exp(-1/x) \) and \( q(x)=1+2x-x^{2}+e(x) \) for \( x>0 \). Find the asymptotic power series of \( q \) as \( x\to 0^{+} \), and explain what this shows about whether such a series determines the function uniquely.

Suppose \( H \) has the asymptotic series \( H(x)\sim\sum_{n\ge 0}\alpha_n x^{n} \) as \( x\to 0^{+} \), and that \( H' \) is continuous on \( [0,\infty) \) and also possesses an asymptotic series \( H'(x)\sim\sum_{n\ge 0}\beta_n x^{n} \). Prove that \( \beta_n=(n+1)\alpha_{n+1} \).
Use integration by parts to obtain the first three terms of the asymptotic expansion, as \( x\to\infty \), of the exponential integral \( \displaystyle E_1(x)=\int_x^{\infty}\frac{e^{-t}}{t}\,dt \).

It is given that \( E_1(x)+\ln x \to -\gamma \) as \( x\to 0^{+} \), where \( \gamma \) is Euler's constant. By differentiating \( E_1(x)+\ln x \) and integrating the resulting series, find the first two non-constant terms of the small-\( x \) expansion of \( E_1(x) \).

Let \( s(x)=\sin x \). Show that integrating the bound \( s(x)=O(1) \) over \( [0,x] \) is consistent with \( \int_0^x \sin t\,dt = O(1) \), but that differentiating the (bounded) primitive does NOT lower the order. State, in one line, the general moral about which operation is safe.

Given \( \displaystyle G(x)=\int_0^{\infty}\frac{e^{-t}}{(1+xt)^{2}}\,dt \sim \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(-1)^n (n+1)!\,x^{n} \) as \( x\to 0^{+} \), integrate the series term by term to find the asymptotic series of \( \displaystyle \Phi(x)=\int_0^x G(s)\,ds \). Identify the closed form of \( \Phi \).

The Stieltjes series \( F(x)\sim\sum (-1)^n n!\,x^{n} \) and \( G(x)\sim\sum(-1)^n(n+1)!\,x^{n} \) satisfy \( F'=G \) for \( \rho(t)=x e^{-t} \). Comment precisely on the relationship between the two series, i.e. show \( G \)'s series is the term-by-term derivative of \( F \)'s.

Find the asymptotic series, as \( x\to\infty \), of \( \displaystyle J(x)=\int_x^{\infty}\frac{e^{-t}}{t^{2}}\,dt \) to three terms by integration by parts, and verify it equals \( -\frac{d}{dx} \) applied term-by-term to \( e^{-x}/x \) is NOT the right relation — instead relate \( J \) to \( E_1 \).

The error function complement satisfies \( \operatorname{erfc}(x)=\frac{2}{\sqrt\pi}\int_x^{\infty}e^{-t^{2}}\,dt \). Using integration by parts, find the first two terms of its asymptotic expansion as \( x\to\infty \).

Suppose \( f(x)=o(e^{x}) \) as \( x\to\infty \) with \( f \) continuous. By integrating, find the sharpest order bound of the form \( o(g(x)) \) for \( \displaystyle\int_0^x f(t)\,dt \), and explain why the naive answer \( o(x e^{x}) \) is not the sharpest here.

Give an explicit smooth \( H:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty) \) that admits an asymptotic power series \( \sum\alpha_n x^{n} \) as \( x\to 0^{+} \) but for which term-by-term differentiation does NOT give an asymptotic series for \( H' \). Justify each claim.

For the Stieltjes integral \( \displaystyle G(x)=\int_0^{\infty}\frac{e^{-t}}{(1+xt)^{2}}\,dt \sim \sum_{n\ge 0}(-1)^n(n+1)!\,x^{n} \), use optimal truncation at \( x=0.1 \) to estimate \( G(0.1) \), and compare with the exact value \( 0.84366660602\ldots \).

Show that if \( f \) is continuous and \( f(x)=o(\varphi(x)) \) as \( x\to\infty \) with \( \varphi \) continuous, positive and non-decreasing, then for any fixed \( c>a \), \( \displaystyle\int_c^x f(t)\,dt = o(x\varphi(x)) \); and explain why the result can FAIL if \( \varphi \) is allowed to decrease.

The Stieltjes integral \( \displaystyle F(x)=\int_0^{\infty}\frac{e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \) has \( F\sim\sum(-1)^n n!\,x^n \) and derivative \( G=F' \) (with \( \rho=xe^{-t} \) framing). Verify the identity \( F'(x)=G(x) \) directly at \( x=0.1 \) by computing both sides, and state what this confirms about differentiating the asymptotic series.

Starting from \( E_1(x)\sim e^{-x}\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n n!\,x^{-n-1} \) as \( x\to\infty \), confirm by differentiating term by term that the resulting series is consistent with the exact relation \( E_1'(x)=-e^{-x}/x \). State to what extent term-by-term differentiation is justified.

Define \( \displaystyle S(x)=\int_0^x \frac{\sin t}{t}\,dt \) (so \( S\to\pi/2 \) as \( x\to\infty \)). Using integration by parts on \( \int_x^{\infty}\frac{\sin t}{t}\,dt \), find the first two terms of the large-\( x \) expansion of \( \frac{\pi}{2}-S(x) \).

It is given that \( \displaystyle\int_x^{\infty}t^{-1}e^{-t}\,dt = E_1(x) \) has remainder bound \( |\text{Err}_N|\le N!\,e^{-x}x^{-N-1} \). Using optimal truncation \( N+1=\lfloor x\rfloor \) and Stirling's formula, show the optimal error is \( O\big(x^{1/2}e^{-2x}\big) \) and hence beyond all algebraic orders relative to \( e^{-x} \).

Let \( \displaystyle F(x)=\int_0^{\infty}\frac{e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \) with \( F\sim\sum(-1)^n n!\,x^n \). Using optimal truncation at \( x=0.2 \), estimate \( F(0.2) \) and compare with the exact value \( 0.85211088\ldots \). State which term is the smallest.

Suppose \( H'(x) \) is continuous on \( [0,\infty) \) with \( H'(x)\sim 4 + 6x + 3x^{2} + \cdots \) as \( x\to 0^{+} \) and \( H(0)=7 \). Find the asymptotic series of \( H \) to order \( x^{3} \), and confirm that re-differentiating recovers the given series for \( H' \).

By integrating its derivative, find the leading two terms of the small-\( x \) expansion of \( \displaystyle \operatorname{Ci}(x)=-\int_x^{\infty}\frac{\cos t}{t}\,dt \), given \( \operatorname{Ci}(x)=\gamma+\ln x+\int_0^x\frac{\cos t-1}{t}\,dt \). Hence give \( \operatorname{Ci}(x) \) to order \( x^{2} \).

Construct a smooth \( f:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R} \) with \( f(x)=o(1) \) as \( x\to\infty \) whose derivative \( f' \) is NOT \( o(1) \) (indeed unbounded), and use it to argue that an estimate \( f=o(\varphi) \) can never, in general, be differentiated. Contrast with the safe integration result.

The incomplete Gamma function \( \displaystyle \Gamma(a,x)=\int_x^{\infty}t^{a-1}e^{-t}\,dt \) satisfies \( \partial_x\Gamma(a,x)=-x^{a-1}e^{-x} \). Find the first three terms of its large-\( x \) expansion by integration by parts, and confirm the series is consistent with that derivative under term-by-term differentiation.

am2a.questionText: The Stieltjes-type integral \( F(x) = \int_0^\infty \dfrac{\rho(t)}{1+xt}\,dt \) has the formal asymptotic series \( F(x) \sim \sum_{n=0}^\infty (-1)^n a_n x^n \) as \( x \to 0^+ \). State the coefficient \( a_n \) as an integral of \( \rho \).
For the density \( \rho(t) = e^{-t} \) on \( [0,\infty) \), compute the moment coefficient \( a_n = \int_0^\infty t^n e^{-t}\,dt \).
Using the moments of \( \rho(t)=e^{-t} \), write down the first four terms of the asymptotic series of \( F(x)=\int_0^\infty \dfrac{e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \) as \( x\to 0^+ \).
Show, using the ratio test, that the series \( \sum_{n=0}^\infty (-1)^n n!\,x^n \) diverges for every \( x>0 \).
For \( \rho(t) = e^{-2t} \) on \( [0,\infty) \), find the moment coefficient \( a_n = \int_0^\infty t^n e^{-2t}\,dt \).
A density is supported on the unit interval: \( \rho(t)=1 \) for \( 0\le t\le 1 \) and \( \rho(t)=0 \) otherwise. Find the moment coefficient \( a_n=\int_0^1 t^n\,dt \).

The function \( \rho \) is continuous and satisfies \( 0\le\rho(t)\le C e^{-\epsilon t} \) for some \( C,\epsilon>0 \) and all \( t\ge 0 \). Show that \( F(x)=\int_0^\infty \dfrac{\rho(t)}{1+xt}\,dt \) admits the asymptotic expansion \( F(x)\sim\sum_{n=0}^\infty (-1)^n a_n x^n \) as \( x\to 0^+ \), with \( a_n=\int_0^\infty t^n\rho(t)\,dt \).
For \( \rho(t)=e^{-t} \), show that \( F(x)=\int_0^\infty \dfrac{e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \sim \sum_{n=0}^\infty (-1)^n n!\,x^n \) as \( x\to 0^+ \), and explain in one line why the series diverges.
Find the asymptotic expansion as \( x\to 0^+ \) of \( F(x)=\int_0^\infty \dfrac{e^{-2t}}{1+xt}\,dt \), giving the general term.
For the bounded-support density \( \rho(t)=1 \) on \( [0,1] \), evaluate \( F(x)=\int_0^1 \dfrac{dt}{1+xt} \) in closed form, and hence write its (convergent) Maclaurin series in \( x \).
Show that for \( \rho(t)=e^{-t} \) the remainder \( R_N(x)=F(x)-\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}(-1)^n n!\,x^n \) satisfies \( |R_N(x)|\le N!\,x^N \) as \( x\to 0^+ \).

For \( \rho(t)=e^{-t} \) at \( x=0.1 \), the term magnitudes are \( |u_n|=n!\,(0.1)^n \). Find the value of \( n \) for which \( |u_{n+1}|/|u_n|=1 \), i.e. where the terms stop decreasing, and hence state where to truncate optimally.
Let \( G(x)=\int_0^\infty \dfrac{e^{-t}}{(1+xt)^2}\,dt \). By expanding \( (1+xt)^{-2} \), show that \( G(x)\sim\sum_{n=0}^\infty (-1)^n (n+1)!\,x^n \) as \( x\to 0^+ \).

Given \( F(x)=\int_0^\infty \dfrac{e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \) and \( G(x)=\int_0^\infty \dfrac{e^{-t}}{(1+xt)^2}\,dt \), differentiate under the integral sign to relate \( F' \) and \( G \), and confirm the relation at the level of their asymptotic series.
For \( \rho(t)=t\,e^{-t} \), find the moments \( a_n=\int_0^\infty t^n\,t e^{-t}\,dt \) and write the asymptotic series of \( F(x)=\int_0^\infty \dfrac{t e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \) as \( x\to 0^+ \).

By comparing the two integrals, show that \( \int_0^\infty \dfrac{t e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \) and \( \int_0^\infty \dfrac{e^{-t}}{(1+xt)^2}\,dt \) share the same asymptotic series, and give an algebraic identity between their integrands that explains why.
For \( \rho(t)=e^{-t^2} \) on \( [0,\infty) \), find the moments \( a_n=\int_0^\infty t^n e^{-t^2}\,dt \) in terms of the Gamma function, and state \( a_0 \) and \( a_1 \) explicitly.

Explain carefully why the expansion \( F(x)\sim\sum (-1)^n n!\,x^n \) is an ASYMPTOTIC series and not a Taylor series, addressing both convergence and the behaviour of the remainder as \( x\to 0^+ \).

For \( \rho(t)=e^{-t} \), express \( F(x)=\int_0^\infty \dfrac{e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \) exactly in terms of the exponential integral \( E_1 \), where \( E_1(z)=\int_z^\infty \dfrac{e^{-s}}{s}\,ds \). Hence recover the leading asymptotic behaviour as \( x\to 0^+ \).

For \( G(x)=\int_0^\infty \dfrac{e^{-t}}{(1+xt)^2}\,dt \sim\sum_{n=0}^\infty (-1)^n (n+1)!\,x^n \) at \( x=0.1 \), identify the smallest term in the series and use optimal truncation to estimate \( G(0.1) \), comparing with the known value \( G(0.1)=0.84366660602\ldots \).

Suppose \( f(x)\sim\sum a_n x^n \) and \( g(x)\sim\sum b_n x^n \) as \( x\to 0^+ \). Show that \( f(x)g(x)\sim\sum c_n x^n \) with \( c_n=\sum_{k=0}^n a_{n-k}b_k \), and apply this to square the Stieltjes series \( F(x)\sim\sum (-1)^n n! x^n \), giving \( c_0,c_1,c_2 \).

Given \( f(x)\sim a_0 + a_1 x + a_2 x^2 + \cdots \) with \( a_0\ne 0 \), show that \( 1/f(x)\sim \dfrac{1}{a_0}\sum_{n=0}^\infty d_n x^n \) where \( d_0=1 \) and \( \sum_{k=0}^n d_{n-k}a_k=0 \) for \( n\ge 1 \). Compute \( d_1,d_2 \) for \( F(x)\sim 1 - x + 2x^2 - \cdots \).

Consider \( H(x)=\int_0^\infty \dfrac{\rho(t)}{1+xt}\,dt \) with \( \rho(t)=\dfrac{1}{\pi}\,\dfrac{1}{1+t^2} \cdot 2 \) on \( [0,\infty) \) (so \( \int_0^\infty\rho=1 \)). Show that the formal moments \( a_n=\int_0^\infty t^n\rho(t)\,dt \) DIVERGE for \( n\ge 1 \), and explain what this means for the existence of a power-series asymptotic expansion of \( H \).

For \( \rho(t)=e^{-t} \), define optimal truncation by \( N+1=[1/x] \) (integer part). Using the error bound \( \mathrm{Err}_N\le (N+1)!\,x^{N+1} \) and Stirling's formula, show that the optimal error is \( O\!\bigl([1/x]^{1/2}e^{-[1/x]}\bigr)=o(x^M) \) as \( x\to0^+ \) for every positive integer \( M \).

Use integration by parts on \( E_1(x)=\int_x^\infty \dfrac{e^{-t}}{t}\,dt \) to derive its asymptotic expansion \( E_1(x)\sim e^{-x}\bigl(\tfrac1x-\tfrac1{x^2}+\tfrac{2}{x^3}-\cdots\bigr) \) as \( x\to\infty \), showing the remainder after \( N \) terms is \( O(e^{-x}x^{-N-1}) \), and connect this to the Stieltjes form \( F=\tfrac{e^{1/x}}{x}E_1(1/x) \).

Show that the Stieltjes integral \( F(x)=\int_0^\infty \dfrac{e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \) is the Borel sum of its divergent series \( \sum (-1)^n n! x^n \): form the Borel transform \( B(\xi)=\sum \tfrac{(-1)^n n!}{n!}\xi^n \), sum it, and recover \( F \) by the Borel integral.

A density \( \rho \) is smooth with \( \rho(t)\sim \sum_{k\ge 0} c_k t^k \) as \( t\to0^+ \) and decays exponentially at infinity. Using Watson's lemma ideas, explain why the small-\( x \) Stieltjes expansion of \( F(x)=\int_0^\infty \rho(t)/(1+xt)\,dt \) is governed by the full moments \( a_n=\int_0^\infty t^n\rho \), NOT by the local data \( c_k \) at \( t=0 \). Contrast this with a Laplace-type integral \( \int_0^\infty \rho(t)e^{-t/x}\,dt \).

For \( \rho(t)=e^{-t} \) and the convergent (bounded-support) companion \( F_b(x)=\int_0^1 \dfrac{dt}{1+xt}=\dfrac{\ln(1+x)}{x} \), compute the ratio of the third asymptotic coefficients \( a_2^{(e)}/a_2^{(b)} \) and comment on which series converges.

Let \( F(x)=\int_0^\infty \dfrac{e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \sim \sum (-1)^n n! x^n \). Using the optimal-truncation error estimate at general small \( x \), show that the least achievable error is \( \approx \sqrt{2\pi/x}\;e^{-1/x} \), and hence determine the number of correct decimal digits obtainable at \( x=0.05 \).

Consider the generalised Stieltjes integral \( F_s(x)=\int_0^\infty \dfrac{e^{-t}}{(1+xt)^s}\,dt \) for real \( s>0 \). Derive the asymptotic series as \( x\to0^+ \) using the binomial expansion of \( (1+xt)^{-s} \), and verify it reduces to the \( s=1 \) and \( s=2 \) cases.

am2b.questionText: Consider the divergent asymptotic series whose general term has magnitude \( |t_n| = \dfrac{n!}{x^{\,n+1}} \) (the terms of \( E_1(x) \)). For \( x = 8 \), find the value of \( n \) that minimises \( |t_n| \).
An asymptotic series has term magnitudes \( |t_n| = n!\,x^{n} \) (the terms of the Stieltjes integral \( F(x) \)). For \( x = \tfrac{1}{5} \), find the index \( n \) of the least term.
State, in words, the standard convention for the optimal truncation of a divergent asymptotic series, and explain which partial sum it tells you to retain.

For the series with term magnitudes \( |t_n| = \dfrac{n!}{x^{\,n+1}} \), use the rule of thumb to estimate the least-term index \( n^\ast \) for general large \( x \), and hence give the order of magnitude of the optimal error.
An asymptotic series has term magnitudes \( |t_n| = (n+1)!\,x^{n} \) (the terms of the Stieltjes integral \( G(x) \)). For \( x = \tfrac{1}{10} \), find the least-term index \( n \).
The complementary error function has the asymptotic series with term magnitudes \( |t_n| = \dfrac{(2n-1)!!}{(2x^2)^n} \). For \( x = 2 \), find the index \( n \) of the least term.

The exponential integral \( E_1(x)=\displaystyle\int_x^\infty \frac{e^{-t}}{t}\,dt \) has the asymptotic series \( E_1(x)\sim e^{-x}\sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(-1)^n n!}{x^{\,n+1}} \). For \( x = 5 \), locate the least term and use optimal truncation to estimate \( E_1(5) \). (Reference value \( E_1(5)=0.00114830 \).)

Using the same series for the exponential integral, \( E_1(x)\sim e^{-x}\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{(-1)^n n!}{x^{n+1}} \), apply optimal truncation at \( x = 8 \) to estimate \( E_1(8) \). (Reference value \( E_1(8)=3.7666\times10^{-5} \).)

The Stieltjes integral \( G(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-t}}{(1+xt)^2}\,dt \) has the asymptotic series \( G(x)\sim\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n (n+1)!\,x^n \). For \( x = 0.1 \), find the least term and use optimal truncation to estimate \( G(0.1) \). (Reference value \( G(0.1)=0.843667 \).)

The Stieltjes integral \( F(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \) has the asymptotic series \( F(x)\sim\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n n!\,x^n \). For \( x = 0.1 \), apply optimal truncation to estimate \( F(0.1) \). (Reference value \( F(0.1)=0.915633 \).)

The complementary error function satisfies \( \operatorname{erfc}(x)\sim\dfrac{e^{-x^2}}{x\sqrt\pi}\sum_{n\ge0}\dfrac{(-1)^n (2n-1)!!}{(2x^2)^n} \). For \( x = 2.5 \), locate the least term and use optimal truncation to estimate \( \operatorname{erfc}(2.5) \). (Reference value \( \operatorname{erfc}(2.5)=4.0695\times10^{-4} \).)

For the exponential-integral series with term magnitudes \( e^{-x}\,n!/x^{n+1} \), the smallest term at \( x = 6 \) occurs at \( n^\ast = 5 \). Estimate the smallest achievable truncation error, and state how many correct significant figures this implies for \( E_1(6) \).

Apply optimal truncation to the Stieltjes series \( F(x)\sim\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n n!\,x^n \) at \( x = 0.2 \). Find the least-term index, give the truncated estimate of \( F(0.2) \), and quote the resulting error. (Reference value \( F(0.2)=0.852111 \).)
Use optimal truncation on the exponential-integral series at \( x = 4 \) to estimate \( E_1(4) \), and state the error. (Reference value \( E_1(4)=3.7794\times10^{-3} \).)

Two asymptotic series have term magnitudes \( |a_n| = n!/x^{n+1} \) and \( |b_n| = (n+1)!\,y^n \). Find general formulae for the least-term index of each (the integer where the magnitude is smallest), and explain why one favours large \( x \) and the other small \( y \).
Apply optimal truncation to the Stieltjes series \( G(x)\sim\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n(n+1)!\,x^n \) at \( x = 0.2 \) to estimate \( G(0.2) \), and quote the error. (Reference value \( G(0.2)=0.739446 \).)
Apply optimal truncation to the exponential-integral series at \( x = 10 \) to estimate \( E_1(10) \). (Reference value \( E_1(10)=4.15697\times10^{-6} \).)

For the exponential-integral series with least term near \( n^\ast\approx x \), use Stirling's formula to show that the optimal truncation error behaves like \( \sqrt{2\pi/x}\;e^{-x} \), and confirm this is \( o(x^{-M}) \) as \( x\to\infty \) for every integer \( M \).

Starting from \( G(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-t}}{(1+xt)^2}\,dt \), derive its asymptotic series, locate the least term at \( x = 0.1 \), and use optimal truncation to estimate \( G(0.1) \). Compare with the exact value \( G(0.1)=0.843667 \) and comment on the accuracy. (This is example-sheet Q9(c) with the convention spelled out.)

The Stieltjes integrals satisfy \( G(x)=\frac{d}{dx}\big[x\,F(x)\big] \), with series \( F\sim\sum(-1)^n n!\,x^n \) and \( G\sim\sum(-1)^n(n+1)!\,x^n \). Show that the least-term index of \( G \) is one less than that of \( F \) for the same \( x \), and explain why this differentiation shifts the optimal truncation point.

Derive the asymptotic series of \( E_1(x)=\int_x^\infty t^{-1}e^{-t}\,dt \) by repeated integration by parts, then for \( x = 6 \) locate the least term and use optimal truncation to estimate \( E_1(6) \). Compare with \( E_1(6)=3.60082\times10^{-4} \).

Apply optimal truncation to the complementary error function series at \( x = 3 \) to estimate \( \operatorname{erfc}(3) \), and verify the error matches the least-term magnitude. (Reference value \( \operatorname{erfc}(3)=2.209050\times10^{-5} \).)

For the case \( \rho(t)=e^{-t} \), the Stieltjes integral gives \( F(x)=\sum_{n=0}^{N}(-1)^n n!\,x^n + \mathrm{Err}_N \) with bound \( |\mathrm{Err}_N|\le (N+1)!\,x^{N+1} \). Defining optimal truncation by \( N+1=\lfloor x^{-1}\rfloor \), use Stirling's formula to show the optimal error bound is \( O\big(x^{-1/2}e^{-1/x}\big) \) and hence \( o(x^M) \) as \( x\to0^+ \) for every integer \( M \). (Example-sheet Q9(d), varied.)

A divergent asymptotic series has term magnitudes \( |t_n| = \Gamma(n+a)\,z^{-n} \) for a fixed constant \( a>0 \) and large \( z \). Find the least-term index \( n^\ast \) in terms of \( z \) and \( a \), and the leading behaviour of the least-term magnitude.

Compare optimal truncation of the exponential-integral series at \( x = 5 \) and \( x = 7 \): in each case give \( n^\ast \), the optimally truncated estimate of \( E_1(x) \), and the error, then state how many extra correct figures the larger \( x \) buys. (References: \( E_1(5)=1.14830\times10^{-3} \), \( E_1(7)=1.15482\times10^{-4} \).)

For an alternating divergent series with term magnitudes \( |t_n| \), show that the optimal-truncation error is bounded by the first omitted term, and explain why for an alternating asymptotic series the true sum is bracketed between consecutive partial sums. Apply this to bound the error of \( F(0.1)\sim\sum(-1)^n n!\,0.1^n \) truncated at the least term.

Consider \( I(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-t}}{1+x^2 t}\,dt \). Find its asymptotic series in powers of \( x^2 \), locate the least term at \( x = 0.4 \) (so \( x^2 = 0.16 \)), and use optimal truncation to estimate \( I(0.4) \). (Reference value \( I(0.4)=0.875687 \).)

Explain the principle of superasymptotics: that the optimal (least-term) truncation error of a factorially divergent series is exponentially small in the large parameter, and contrast this with the algebraically small error of an ordinary convergent power series truncated at \( N \) terms. Illustrate using the generic term \( |t_n| = n!/x^{n+1} \).

For the Stieltjes integral \( F(x)=\int_0^\infty e^{-t}/(1+xt)\,dt \) at \( x = 0.25 \), determine the least-term index, apply optimal truncation to estimate \( F(0.25) \), and explain why optimal truncation gives a poor estimate here. (Reference value \( F(0.25)=0.825383 \).)

A function has the asymptotic series \( S(x)\sim\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n c_n\,x^{-n} \) with \( c_n = A^{-n}\,n! \) for a constant \( A>0 \) (a factorially divergent tail with 'singularity distance' \( A \)). Find the least-term index and magnitude as functions of \( x \) and \( A \), and state how the optimal error depends on \( A \).

am2c.questionText: The asymptotic series for a function has terms \( a_n = (-1)^n n!\,x^{n} \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \). For \( x = \tfrac{1}{10} \), find the value of \( n \) at which the term magnitude \( |a_n| \) is smallest.
An asymptotic series has terms of magnitude \( |a_n| = n!\,x^{n} \). Show that, as \( x \to 0^{+} \), the index of the smallest term is approximately \( n^{*} \approx 1/x \).

For the asymptotic expansion \( E_1(x) \sim e^{-x}\sum_{n\ge 0} (-1)^{n} n!\,x^{-(n+1)} \) of the exponential integral as \( x \to +\infty \), the term magnitudes are \( |a_n| = n!\,x^{-(n+1)} \). Find the index \( n \) of the smallest term when \( x = 5 \).

State the optimal-truncation rule for a divergent asymptotic series and the resulting error bound. (Take optimal truncation to mean keeping every term up to the one immediately before the smallest, and recall that for an alternating asymptotic series the truncation error is bounded by the first omitted term.)
For the series with terms \( |a_n| = n!\,x^{n} \) at \( x = \tfrac{1}{20} \), use \( N+1 = [\,1/x\,] \) (integer part) to find how many terms \( N+1 \) optimal truncation keeps.

Using Stirling's formula \( m! \sim \sqrt{2\pi m}\,(m/e)^{m} \), find an approximation for the least-term magnitude \( a_{n^{*}} = (n^{*})!\,x^{n^{*}} \) of the series \( \sum n!\,x^{n} \), taking \( n^{*} = 1/x \).

The Stieltjes integral \( F(x) = \displaystyle\int_0^{\infty} \frac{e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \) has the divergent asymptotic expansion \( F(x) \sim \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} (-1)^n n!\,x^{n} \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \). For \( x = \tfrac{1}{10} \), find the smallest-term magnitude and hence the optimal-truncation error bound.

For the Stieltjes integral expansion \( F(x) \sim \sum (-1)^n n!\,x^{n} \) with \( x = \tfrac{1}{10} \), optimal truncation keeps \( N+1 = [\,1/x\,] = 10 \) terms. Given the exact value \( F(0.1) = 0.9156333\ldots \), compute the optimal-truncation estimate \( S_9 = \sum_{n=0}^{9} (-1)^n n!\,(0.1)^n \) and verify the error is below the least-term bound.

The companion integral \( G(x) = \displaystyle\int_0^{\infty}\frac{e^{-t}}{(1+xt)^2}\,dt \) has expansion \( G(x) \sim \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} (-1)^n (n+1)!\,x^{n} \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \). For \( x = \tfrac{1}{10} \), find the index of the smallest term.

For the exponential-integral expansion \( E_1(x) \sim e^{-x}\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n n!\,x^{-(n+1)} \) as \( x \to +\infty \), the truncation error after \( N \) terms satisfies \( |\mathrm{Err}_N| \le e^{-x} N!\,x^{-(N+1)} \). For \( x = 5 \), find the value of \( N \) giving the tightest bound and the resulting bound.
Show, using Stirling's formula, that the least-term magnitude of the series \( \sum n!\,x^{n} \) (taken at \( n^{*} = 1/x \)) is \( O\!\left(x^{-1/2}e^{-1/x}\right) \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \).
Show that \( x^{-1/2}e^{-1/x} = o(x^{M}) \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \) for every fixed positive integer \( M \), i.e. the optimal error is beyond all algebraic orders (exponentially accurate).
An asymptotic series as \( x \to 0^{+} \) has term magnitudes \( |a_n| = (2n)!\,x^{n} \). For \( x = \tfrac{1}{100} \), find the index of the smallest term.

For the case \( \rho(t) = e^{-t} \), the Stieltjes integral gives \( F(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{N}(-1)^n n!\,x^{n} + \mathrm{Err}_N \) with rigorous bound \( |\mathrm{Err}_N| \le (N+1)!\,x^{N+1} \). Verify that minimising this bound over \( N \) reproduces the optimal-truncation rule \( N+1 = [\,1/x\,] \).

For the series with term magnitudes \( |a_n| = n!\,x^{n} \) at \( x = \tfrac{1}{50} \), use Stirling's formula to estimate the optimal-truncation error bound \( \sqrt{2\pi/x}\,e^{-1/x} \) and give it to two significant figures.

Show that for an alternating asymptotic series \( f(x) \sim \sum (-1)^n a_n \) with \( a_n > 0 \), if the magnitudes are first decreasing then increasing, the partial-sum error is bounded by the first omitted term whenever truncation stops within the decreasing run.

A function has asymptotic series with term magnitudes \( |a_n| = n!\,(2x)^{n} \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \). For \( x = \tfrac{1}{8} \), find the index of the smallest term and the number of terms \( N+1 \) kept by optimal truncation.

The companion integral satisfies \( G(0.1) = 0.84366660602\ldots \), with expansion \( G(x) \sim \sum (-1)^n (n+1)!\,x^{n} \). Optimal truncation keeps terms up to \( n = 8 \). Compute \( S_8 = \sum_{n=0}^{8}(-1)^n (n+1)!\,(0.1)^n \) and state the truncation error to one significant figure.

For \( \rho(t) = e^{-t} \) the Stieltjes integral gives the rigorous bound \( |\mathrm{Err}_N| \le (N+1)!\,x^{N+1} \). Define optimal truncation by \( N+1 = [\,1/x\,] \) and use Stirling's formula to show the resulting optimal error bound is \( O\!\left(x^{-1/2}e^{-1/x}\right) = o(x^{M}) \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \) for every positive integer \( M \).

A divergent asymptotic series as \( z \to \infty \) has term magnitudes \( |a_n| = n!\,z^{-n} \). Show that the least-term index is \( n^{*} \approx z \) and that the optimal error is \( O\!\left(z^{1/2}e^{-z}\right) \), hence exponentially small in \( z \).

Using integration by parts, derive the asymptotic expansion \( E_1(x) = \int_x^{\infty}\frac{e^{-t}}{t}\,dt \sim e^{-x}\left(\frac{1}{x} - \frac{1}{x^2} + \frac{2!}{x^3} - \cdots\right) \) as \( x \to \infty \), and show the remainder after \( N \) terms is \( O\!\left(e^{-x}x^{-(N+1)}\right) \). Hence give the optimal-truncation error order.

For the Stieltjes series \( F(x) \sim \sum (-1)^n n!\,x^{n} \) with \( x = \tfrac{1}{6} \), determine (i) the least-term index, (ii) the least-term magnitude, and (iii) confirm numerically that the optimal-truncation error is below this magnitude given \( F(1/6) = 0.871606\ldots \). Give the least-term index.

An asymptotic expansion as \( x \to 0^{+} \) has term magnitudes \( |a_n| = \Gamma(n + \tfrac12)\,x^{n} \). Show that the least-term index satisfies \( n^{*} \approx 1/x \) and find, via Stirling, the order of the least-term magnitude.

Explain why summing a divergent asymptotic series \( \sum a_n \) beyond its least term increases the error, and prove that for term magnitudes \( |a_n| = n!\,x^n \) the partial-sum-to-partial-sum change \( |a_{n+1}| \) exceeds \( |a_n| \) once \( n > 1/x - 1 \).

Two divergent series have term magnitudes \( |a_n| = n!\,x^{n} \) and \( |b_n| = n!\,(x/2)^{n} \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \). For \( x = \tfrac{1}{5} \), find the ratio of their least-term magnitudes \( a_{n^{*}_a}/b_{n^{*}_b} \) using the Stirling estimate \( \sqrt{2\pi/p}\,e^{-1/p} \) for the series with parameter \( p \).

Suppose \( f(x) \) has a divergent asymptotic series \( \sum a_n x^n \) with \( |a_n| \sim C\,n!\,A^{n} \) for constants \( C, A > 0 \) (a Gevrey-1 series). Show the least term is attained near \( n^{*} = 1/(Ax) \) and that the optimal error is \( O\!\left(x^{-1/2}e^{-1/(Ax)}\right) \), identifying \( 1/A \) as the radius governing the exponential rate.

For the exponential integral series \( E_1(x) \sim e^{-x}\sum(-1)^n n!\,x^{-(n+1)} \) at \( x = 10 \), compute the least-term magnitude \( e^{-10}\,9!\,10^{-10} \) to two significant figures, and state how many significant figures of \( E_1(10) = 4.157\times10^{-6} \) are reliably obtained.

Show that doubling the small parameter from \( x \) to \( 2x \) in the Gevrey-1 series \( \sum n!\,x^n \) worsens the optimal error from \( O\!\left(x^{-1/2}e^{-1/x}\right) \) to \( O\!\left(x^{-1/2}e^{-1/(2x)}\right) \), and quantify the loss as an exponential factor \( e^{1/(2x)} \).

The Stieltjes integral \( F(x) = \int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \) at \( x = \tfrac{1}{10} \) has exact value \( 0.9156333\ldots \) and least term \( 9!\,(0.1)^9 = 3.6288\times10^{-4} \). Compute the relative optimal accuracy \( |a_{n^{*}}|/F(0.1) \) and express it as a number of correct decimal places.

Prove that, for the Stieltjes series with rigorous bound \( |\mathrm{Err}_N| \le (N+1)!\,x^{N+1} \), no choice of \( N \) can make the error smaller than \( c\,x^{-1/2}e^{-1/x} \) for some constant \( c > 0 \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \); hence the exponentially small optimal error cannot be beaten by truncating the algebraic series, and capturing it requires going beyond all orders.

am2d.questionText: Determine the radius of convergence of the power series \( \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} (-1)^n\,n!\,x^n \), and hence classify it as a convergent or a (formally) divergent series for \( x \neq 0 \).

The geometric series \( \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} z^n \) has sum \( \dfrac{1}{1-z} \) for \( |z|<1 \). Using the analytic continuation of this closed form, assign a finite value to the divergent series \( 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + \cdots \).
Form the Borel transform \( B(t) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \dfrac{a_n}{n!}\,t^n \) of the formal series \( \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n x^n \) with \( a_n = (-1)^n\,n! \), and write \( B(t) \) in closed form.

For the alternating factorial series \( \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} (-1)^n\,n!\,x^n \) with small \( x>0 \), the magnitude of the \( n \)-th term is \( u_n = n!\,x^n \). Find the integer \( n \) at which \( u_n \) is smallest, in terms of \( x \).

By expanding the integrand as a geometric series and integrating term by term, find the formal (asymptotic) series of \( F(x) = \displaystyle\int_0^{\infty} \frac{e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \) as \( x \to 0^{+} \).

Define the Borel sum of a formal series \( \sum a_n x^n \) (with Borel transform \( B(t) \)) as \( S(x) = \dfrac{1}{x}\displaystyle\int_0^{\infty} e^{-t/x}\,B(t)\,dt \). Given that the Borel transform of \( \sum (-1)^n n! x^n \) is \( B(t)=1/(1+t) \), write \( S(x) \) as a single integral and evaluate \( S(1) \) in closed form.

Show that the Stieltjes-type integral \( F(x) = \displaystyle\int_0^{\infty} \frac{e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \) satisfies \( F(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} (-1)^n n!\,x^n + R_N(x) \) with a remainder \( R_N(x) \) you should write as an integral, and deduce that \( |R_N(x)| \le N!\,x^N \) for \( x>0 \).

Using optimal truncation of the Euler series \( F(x)\sim\sum (-1)^n n! x^n \) at \( x=0.1 \) (keep all terms up to the one before the smallest), estimate \( F(0.1) \) and compare with the exact value \( F(0.1)=0.915633\ldots \). State the optimal truncation index.

Find the first three terms of the asymptotic expansion of the exponential integral \( E_1(x) = \displaystyle\int_x^{\infty} \frac{e^{-t}}{t}\,dt \) as \( x\to\infty \), using repeated integration by parts, and state the general term.

The function \( e(x)=\exp(-1/x) \) for \( x>0 \) is to be expanded in an asymptotic power series \( e(x)\sim \beta_0 + \beta_1 x + \beta_2 x^2 + \cdots \) as \( x\to 0^{+} \). Show that every coefficient \( \beta_k \) is zero, and state \( \beta_2 \).

Given the formal asymptotic series \( f(z) \sim a_0 + \dfrac{a_1}{z} + \dfrac{a_2}{z^2} + \cdots \) as \( z\to\infty \) with \( a_0\neq 0 \), find the first three coefficients \( d_0,d_1,d_2 \) of the reciprocal expansion \( \dfrac{1}{f(z)} \sim \dfrac{1}{a_0}\sum_{n\ge 0}\dfrac{d_n}{z^n} \), where \( d_0=1 \) and \( \sum_{k=0}^{n} d_{n-k}\,a_k = 0 \) for \( n\ge 1 \).

Find the asymptotic series of \( G(x) = \displaystyle\int_0^{\infty} \frac{e^{-t}}{(1+xt)^2}\,dt \) as \( x\to 0^{+} \), and explain its relation to the Euler series for \( F(x)=\int_0^\infty e^{-t}/(1+xt)\,dt \).
Using Watson's lemma, find the leading two terms of the asymptotic expansion as \( x\to\infty \) of \( I(x) = \displaystyle\int_0^{\infty} \frac{e^{-xt}}{1+t}\,dt \), and state the full series.

Show that if \( f \) admits an asymptotic power series \( f(x)\sim\sum_{n\ge0} a_n x^n \) as \( x\to 0^{+} \) then the coefficients \( a_n \) are uniquely determined by \( f \). Give the formula for \( a_2 \).

If \( f(z)\sim\sum_{n\ge0} a_n z^{-n} \) and \( g(z)\sim\sum_{n\ge0} b_n z^{-n} \) as \( z\to\infty \), show that the product \( f(z)g(z) \) has asymptotic series \( \sum_{n\ge0} c_n z^{-n} \), and give \( c_n \) and \( c_2 \) explicitly.
Determine whether \( \phi_n(x) = 1 - \cosh(x^n) \), for \( n\in\{1,2,3,\dots\} \), forms an asymptotic sequence as \( x\to 0 \); i.e. check whether \( \phi_{n+1}(x) = o(\phi_n(x)) \).
Use Abel summation (the radial limit of the analytically-continued power series) to assign a value to Grandi's series \( 1 - 1 + 1 - 1 + \cdots \).

Show that if \( f \) is continuous and \( f(x)=o(\phi(x)) \) as \( x\to\infty \), where \( \phi \) is continuous, positive and non-decreasing, then \( \displaystyle\int_a^{x} f(t)\,dt = o\big(x\,\phi(x)\big) \) as \( x\to+\infty \).

Show that the Euler series \( \sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n n! x^n \) is Borel summable for \( x>0 \) and that its Borel sum equals \( \displaystyle\int_0^{\infty}\frac{e^{-t}}{1+xt}\,dt \). Hence give the Borel sum at \( x=1 \) in terms of the exponential integral, and its numerical value.

For the Euler series \( F(x)\sim\sum(-1)^n n! x^n \), optimal truncation keeps terms up to \( N\approx 1/x \). Using Stirling's formula, show that the resulting optimal error is exponentially small, of order \( O\big(x^{-1/2}e^{-1/x}\big) \) as \( x\to 0^{+} \).

The series \( \sum_{n\ge0} n!\,x^n \) (no alternating sign) has Borel transform \( B(t)=1/(1-t) \), which is singular at \( t=1 \). Define its Borel sum at \( x=1 \) by the Cauchy principal value \( \mathrm{PV}\!\int_0^{\infty}\frac{e^{-t}}{1-t}\,dt \). Evaluate this in closed form and give its numerical value.

Obtain the asymptotic expansion of \( E_1(x) \) as \( x\to 0^{+} \) by considering \( \dfrac{d}{dx}\big[E_1(x)+\ln x\big] \) and integrating, given that \( \lim_{x\to0^{+}}\big[E_1(x)+\ln x\big]=-\gamma \), where \( \gamma \) is Euler's constant. Give the first three terms.

Consider the Stieltjes integral \( F(x)=\int_0^{\infty}\frac{\rho(t)}{1+xt}\,dt \) with \( \rho(t)=t\,e^{-t} \). Show that \( F(x)\sim\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n (n+1)!\,x^{n} \) as \( x\to0^{+} \), where the coefficients are the moments \( a_n=\int_0^\infty t^n\rho(t)\,dt \). Identify \( a_n \) and the first two terms.

Using Watson's lemma, find the full asymptotic expansion as \( x\to\infty \) of \( J(x)=\int_0^{\infty}\frac{e^{-xt}}{1+t^2}\,dt \), and give the first two non-zero terms. Comment on whether the series converges.

Give an example of a smooth function \( H:(0,\infty)\to(0,\infty) \) that admits an asymptotic expansion \( H(x)\sim\sum_{n\ge0}\alpha_n x^n \) as \( x\to0^{+} \) but for which term-by-term differentiation fails to give an asymptotic expansion of \( H'(x) \). Justify briefly.

Show by repeated integration by parts, or otherwise, that \( \Phi(x)=\int_x^{\infty} e^{x^2-t^2}\,dt \) (related to the complementary error function) has the asymptotic expansion \( \Phi(x)\sim\frac{1}{2x}\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n\frac{(2n-1)!!}{(2x^2)^n} \) as \( x\to\infty \). Give the first two terms and the general term.

Apply the Euler transform \( \sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n a_n = \sum_{k\ge0}\dfrac{(-1)^0\,\Delta^k a_0}{2^{k+1}} \) (with forward differences \( \Delta^k a_0 \)) to accelerate, and hence assign a value to, the divergent series \( \sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^n \) (i.e. \( a_n=1 \)). Evaluate the resummed value.

For the Euler integral \( F(x)=\int_0^\infty e^{-t}/(1+xt)\,dt \) at \( x=0.2 \), the exact value is \( F(0.2)=0.852111\ldots \). Determine the optimal truncation index of the series \( \sum(-1)^n n!(0.2)^n \), evaluate the optimally truncated partial sum, and bound the error by the first omitted term.

Establish the contrast between convergent and asymptotic behaviour for \( I(x)=\int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-xt}}{1+t}\,dt \): show its large-\( x \) expansion \( \sum (-1)^n n!/x^{n+1} \) diverges, while the related sum \( \sum_{n\ge1}(-1)^{n-1}/n \) (the Mercator/Leibniz-type series) converges. Identify the convergent sum's value.

Define \( K(x)=\int_0^{\infty}\frac{e^{-t}}{1+x^2 t^2}\,dt \). Find its asymptotic series as \( x\to0^{+} \), determine the Borel transform of that series, and evaluate the Borel sum at \( x=1 \) in closed form.

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 01
am3a.questionText: Consider the exponential integral \( E_1(x) = \int_x^{\infty} \dfrac{e^{-t}}{t}\,dt \) for large \( x > 0 \). Apply integration by parts once, taking \( u = 1/t \) and \( dv = e^{-t}\,dt \), to find the leading behaviour of \( E_1(x) \) as \( x \to \infty \).

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 02
am3a.questionText: Let \( I(x) = \int_x^{\infty} \dfrac{e^{-t}}{t^{2}}\,dt \) for large \( x > 0 \). Integrate by parts once to extract the leading term of \( I(x) \) as \( x \to \infty \).

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 03
am3a.questionText: Find the leading asymptotic behaviour of \( J(x) = \int_x^{\infty} e^{-t^{2}}\,dt \) as \( x \to \infty \) by writing \( e^{-t^2} = -\dfrac{1}{2t}\dfrac{d}{dt}\,e^{-t^2} \) and integrating by parts once.

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 04
am3a.questionText: Let \( K(x) = \int_x^{\infty} \dfrac{e^{-2t}}{t}\,dt \) for large \( x > 0 \). Integrate by parts once to find the leading term as \( x \to \infty \).

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 05
am3a.questionText: Evaluate \( L(x) = \int_x^{\infty} t\,e^{-t}\,dt \) in closed form by integration by parts, and hence state its leading behaviour as \( x \to \infty \).

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 06
am3a.questionText: Find the leading asymptotic term of \( M(x) = \int_x^{\infty} \dfrac{e^{-t}}{\sqrt{t}}\,dt \) as \( x \to \infty \) using one integration by parts.

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 07
am3a.questionText: Use repeated integration by parts to find the first three terms of the asymptotic expansion of the exponential integral \( E_1(x) = \int_x^{\infty} \dfrac{e^{-t}}{t}\,dt \) as \( x \to \infty \).

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 08
am3a.questionText: Show by repeated integration by parts that the exponential integral has the asymptotic expansion \( E_1(x) = \int_x^{\infty} \dfrac{e^{-t}}{t}\,dt \sim e^{-x}\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \dfrac{(-1)^{n} n!}{x^{\,n+1}} \) as \( x \to \infty \). (Identify the general term; you need not prove the remainder estimate here.)

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 09
am3a.questionText: Find the first three terms of the asymptotic expansion of the complementary-error-function tail \( J(x) = \int_x^{\infty} e^{-t^{2}}\,dt \) as \( x \to \infty \).

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 10
am3a.questionText: Find the first three terms of the asymptotic expansion of \( G(x) = \int_x^{\infty} \dfrac{e^{-t}}{t^{2}}\,dt \) as \( x \to \infty \).

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 11
am3a.questionText: The upper incomplete gamma function is \( \Gamma(a+1, x) = \int_x^{\infty} t^{a}\,e^{-t}\,dt \). For fixed \( a \), use integration by parts to find the first three terms of its asymptotic expansion as \( x \to \infty \).

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 12
am3a.questionText: Find the first three terms of the asymptotic expansion of \( M(x) = \int_x^{\infty} \dfrac{e^{-t}}{\sqrt{t}}\,dt = \Gamma\!\left(\tfrac12, x\right) \) as \( x \to \infty \).

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 13
am3a.questionText: By writing \( F(x) = \int_0^{\infty} \dfrac{e^{-xt}}{1+t}\,dt \) and integrating by parts repeatedly in \( t \), find the first three terms of the asymptotic expansion of \( F(x) \) as \( x \to \infty \).

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 14
am3a.questionText: Find the first three terms of the asymptotic expansion of \( P(x) = \int_x^{\infty} \dfrac{e^{-t}}{t+1}\,dt \) as \( x \to \infty \).

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 15
am3a.questionText: Find the first three terms of the asymptotic expansion of the Gaussian-weighted integral \( Q(x) = \int_x^{\infty} t\,e^{-t^{2}}\,dt \) as \( x \to \infty \), and comment on what you observe.

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 16
am3a.questionText: Find the first two terms of the asymptotic expansion of \( \displaystyle\int_x^{\infty} \dfrac{\ln t}{t}\,e^{-t}\,dt \) as \( x \to \infty \).

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 17
am3a.questionText: The integral \( G(x) = \int_0^{\infty} \dfrac{e^{-t}}{(1+xt)^{2}}\,dt \). By integrating by parts in \( t \), find the first two terms of its asymptotic expansion as \( x \to \infty \).

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 18
am3a.questionText: Find the first three terms of the asymptotic expansion of \( \displaystyle\int_x^{\infty} e^{-t^{3}}\,dt \) as \( x \to \infty \).

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 19
am3a.questionText: For the exponential integral \( E_1(x) = \int_x^{\infty}\dfrac{e^{-t}}{t}\,dt \), write \( E_1(x) = e^{-x}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\dfrac{(-1)^n n!}{x^{n+1}} + R_N(x) \). Obtain the exact remainder \( R_N(x) \) and show that \( R_N(x) = O\!\left(e^{-x} x^{-N-1}\right) \) as \( x \to \infty \), confirming the series is asymptotic.

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 20
am3a.questionText: Find the first three terms of the asymptotic expansion as \( x \to \infty \) of the oscillatory integral \( S(x) = \int_x^{\infty} \dfrac{\sin t}{t}\,dt \), and explain why integration by parts is legitimate here despite \( \sin t \) not decaying.

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 21
am3a.questionText: Find the first three terms of the asymptotic expansion as \( x \to \infty \) of \( C(x) = \int_x^{\infty} \dfrac{\cos t}{t}\,dt \). [Note \( C(x) = -\mathrm{Ci}(x) \).]

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 22
am3a.questionText: For \( J(x) = \int_x^{\infty} e^{-t^2}\,dt \), write \( J(x) = \dfrac{e^{-x^2}}{2x}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}(-1)^n\dfrac{(2n-1)!!}{(2x^2)^n} + R_N(x) \). Show that the remainder \( R_N(x) \) has the same sign as, and is bounded in magnitude by, the first neglected term, so the series is asymptotic and enveloping.

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 23
am3a.questionText: Using the IBP expansion \( E_1(x) = e^{-x}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\dfrac{(-1)^n n!}{x^{n+1}} + R_N(x) \) with \( |R_N(x)| \le N!\,e^{-x}/x^{N+1} \), determine the optimal truncation point (the term of smallest magnitude) for \( x = 5 \), and estimate the resulting smallest achievable error.

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 24
am3a.questionText: Cross-check the IBP expansion of \( E_1(x) = \int_x^{\infty}\dfrac{e^{-t}}{t}\,dt \) by substituting \( t = x(1+s) \) and applying Watson's lemma to the resulting integral. Confirm the leading two terms agree with the IBP result.

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 25
am3a.questionText: Suppose \( f \) is continuous and \( f(x) = o\big(\phi(x)\big) \) as \( x \to \infty \), where \( \phi \) is continuous, positive and non-decreasing. Show that \( \displaystyle\int_a^{x} f(t)\,dt = o\big(x\,\phi(x)\big) \) as \( x \to +\infty \).

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 26
am3a.questionText: By considering \( \dfrac{d}{dx}\big[E_1(x) + \ln x\big] \) and integrating, obtain the small-\( x \) expansion \( E_1(x) = -\gamma - \ln x + x - \dfrac{x^2}{4} + \cdots \) as \( x \to 0^+ \). [You may assume \( \lim_{x\to0}\big[E_1(x)+\ln x\big] = -\gamma \).]

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 27
am3a.questionText: Consider the finite-range integral \( I(x) = \int_0^{1} \dfrac{e^{-xt}}{1+t}\,dt \). By integrating by parts in \( t \), find the first three terms of its asymptotic expansion as \( x \to \infty \), and explain why the contribution from the upper limit \( t = 1 \) may be discarded.

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 28
am3a.questionText: Let \( F(x) = \int_x^{\infty}\dfrac{e^{-t}}{t}\,dt = E_1(x) \) and define \( G(x) = \int_x^{\infty}\dfrac{e^{-t}}{t^2}\,dt \). Show by integration by parts that \( F'(x) = -e^{-x}/x \) and that the asymptotic series for \( -F'(x) \) is obtained from that of \( F \) by term-by-term differentiation, and comment on when such differentiation of an asymptotic series is valid.

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 29
am3a.questionText: Find the first two terms of the asymptotic expansion as \( x \to \infty \) of \( W(x) = \int_0^{\infty} \dfrac{e^{-xt}}{\sqrt{1+t}}\,dt \), and identify the gauge sequence in which the expansion proceeds.

am3a.topicTitle: Integration by parts for integral asymptotics 30
am3a.questionText: The Fresnel-type integral \( \Phi(x) = \int_x^{\infty} e^{i t}\,\dfrac{dt}{t} \) (interpreted as a convergent improper integral). Using integration by parts, find the first three terms of its asymptotic expansion as \( x \to +\infty \), and verify that taking real and imaginary parts recovers the cosine- and sine-integral tails.

am3b.topicTitle: The exponential integral E₁ (large- and small-x) 01
am3b.questionText: The exponential integral is defined by \( E_1(x) = \int_x^{\infty} \dfrac{e^{-t}}{t}\,dt \). Perform one integration by parts (integrating \( e^{-t} \)) to extract the leading behaviour as \( x \to \infty \).

am3b.topicTitle: The exponential integral E₁ (large- and small-x) 02
am3b.questionText: Starting from \( E_1(x) = \dfrac{e^{-x}}{x} - \displaystyle\int_x^{\infty} \dfrac{e^{-t}}{t^2}\,dt \), integrate by parts once more to obtain the first two terms of the large-\( x \) expansion.

am3b.topicTitle: The exponential integral E₁ (large- and small-x) 03
am3b.questionText: Differentiate the function \( g(x) = E_1(x) + \ln x \), where \( E_1(x) = \int_x^{\infty} \dfrac{e^{-t}}{t}\,dt \). Give \( g'(x) \) in a form that is finite as \( x \to 0^{+} \).

am3b.topicTitle: The exponential integral E₁ (large- and small-x) 04
am3b.questionText: Expand \( \dfrac{1 - e^{-x}}{x} \) as a power series in \( x \) about \( x = 0 \), giving terms up to \( x^2 \).

am3b.topicTitle: The exponential integral E₁ (large- and small-x) 05
am3b.questionText: Write down the general term and the remainder estimate for the large-\( x \) asymptotic expansion \( E_1(x) \sim e^{-x}\big(b_1 x^{-1} + b_2 x^{-2} + b_3 x^{-3} + \cdots\big) \). State \( b_1, b_2, b_3, b_4 \).

am3b.topicTitle: The exponential integral E₁ (large- and small-x) 06
am3b.questionText: Given that \( \lim_{x\to 0}[E_1(x)+\ln x] = -\gamma \) (Euler's constant), and that \( \dfrac{d}{dx}[E_1(x)+\ln x] = \dfrac{1-e^{-x}}{x} \), find the small-\( x \) expansion of \( E_1(x) \) up to the term in \( x \).

am3b.topicTitle: The exponential integral E₁ (large- and small-x) 07
am3b.questionText: Use repeated integration by parts to find the large-\( x \) asymptotic expansion of \( E_1(x) = \displaystyle\int_x^{\infty} \dfrac{e^{-t}}{t}\,dt \) up to and including the term in \( x^{-4} \), and state the order of the remainder.

am3b.topicTitle: The exponential integral E₁ (large- and small-x) 08
