The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = 3x^2 \).\newline (a) Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \) by differentiating from first principles.\newline (b) Find the coordinates of the point on \( C \) where the gradient is \( -18 \).

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^2 - 5x \).\newline (a) Differentiate from first principles to find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \).\newline (b) Find the \( x \)-value where the tangent to \( C \) is parallel to the \( x \)-axis.

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^3 \).\newline (a) Differentiate from first principles to show \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 3x^2 \).\newline (b) Find the two values of \( x \) where the gradient of \( C \) is 27.

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^2 + 3 \). A tangent to \( C \) has gradient 10.\newline (a) Differentiate \( y = x^2 + 3 \) from first principles.\newline (b) Find the equation of the tangent.
Explain what \( f'(x) \) represents geometrically for the curve \( y = f(x) \), and describe what it means when \( f'(x) > 0 \), \( f'(x) = 0 \), and \( f'(x) < 0 \).

The function \( f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 1 \) has derivative \( f'(x) = 2x - 4 \).\newline (a) Find the value of \( x \) where the gradient is zero.\newline (b) Determine whether the function is increasing or decreasing at \( x = 0 \) and \( x = 4 \).
Explain the difference between the gradient of a chord and the gradient of a tangent to a curve at a point, and how differentiation from first principles connects the two.

The area \( A \) cm² of a square with side \( x \) cm is given by \( A = x^2 \).\newline By differentiating from first principles, find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}A}{\mathrm{d}x} \) and interpret its meaning.
Show, by differentiating from first principles, that the derivative of any constant \( f(x) = c \) is zero.
Differentiate \( f(x) = x \) from first principles and comment on the result.

(a) Differentiate \( f(x) = x^2 + 2x - 3 \) from first principles.\newline (b) Hence find the gradient of the curve at the point where \( x = -1 \).\newline (c) Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at this point.

(a) Show, by differentiating \( f(x) = x^2 \) from first principles, that \( f'(x) = 2x \).\newline (b) The point \( P \) lies on the curve \( y = x^2 \). The gradient of the curve at \( P \) is \(-6\). Find the coordinates of \( P \).

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = 2x^2 - x \).
ewline (a) Differentiate from first principles to find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \).
ewline (b) Find the gradient of \( C \) at the point \( A(2, 6) \).
ewline (c) Find the equation of the tangent to \( C \) at \( A \).

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^3 - 2 \).
ewline (a) By differentiating from first principles, show that \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 3x^2 \).
ewline (b) Find the two points on \( C \) where the gradient is 12.
ewline (c) Find the gradient of \( C \) at the origin.

(a) Differentiate \( f(x) = x^2 \) from first principles to show that \( f'(x) = 2x \).\newline (b) The tangent to \( y = x^2 \) at the point \( P(a, a^2) \) has equation \( y = 2ax - a^2 \). Verify this using the result from part (a).

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^2 + x \). Find the gradient of the chord from the point where \( x = 1 \) to the point where:\newline (i) \( x = 2 \) \quad (ii) \( x = 1.1 \) \quad (iii) \( x = 1.01 \)\newline Hence suggest the gradient of \( C \) at \( x = 1 \).

The curve \( C \) is given by \( y = x^3 - x \). Find the gradient of the chord from the point \( (1, 0) \) to the point where:\newline (i) \( x = 1.5 \) \quad (ii) \( x = 1.1 \) \quad (iii) \( x = 1.01 \)\newline What does this suggest about the gradient of \( C \) at \( x = 1 \)?

For the curve \( y = 2x^2 \), find the gradient of the chord joining \( x = -1 \) to:\newline (i) \( x = 0 \) \quad (ii) \( x = -0.5 \) \quad (iii) \( x = -0.9 \)\newline Deduce the gradient of the curve at \( x = -1 \).

A student estimates the gradient of \( y = x^2 \) at \( x = 4 \) using chords to \( x = 4 + h \) for \( h = 1, 0.1, 0.01 \). Tabulate the three chord gradients and state what the gradient at \( x = 4 \) appears to be.

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = 3 - x^2 \). Find the gradient of the chord joining \( (2, -1) \) to the point where \( x = 2 + h \). Simplify your answer and deduce the gradient of \( C \) at \( x = 2 \) by letting \( h \to 0 \).
Differentiate \( f(x) = 3x^2 \) from first principles.
Differentiate \( f(x) = x^2 - 4x \) from first principles.
Use first principles to differentiate \( f(x) = x^2 + 3x - 1 \).
Differentiate \( f(x) = 2x^3 \) from first principles.
Differentiate \( f(x) = x^3 + 2x \) from first principles.
Use first principles to show that the derivative of \( f(x) = 5x^2 - 3 \) is \( 10x \).
Use first principles to find the gradient of the curve \( y = x^2 + 2x \) at the point where \( x = 3 \).
Find, from first principles, the gradient of the curve \( y = x^3 \) at the point where \( x = -2 \).
Using first principles, find the gradient of the curve \( y = 4x^2 - x \) at \( x = 1 \).
A curve has equation \( y = x^2 - 6x + 5 \). Use first principles to show that the gradient of the curve at \( x = 4 \) is 2.
The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = 2x^2 + 5x \). Find the gradient of \( C \) at the point where \( x = -1 \), using first principles.
Find, from first principles, the gradient of \( y = x^3 + x \) at the point where \( x = 2 \).
A curve has equation \( y = x^2 + 4x - 7 \). (a) Find \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} \) from first principles. (b) Hence find the gradient of the curve at the point where \( x = -3 \).
The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^2 - 5x \). (a) Use first principles to find the gradient function. (b) Find the value of \( x \) at which the gradient of \( C \) is zero.
A curve has equation \( y = 3x^2 - 12x + 5 \). Using first principles, find the value of \( x \) at which the tangent to the curve is horizontal.
The curve \( C \) is given by \( y = x^3 - 3x \). (a) Find \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} \) from first principles. (b) Find the gradient of \( C \) at the points where \( x = 0 \) and \( x = 1 \).
The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^2 + 2x - 3 \). Find the coordinates of the point on \( C \) at which the gradient is equal to 6.
Find the coordinates of the point on the curve \( y = x^2 - 4x + 1 \) where the gradient is \( -2 \).
The displacement \( s \) metres of a particle at time \( t \) seconds is modelled by \( s = t^2 + 3t \). (a) Find the velocity \( \dfrac{ds}{dt} \). (b) Find the velocity when \( t = 4 \).
A ball is thrown so that its height \( h \) metres after \( t \) seconds is \( h = 20t - 5t^2 \). Find the rate at which the height is changing when \( t = 1 \).
The volume \( V \) cm\( ^3 \) of a balloon at time \( t \) seconds is \( V = 4t^2 + t \). Find \( \dfrac{dV}{dt} \) and state the rate at which the volume is increasing when \( t = 3 \).

A company models its profit \( P \) (in £thousands) as a function of units sold \( x \) by \( P = -x^2 + 40x - 100 \). Find \( \dfrac{dP}{dx} \) and determine the value of \( x \) at which profit is momentarily constant (the marginal profit is zero).

A cup of hot coffee cools so that its temperature \( T \) °C after \( t \) minutes is modelled by \( T = 90 - 2t^2 \). Find the rate of change of temperature when \( t = 3 \) and interpret your answer.
Differentiate \( f(x) = x^4 \) from first principles.
The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^3 - 2x^2 + x \). (a) Use first principles to find \( \dfrac{dy}{dx} \). (b) Hence find the values of \( x \) at which the tangent to \( C \) has gradient 1.
Use first principles to show that if \( f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \) then \( f'(x) = 2ax + b \), where \( a, b, c \) are constants.

The points \( A \) and \( B \) both lie on the curve \( y = x^2 \). The chord \( AB \) has gradient 5. Given that the \( x \)-coordinate of \( A \) is \( a \) and the \( x \)-coordinate of \( B \) is \( a + h \) with \( h \neq 0 \), show that \( 2a + h = 5 \). Hence state the gradient of the tangent to the curve at the midpoint of \( AB \).

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^2 - 2x + 4 \). The point \( P \) lies on \( C \) and has \( x \)-coordinate 3. (a) Find the coordinates of \( P \). (b) Use first principles to find the gradient of \( C \) at \( P \). (c) Find the equation of the tangent to \( C \) at \( P \), in the form \( y = mx + c \).

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^2 \). The chord joining the points \( P(p, p^2) \) and \( Q(q, q^2) \) has gradient \( m \), where \( p \neq q \). (a) Show that \( m = p + q \). (b) Hence, by letting \( q \to p \), deduce the gradient of the tangent to \( C \) at \( P \).

A curve has equation \( y = x^3 \). The chord joining the points \( (a, a^3) \) and \( (a + h, (a+h)^3) \), where \( h \neq 0 \), has gradient \( m \). (a) Show that \( m = 3a^2 + 3ah + h^2 \). (b) By letting \( h \to 0 \), deduce that the gradient of the tangent to the curve at \( x = a \) is \( 3a^2 \). (c) Hence find the gradient of the curve at the point where \( x = -1 \).

d2.questionText: Differentiate \( y = x^5 \).
Differentiate \( y = x^7 \).
Differentiate \( y = 6x^4 \).
Differentiate \( y = \sqrt{x} \).
Differentiate \( y = \dfrac{1}{x^3} \).
Differentiate \( y = 5x^3 - 4x^2 + 7x - 2 \).
Differentiate \( f(x) = 2x^4 - 9x^2 + 1 \).
Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \) when \( y = 3x^{-2} + 5x \).
Expand and differentiate \( y = x(x - 3)^2 \).
Expand and differentiate \( y = (2x + 1)(x - 4) \).
Find \( f'(x) \) for \( f(x) = \dfrac{x^3 + 4x}{x} \).
Simplify and differentiate \( y = \dfrac{x^4 - 3x^2}{x^2} \).
Differentiate \( y = 4\sqrt{x} - \dfrac{2}{x} \).
Find the gradient of \( y = 3x^2 - 5x + 1 \) at \( x = 2 \).
Find the gradient of the curve \( y = 2x^3 - x \) at the point \( (1, 1) \).
Find the gradient of \( f(x) = 2\sqrt{x} \) at the point \( (9, 6) \).
Find the gradient of \( y = x^4 - 3x^2 + 2 \) when \( x = -1 \).
Find the coordinates of the point on \( y = x^2 - 6x + 5 \) where the gradient is \( 0 \).
Find the coordinates of the points on \( y = x^3 - 3x \) where the gradient is \( 0 \).
Find the equation of the tangent to \( y = x^2 + 3x \) at the point \( (1, 4) \). Give your answer in the form \( y = mx + c \).
Find the equation of the tangent to \( y = 2x^3 - 5 \) at the point \( (1, -3) \). Give your answer in the form \( ax + by + c = 0 \), where \( a \), \( b \), and \( c \) are integers.
Find the equation of the normal to \( y = x^2 - 4x + 3 \) at the point \( (3, 0) \). Give your answer in the form \( y = mx + c \).
Find the equation of the normal to \( y = x^3 - 2x + 1 \) at the point \( (2, 5) \). Give your answer in the form \( ax + by + c = 0 \).
Differentiate \( f(x) = (x+2)(x-5) \) and find the value of \( x \) where \( f'(x) = 3 \).
Differentiate \( y = \dfrac{x^3 - 5x^2 + 2x}{x} \).
Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \) when \( y = \dfrac{3x^3 + x}{\sqrt{x}} \).
Expand then differentiate \( y = (3x - 1)^2 \).
Find the gradient of \( y = \dfrac{x^2 - 4}{x} \) at the point \( (-2, 0) \).
Differentiate \( y = \sqrt{x}\,(x - 4) \).
Find the equation of the tangent to \( y = (x-1)(x+3) \) at the point \( (2, 5) \). Give your answer in the form \( y = mx + c \).
Find the equation of the normal to \( y = 4\sqrt{x} \) at the point \( (4, 8) \). Give your answer in the form \( ax + by + c = 0 \), where \( a \), \( b \), and \( c \) are integers.

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^3 - 4x + 3 \).
(a) Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \).
(b) Show that the point \( P(2, 3) \) lies on \( C \).
(c) Find the equation of the tangent to \( C \) at \( P \), giving your answer in the form \( y = mx + c \).

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = 2x^2 - 7x + 4 \).
(a) Find the gradient of \( C \) at the point \( A(3, 1) \).
(b) Hence find the equation of the normal to \( C \) at \( A \), giving your answer in the form \( ax + by + c = 0 \).

The function \( f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 2 \).
(a) Find \( f'(x) \).
(b) Find the coordinates of the two stationary points of the curve \( y = f(x) \).
(c) Find the equation of the tangent to the curve at the point where \( x = 4 \). Give your answer in the form \( y = mx + c \).

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = f(x) \), where \( f(x) = \dfrac{x^3 - 4x}{\sqrt{x}} \) for \( x > 0 \).
(a) Show that \( f(x) \) can be written in the form \( ax^p + bx^q \), stating the values of \( a \), \( p \), \( b \), and \( q \).
(b) Find \( f'(x) \).
(c) Find the equation of the tangent to \( C \) at the point where \( x = 4 \), giving your answer in the form \( y = mx + c \).
Differentiate \( y = \dfrac{5}{x^2} \).
Differentiate \( f(x) = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{x}} \).
Differentiate \( y = 3\sqrt[3]{x} \).
Differentiate \( y = 6x^{2/3} - 4x^{-1} \).
Differentiate \( f(x) = \dfrac{x^2 + 1}{x^3} \).
Differentiate \( y = \dfrac{2x^{3/2} - 5}{\sqrt{x}} \).
Differentiate \( y = (x^2 - 3)(x + 1) \).
Expand and differentiate \( y = (2x - 1)^2 (x + 3) \).
Differentiate \( y = \sqrt{x}(x^2 - 4) \).
Differentiate \( f(x) = \dfrac{(x + 2)(x - 1)}{x^2} \).
Differentiate \( y = \left( x + \dfrac{1}{x} \right)^2 \).
Differentiate \( y = \dfrac{(\sqrt{x} + 1)^2}{x} \).
Differentiate \( f(x) = (x^2 + 2x)(x - 3) \).
Find the gradient of the curve \( y = x^3 - 2x^2 + 5 \) at the point where \( x = -1 \).
Find the gradient of \( y = \dfrac{4}{x} + x^2 \) at the point where \( x = 2 \).
Find the gradient of \( f(x) = \sqrt{x}(x + 2) \) at the point where \( x = 4 \).
The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^3 - 4x \). Find the values of \( x \) at which the gradient of \( C \) is \( 8 \).
Find the coordinates of the point on \( y = 2x^2 - 3x + 1 \) where the gradient is \( 5 \).
Find the equation of the tangent to \( y = x^3 - 2x \) at the point \( (2, 4) \). Give your answer in the form \( y = mx + c \).
Find the equation of the tangent to \( y = \dfrac{6}{x} \) at the point where \( x = 3 \).
Find the equation of the normal to \( y = x^2 + 2x - 3 \) at the point \( (1, 0) \). Give your answer in the form \( y = mx + c \).
The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = \sqrt{x} \). Find the equation of the tangent to \( C \) at the point where \( x = 9 \). Give your answer in the form \( y = mx + c \).
Find the equation of the normal to \( y = 2x^3 - 3x^2 + 1 \) at the point where \( x = 1 \). Give your answer in the form \( ax + by + c = 0 \) with integer coefficients.
Find the coordinates of the stationary point of \( y = x^2 - 8x + 5 \).
Find the coordinates of the stationary points of \( f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x + 1 \).
The curve \( y = 2x^3 + 3x^2 - 12x + 5 \) has two stationary points. Find their \( x \)-coordinates.
The curve \( y = 4x^3 - 12x + 7 \) has a tangent parallel to the \( x \)-axis. Find the \( y \)-coordinates of the points where this occurs.
Find the values of \( x \) for which the curve \( y = x^3 - 3x^2 + 4 \) has gradient \( 9 \).
The volume \( V \) cm\( ^3 \) of a cube of side \( x \) cm is \( V = x^3 \). Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}x} \) and evaluate it when \( x = 5 \). Interpret your answer.
The displacement \( s \) metres of a particle at time \( t \) seconds is \( s = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t \). Find the velocity when \( t = 2 \).
The cost \( C \) (in £) of producing \( x \) widgets is \( C = 200 + 5x + 0.01x^2 \). Find the marginal cost \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}C}{\mathrm{d}x} \) when \( x = 100 \).
A spherical balloon has volume \( V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \) cm\( ^3 \), where \( r \) is its radius in cm. Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}r} \) and evaluate it when \( r = 10 \).

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 4 \).\newline (a) Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \).\newline (b) The tangent at the point \( P \) on \( C \) is parallel to the line \( y = 2x + 1 \). Find the \( x \)-coordinates of the possible positions of \( P \).

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = 2\sqrt{x} + \dfrac{8}{\sqrt{x}} \) for \( x > 0 \).\newline (a) Show that \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{x - 4}{x\sqrt{x}} \).\newline (b) Find the coordinates of the stationary point of \( C \).

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^3 - 3x^2 - 24x + 1 \).
ewline (a) Find the coordinates of the two stationary points of \( C \).
ewline (b) Find the equation of the tangent to \( C \) at the point where \( x = 0 \), giving your answer in the form \( y = mx + c \).
ewline (c) Determine the values of \( x \) for which \( C \) has gradient greater than 0.

d3.questionText: Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \) when \( y = x^4 \).
Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \) when \( y = 5x^3 - 2x \).
Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \) when \( y = 4x^5 - 3x^3 + 7x - 2 \).
Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \) when \( y = \sqrt{x} \).
Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \) when \( y = 6x^2 - \dfrac{1}{x} \).
Given \( f(x) = 2x^3 - 9x^2 + 12x - 5 \), find \( f''(x) \) and hence find the value of \( x \) where \( f''(x) = 0 \).
Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \) when \( y = (x + 2)(x - 3) \).
Find the second derivative of \( y = \dfrac{x^4 - 2x^2}{x} \).
Find the value of \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \) when \( x = 2 \), given that \( y = x^3 - 5x \).
Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \) when \( x = -1 \), given \( y = 2x^4 - x^3 + 5 \).
For the curve \( y = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 1 \), find the coordinates of the stationary points and use the second derivative test to determine their nature.
Find the stationary point of \( y = x^2 - 8x + 3 \) and use the second derivative to determine its nature.
Find the stationary points of \( y = 2x^3 - 3x^2 - 12x + 5 \) and determine their nature using the second derivative test.
Show that the curve \( y = x^3 \) has a stationary point of inflection at the origin.
Find the stationary point of \( y = -x^2 + 6x - 4 \) and determine its nature.
Find and classify the stationary points of \( f(x) = x^4 - 4x^2 \).
Find the second derivative of \( y = 3x^{1/3} \) and write your answer without negative or fractional indices.
Find the second derivative of \( y = x(x^2 - 5) \).
Find the second derivative of \( f(x) = \dfrac{x^5 + 3x^3}{x^2} \).
The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^3 - 12x \). Find the coordinates of both stationary points. Use the second derivative to determine whether each is a maximum or minimum.
A function is defined as \( f(x) = x^3 + px^2 + q \), where \( p \) and \( q \) are constants. Given that \( f''(2) = 0 \), find the value of \( p \).

A curve has equation \( y = ax^3 + bx \). Given that \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0 \) at \( x = 1 \) and \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} = -6 \) at \( x = 1 \), find the values of \( a \) and \( b \).
For \( y = x^4 - 2x^3 \), find both stationary points and determine their nature.
Verify that \( y = 4x^3 - 3x^4 \) has a local maximum at \( x = 1 \) by finding \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \) and evaluating it there.

A function is given by \( f(x) = 2x^3 - 3x^2 - 36x + 10 \).
(a) Find \( f''(x) \).
(b) Find the value(s) of \( x \) for which \( f''(x) < 0 \).
Find and classify the stationary point of \( y = x^2 + 4x - 7 \).
Given \( y = 5x^2 - x^3 \), find the range of values of \( x \) for which the curve is concave (i.e. \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} < 0 \)).

A curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x + 5 \).
(a) Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \) and \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \).
(b) Find the coordinates of the stationary points of \( C \).
(c) Determine the nature of each stationary point.

A curve has equation \( y = x^4 - 8x^2 + 3 \).
(a) Find all stationary points.
(b) Use the second derivative to classify each one.
(c) State the coordinates of the global minimum for \( x \geq 0 \).

The function \( f(x) = \dfrac{k}{x^2} + 4x \), where \( k \) is a positive constant, has a stationary point at \( x = 2 \).
(a) Show that \( k = 16 \).
(b) Use the second derivative to confirm that this stationary point is a minimum.

A curve \( C \) has equation \( y = f(x) \), where \( f(x) = 2x^3 + 3x^2 - 12x + 1 \).
(a) Find \( f'(x) \) and \( f''(x) \).
(b) Find the coordinates of the stationary points of \( C \).
(c) Determine the nature of each stationary point using the second derivative.
(d) Find the range of values of \( x \) for which \( f''(x) > 0 \).

A manufacturer models the profit \( P \) (in thousands of pounds) from producing \( x \) units (in hundreds) as \( P(x) = -x^3 + 6x^2 + 15x \) for \( 0 \leq x \leq 8 \).
(a) Find \( P'(x) \) and \( P''(x) \).
(b) Find the value of \( x \) that gives a stationary point in \( (0, 8) \) and verify it is a maximum using the second derivative.
(c) State the maximum profit.
Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \) when \( y = \dfrac{3}{x^2} \).
Find \( f''(x) \) when \( f(x) = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{x}} \).
Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \) when \( y = 2x^3 + \dfrac{5}{x} \).
Given \( y = x^{3/2} + 4x^{1/2} \), find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \).
Find the second derivative of \( f(x) = \dfrac{x^3 - 2x}{x^2} \) for \( x \neq 0 \).
Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \) when \( y = (x + 3)^2 \).
Find the second derivative of \( y = \sqrt{x}(x - 3) \).
Given \( y = 3x^2 - 2\sqrt{x} \), find the value of \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \) at \( x = 4 \).
A curve has equation \( y = ax^3 + bx^2 \). Given that \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} = 12x - 4 \), find the values of \( a \) and \( b \).
Given \( f(x) = x^3 - kx^2 + 3x \), find the value of \( k \) for which \( f''(2) = 0 \).
For \( y = 2x^3 + 5x^2 - 4x \), find the value of \( x \) at which \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} = 0 \).
Given \( f(x) = x^4 - 4x^3 \), find all values of \( x \) for which \( f''(x) = 0 \).
Find the stationary points of \( y = x^3 - 12x + 5 \) and use the second derivative to classify them.
The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = 2x^3 + 3x^2 - 36x + 1 \). Find its stationary points and classify them using the second derivative.
Find the stationary points of \( f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x - 2 \) and classify each using \( f''(x) \).
Find the stationary points of \( y = x^4 - 4x^3 + 4x^2 + 1 \) and classify them.
For \( y = x + \dfrac{9}{x} \), \( x > 0 \), find the stationary point and use the second derivative to show that it is a minimum.
The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^3 - 3x \). (a) Find the stationary points. (b) Classify each using the second derivative.
Find the range of values of \( x \) for which the curve \( y = x^3 - 6x^2 + 5 \) is concave up.
Find the \( x \)-coordinate of the point of inflection of \( y = x^3 - 9x^2 + 24x - 15 \).
A curve has equation \( y = x^4 - 6x^2 \). Find the range of values of \( x \) for which the curve is concave down.
The curve \( y = 2x^3 - 9x^2 + 12x \) has a point of inflection. Find its coordinates.
Find the values of \( x \) for which the curve \( y = x^3 - 3x^2 \) is decreasing and concave up.
Show that the curve \( y = x^4 + 2 \) has no point of inflection.

A rectangular enclosure has perimeter 20 m. Its area \( A \) (in m²) is given by \( A = x(10 - x) \), where \( x \) is the length of one side. Find the value of \( x \) that maximises \( A \), and use the second derivative to justify that it is a maximum.

The height of a projectile \( h \) metres after \( t \) seconds is \( h = 25t - 5t^2 \). (a) Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t} \) and \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2h}{\mathrm{d}t^2} \). (b) Find the time at which the height is maximum and state the maximum height. (c) Interpret the sign of \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2h}{\mathrm{d}t^2} \).

An open-top box is made from a square sheet of side 12 cm by cutting a square of side \( x \) cm from each corner and folding up the sides. The volume is \( V = x(12 - 2x)^2 \) cm³. Find the value of \( x \) that maximises the volume and verify it is a maximum using the second derivative.

The population \( P \) (in thousands) of a species \( t \) years after a study begins is modelled by \( P = 20 + 6t - t^2 \). (a) Find the time at which the population is greatest and its value. (b) State the sign of \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2P}{\mathrm{d}t^2} \) and interpret it.
A cylinder has surface area \( S = 2\pi r^2 + \dfrac{200}{r} \) for \( r > 0 \). Find the value of \( r \) that minimises \( S \), and use the second derivative to confirm it is a minimum.

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^3 - 3ax^2 + 3a^2 x \), where \( a \) is a positive constant. (a) Find the stationary points of \( C \) in terms of \( a \). (b) Find the nature of each stationary point using the second derivative.

A function is defined by \( f(x) = x^3 + px^2 + qx + 1 \), where \( p \) and \( q \) are constants. The curve \( y = f(x) \) has a stationary point at \( (2, -3) \). (a) Find \( p \) and \( q \). (b) Determine the nature of the stationary point.

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^4 - 4x^3 + 4x^2 \). (a) Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \) and \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \). (b) Find the stationary points and classify them. (c) Find the coordinates of any points of inflection.

An open rectangular tank has a square base of side \( x \) metres and height \( h \) metres. Its volume is \( 32 \) m³. (a) Show that its external surface area is \( S = x^2 + \dfrac{128}{x} \). (b) Find the value of \( x \) that minimises \( S \), using the second derivative to confirm it is a minimum.

A function is defined by \( f(x) = 2x^3 - 15x^2 + 24x + 7 \). (a) Find \( f'(x) \) and \( f''(x) \). (b) Find the coordinates of the stationary points. (c) Use the second derivative test to determine the nature of each. (d) State the range of values of \( x \) for which \( f(x) \) is concave up.

d4.questionText: Find the \( x \)-coordinates of the stationary points of \( y = x^2 - 10x + 3 \).
Find the \( x \)-coordinates of the stationary points of \( y = x^3 - 3x^2 - 24x + 1 \).
Find the coordinates of the stationary points of \( y = 2x^3 - 9x^2 + 12x - 3 \).
Find the coordinates of the stationary point of \( y = -x^2 + 8x - 10 \) and state its nature.
Find the coordinates of the stationary points of \( y = x^3 + 3x^2 - 45x + 7 \) and classify each one.
Show that the function \( f(x) = x^2 + 4x + 9 \) has no real roots, and find the coordinates of its stationary point.
Show that \( f(x) = x^3 + 5x + 2 \) has no stationary points.
A function is given by \( f(x) = x^3 + kx \), where \( k \) is a constant. Given that \( f(x) \) has no stationary points, find the range of values of \( k \).
Find the coordinates of the stationary points of \( y = x^4 - 8x^2 + 5 \) and classify them.
Find the values of \( x \) for which \( y = x^2 - 6x + 5 \) is an increasing function.
Find the values of \( x \) for which \( y = x^2 + 4x - 3 \) is a decreasing function.
Find the values of \( x \) for which \( f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x + 2 \) is increasing.
Find the values of \( x \) for which \( f(x) = 2x^3 - 3x^2 - 36x + 5 \) is decreasing.
Use differentiation to explain why \( f(x) = x^3 + 3x^2 + 3x + 5 \) is an increasing function for all real values of \( x \).
Find the range of values of \( x \) for which \( y = x^3 - 12x + 1 \) is decreasing.
The function \( y = 4 + 6x - x^2 \) is decreasing for \( x > k \). Find the value of \( k \).
Find the range of values of \( x \) for which \( f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 15x - 7 \) is increasing.
Given that \( g(x) = 3 - 4x - 2x^2 \) is a decreasing function for \( x > k \), find \( k \).

Sketch the curve \( y = x^3 - 3x^2 \), clearly labelling: (i) the coordinates where the curve crosses the axes, (ii) the coordinates of any stationary points, and (iii) the nature of each stationary point.

For the curve \( y = x^3 - 4x \):
(a) Find the coordinates where the curve crosses the \( x \)-axis.
(b) Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \) and the coordinates of the stationary points.
(c) Determine the nature of each stationary point.
Sketch the curve \( y = x^3 + 3x^2 \), labelling the coordinates of all stationary points and axis intercepts.

For the function \( f(x) = x^3 + 2x^2 - 4x + 1 \):
(a) Find \( f'(x) \).
(b) Find the range of values of \( x \) for which \( f \) is increasing.
(c) Find the range of values of \( x \) for which \( f \) is decreasing.

A function \( f \) satisfies \( f(2) = -3 \), \( f'(2) = 0 \) and \( f''(2) = 5 \).
(a) Write down the coordinates of a stationary point of \( f \).
(b) Determine its nature, giving a reason.
A function is given by \( y = x^3 + ax^2 + bx + 5 \). The curve has a stationary point at \( (1, 4) \). Find the values of \( a \) and \( b \).

For the curve \( y = 3x^2 - x^3 \):
(a) Find the coordinates of both stationary points.
(b) Find the range of values of \( x \) for which the curve is increasing.
Given \( f(x) = x^2 + \dfrac{16}{x} \) for \( x > 0 \), find the value of \( x \) at which \( f \) has a stationary point and determine its nature.
Find the stationary points on \( y = 5x^4 - 4x^5 \) and determine their nature.
Find the range of values of \( x \) for which \( y = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x + 4 \) is increasing.

A curve has equation \( y = x^3 - 3x + 2 \).
(a) Find the \( x \)-intercepts.
(b) Find and classify the stationary points.
(c) Describe the shape of a sketch of the curve.
The function \( y = 5 - 3x - ax^2 \) is a decreasing function for all real values of \( x \). Find the range of possible values of \( a \).

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = f(x) \) where \( f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x - 2 \).
(a) Find \( f'(x) \).
(b) Find the coordinates of the stationary points of \( C \).
(c) Determine the nature of each stationary point.
(d) Find the range of values of \( x \) for which \( f(x) \) is increasing.
Sketch the graph of \( y = x^3 + 6x^2 + 9x \), clearly labelling all axis intercepts and stationary points with their coordinates.

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^4 - 4x^3 + 4 \).
(a) Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \) and \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} \).
(b) Find the coordinates of all stationary points and determine their nature.
(c) Find the range of values of \( x \) for which \( C \) is decreasing.

The curve \( y = x^3 + ax^2 + bx + c \) has a stationary point at \( (3, 27) \) and \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2y}{\mathrm{d}x^2} = 0 \) at \( (3, 27) \). Given also that the curve passes through the origin, find \( a \), \( b \), and \( c \).

A manufacturer models the cost \( C \) (£ thousands) of producing \( x \) hundred units as \( C(x) = x^3 - 9x^2 + 24x + 10 \) for \( 0 \leq x \leq 6 \).
(a) Find \( C'(x) \).
(b) Find the stationary points of \( C \) and classify them.
(c) State the values of \( x \) for which \( C \) is decreasing, and explain what this means in context.
(d) Find the minimum cost in the given domain.
Find the stationary points of \( y = x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x + 1 \) and use the first derivative sign test to classify them.
Find the stationary points of \( y = x^3 + 3x^2 - 24x + 5 \) and classify them using the first-derivative sign test.
Find the stationary point of \( y = 2x^3 - 3x^2 + 1 \) and determine its nature.
Find and classify the stationary points of \( y = 3x^4 - 8x^3 + 5 \).
Find the stationary points of \( f(x) = x^3 - 6x^2 + 12x - 3 \) and determine their nature.
Find the stationary points of \( y = x(x - 4)^2 \) and classify them.
A curve has equation \( y = x^3 - 3x^2 + 3x + 2 \). Show that the curve has no turning points and state the nature of any stationary points.
Find the range of values of \( x \) for which \( f(x) = x^4 - 2x^2 \) is increasing.
Find the range of values of \( x \) for which \( f(x) = x^3 - 12x \) is decreasing.
Find the values of \( x \) for which the curve \( y = x^4 - 4x^3 \) is increasing.
For \( f(x) = x + \dfrac{4}{x} \), \( x > 0 \), find the range of values of \( x \) for which \( f \) is increasing.
Show that \( f(x) = \dfrac{x^3}{3} - 2x^2 + 5x + 1 \) is an increasing function for all real \( x \).
The function \( y = x^3 - 3x^2 - 24x \) is increasing for \( x < a \) and \( x > b \), where \( a < b \). Find \( a \) and \( b \).
For the curve \( y = x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x \): (a) find the axis intercepts, (b) find the coordinates of the stationary points and classify each, (c) describe the shape of the curve.
Sketch the curve \( y = -x^3 + 6x^2 - 9x \), labelling the coordinates of any intercepts and stationary points.
For the curve \( y = x^4 - 4x^2 + 3 \): (a) find the axis intercepts, (b) find and classify the stationary points.
Sketch the curve \( y = x^3 - 3x^2 + 4 \), labelling intercepts and stationary points.
For \( y = x^4 - 2x^2 \): (a) find the \( x \)-intercepts, (b) find and classify all stationary points.
Sketch \( y = x^3 - 12x + 16 \), labelling any stationary points and the \( y \)-intercept. Determine the nature of each stationary point.
The curve \( y = x^3 + ax^2 + bx \) has a stationary point at \( x = -1 \) and passes through \( (2, 6) \). Find \( a \) and \( b \).
A curve \( y = ax^3 + bx \) has a local maximum of 4 at \( x = -1 \). Find \( a \) and \( b \).
The function \( f(x) = x^3 + px^2 + qx + 5 \) has stationary points at \( x = 1 \) and \( x = 3 \). Find \( p \) and \( q \).
The curve \( y = x^2 + \dfrac{k}{x} \) for \( x > 0 \) has a minimum at \( x = 2 \). Find \( k \) and the minimum value.
A curve has equation \( y = x^3 + ax^2 + bx + c \). It has a stationary point at \( (2, -9) \) and passes through \( (0, 3) \). Find \( a \), \( b \), and \( c \).
The quartic \( y = x^4 + ax^2 + b \) has a minimum value of \( -3 \) at \( x = 2 \). Find \( a \) and \( b \).

A rectangle has perimeter 40 m. Let \( x \) be the length of one side. (a) Write the area \( A \) as a function of \( x \). (b) Find the value of \( x \) that maximises \( A \) and state the maximum area.
A closed cylindrical can has volume 500 cm³. Its surface area in terms of the radius \( r \) is \( S = 2\pi r^2 + \dfrac{1000}{r} \). Find the value of \( r \) that minimises \( S \).

A farmer has 120 m of fencing to make a rectangular enclosure against an existing wall; no fence is needed on the wall side. Let \( x \) m be the length perpendicular to the wall. (a) Express the area \( A \) as a function of \( x \). (b) Find the maximum area.
The height of a ball in metres above the ground after \( t \) seconds is \( h = 40t - 5t^2 \). Find the time at which the ball is at its maximum height and state the maximum height.

An open-top box is made from a 20 cm by 12 cm sheet of card by cutting equal squares of side \( x \) cm from each corner. (a) Show that the volume is \( V = x(20 - 2x)(12 - 2x) \). (b) Find, to 1 decimal place, the value of \( x \) that maximises \( V \).

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^3 - 3x^2 + 4 \).
ewline (a) Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \) and the coordinates of the stationary points of \( C \).
ewline (b) Determine the nature of each stationary point.
ewline (c) Show that the equation of the tangent to \( C \) at the point where \( x = 1 \) is \( y = -3x + 5 \).

A curve has equation \( y = \dfrac{x^3}{3} - \dfrac{3x^2}{2} + 2x + 1 \).
ewline (a) Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} \).
ewline (b) Find the stationary points and classify them.
ewline (c) Find the range of values of \( x \) for which the curve is concave up.

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = x^4 - 8x^2 + 16 \).\newline (a) Show that \( y \geq 0 \) for all \( x \) and find where equality holds.\newline (b) Find the coordinates of all stationary points and classify them.

A function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 2x^3 - 9x^2 + 12x - 4 \).
ewline (a) Find \( f'(x) \) and \( f''(x) \).
ewline (b) Find the stationary points of \( f \) and determine their nature.
ewline (c) Find the range of values of \( x \) for which \( f \) is decreasing.
ewline (d) Sketch \( y = f(x) \), labelling key features.

A cyclist's speed \( v \) (m/s) along a straight road after \( t \) seconds is given by \( v(t) = 0.5t^3 - 4.5t^2 + 12t \) for \( 0 \leq t \leq 8 \).\newline (a) Find the times at which the acceleration is zero.\newline (b) Find the times at which the speed is greatest and least in the interval and state both values.

d5.questionText:
A particle moves along a straight line. Its displacement \( s \) metres from a fixed point after \( t \) seconds is given by \( s = 4t^2 - 3t \).
(a) Find the velocity \( v \) as a function of \( t \).
(b) Find the velocity when \( t = 5 \) seconds.

A particle's displacement is \( s = t^3 - 6t^2 + 5 \) metres after \( t \) seconds.
(a) Find the velocity function.
(b) Find the acceleration function.
(c) Find the acceleration when \( t = 4 \) seconds.

A stone is thrown upwards. Its height \( h \) metres above the ground after \( t \) seconds is \( h = 20t - 5t^2 \).
(a) Find the velocity of the stone after \( t \) seconds.
(b) Find the time at which the stone is momentarily stationary (at its maximum height).
(c) Find the maximum height reached.

A particle moves along a straight line. Its displacement \( s \) metres after \( t \) seconds is \( s = t^3 - 9t^2 + 24t \) for \( t \geq 0 \).
(a) Find the velocity function \( v(t) \).
(b) Find the values of \( t \) at which the particle is momentarily at rest.

A motorbike starts from rest and travels along a straight road. After \( t \) seconds its displacement is \( s = 3t^2 \) metres.
(a) Find the velocity after \( t \) seconds.
(b) Find the velocity after 6 seconds.
(c) Find the constant acceleration of the motorbike.

A particle's displacement in metres is given by \( s = 2t^3 - 15t^2 + 36t \) for \( t \geq 0 \).
(a) Find the velocity when \( t = 3 \).
(b) Find the acceleration when \( t = 3 \).
(c) Find the value of \( t \) when the acceleration is zero.

A particle moves so that its displacement is \( s = 5t - t^2 \) metres for \( 0 \leq t \leq 5 \).
(a) Find the velocity function.
(b) Find the time when the particle changes direction.
(c) Find the maximum displacement from the starting point.

A ball is dropped from a height. Its velocity \( v \) ms\(^{-1}\) after \( t \) seconds is \( v = 10t \).
(a) Find the acceleration of the ball.
(b) Find the time taken for the ball to reach \( 35 \text{ ms}^{-1} \).

A particle's displacement is \( s = t^3 - 4t^2 + 4t \) metres after \( t \) seconds.
(a) Find the velocity function.
(b) Find the times when the particle is at rest.
(c) Find the acceleration when \( t = 1 \).

A rectangular garden has length \( x \) m and width \( y \) m. The perimeter of the garden is \( 60 \) m.
(a) Write \( y \) in terms of \( x \).
(b) Write down an expression for the area \( A \) in terms of \( x \) only.
(c) Use calculus to find the value of \( x \) that maximises the area, and find that maximum area.

A farmer uses \( 80 \) m of fencing to enclose a rectangular field on three sides (the fourth side is a wall). The width of the field is \( x \) m.
(a) Show that the area of the field is \( A = x(80 - 2x) \).
(b) Find the maximum possible area using calculus.

A ball is thrown vertically upwards with an initial speed of \( 25 \) ms\(^{-1}\). After \( t \) seconds its height is \( h = 25t - 5t^2 \) metres.
(a) Find the height after 1 second.
(b) Use calculus to find the maximum height.
(c) Find the time when the ball returns to ground level.
A rectangular enclosure is to be made with \( 120 \) m of fencing, enclosing a field on all four sides. Find the dimensions that give the maximum area, and state that area.

A child cuts equal squares of side \( x \) cm from each corner of a \( 30 \times 30 \) cm piece of card and folds the sides up to make an open box.
(a) Show that the volume of the box is \( V = x(30 - 2x)^2 \).
(b) Find the value of \( x \) that maximises the volume.

A closed cylindrical can has radius \( r \) cm and height \( h \) cm. Its volume is \( 250\pi \) cm\(^3\).
(a) Show that the total surface area is \( A = 2\pi r^2 + \dfrac{500\pi}{r} \).
(b) Find the value of \( r \) that minimises \( A \).

A particle moves so that its velocity at time \( t \) seconds is \( v = 3t^2 - 12t + 9 \) ms\(^{-1}\).
(a) Find the acceleration function.
(b) Find the acceleration when the particle has zero velocity.
(c) Find the minimum velocity.

A square piece of metal of side 24 cm has squares of side \( x \) cm cut from each corner and is then folded into an open tray.
(a) Write down an expression for the volume \( V \) of the tray.
(b) Find the value of \( x \) that gives the maximum volume, and state this maximum volume.

A rectangular sheet of cardboard measures \( 20 \) cm by \( 12 \) cm. Equal squares of side \( x \) cm are cut from each corner and the sides folded up to form an open box.
(a) Show that the volume is \( V = 4x^3 - 64x^2 + 240x \).
(b) Find the value of \( x \) that maximises the volume.

A cylindrical storage tank (open at the top) has radius \( r \) m and height \( h \) m. The volume must be \( 16\pi \) m\(^3\).
(a) Express \( h \) in terms of \( r \).
(b) Show that the surface area (base + curved side) is \( A = \pi r^2 + \dfrac{32\pi}{r} \).
(c) Find the value of \( r \) that minimises the surface area.

A particle's displacement is \( s = t^4 - 8t^2 \) metres after \( t \) seconds for \( t \geq 0 \).
(a) Find the velocity and acceleration functions.
(b) Find the values of \( t \) when the particle is at rest.
(c) Find the acceleration at each of those times.
A wire of length \( 48 \) cm is bent to form a rectangle. Find the dimensions that maximise the area enclosed, and state that maximum area.

A rectangular pen is built against a long straight wall (the wall forms one side). The pen uses \( 100 \) m of fencing for the remaining three sides, and the width of the pen (perpendicular to the wall) is \( x \) m.
(a) Write down the length of the pen in terms of \( x \).
(b) Show that the area is \( A = 100x - 2x^2 \).
(c) Find the maximum area and the dimensions of the pen.

A model rocket's height in metres after \( t \) seconds is \( h = -2t^3 + 18t^2 + 5 \) for \( 0 \leq t \leq 10 \).
(a) Find the velocity \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}h}{\mathrm{d}t} \).
(b) Find the times when the rocket is neither ascending nor descending.
(c) Find the maximum height.

A piece of wire 60 cm long is cut into two pieces. One piece is bent into a square of side \( x \) cm and the other into a rectangle of dimensions \( 2x \) cm by \( y \) cm.
(a) Write an expression for \( y \) in terms of \( x \).
(b) Find the total area \( A \) of both shapes in terms of \( x \).
(c) Use calculus to find the value of \( x \) that minimises the total area.

A closed rectangular box has a square base of side \( x \) cm and height \( h \) cm. The total surface area is \( 150 \) cm\(^2\).
(a) Show that the volume is \( V = \dfrac{150x - 2x^3}{4} \).
(b) Find the value of \( x \) that maximises the volume.

A particle moves along a straight line. The displacement from the origin after \( t \) seconds is \( s = 6t - t^2 \) m for \( 0 \leq t \leq 8 \).
(a) Find the velocity when \( t = 1 \).
(b) Find the displacement at the instant when the particle is momentarily at rest.
(c) Find the total distance travelled in the first 8 seconds.

An open-topped cylindrical bucket is to be made from a fixed area of metal \( 300\pi \) cm\(^2\). The radius is \( r \) cm and the height is \( h \) cm.
(a) Show that \( h = \dfrac{300 - r^2}{2r} \).
(b) Show that the volume is \( V = \dfrac{\pi r}{2}(300 - r^2) \).
(c) Find the value of \( r \) that maximises the volume.

A particle moves along the \( x \)-axis. Its displacement is \( x = t^3 - 6t^2 + 12t - 3 \) metres at time \( t \) seconds.
(a) Find the velocity and acceleration functions.
(b) Find the time when the acceleration is zero.
(c) Show that the velocity is always positive for \( t \geq 0 \).

A farmer needs to fence a rectangular area of \( 200 \) m\(^2\) on all four sides.
(a) Let the width be \( x \) m. Write down the length in terms of \( x \).
(b) Find an expression for the total length of fencing needed.
(c) Use calculus to find the dimensions that minimise the fencing used.

A particle travels along a straight line. Its displacement \( s \) metres from a fixed point \( O \) after \( t \) seconds is \( s = t^3 - 3t^2 - 9t + 2 \) for \( t \geq 0 \).
(a) Find the velocity function and hence the times when the particle passes through \( O \) travelling in the positive direction.
(b) Find the acceleration when \( t = 4 \).

A drinks can manufacturer designs a cylindrical can of volume \( 330 \) cm\(^3\). The radius is \( r \) cm and the height is \( h \) cm.
(a) Show that the total surface area (including both circular ends) is \( A = 2\pi r^2 + \dfrac{660}{r} \).
(b) Find the value of \( r \) that minimises the surface area, giving your answer to 3 significant figures.
(c) Find the minimum surface area to 3 significant figures.

A particle moves along a straight line so that its displacement \( s \) metres at time \( t \) seconds is \( s = 2t^3 - 5t^2 + 4t \) for \( t \geq 0 \).
(a) Find the velocity function and determine when the particle first comes to rest.
(b) Find the acceleration at that instant.
(c) Determine whether the particle is speeding up or slowing down just before it comes to rest.

An architect designs a Norman window consisting of a rectangle surmounted by a semicircle. The perimeter of the window (including the base) is \( 6 \) m and the width of the rectangle is \( 2r \) m.
(a) Show that the height of the rectangular part is \( h = 3 - r - \dfrac{\pi r}{2} \).
(b) Show that the total area is \( A = 6r - 2r^2 - \dfrac{\pi r^2}{2} \).
(c) Find the value of \( r \) that maximises the area, giving your answer in exact form.

A particle \( P \) moves along the \( x \)-axis. Its displacement from the origin \( O \) at time \( t \) seconds is \( x = t^3 - 12t + 4 \) metres for \( t \geq 0 \).
(a) Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} \) and \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}^2x}{\mathrm{d}t^2} \).
(b) Find the times when \( P \) is at rest.
(c) Find the position of \( P \) at each of those times.
(d) Determine the direction \( P \) is travelling just after \( t = 2 \).

A company makes storage crates that are open-topped rectangular boxes. Each crate has a square base of side \( x \) m, height \( h \) m, and a volume of \( 4 \) m\(^3\).
(a) Show that the surface area (base and four sides) is \( A = x^2 + \dfrac{16}{x} \).
(b) Use calculus to find the value of \( x \) that minimises the surface area.
(c) Find the minimum surface area and the corresponding height.
(d) Show that your answer is a minimum.

A particle moves on a straight line with displacement \( s = 2t^3 - 9t^2 + 12t \) metres after \( t \) seconds.
(a) Find the velocity \( v \).
(b) Find the values of \( t \) at which the particle is instantaneously at rest.
A particle has velocity \( v = 6t^2 - 4t + 1 \) ms\(^{-1}\) at time \( t \) seconds. Find the acceleration when \( t = 3 \).

An open box is made by cutting equal squares of side \( x \) cm from the corners of a square sheet of card of side 12 cm and folding up the sides. The volume is \( V = x(12 - 2x)^2 \) cm\(^3\).
(a) Find \( \dfrac{\mathrm{d}V}{\mathrm{d}x} \).
(b) Find the value of \( x \) that maximises \( V \) and the maximum volume.
A small business has profit \( P = -2x^2 + 80x - 200 \) pounds when \( x \) units are sold per day. Find the value of \( x \) that maximises profit and the maximum profit.

(a) Write \( \bar{C}(x) \) explicitly.
(b) Find the value of \( x \) that minimises \( \bar{C} \) and the minimum average cost.

A particle moves with displacement \( s = 12t - t^3 \) metres after \( t \) seconds, for \( t \ge 0 \). Find the maximum displacement and the time at which it occurs.
A firm's revenue from selling \( x \) items is \( R(x) = 200x - 0.5x^2 \) pounds. Find the marginal revenue when \( x = 20 \).

A stone is dropped from a cliff. Its height above the ground after \( t \) seconds is \( h = 80 - 5t^2 \) metres.
(a) Find the time taken for the stone to reach the ground.
(b) Find the speed of the stone when it hits the ground.
An open cylindrical container (no lid) has volume \( 27\pi \) cm\(^3\). The radius is \( r \) cm and the height is \( h \) cm. Find the radius and height that minimise the surface area.
A farmer has 60 m of fencing and wants to enclose a rectangular area against a long straight wall, using the wall as one side. Find the dimensions and the maximum area.
A piece of wire of length 40 cm is cut into two pieces and each piece is bent into a square. Find the lengths so that the total area enclosed is a minimum.
The power output of an engine is modelled by \( P = 120t - 3t^2 \) watts, where \( t \) is in seconds. Find the time at which the power is greatest and the maximum power.
A tank is being drained. The volume after \( t \) seconds is \( V = 400 - 20t + \dfrac{t^2}{4} \) litres. Find the rate at which the volume is changing at \( t = 10 \) s, and interpret the sign.

A closed rectangular box has a square base of side \( x \) cm, height \( h \) cm and volume \( 27 \) cm\(^3\).
(a) Show that the surface area is \( S = 2x^2 + \dfrac{108}{x} \).
(b) Find the value of \( x \) that minimises \( S \), and find the minimum surface area.
A particle's displacement is \( s = t^3 - 12t^2 + 36t \) metres after \( t \) seconds. Find the times at which the particle is momentarily at rest and the displacement at each.
In a free-fall model, distance fallen is \( s = 4.9 t^2 \) metres after \( t \) seconds. Find the speed of the falling object after 5 seconds.
A car has displacement \( s = t^3 - 3t^2 - 9t + 5 \) metres after \( t \) seconds, for \( t \ge 0 \). Find the time at which the car is momentarily at rest.
A farmer has 200 m of fencing to build a rectangular field bordered on one side by a straight river (no fence on the river side). Find the maximum area she can enclose.
A company's profit (in pounds) on \( x \) units sold is \( P(x) = 60x - x^2 - 200 \). Find the number of units that maximises profit and the maximum profit.
A firm's profit is \( P(x) = 20x - 0.1x^2 - 50 \) pounds, where \( x \) is the number of items sold. Find the marginal profit when \( x = 40 \).
A particle's displacement is \( s = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t + 2 \) metres after \( t \) seconds. Find the acceleration at each instant the particle is momentarily at rest.
An open cylindrical container (no lid) has volume \( 8\pi \) cm\(^3\). Find the radius and height that minimise the surface area, and the minimum surface area.

The temperature inside an oven \( t \) minutes after switching on is modelled by \( T = 20 + 30t - t^2 \) °C, for \( 0 \le t \le 30 \). Find the maximum temperature reached and the time at which it occurs.

A ball is thrown upwards. Its height (in metres) above the ground after \( t \) seconds is \( h = 2 + 10t - 5t^2 \).
(a) Find the maximum height reached.
(b) Find the time at which the ball hits the ground.
(c) Find the speed at which the ball hits the ground.
A particle has displacement \( s = t^3 - 3t \) metres after \( t \) seconds. Find the minimum velocity for \( t \ge 0 \).

A manufacturer's total cost (in pounds) of producing \( N \) items per day is \( C = 2N^2 + 10N + 800 \). The average cost per item is \( \bar{C} = \dfrac{C}{N} \). Find the value of \( N \) that minimises the average cost and the minimum average cost.
A rectangular postcard has area 100 cm\(^2\). Find the dimensions that minimise the perimeter and state the minimum perimeter.

A ball rolls down a slope. Its distance travelled is \( s = 2t^2 + 3t \) metres after \( t \) seconds.
(a) Find the velocity after \( t \) seconds.
(b) Find the velocity at \( t = 3 \).
(c) Find the acceleration.
A particle moves with displacement \( s = 2t^2 - \dfrac{t^3}{3} \) metres for \( t \ge 0 \). Find the maximum velocity.

An open-topped box has a rectangular base whose length is twice its width \( w \) cm, and height \( h \) cm. The volume is \( 36 \) cm\(^3\).
(a) Show that the surface area is \( S = 2w^2 + \dfrac{108}{w} \).
(b) Find the value of \( w \) that minimises \( S \), and find the minimum surface area.
