| 2 | 0 1 4 4 6 7 9 |
| 3 | 1 3 5 5 8 |
| 4 | 2 5 7 |

Key: 1 | 2 means 12 press-ups.

a) Find the median.

b) Find \( Q_1 \) and \( Q_3 \).

c) Calculate the IQR.

d) Determine whether there are any outliers.

The table below shows the times (in minutes) spent exercising by a sample of adults.

| Time \( t \) (min) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 0 \leq t < 15 \) | 5 |
| \( 15 \leq t < 30 \) | 12 |
| \( 30 \leq t < 45 \) | 18 |
| \( 45 \leq t < 60 \) | 10 |
| \( 60 \leq t < 90 \) | 5 |

a) Estimate the mean time spent exercising.

b) Estimate the standard deviation of the time spent exercising.

Two athletes, A and B, record their 100m sprint times (in seconds) over 10 races.

Athlete A: mean = 11.8, standard deviation = 0.3
Athlete B: mean = 11.6, standard deviation = 0.7

a) Compare the performances of the two athletes.

b) A coach says: "Athlete B is the better choice for the team because their average time is lower." Comment on this statement.
A company has 400 employees: 240 men and 160 women. Explain how to take a stratified sample of 50 employees.

State whether each of the following is qualitative or quantitative data, and if quantitative whether it is discrete or continuous.

a) Shoe size

b) Hair colour

c) Height of a plant

d) Number of siblings

The ages of 10 people are: 14, 17, 19, 22, 23, 25, 27, 30, 35, 42.

Find:
a) the median
b) the lower quartile
c) the upper quartile
d) the interquartile range.

The data below shows test scores for 12 students:

45, 52, 58, 60, 63, 65, 67, 70, 72, 78, 85, 92

An outlier is defined as a value more than \( 1.5 \times IQR \) beyond the nearest quartile. Determine whether there are any outliers.

The following grouped frequency table shows the weights (kg) of 50 packages.

| Weight \( w \) (kg) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 0 < w \leq 5 \) | 8 |
| \( 5 < w \leq 10 \) | 15 |
| \( 10 < w \leq 15 \) | 12 |
| \( 15 < w \leq 20 \) | 10 |
| \( 20 < w \leq 30 \) | 5 |

a) Estimate the mean weight.

b) Find the modal class.

Use linear interpolation to estimate the median from the following data.

| Time \( t \) (min) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 0 \leq t < 10 \) | 6 |
| \( 10 \leq t < 20 \) | 14 |
| \( 20 \leq t < 30 \) | 20 |
| \( 30 \leq t < 40 \) | 8 |
| \( 40 \leq t < 60 \) | 2 |

Give one advantage and one disadvantage of:

a) opportunity sampling

b) quota sampling.

The scores of 8 students in a test are: 12, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25, 28, 80.

a) Calculate the mean and standard deviation.

b) One value is an outlier. Identify it and explain whether the mean or the median is a better measure of central tendency for this data.
A data set has \( n = 20 \), \( \sum x = 140 \) and \( \sum x^2 = 1120 \). Find the mean and standard deviation.
A coded data set uses \( y = x - 50 \). Given \( \sum y = 30 \), \( \sum y^2 = 250 \) and \( n = 10 \), find the mean and standard deviation of the original data \( x \).

The marks for 15 students are given below.

23, 25, 28, 30, 32, 35, 37, 40, 42, 45, 48, 52, 55, 60, 68

Draw a box plot for this data.

From the box plot below:
Minimum = 12, Q1 = 18, Median = 25, Q3 = 34, Maximum = 50.

a) Find the IQR.

b) Are there any outliers? Use the \( 1.5 \times IQR \) rule.

c) Describe the skewness of the distribution.
Explain the difference between a population and a sample. Give an example of each.
A data set of 20 values has mean 15 and standard deviation 4. An extra value of 35 is added. Find the new mean and the new standard deviation.

The frequency table below shows the number of goals scored per match in a football season.

| Goals | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 4 | 8 | 12 | 10 | 4 | 2 |

Find the mean, median and mode.

A school has 600 students in Years 7–11. The table shows the number of students in each year.

| Year | 7 | 8 | 9 | 10 | 11 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Students | 140 | 130 | 120 | 110 | 100 |

A stratified sample of 60 students is to be taken. Calculate the number of students to be sampled from each year.

Two classes sit the same test. Class A: mean = 62, SD = 8. Class B: mean = 58, SD = 12.

a) Compare the results.

b) A student scored 74. In which class is this a more impressive result? Explain using standardised scores.
Explain what is meant by a census. Give one advantage and one disadvantage of using a census rather than a sample.

A set of data has \( n = 12 \), \( \sum x = 84 \), \( \sum x^2 = 700 \). Two values, 5 and 9, are removed.

a) Find the new mean.

b) Find the new standard deviation.

The cumulative frequency table below shows the heights (cm) of 80 plants.

| Height \( h \) (cm) | Cumulative frequency |
|---|---|
| \( h \leq 10 \) | 5 |
| \( h \leq 20 \) | 18 |
| \( h \leq 30 \) | 42 |
| \( h \leq 40 \) | 65 |
| \( h \leq 50 \) | 76 |
| \( h \leq 60 \) | 80 |

a) Estimate the median height.

b) Estimate the interquartile range.

State which type of sampling is being used in each scenario.

a) Asking every 10th person who enters a shop.

b) Selecting people from each age group in proportion.

c) Asking the first 20 people you see in the street.

d) Every member gets a ticket, and 50 tickets are drawn from a hat.
The coded data \( y = \frac{x - 100}{5} \) gives \( \bar{y} = 3.2 \) and \( \sigma_y = 1.5 \). Find \( \bar{x} \) and \( \sigma_x \).

Two box plots for the daily temperatures (°C) in two cities are summarised below.

City A: Min = 5, Q1 = 10, Median = 15, Q3 = 20, Max = 28
City B: Min = 8, Q1 = 14, Median = 18, Q3 = 22, Max = 25

Compare the two distributions.
Calculate the mean and standard deviation of: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11.

A histogram has the following bars.

| Class | Frequency density |
|---|---|
| \( 0 \leq x < 10 \) | 1.2 |
| \( 10 \leq x < 20 \) | 2.5 |
| \( 20 \leq x < 30 \) | 3.0 |
| \( 30 \leq x < 50 \) | 1.5 |

Find the frequency for each class and the total number of data values.
Explain what is meant by positive skew and negative skew. For each, state the relationship between the mean and the median.
A data set has quartiles \( Q_1 = 20 \), \( Q_2 = 28 \), \( Q_3 = 32 \). Using the \( 1.5 \times IQR \) rule, find the boundaries for outliers. Would a value of 3 be an outlier?
What is a sampling frame? Why is it important for random sampling?

The grouped frequency table shows journey times (minutes) to work for 100 employees.

| Time \( t \) (min) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 0 \leq t < 15 \) | 12 |
| \( 15 \leq t < 30 \) | 28 |
| \( 30 \leq t < 45 \) | 35 |
| \( 45 \leq t < 60 \) | 18 |
| \( 60 \leq t < 90 \) | 7 |

a) Estimate the mean.

b) Use interpolation to estimate the median.

c) Estimate the standard deviation.

Two factories produce bolts. A sample from each is measured.

Factory A: \( n = 50 \), \( \bar{x} = 25.2 \) mm, \( \sigma = 0.4 \) mm.
Factory B: \( n = 50 \), \( \bar{x} = 25.0 \) mm, \( \sigma = 0.1 \) mm.

The target length is 25.0 mm.

a) Compare the two factories.

b) Which factory produces more reliable bolts? Explain.

s2.questionText:
A school has 1200 students. A researcher wants to survey 60 students about their lunch preferences.

a) Describe how the researcher could take a simple random sample of 60 students.

b) Give one advantage and one disadvantage of using a simple random sample.

A factory produces 5000 bolts per day. A quality control inspector wants to check a sample of 100 bolts.

a) Describe how a systematic sample of 100 bolts could be taken.

b) Give one advantage of systematic sampling over simple random sampling in this context.

A sixth form college has the following students:

| Year group | Number of students |
|---|---|
| Year 12 | 180 |
| Year 13 | 120 |

A stratified sample of 50 students is to be taken.

a) How many students should be sampled from each year group?

b) Explain why stratified sampling is appropriate here.

A company has employees in four departments:

| Department | Staff |
|---|---|
| Sales | 48 |
| Marketing | 32 |
| Finance | 24 |
| IT | 16 |

A stratified sample of 30 employees is required. Calculate the number of employees to be sampled from each department.

A student stands outside a supermarket on a Saturday afternoon and asks the first 50 people who walk past about their weekly food spending.

a) What type of sampling method is this?

b) Give two reasons why this sample may not be representative of the population.

Classify each of the following variables as qualitative or quantitative. If quantitative, state whether it is discrete or continuous.

a) The number of pets a household owns.

b) The colour of a car.

c) The time taken to run 100 metres.

d) The number of pages in a book.

The ages (in years) of 10 members of a swimming club are:

12, 15, 14, 18, 12, 16, 19, 14, 17, 13

a) Calculate the mean age.

b) Find the median age.

c) State the mode.

The table shows the number of hours of sunshine per day recorded over 30 days.

| Hours (\( h \)) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 0 \leq h < 2 \) | 3 |
| \( 2 \leq h < 4 \) | 7 |
| \( 4 \leq h < 6 \) | 10 |
| \( 6 \leq h < 8 \) | 6 |
| \( 8 \leq h < 10 \) | 4 |

a) Write down the modal class.

b) Estimate the mean number of hours of sunshine per day.

The following frequency table shows the marks scored by 25 students in a test.

| Mark | Frequency |
|---|---|
| 3 | 2 |
| 4 | 5 |
| 5 | 8 |
| 6 | 6 |
| 7 | 3 |
| 8 | 1 |

a) Find the median mark.

b) Calculate the mean mark.

The class that contains the median of a grouped frequency distribution is called the median class. The table shows the weights (kg) of 40 parcels.

| Weight \( w \) (kg) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 0 < w \leq 2 \) | 8 |
| \( 2 < w \leq 4 \) | 14 |
| \( 4 < w \leq 6 \) | 11 |
| \( 6 < w \leq 8 \) | 5 |
| \( 8 < w \leq 10 \) | 2 |

a) Write down the median class.

b) Use linear interpolation to estimate the median weight.

The marks scored by 9 students in a quiz are:

3, 5, 7, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12

a) Find the lower quartile \( Q_1 \), the median \( Q_2 \), and the upper quartile \( Q_3 \).

b) Calculate the interquartile range (IQR).

c) Calculate the range.

The following data gives the daily rainfall (mm) over 11 days:

0, 1, 2, 3, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 12, 25

a) Find \( Q_1 \), \( Q_2 \) and \( Q_3 \).

b) An outlier is defined as a value more than \( 1.5 \times \text{IQR} \) beyond the nearest quartile. Determine whether there are any outliers.

For the data set: 4, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12

a) Calculate the mean.

b) Calculate the variance.

c) Calculate the standard deviation.

A data set has \( n = 20 \), \( \sum x = 140 \) and \( \sum x^2 = 1120 \).

a) Calculate the mean.

b) Calculate the standard deviation.

For a data set of 15 values, \( \sum x = 90 \) and \( \sum x^2 = 640 \).

A coding \( y = x - 5 \) is applied to each data value.

a) Find \( \sum y \).

b) Find \( \sum y^2 \).

c) Hence find the mean and variance of \( y \).

d) What is the mean and variance of \( x \)?

The table shows the times (minutes) taken by 50 commuters to travel to work.

| Time \( t \) (min) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 0 \leq t < 10 \) | 5 |
| \( 10 \leq t < 20 \) | 12 |
| \( 20 \leq t < 30 \) | 18 |
| \( 30 \leq t < 50 \) | 10 |
| \( 50 \leq t < 80 \) | 5 |

a) Calculate the frequency density for each class.

b) Draw a histogram to represent the data.

A histogram is drawn to represent the lengths (cm) of 80 leaves. The bar for the class \( 4 \leq l < 6 \) has a width of 2 cm and a height (frequency density) of 8.

a) How many leaves are in the class \( 4 \leq l < 6 \)?

b) The bar for the class \( 6 \leq l < 10 \) has a frequency density of 3.5. How many leaves are in this class?

c) The remaining leaves are in the class \( 10 \leq l < 15 \). Calculate the frequency density for this class.

The table shows the ages of 60 people at a concert.

| Age \( a \) (years) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 15 \leq a < 20 \) | 10 |
| \( 20 \leq a < 25 \) | 18 |
| \( 25 \leq a < 35 \) | 20 |
| \( 35 \leq a < 50 \) | 9 |
| \( 50 \leq a < 70 \) | 3 |

a) Calculate the frequency density for each class.

b) Estimate the mean age of the concert-goers.

The histogram below represents the distances (km) that 100 employees travel to work.

The frequency densities are:
\( 0\text{–}5 \): 2.4, \( 5\text{–}10 \): 4.0, \( 10\text{–}15 \): 3.2, \( 15\text{–}25 \): 1.2, \( 25\text{–}40 \): 0.4

a) Use the histogram to complete a frequency table.

b) Estimate how many employees travel more than 12 km.

The masses (grams) of 50 apples are recorded in the table below.

| Mass \( m \) (g) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 100 \leq m < 120 \) | 6 |
| \( 120 \leq m < 140 \) | 14 |
| \( 140 \leq m < 150 \) | 15 |
| \( 150 \leq m < 170 \) | 10 |
| \( 170 \leq m < 200 \) | 5 |

a) Explain why a histogram is more appropriate than a bar chart for this data.

b) Calculate the frequency densities and draw a histogram.

The table shows the times (seconds) taken by 60 runners to complete a 400m race.

| Time \( t \) (s) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 50 \leq t < 55 \) | 4 |
| \( 55 \leq t < 60 \) | 10 |
| \( 60 \leq t < 65 \) | 22 |
| \( 65 \leq t < 70 \) | 16 |
| \( 70 \leq t < 80 \) | 8 |

a) Complete a cumulative frequency table.

b) Draw a cumulative frequency diagram.

c) Use your diagram to estimate the median and the interquartile range.

The following data gives the number of minutes spent on homework by 15 students, already in order:

10, 15, 20, 22, 25, 28, 30, 32, 35, 38, 40, 42, 50, 55, 70

a) Find \( Q_1 \), \( Q_2 \) and \( Q_3 \).

b) Draw a box plot to represent the data.

c) Identify any outliers using the \( 1.5 \times \text{IQR} \) rule.

A box plot has the following five-number summary:

Minimum = 5, \( Q_1 = 12 \), Median = 18, \( Q_3 = 25 \), Maximum = 40.

a) Calculate the IQR.

b) Determine whether there are any outliers using the \( 1.5 \times \text{IQR} \) rule.

c) Describe the skewness of the distribution.

The heights (cm) of 40 plants are summarised in the grouped frequency table below.

| Height \( h \) (cm) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 0 \leq h < 5 \) | 2 |
| \( 5 \leq h < 10 \) | 8 |
| \( 10 \leq h < 15 \) | 14 |
| \( 15 \leq h < 20 \) | 10 |
| \( 20 \leq h < 30 \) | 6 |

a) Draw a cumulative frequency diagram.

b) Use your diagram to estimate the median and the IQR.

The waiting times (minutes) at a GP surgery are summarised below.

Minimum = 2, \( Q_1 = 8 \), Median = 14, \( Q_3 = 22 \), Maximum = 45.

a) Draw a box plot for this data.

b) An outlier is defined as more than \( 1.5 \times \text{IQR} \) beyond the nearest quartile. Identify any outliers.

c) Redraw the box plot with any outliers shown as crosses and the whiskers ending at the last non-outlier values.

The box plots below show the test scores for two classes, A and B.

Class A: Min = 30, \( Q_1 = 45 \), Median = 55, \( Q_3 = 65 \), Max = 80.
Class B: Min = 40, \( Q_1 = 50 \), Median = 60, \( Q_3 = 70 \), Max = 90.

Compare the two distributions. You must make two comparisons, one about a measure of location and one about a measure of spread.

A data set has the following summary statistics:
\( n = 10 \), \( \sum x = 80 \), \( \sum x^2 = 720 \).

A new data value of 10 is added to the set.

a) Find the new values of \( n \), \( \sum x \) and \( \sum x^2 \).

b) Calculate the new mean.

c) Calculate the new standard deviation.

The stem-and-leaf diagram below shows the number of press-ups completed by 20 students.

| Stem | Leaf |
|---|---|
| 1 | 2 3 5 8 |
| 2 | 0 1 4 4 6 7 9 |
| 3 | 1 3 5 5 8 |
| 4 | 2 5 7 |

Key: 1 | 2 means 12 press-ups.

a) Find the median.

b) Find \( Q_1 \) and \( Q_3 \).

c) Calculate the IQR.

d) Determine whether there are any outliers.

The table below shows the times (in minutes) spent exercising by a sample of adults.

| Time \( t \) (min) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 0 \leq t < 15 \) | 5 |
| \( 15 \leq t < 30 \) | 12 |
| \( 30 \leq t < 45 \) | 18 |
| \( 45 \leq t < 60 \) | 10 |
| \( 60 \leq t < 90 \) | 5 |

a) Estimate the mean time spent exercising.

b) Estimate the standard deviation of the time spent exercising.

Two athletes, A and B, record their 100m sprint times (in seconds) over 10 races.

Athlete A: mean = 11.8, standard deviation = 0.3
Athlete B: mean = 11.6, standard deviation = 0.7

a) Compare the performances of the two athletes.

b) A coach says: "Athlete B is the better choice for the team because their average time is lower." Comment on this statement.

The table shows the number of books read by 30 students in a month.

| Books | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 3 | 7 | 9 | 6 | 4 | 1 |

Draw a bar chart for this data.
Explain the difference between a bar chart and a histogram.

The histogram below shows the distribution of waiting times (minutes) at a clinic.

| Time \( t \) (min) | Frequency density |
|---|---|
| \( 0 \leq t < 5 \) | 2.4 |
| \( 5 \leq t < 10 \) | 4.0 |
| \( 10 \leq t < 20 \) | 3.0 |
| \( 20 \leq t < 40 \) | 1.0 |

a) Find the frequency for each class.

b) Estimate the number of patients who waited between 8 and 15 minutes.

The cumulative frequency table below shows the marks of 80 students.

| Mark \( m \) | Cumulative frequency |
|---|---|
| \( m \leq 20 \) | 4 |
| \( m \leq 40 \) | 18 |
| \( m \leq 60 \) | 50 |
| \( m \leq 80 \) | 72 |
| \( m \leq 100 \) | 80 |

a) Draw a cumulative frequency curve.

b) Use your curve to estimate the median and IQR.

c) Estimate the number of students who scored more than 70.

The data below shows the daily rainfall (mm) for 10 days: 0, 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 15, 18, 22, 35.

Draw a stem-and-leaf diagram for this data.

From the following box plot data, draw a box plot and comment on the skewness.

Minimum = 10, Q1 = 25, Median = 30, Q3 = 50, Maximum = 70.

A set of data has the following summary statistics: \( n = 40 \), \( \sum x = 280 \), \( \sum x^2 = 2240 \).

a) Calculate the mean.

b) Calculate the variance and standard deviation.

The following frequency table shows the number of customers visiting a shop each day.

| Customers \( c \) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 0 \leq c < 20 \) | 5 |
| \( 20 \leq c < 40 \) | 12 |
| \( 40 \leq c < 50 \) | 18 |
| \( 50 \leq c < 70 \) | 10 |
| \( 70 \leq c < 100 \) | 5 |

Calculate the frequency densities and draw a histogram.

The heights (cm) of 20 students are:

152, 155, 158, 160, 162, 163, 165, 167, 168, 170, 171, 172, 174, 175, 176, 178, 180, 182, 185, 190.

Draw a stem-and-leaf diagram. Use the diagram to find the median.

A pie chart shows the favourite colours of 120 people. The angle for blue is 90°, red is 120°, green is 60°, and other is 90°.

a) How many people chose each colour?

b) What fraction chose red?

The back-to-back stem-and-leaf diagram below shows test scores for two classes.

Class A: leaves go left. Class B: leaves go right.

| Class A | Stem | Class B |
|---|---|---|
| 8 5 3 | 4 | 2 6 9 |
| 7 4 2 1 | 5 | 0 3 5 8 |
| 9 6 5 | 6 | 1 4 7 |
| 3 | 7 | 2 5 |

Key: 4|2 = 42 for Class B, 3|4 = 43 for Class A.

Compare the two distributions.
Explain what a cumulative frequency diagram is and describe how to use it to estimate the median and quartiles.

The grouped frequency table shows distances (km) cycled by 60 people in a week.

| Distance \( d \) (km) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 0 \leq d < 10 \) | 8 |
| \( 10 \leq d < 20 \) | 15 |
| \( 20 \leq d < 30 \) | 20 |
| \( 30 \leq d < 50 \) | 12 |
| \( 50 \leq d < 80 \) | 5 |

a) Draw a cumulative frequency diagram.

b) Estimate the median and IQR.

c) Estimate the 90th percentile.

A frequency polygon is drawn from the following data.

| Score | 10 | 20 | 30 | 40 | 50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 3 | 8 | 12 | 7 | 2 |

Describe how to draw the frequency polygon.

Two box plots are given:

Males: Min = 155, Q1 = 165, Median = 172, Q3 = 180, Max = 195
Females: Min = 148, Q1 = 158, Median = 164, Q3 = 170, Max = 182

a) Compare the heights.

b) Identify any outliers using the \( 1.5 \times IQR \) rule.
What does the area of a bar in a histogram represent?

The weights (g) of 100 eggs are given in the table.

| Weight \( w \) (g) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 40 \leq w < 50 \) | 10 |
| \( 50 \leq w < 55 \) | 25 |
| \( 55 \leq w < 60 \) | 35 |
| \( 60 \leq w < 70 \) | 20 |
| \( 70 \leq w < 90 \) | 10 |

Calculate frequency densities and explain why a histogram is more appropriate than a bar chart.

A data set has \( Q_1 = 14 \), \( Q_2 = 20 \), \( Q_3 = 38 \).

a) Calculate the IQR.

b) Describe the skewness. Justify your answer.

c) Would the mean be greater than, less than, or equal to the median? Explain.

The table shows how 200 students travel to school.

| Method | Walk | Bus | Car | Cycle |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 70 | 60 | 50 | 20 |

Calculate the angle for each sector of a pie chart.
A set of data has coding \( y = 2(x - 30) \). Given \( \bar{y} = 8 \) and \( \sigma_y = 6 \), find \( \bar{x} \) and \( \sigma_x \).

A histogram shows the ages of people at an event. One bar has class 20–30 with frequency density 2.5. Another bar has class 30–50 with frequency density 1.2.

a) Find the frequency for each class.

b) Explain why the second bar looks shorter despite having more people.

The five-number summary for a data set is: 5, 12, 18, 25, 40.

a) Draw a box plot.

b) Calculate the IQR.

c) Is the data symmetric, positively skewed, or negatively skewed?

A grouped frequency table and histogram are given for the reaction times (seconds) of 50 drivers.

| Time \( t \) (s) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 0.1 \leq t < 0.2 \) | 5 |
| \( 0.2 \leq t < 0.3 \) | 12 |
| \( 0.3 \leq t < 0.4 \) | 18 |
| \( 0.4 \leq t < 0.5 \) | 10 |
| \( 0.5 \leq t < 0.8 \) | 5 |

a) Estimate the mean reaction time.

b) Estimate the median reaction time.
Give three advantages of using a box plot to represent data.

Two histograms show the distribution of exam marks for Year 12 and Year 13. The Year 12 histogram has a tall peak at 50–60 marks. The Year 13 histogram is more spread out with a peak at 60–70.

Compare and contrast the two distributions.
The data 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 has mean 6. Each value is multiplied by 3 and then 5 is added. Find the new mean and standard deviation.

An outlier is removed from the data set 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 50. The outlier is 50.

a) Find the mean and SD before removing the outlier.

b) Find the mean and SD after removing the outlier.

c) Comment on the effect of removing the outlier.

A frequency table shows the number of cars passing a junction each minute.

| Cars | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 2 | 5 | 8 | 10 | 8 | 4 | 3 |

Find the mean, mode and median.
Explain why the median is sometimes preferred over the mean as a measure of central tendency. Give an example.

The lengths (cm) of 80 leaves are summarised in the grouped frequency table.

| Length \( l \) (cm) | Frequency |
|---|---|
| \( 0 < l \leq 2 \) | 5 |
| \( 2 < l \leq 4 \) | 15 |
| \( 4 < l \leq 6 \) | 28 |
| \( 6 < l \leq 8 \) | 22 |
| \( 8 < l \leq 12 \) | 10 |

a) Draw a histogram.

b) Estimate the mean.

c) Use interpolation to estimate the median.

s3.questionText:
The ages (in years) of 7 members of a quiz team are:

\( 18,; 21,; 19,; 25,; 22,; 19,; 20 \)

Calculate the mean age.

The number of goals scored by a football team in 9 matches were:

\( 3,; 1,; 0,; 2,; 4,; 1,; 3,; 2,; 1 \)

Find the median number of goals.

A shop records the shoe sizes sold in one day:

\( 6,; 7,; 8,; 7,; 9,; 6,; 7,; 10,; 8,; 7 \)

a) State the mode.

b) Give one reason why the mode is a useful average for shoe sizes.

The table shows the number of pets owned by students in a class.

| Pets (\(x\)) | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency (\(f\)) | 5 | 8 | 7 | 3 | 2 |

Calculate the mean number of pets.

Using the same data as Q4:

| Pets (\(x\)) | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency (\(f\)) | 5 | 8 | 7 | 3 | 2 |

Find the median number of pets.

The heights (in cm) of 8 plants are:

\( 12,; 15,; 9,; 18,; 14,; 11,; 16,; 13 \)

Find the median height.

The daily wages (in £) of 6 workers in a small company are:

\( 80,; 85,; 80,; 90,; 85,; 250 \)

a) Calculate the mean, median and mode.

b) Which average best represents the data? Give a reason.

A student scores 72 on Paper 1 (weighted 40%) and 85 on Paper 2 (weighted 60%).

Calculate the student's overall weighted mean score.

The table shows the times (in minutes) taken by 30 students to complete a puzzle.

| Time (\(t\) min) | \(0 \leq t < 5\) | \(5 \leq t < 10\) | \(10 \leq t < 15\) | \(15 \leq t < 20\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 4 | 12 | 10 | 4 |

Estimate the mean time.

A dataset has 10 values with a mean of 15.

a) Calculate \(\sum x\).

b) An extra value of 48 is added. Calculate the new mean.

c) Has the extra value had a large effect on the mean? Explain your answer.

The test marks of 8 students are:

\( 65,; 72,; 58,; 80,; 74,; 69,; 85,; 77 \)

Calculate the mean mark.

The weights (kg) of 6 parcels are:

\( 2.4,; 3.1,; 1.8,; 2.7,; 3.5,; 2.9 \)

Find the mean weight, giving your answer to 3 s.f.

The midday temperatures (°C) at 5 locations on one day are:

\( -3,; 2,; -1,; 4,; -2 \)

Calculate the mean temperature.

A set of 12 values has a total of 156.

Find the mean.

The mean of 15 numbers is 24.

Find the total of the 15 numbers.

The reaction times (seconds) of 7 students are:

\( 0.24,; 0.31,; 0.22,; 0.28,; 0.35,; 0.19,; 0.26 \)

Find the median.

The ages of 10 members of a club are:

\( 18,; 22,; 25,; 19,; 21,; 24,; 20,; 23,; 26,; 22 \)

Find the median age.

The scores on a quiz were:

\( 8,; 7,; 9,; 8,; 6,; 10,; 8,; 9 \)

Find the median score.

A stem-and-leaf diagram shows the ages of 10 people.

```
2 | 3 5 7
3 | 1 2 4 6 8
4 | 0 3
```

Key: 2 | 3 means 23.

Find the median age.

The heights (m) of 9 plants are:

\( 1.62,; 1.58,; 1.70,; 1.65,; 1.73,; 1.68,; 1.60,; 1.64,; 1.72 \)

Find the median height.

A survey asked 9 students their favourite colour:

Red, Blue, Red, Green, Blue, Red, Yellow, Red, Blue.

Find the mode.

The shoe sizes sold in a shop one morning are:

\( 4,; 5,; 6,; 5,; 7,; 6,; 5,; 6,; 8,; 7 \)

Find the mode(s).
Explain why the dataset \(1,; 2,; 3,; 4,; 5,; 6,; 7\) has no mode.

The number of pets owned by 23 students is shown.

| Pets | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 4 | 9 | 7 | 2 | 1 |

State the mode.

A teacher tallies the number of siblings each of her 28 students has:

\( 0\!:\! \cancel{|\!\!\!\!\!|};||\quad 1\!:\!\cancel{|\!\!\!\!\!|};\cancel{|\!\!\!\!\!|};|\quad 2\!:\!\cancel{|\!\!\!\!\!|}\quad 3\!:\!|||\quad 4\!:\!|| \)

Frequencies: 0→7, 1→11, 2→5, 3→3, 4→2.

State the mode.

The number of children per household in a survey of 40 homes:

| Children | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 8 | 15 | 12 | 4 | 1 |

Calculate the mean number of children.

The lengths (m) of ribbons cut for a project:

| Length (\(x\)) | 0.5 | 1.0 | 1.5 | 2.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 4 | 10 | 8 | 3 |

Calculate the mean length.

A frequency table contains an unknown frequency \(k\):

| \(x\) | 10 | 20 | 30 |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(f\) | 5 | \(k\) | 3 |

The mean is 18. Find \(k\).

The number of phone calls made per day by an office over 50 days:

| Calls (\(x\)) | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 10 | 15 | 12 | 8 | 5 |

Calculate the mean number of calls per day.

The number of goals scored by a football team in 30 matches:

| Goals | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 5 | 9 | 8 | 5 | 2 | 1 |

State the median, mode and mean.

In a frequency table, the cumulative frequencies so far are 3, 11, 18, 27, 36, 40. The median is the 20.5th value.

Which value of \(x\) contains the median, given \(x\) takes values 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (in order)?

The number of emails received per day by 100 workers one morning:

| Emails (\(x\)) | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 8 | 14 | 22 | 25 | 17 | 9 | 5 |

Find the median.

The times (in minutes) taken to complete a task:

| Time (\(t\)) | \(0 \leq t < 10\) | \(10 \leq t < 20\) | \(20 \leq t < 30\) | \(30 \leq t < 40\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 6 | 15 | 12 | 7 |

Estimate the mean time.

The speeds (mph) of 60 cars passing a monitor:

| Speed (\(v\)) | \(20 \leq v < 30\) | \(30 \leq v < 40\) | \(40 \leq v < 50\) | \(50 \leq v < 60\) | \(60 \leq v < 70\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 5 | 18 | 22 | 10 | 5 |

Estimate the mean speed, to 2 d.p.

The ages of 60 attendees at a concert:

| Age (\(a\)) | \(0 \leq a < 20\) | \(20 \leq a < 40\) | \(40 \leq a < 60\) | \(60 \leq a < 80\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 8 | 22 | 18 | 12 |

Estimate the mean age, to 2 d.p.

A grouped table with unequal class widths:

| Mass (\(m\), g) | \(0 \leq m < 50\) | \(50 \leq m < 100\) | \(100 \leq m < 200\) | \(200 \leq m < 400\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 12 | 20 | 15 | 3 |

Estimate the mean mass.
Explain why the mean calculated from a grouped frequency table is only an estimate.

From the table:

| Length (\(\ell\), cm) | \(0\leq\ell<10\) | \(10\leq\ell<20\) | \(20\leq\ell<30\) | \(30\leq\ell<40\) | \(40\leq\ell<50\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 5 | 12 | 25 | 20 | 18 |

State the modal class.
Using the same table as Q41, find the class containing the median.

Using the same grouped data as Q41:

| Length (\(\ell\), cm) | \(0\leq\ell<10\) | \(10\leq\ell<20\) | \(20\leq\ell<30\) | \(30\leq\ell<40\) | \(40\leq\ell<50\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 5 | 12 | 25 | 20 | 18 |

Use linear interpolation to estimate the median.
Using the same table as Q41, use linear interpolation to estimate Q₁.
Using the same table as Q41, use linear interpolation to estimate Q₃.

Group A contains 20 students with mean score 15.

Group B contains 30 students with mean score 18.

Find the combined mean.

A student's final grade is weighted as:

- Paper 1 (50%): 68
- Paper 2 (30%): 72
- Coursework (20%): 80

Calculate the final weighted mean.

Class A has 25 students with mean 55.
Class B has 15 students with mean 63.

Find the combined mean for the 40 students.

A course has three modules weighted 40%, 35%, 25%. A student scores 73, 68 and 85 respectively.

Find the weighted mean.

Three groups of students took a test:

- Group 1: 10 students, mean 72
- Group 2: 15 students, mean 68
- Group 3: 25 students, mean 75

Find the combined mean for all 50 students.

Six numbers are 7, 12, 9, \(x\), 14, 10. Their mean is 11.

Find \(x\).

Five values have a mean of 20. Four of the values are 15, 18, 22 and 25.

Find the fifth value.

Nine values have a mean of 25. A tenth value is added and the mean increases to 27.

Find the tenth value.

The mean of 8 numbers is 18. One number is removed and the mean of the remaining 7 is 19.

Find the number that was removed.

A frequency table contains an unknown frequency \(k\):

| \(x\) | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \(f\) | 3 | 5 | \(k\) | 4 | 2 |

The mean is 2.8. Find \(k\).

Consider the dataset: \(3,; 4,; 4,; 5,; 5,; 5,; 6,; 7,; 8,; 50\).

a) Calculate the mean and median.

b) Which average best represents the data? Explain.

Consider the data: \(10,; 12,; 14,; 15,; 16,; 18,; 100\).

a) Calculate the mean and median with the outlier 100 included.

b) Calculate the mean and median without the outlier.

c) Compare how each measure changed.

A dataset \(x\) has mean 20 and mode 18. Each value is transformed using \(y = x + 5\).

State the new mean and new mode.

The mean of a set of values \(x\) is 30. A new variable is defined as \(y = x + 4\).

State \(\bar{y}\).

The mean of a set of values \(x\) is 12. Let \(y = 2x + 3\).

State \(\bar{y}\), and explain.

s4.questionText:
Find the range and interquartile range of the following data set:

41, 49, 26, 20, 31, 9, 12, 39, 4, 21, 9, 12, 48, 23, 26, 10

The diameters (in miles) of the eight planets in the Solar System are given below:

3032, 7521, 7926, 4222, 88846, 74898, 31763, 30778

For this data set, calculate:
a) the range
b) the upper and lower quartiles
c) the interquartile range.

Find the median and interquartile range of the following data set:

2, 5, 3, 11, 6, 8, 3, 8, 1, 6, 2, 23, 9, 11, 18, 19, 22, 7

The heights of trees in a park are measured to the nearest metre. The results are shown below.

| Height (m) | 0–5 | 6–10 | 11–15 | 16–20 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of trees | 26 | 17 | 11 | 6 |

Estimate the interquartile range of the tree heights using linear interpolation.

A reptile specialist records the mass (\( m \), in kilograms) of 150 tortoises. Her results are shown in the table.

| Mass (kg) | \( 0.2 \leq m < 0.6 \) | \( 0.6 \leq m < 1.0 \) | \( 1.0 \leq m < 1.4 \) | \( 1.4 \leq m < 1.8 \) | \( 1.8 \leq m < 2.2 \) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 27 | 43 | 35 | 31 | 14 |

Estimate the 10th percentile for this data.

The speeds (in mph) of 18 cars observed in town at 8:45 am are:

14, 16, 15, 18, 15, 17, 16, 16, 18, 16, 15, 13, 15, 14, 16, 17, 18, 15

Calculate:
a) the range and the interquartile range
b) the 30% to 70% interpercentile range.

The lengths (\( l \)) of a zoo's beetles are measured to the nearest mm. The data is shown below.

| Length (mm) | 0–5 | 6–10 | 11–15 | 16–30 | 31–50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of beetles | 82 | 28 | 44 | 30 | 16 |

Estimate:
a) the interquartile range
b) the 20% to 80% interpercentile range.

The ages (in years) of students at a school are shown in the table.

| Age (years) | 11–12 | 13–14 | 15–16 | 17–18 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of students | 50 | 65 | 58 | 27 |

a) Draw a cumulative frequency diagram.

b) Estimate the median and interquartile range from the graph.

The distance walked (in km) by 20 people is shown below.

| Distance, \( d \) (km) | \( 0 < d \leq 2 \) | \( 2 < d \leq 4 \) | \( 4 < d \leq 6 \) | \( 6 < d \leq 8 \) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of walkers | 1 | 10 | 7 | 2 |

a) Draw a cumulative frequency diagram.

b) Use your diagram to estimate the median and IQR.

A cumulative frequency diagram shows the monthly earnings (in £) of some sixteen-year-olds. From the diagram:
  Total number sampled = 80
  Median ≈ £62
  Q₁ ≈ £44
  Q₃ ≈ £86

a) Estimate the interquartile range.

b) Estimate how many earned less than £84.

c) Estimate how many earned between £46 and £84.

The lower and upper quartiles of a data set are 19 and 31. Determine whether the data values 4 and 52 are outliers, using the fences \( Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR} \) and \( Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR} \).

A set of data was analysed and the following values were found:
  Minimum = 4, Q₁ = 16, Median = 24, Q₃ = 37, Maximum = 49.

a) Find the interquartile range.

b) Are there any outliers in this data set?

c) Draw a box plot to illustrate this data set.

The IQs of 21 Year 11 students are shown in the stem and leaf diagram.

| Stem | Leaf |
|---|---|
| 9 | 3 |
| 10 | 5  8  9 |
| 11 | 0  2  3  5  6  8  9 |
| 12 | 0  0  1  3  4  6  8 |
| 13 | 2  4 |
| 14 | 4 |

Key: 10 | 5 means an IQ of 105

Draw a box plot to represent this data, using the fences \( Q_1 - 1.5 \times \text{IQR} \) and \( Q_3 + 1.5 \times \text{IQR} \) to identify outliers.

The numbers of items of junk mail received in six months by people in Pigham are:

14, 17, 20, 20, 32, 33, 35, 35, 42, 46, 48, 52

a) Are any of the data values outliers? Use the \( 1.5 \times \text{IQR} \) rule.

b) Draw a box plot to illustrate the data from Pigham.

The numbers of items of junk mail received in six months by people in Goossea are:

0, 2, 6, 13, 15, 17, 19, 24, 27, 28, 28, 31, 32, 35, 41, 44, 50, 75

a) Find the quartiles and determine whether any values are outliers.

b) Draw a box plot, marking any outliers with crosses.

c) Compare the distributions of junk mail in Goossea and Pigham (from Q14).

Find the variance and standard deviation of the following data set:

2, 3, 4, 4, 6, 11, 12
Use the fences \( \bar{x} \pm 2 \) standard deviations to check the data set in Q16 for outliers.

The attendance figures (\( x \)) for Wessex Football Club's first six matches of the season were:

756, 755, 764, 778, 754, 759

a) Find the mean (\( \bar{x} \)) of these attendance figures.

b) Calculate the sum of the squares, \( \sum x^2 \).

c) Use your answers to find the variance and standard deviation.

The number of TVs (\( x \)) in the households of 20 students are shown in the table.

| \( x \) | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency, \( f \) | 7 | 8 | 4 | 1 |

a) Find the mean number of TVs.

b) By adding rows showing \( x^2 \) and \( fx^2 \) to the table, find \( \sum fx^2 \).

c) Calculate the variance and standard deviation.

A data set is summarised as follows: \( n = 10 \), \( \sum x = 29 \) and \( \sum x^2 = 95.03 \).

a) Find the standard deviation for this data.

b) The lowest value in the data set is 0.35. Use the fence \( \bar{x} - 3 \) standard deviations to determine whether or not this value is an outlier.

The heights of sunflowers (\( h \), in cm) in a garden are recorded in the table.

| Height (cm) | \( 150 \leq h < 170 \) | \( 170 \leq h < 190 \) | \( 190 \leq h < 210 \) | \( 210 \leq h < 230 \) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 5 | 10 | 12 | 3 |

Estimate the variance and standard deviation of the heights.

Find the sample standard deviation of the following data:

15, 33, 31, 24, 30, 28, 14, 19, 22, 18, 39, 27

Find the mean and standard deviation of:

1 862 020, 1 862 040, 1 862 010 and 1 862 050

by using a suitable coding.

A set of data values (\( x \)) are coded using \( y = \frac{x - 20\,000}{15} \).

The mean of the coded data (\( \bar{y} \)) is 12.4, and the standard deviation of the coded data is 1.34.

Find the mean and standard deviation of the original data set.

The widths (in cm) of 10 sunflower seeds in a packet are:

0.61, 0.67, 0.63, 0.66, 0.65, 0.64, 0.68, 0.64, 0.62

Wait — that's only 9. The 10th seed is 0.62 cm.

a) Code the data to form a set of integer values (\( y \)) between 1 and 10.

b) Find the mean and standard deviation of the original values (\( x \)).

The table shows the weight (\( x \), in g) of 12 items on a production line.

| Weight (g) | 100–104 | 105–109 | 110–114 | 115–119 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 2 | 6 | 3 | 1 |

Use the coding \( y = x - 102 \) to estimate the mean and standard deviation of the items' weights.

Twenty pieces of data (\( x \)) have been summarised as follows:

\( \sum(x + 2) = 7 \) and \( \sum(x + 2)^2 = 80 \)

Calculate the mean and standard deviation of the data.

The table summarises the marks obtained by a group of students in Maths "Calculator" and "Non-calculator" papers.

| | Calculator paper | Non-calculator paper |
|---|---|---|
| Median, Q₂ | 58 | 42 |
| Interquartile range | 30 | 21 |
| Mean | 55 | 46 |
| Standard deviation | 21.2 | 17.8 |

Compare the location and dispersion of the distributions.

Two box plots show the masses (in g) of tomatoes in two harvests.

Harvest 1: Min = 15, Q₁ = 35, Median = 50, Q₃ = 65, Max = 90.
Harvest 2: Min = 25, Q₁ = 40, Median = 45, Q₃ = 55, Max = 70.

Compare the distributions of the two harvests.

Su and Ellen are collecting data on the durations of eruptions of a volcano. Between them, they have recorded the duration of the last 60 eruptions.

  Su has timed 23 eruptions, with average duration 3.42 minutes and s.d. 1.07 minutes.
  Ellen has timed 37 eruptions, with average duration 3.92 minutes and s.d. 0.97 minutes.

a) Calculate the combined mean duration of all the observed eruptions.

b) Find the variance and standard deviation of the combined set of 60 eruptions.

The noon temperatures (in °C) on 7 consecutive days were:

\( 14,; 17,; 12,; 19,; 15,; 21,; 16 \)

Find the range.

The heights (in cm) of 11 plants are:

\( 7,; 12,; 8,; 15,; 10,; 9,; 14,; 11,; 13,; 16,; 6 \)

Find the interquartile range.

The test marks of 12 students are:

\( 22,; 31,; 18,; 27,; 35,; 24,; 29,; 33,; 20,; 28,; 26,; 32 \)

Find Q₁, Q₂ (the median) and Q₃.

For a set of data, Q₁ = 14.3 and Q₃ = 27.6.

a) State the IQR.

b) Find the semi-interquartile range.

A teacher says: "The range is a better measure of spread than the interquartile range because it uses every value."

Explain whether you agree. Support your answer with a reason.
Using the same data as Q36, find the 20-to-80 interpercentile range.

The cumulative frequency table shows the times (in minutes) taken by 80 competitors in a race.

| Time ≤ (min) | 40 | 45 | 50 | 55 | 60 | 65 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cumulative frequency | 4 | 18 | 45 | 66 | 76 | 80 |

Estimate the median.
Using the cumulative frequency table from Q38, estimate Q₁.
Using the cumulative frequency table from Q38, estimate the 95th percentile.

A dataset has Q₁ = 18 and Q₃ = 34.

An outlier is defined as more than \(1.5 \times \text{IQR}\) above Q₃ or below Q₁.

Determine whether the value 60 is an outlier.

A set of data has mean 52 and standard deviation 6.

Using the rule that a value is an outlier if it is more than 2 standard deviations from the mean, determine whether 65 is an outlier.

The following summary statistics describe a dataset: min = 12, Q₁ = 19, Q₂ = 25, Q₃ = 30, max = 42.

Describe the five-number summary you would use to draw a box plot.

A box plot shows the following values: min = 3, Q₁ = 7, Q₂ = 11, Q₃ = 14, max = 25.

a) State the IQR.

b) Comment on the skewness of the distribution.

Two box plots compare pulse rates (beats per minute) for students before and after exercise.

**Before exercise:** min = 60, Q₁ = 66, Q₂ = 70, Q₃ = 74, max = 80.

**After exercise:** min = 82, Q₁ = 90, Q₂ = 96, Q₃ = 104, max = 120.

Make two comparisons between the distributions.

The ages (in years) of 5 children are:

\( 4,; 6,; 7,; 9,; 14 \)

Calculate the standard deviation.

Eight values of \(x\) have \(\sum x = 64\) and \(\sum x^2 = 600\).

Calculate the variance.

A set of 10 values has \(\sum x = 60\) and \(\sum x^2 = 430\).

Find the standard deviation.

Six numbers have mean 10 and standard deviation 2. A seventh number, 17, is added.

a) Find the new mean.

b) Find the new standard deviation. Give your answer to 3 s.f.

A data set contains five values: 3, 7, \(a\), 11, 14. The mean of the five values is 9.

a) Find \(a\).

b) Calculate the standard deviation.

The number of goals scored per match by a hockey team is shown.

| Goals (\(x\)) | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency (\(f\)) | 3 | 6 | 5 | 4 | 2 |

Calculate the variance.
Using the frequency table from Q51, find the standard deviation to 3 s.f.

The table shows the weekly shopping spend (in £) of 40 shoppers.

| Spend (\(x\)) | \(20 \leq x < 30\) | \(30 \leq x < 40\) | \(40 \leq x < 50\) | \(50 \leq x < 60\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 8 | 14 | 12 | 6 |

Estimate the standard deviation.

Summary statistics for grouped data: \(n = 25\), \(\sum fx = 325\), \(\sum fx^2 = 4625\).

Estimate the variance.
For the sample 4, 6, 9, 12, 14, calculate the sample standard deviation \(s\) using \(s^2 = \dfrac{\sum (x - \bar{x})^2}{n-1}\).

A dataset \(x\) has mean 57 and standard deviation 4. Let \(y = x - 50\).

State the mean and standard deviation of \(y\).

A dataset \(x\) has mean 205 and standard deviation 15. Let \(y = \dfrac{x - 200}{5}\).

State the mean and standard deviation of \(y\).

The coded data \(y = \dfrac{x - 100}{10}\) has mean \(\bar{y} = 2.4\) and standard deviation \(\sigma_y = 1.5\).

Find the mean and standard deviation of the original data \(x\).

The times taken by 30 students to solve a puzzle are summarised by:

Class A: mean 18 min, SD 3.2 min.

Class B: mean 22 min, SD 5.1 min.

Compare the distributions of times.

Two datasets have the following summary statistics:

| | Dataset A | Dataset B |
|---|---|---|
| Median | 42 | 45 |
| IQR | 9 | 16 |
| Minimum | 28 | 20 |
| Maximum | 60 | 72 |

a) Make two comparisons between the datasets.

b) Explain why the median and IQR are preferred to the mean and SD when comparing distributions that may contain outliers.

s5.questionText:
The table shows the ages (years) and heights (cm) of 8 saplings in a garden centre.

| Age (years) | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Height (cm) | 15 | 28 | 40 | 55 | 63 | 80 | 90 | 105 |

a) Plot a scatter diagram for this data.

b) Describe the correlation shown.

c) Interpret the correlation in context.

A car dealership records the age (years) and value (£1000s) of 8 second-hand cars.

| Age (years) | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 7 | 8 | 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Value (£1000s) | 18 | 15 | 13 | 11 | 9.5 | 6 | 4.5 | 2 |

a) Plot a scatter diagram for this data.

b) Describe the type and strength of the correlation.

c) Interpret your answer to part (b) in context.

A teacher records the shoe sizes and maths test scores of 10 students.

| Shoe size | 5 | 7 | 4 | 9 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 3 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Test score | 64 | 58 | 71 | 45 | 80 | 52 | 60 | 73 | 55 | 68 |

a) Plot a scatter diagram for this data.

b) Describe the correlation.

c) Comment on whether there is likely to be a causal relationship between shoe size and test score.

8 runners participating in a 1 km race were asked how many hours of exercise they do per week. Their responses and their race times in minutes are shown below.

| Exercise (hours) | 17 | 15 | 5 | 12 | 2 | 2 | 10 | 7.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Race time (min) | 6.7 | 6.8 | 9.5 | 6.1 | 11.5 | 6.3 | 8 | 9.9 |

a) Plot a scatter diagram to show this data.

b) Describe any correlation shown, and identify any results that appear to be outliers.

For each of the following pairs of scatter diagrams descriptions, state whether the correlation is positive, negative, or zero, and whether it is strong or weak.

a) As temperature increases, the number of cold drinks sold increases. The points lie very close to a straight line.

b) As the distance from a city centre increases, house prices decrease. The points are loosely scattered around a downward trend.

c) The amount of rainfall in a month and the number of letters in a person's surname show no pattern when plotted.

Zoe lives near a beach. She records the number of seagulls and the number of people flying kites she sees each day, over the course of one month. She finds negative correlation in the data, and concludes that seagulls must be scared off by kites.

Explain whether the data supports this conclusion.

For each pair of variables, state which is the explanatory variable and which is the response variable.

a) Time spent practising the piano in a week, and the number of mistakes made in a test at the end of the week.

b) Age of a second-hand car, and value of the car.

c) Number of phone calls made in a town in a week, and population of the town.

d) Growth rate of a plant in an experiment, and amount of sunlight falling on the plant.

A scientist is investigating the relationship between the amount of fertiliser (\( x \) grams) applied to a tomato plant and the eventual yield (\( y \) kg). She collects data from 10 plants.

a) Which variable is the explanatory variable? Explain your answer.

b) Which variable is the response variable?

c) The scientist calculates the regression line of \( y \) on \( x \) to be \( y = 1.2 + 0.03x \). Interpret the values of 1.2 and 0.03 in context.

A company is collecting data on the fuel efficiency of a type of lorry. They compare the load on the lorry, \( x \) (in tonnes), with the fuel efficiency, \( y \) (in km per litre), and calculate the regression line of \( y \) on \( x \) to be:

\( y = 12.5 - 0.8x \)

a) Interpret the value of 12.5 in this context.

b) Interpret the value of −0.8 in this context.

c) Predict the fuel efficiency when the lorry carries a load of 5 tonnes.

The equation of the regression line of \( y \) on \( x \) is \( y = 1.67 + 0.107x \).

a) Which variable is the response variable?

b) Find the predicted value of \( y \) corresponding to:
  (i) \( x = 5 \)
  (ii) \( x = 20 \)

A researcher measures the latitude (\( x \) degrees north) of 12 UK towns and the average number of days per year when the temperature exceeds 25°C (\( y \) days). She calculates the regression line:

\( y = 98.4 - 1.6x \)

a) State the explanatory variable and the response variable.

b) Interpret the value of −1.6 in context.

c) The latitudes of the towns in the data ranged from 50° to 57°. Predict the number of hot days for a town at latitude 53°. Comment on the reliability of your answer.

The table shows the average length (\( x \) cm) and average circumference (\( y \) cm) of eggs from several species of bird.

| Length \( x \) | 5.9 | 2.1 | 3.4 | 5.1 | 8.9 | 6.6 | 7.2 | 4.5 | 6.8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Circumference \( y \) | 19.6 | 6.3 | 7.1 | 9.9 | 3.5 | 21 | 18.7 | 8.3 | 18.4 |

a) Plot a scatter diagram to show this data.

b) Describe any trends in the data.

c) One of the measurements was recorded incorrectly. Use your scatter diagram to determine which.

The length of a spring (\( y \), in cm) when loaded with different masses (\( m \), in grams) has the regression line of \( y \) on \( m \):

\( y = 7.8 + 0.01043m \)

The smallest value of \( m \) used was 200 g and the largest was 500 g.

a) Estimate the length of the spring when loaded with a mass of:
  (i) 370 g
  (ii) 670 g

b) Comment on the reliability of the estimates in part (a).

A volunteer counted the number of spots (\( s \)) on an area of skin after \( d \) days of acne treatment, where \( d \) had values 2, 6, 10, 14, 18 and 22. The equation of the regression line of \( s \) on \( d \) is:

\( s = 58.8 - 2.47d \)

a) Estimate the number of spots the volunteer had on day 7. Comment on the reliability of your answer.

b) She forgot to count how many spots she had before starting to use the product (day 0). Estimate this number. Comment on your answer.

c) The volunteer claims that the regression equation must be wrong, because it predicts that after 30 days she should have a negative number of spots. Comment on this claim.

A student investigates the relationship between the number of hours of revision (\( x \)) and the percentage score (\( y \)) in a mock exam. She collects data from 12 classmates, with \( x \) ranging from 3 to 15 hours.

The regression line of \( y \) on \( x \) is \( y = 32 + 3.8x \).

a) Predict the score for a student who revises for 10 hours.

b) Predict the score for a student who revises for 25 hours.

c) Comment on the reliability of each prediction, giving a reason.

A farmer records the amount of rainfall \( x \) (mm) and the yield \( y \) (tonnes) from his wheat field over 8 years. He finds the regression line of \( y \) on \( x \) is:

\( y = 0.5 + 0.012x \)

The rainfall values in his data ranged from 400 mm to 900 mm.

a) Predict the yield when rainfall is 600 mm.

b) Predict the yield when rainfall is 1500 mm.

c) State, with a reason, which prediction is more reliable.

d) Give one reason why rainfall alone may not be a good predictor of yield.

The heights (\( h \) cm) and weights (\( w \) kg) of 15 adults were recorded. The data gave:

\( \bar{h} = 170 \), \( \bar{w} = 72 \)

The regression line of \( w \) on \( h \) passes through \( (\bar{h}, \bar{w}) \).

The equation of the regression line is \( w = -58 + 0.765h \).

a) Verify that the point \( (\bar{h}, \bar{w}) \) lies on the regression line.

b) Predict the weight of an adult who is 175 cm tall.

c) Would it be appropriate to use this regression line to predict the weight of a child who is 100 cm tall? Explain your answer.

A physics student records the temperature \( T \) (°C) of a cooling cup of coffee at various times \( t \) (minutes) after it was poured. She finds the regression line of \( T \) on \( t \):

\( T = 85 - 1.4t \)

The data was collected for values of \( t \) from 0 to 30 minutes.

a) State what the value 85 represents in context.

b) Predict the temperature after 20 minutes.

c) Use the equation to predict the temperature after 70 minutes. Comment on why this prediction is problematic.

The data below shows the number of hours of sunshine (\( x \)) and the number of visitors (\( y \), in hundreds) to a seaside town on 7 days.

| \( x \) | 2 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 9 | 10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \( y \) | 3 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8.5 | 11 | 12 |

a) Calculate \( \bar{x} \) and \( \bar{y} \).

b) The regression line of \( y \) on \( x \) is \( y = 0.50 + 1.16x \). Verify that this line passes through \( (\bar{x}, \bar{y}) \).

c) Use the regression line to estimate the number of visitors on a day with 8 hours of sunshine.

A estate agent collects data on the floor area (\( x \) m²) and selling price (\( y \) £1000s) of 10 houses in a village. The data gives:

\( \sum x = 850 \), \( \sum y = 2750 \), \( \bar{x} = 85 \), \( \bar{y} = 275 \)

The regression line of \( y \) on \( x \) is \( y = -12.5 + 3.38x \).

a) Use the regression line to predict the selling price of a house with a floor area of 100 m².

b) The houses in the data had floor areas ranging from 55 m² to 120 m². State whether your prediction in (a) is an interpolation or an extrapolation.

c) A homeowner with a 70 m² house wants to build a 20 m² extension. Use the model to estimate how much this might increase the value of the house.

A gym records the number of months \( x \) a member has been attending and their resting heart rate \( y \) (bpm). For 10 members:

\( \bar{x} = 8 \), \( \bar{y} = 68 \)

The regression line of \( y \) on \( x \) is \( y = 76 - x \).

a) Verify that the regression line passes through the mean point.

b) Interpret the gradient of −1 in context.

c) A new member joins. Use the model to estimate their resting heart rate at the start (\( x = 0 \)).

d) Explain why using this model for \( x = 80 \) would be inappropriate.

The number of ice creams sold (\( y \)) by a café and the daily maximum temperature (\( x \) °C) are recorded over 12 summer days. The regression line of \( y \) on \( x \) is:

\( y = -35 + 4.2x \)

The temperatures in the data ranged from 18°C to 32°C.

a) Predict how many ice creams are sold on a day when the maximum temperature is 25°C.

b) Explain why the model should not be used when \( x = 5 \).

c) A rival café owner claims: "Heating up the pavement outside would increase ice cream sales." Using the concept of correlation and causation, comment on this claim.

A teacher records the average number of hours of sleep per night (\( x \)) and the percentage attendance (\( y \)) of 10 sixth-form students over a half-term.

She finds \( \bar{x} = 7.5 \) and \( \bar{y} = 88 \), and the regression line:

\( y = 40 + 6.4x \)

a) Verify the regression line passes through the mean point.

b) Interpret the value 6.4 in context.

c) One student sleeps for an average of 5 hours per night. Estimate their attendance percentage.

d) Can the teacher conclude that making students sleep more would improve attendance? Explain your answer.
Explain, using an example, the difference between interpolation and extrapolation. State which is generally more reliable and why.

A concert venue collects data on the number of tickets sold for an event, \( y \), and the amount they spend on advertising for the event, £\( x \). They calculate that the regression curve of \( y \) on \( x \) is:

\( y = 0.002x^2 + 55 \)

a) The venue has budgeted to spend £500 on advertising for a particular event. How many tickets do they expect to sell?

b) The venue has 1500 seats. One of the staff members claims that, if they want to sell out the event, they should spend £850 on advertising. Comment on the validity of this claim.

A scatter diagram of a bivariate data set (\( x \), \( y \)) shows points that follow a curve rather than a straight line — they rise, reach a peak, and then fall.

a) Explain why a linear regression model would not be appropriate for this data.

b) Suggest what type of function might be a better model.

c) State one limitation of using any regression model to make predictions.

A bivariate data set (\( s \), \( t \)) is summarised as follows:

Number of data pairs: 5, range of \( s \): 1.6 to 7.9.

The regression curve of \( t \) on \( s \) is: \( t = 2e^{0.3s} \).

a) Predict the value of \( t \) when \( s = 2 \).

b) Comment on the validity of this estimate.

c) Predict the value of \( t \) when \( s = 12 \). Comment on the validity of this estimate.

The scatter diagram below shows a bivariate data set (\( x \), \( y \)). The points rise steeply at first, then level off, forming a curve that looks like a logarithmic shape.

Which of the following types of function would be the most appropriate as a best-fit model for this data?

  linear \qquad quadratic \qquad cubic \qquad exponential \qquad logarithmic

Explain your choice.

A health researcher investigates the link between daily sugar intake \( x \) (grams) and BMI \( y \) for 15 adults. She finds strong positive correlation and the regression line:

\( y = 18.5 + 0.08x \)

The sugar intakes in the data ranged from 20 g to 120 g.

a) Interpret the value 18.5 in context.

b) Interpret the value 0.08 in context.

c) Predict the BMI for a person with a sugar intake of 80 g.

d) Predict the BMI for a person with a sugar intake of 200 g. Comment on the reliability.

e) A newspaper writes the headline: "Sugar causes obesity." Using your knowledge of statistics, comment on this headline.

The scatter diagram below shows the relationship between engine size \( x \) (litres) and CO₂ emissions \( y \) (g/km) for 12 cars.

The data shows strong positive correlation. The regression line of \( y \) on \( x \) is:

\( y = 65 + 48x \)

Engine sizes in the data ranged from 1.0 to 3.5 litres.

a) Draw the regression line on the scatter diagram by plotting two points.

b) Use the line to predict the CO₂ emissions for a car with a 2.0 litre engine.

c) A car manufacturer produces a new electric car with an engine equivalent of 0 litres. Explain why using this regression line to predict the emissions would be inappropriate.

d) Another study shows that diesel cars have a different regression line from petrol cars. Suggest how the researcher could improve the model.

t1.questionText: In triangle \( ABC \), \( A = 55^\circ \), \( B = 72^\circ \) and \( a = 18 \) cm. Find the length \( b \) to 3 significant figures.
In triangle \( PQR \), \( P = 48^\circ \), \( Q = 65^\circ \) and \( PQ = 22 \) cm. Find the length \( PR \) to 3 s.f.
In triangle \( ABC \), \( A = 35^\circ \), \( C = 80^\circ \) and \( c = 30 \) m. Find the length \( a \) to 3 s.f.
In triangle \( DEF \), \( D = 47^\circ \), \( E = 58^\circ \) and \( DE = 9.5 \) cm. Find the length \( EF \) to 3 s.f.
In triangle \( GHI \), \( G = 62^\circ \), \( H = 44^\circ \) and \( GH = 14 \) cm. Find the length \( GI \) to 3 s.f.
In triangle \( ABC \), \( A = 50^\circ \), \( B = 60^\circ \) and \( AB = 20 \) cm. Find all remaining sides and angles.
In triangle \( JKL \), \( JL = 32 \) cm, \( KL = 25 \) cm and \( L = 54^\circ \). Find the length \( JK \) to 3 s.f.
In triangle \( MNP \), \( MN = 11 \) cm, \( NP = 15 \) cm and \( N = 38^\circ \). Find the length \( MP \) to 3 s.f.
In triangle \( RST \), \( RS = 7 \) cm, \( ST = 10 \) cm and \( S = 120^\circ \). Find the length \( RT \) to 3 s.f.
In triangle \( UVW \), \( UV = 8.4 \) cm, \( VW = 12.6 \) cm and \( V = 95^\circ \). Find the length \( UW \) to 3 s.f.

Two ships leave port \( P \) at the same time. Ship A sails 18 km on a bearing of \( 060^\circ \) and Ship B sails 24 km on a bearing of \( 130^\circ \). Find the distance between the two ships to 3 s.f.
A triangular field has sides of length \( 45 \) m, \( 60 \) m and \( 78 \) m. Find the largest angle of the field to 3 s.f.
In triangle \( ABC \), \( AB = 9 \) cm, \( BC = 11 \) cm and \( AC = 14 \) cm. Find the size of angle \( B \) to 3 s.f.
In triangle \( DEF \), \( DE = 7 \) cm, \( EF = 9 \) cm and \( DF = 13 \) cm. Find the smallest angle to 1 d.p.
In triangle \( PQR \), \( PQ = 5 \) cm, \( QR = 8 \) cm and \( PR = 11 \) cm. Find all three angles, giving your answers to 1 d.p.
In triangle \( XYZ \), \( XY = 6.3 \) cm, \( YZ = 8.1 \) cm and \( XZ = 5.7 \) cm. Find angle \( Y \) to 1 d.p.
The vertices of triangle \( ABC \) have coordinates \( A(0, 0) \), \( B(6, 0) \) and \( C(2, 5) \). Find the angle \( ABC \) to 1 d.p.
In triangle \( ABC \), \( a = 12 \) cm, \( b = 16 \) cm and \( A = 46^\circ \). Find the size of angle \( B \) to 1 d.p.
In triangle \( LMN \), \( LM = 20 \) cm, \( MN = 15 \) cm and \( L = 40^\circ \). Find angle \( N \) to 1 d.p.
In triangle \( PQR \), \( PR = 18 \) m, \( QR = 22 \) m and \( P = 55^\circ \). Find angle \( Q \), showing all working including a check for the ambiguous case.
Find the area of triangle \( ABC \) where \( AB = 9 \) cm, \( AC = 13 \) cm and \( A = 48^\circ \). Give your answer to 3 s.f.
Find the area of triangle \( PQR \) in which \( PQ = 7.2 \) cm, \( PR = 5.8 \) cm and \( P = 110^\circ \). Give your answer to 3 s.f.
The area of triangle \( ABC \) is \( 54 \) cm². If \( AB = 12 \) cm and \( BC = 15 \) cm, find the angle \( B \), giving any possible answers to 1 d.p.
Find the area of the triangle with sides 10 cm, 12 cm and 16 cm to 3 s.f.

Triangle \( RST \) has \( R = 53^\circ \), \( S = 74^\circ \) and \( RS = 11 \) cm.

a) Find the length \( RT \).

b) Find the area of the triangle.

Give all answers to 3 s.f.
A triangular garden has two sides of 8 m and 11 m, and the angle between them is \( 63^\circ \). Find the area of the garden and the length of the third side, each to 3 s.f.

A coastguard station \( C \) observes two boats \( A \) and \( B \). Boat \( A \) is 6.4 km from \( C \) and Boat \( B \) is 9.1 km from \( C \). The angle \( ACB = 74^\circ \). Find the distance \( AB \) to 3 s.f.

Two walkers set off from the same point. Walker A walks 5 km on a bearing of \( 040^\circ \) and Walker B walks 7 km on a bearing of \( 160^\circ \). Find:

a) The distance between the walkers to 3 s.f.

b) The bearing of Walker B from Walker A to 1 d.p.

A ladder 6 m long leans against a vertical wall. The foot of the ladder is on horizontal ground. The wall leans outward at \( 95^\circ \) to the ground (slightly past vertical). The ladder makes an angle of \( 70^\circ \) with the ground. Find how far up the wall the ladder reaches, to 3 s.f.

Points \( A \) and \( B \) are on opposite banks of a river. A surveyor at point \( C \) (on the same bank as \( A \)) measures \( AC = 80 \) m, \( \angle BAC = 68^\circ \) and \( \angle BCA = 54^\circ \).

a) Find the distance \( BC \) to 3 s.f.

b) Find the width of the river (perpendicular distance from \( B \) to line \( AC \)) to 3 s.f.

A quadrilateral \( ABCD \) is divided by diagonal \( AC \) into two triangles. In triangle \( ABC \): \( AB = 15 \) cm, \( BC = 12 \) cm, \( B = 70^\circ \). In triangle \( ACD \): \( CD = 10 \) cm, \( D = 55^\circ \). Find the total area of the quadrilateral to 3 s.f.

In triangle \( ABC \), \( AB = 10 \) cm, \( BC = 14 \) cm and \( AC = 9 \) cm.

a) Find angle \( A \) to 1 d.p.

b) Find the area of triangle \( ABC \) to 3 s.f.

From a point \( A \) on horizontal ground, the angle of elevation of the top \( T \) of a tower is \( 28^\circ \). From a point \( B \), 40 m closer to the tower on the same line, the angle of elevation is \( 43^\circ \). Find the height of the tower to 3 s.f.

A farmer has a field in the shape of a quadrilateral \( PQRS \). A fence runs along diagonal \( PR \).

In triangle \( PQR \): \( PQ = 80 \) m, \( QR = 95 \) m and \( Q = 58^\circ \).

In triangle \( PRS \): \( PS = 110 \) m, \( RS = 75 \) m.

a) Find the length of the fence \( PR \) to 3 s.f.

b) Find the total area of the field to 3 s.f.

In triangle \( ABC \), \( AB = c \), \( BC = a \) and \( CA = b \), with \( a = 2b \).

a) Show that \( \cos A = \dfrac{b^2 + c^2 - 4b^2}{2bc} \) simplifies to \( \cos A = \dfrac{c^2 - 3b^2}{2bc} \).

b) In the specific case where \( b = 5 \) cm, \( c = 7 \) cm, find angle \( A \) to 1 d.p.

c) Find the area of the triangle to 3 s.f.
In triangle \( ABC \), \( A = 40^\circ \), \( B = 75^\circ \) and \( a = 10 \) cm. Find \( b \) to 3 s.f.
In triangle \( PQR \), \( PQ = 8 \) cm, \( QR = 11 \) cm and \( Q = 52^\circ \). Find \( PR \) to 3 s.f.
In triangle \( ABC \), \( a = 7 \), \( b = 9 \), \( c = 12 \). Find angle \( C \) to 1 d.p.
Find the area of triangle \( ABC \) where \( a = 14 \) cm, \( b = 10 \) cm and \( C = 65^\circ \).
In triangle \( XYZ \), \( X = 35^\circ \), \( Y = 80^\circ \) and \( XY = 16 \) cm. Find \( YZ \) to 3 s.f.
Two sides of a triangle are 15 cm and 20 cm. The angle between them is \( 110^\circ \). Find the third side to 3 s.f.
In triangle \( ABC \), \( a = 8 \), \( b = 6 \), \( A = 50^\circ \). Find angle \( B \) to 1 d.p.
A ship sails 12 km on a bearing of \( 050^\circ \), then 8 km on a bearing of \( 120^\circ \). Find the distance from the starting point to 3 s.f.
Find the area of a triangle with sides 8 cm, 10 cm and 14 cm.
In triangle \( ABC \), \( AB = 5 \), \( BC = 7 \), \( B = 60^\circ \). Find \( AC \) exactly.
The area of triangle \( PQR \) is 30 cm\(^2\). \( PQ = 8 \) cm, \( QR = 10 \) cm. Find the two possible values of angle \( Q \).
In triangle \( ABC \), \( A = 30^\circ \), \( a = 6 \), \( b = 10 \). Show there are two possible triangles and find both values of \( B \).
From point \( A \), a tower is on a bearing of \( 060^\circ \) at a distance of 500 m. From point \( B \), 300 m due east of \( A \), find the bearing of the tower from \( B \).
In triangle \( ABC \), \( a = 5 \), \( b = 5 \), \( C = 72^\circ \). Find \( c \) to 3 s.f.
In triangle \( ABC \), \( A = 42^\circ \), \( B = 63^\circ \), \( c = 25 \) cm. Find the perimeter to 3 s.f.
A parallelogram has sides 12 cm and 8 cm. One diagonal is 15 cm. Find the acute angle of the parallelogram.
In triangle \( ABC \), \( AB = 20 \) cm, \( AC = 15 \) cm and \( A = 40^\circ \). Find: (a) \( BC \); (b) the area; (c) angle \( B \).
In triangle \( ABC \), \( a = 3 \), \( b = 4 \), \( c = 5 \). Verify it is right-angled and find all angles.
A field is in the shape of a triangle with sides 120 m, 90 m and 80 m. Find its area in hectares (1 hectare = 10000 m\(^2\)).
In triangle \( DEF \), \( D = 100^\circ \), \( E = 35^\circ \) and \( DE = 18 \) cm. Find the area of the triangle.

Two radar stations are 30 km apart. Station A detects a plane at a bearing of \( 040^\circ \) and station B (due east of A) detects it at \( 330^\circ \). Find the distance from station A to the plane.
In triangle \( ABC \), \( a = 6\sqrt{2} \), \( B = 45^\circ \), \( C = 60^\circ \). Find \( b \) exactly.
A surveyor measures a triangular plot: \( AB = 85 \) m, \( BC = 110 \) m, angle \( ABC = 72^\circ \). Find the perimeter and area.
In an equilateral triangle of side 10 cm, a point P is 6 cm from one vertex and 8 cm from another. Find the distance from P to the third vertex.
In triangle \( ABC \), \( AB = 13 \) cm, \( BC = 14 \) cm and \( AC = 15 \) cm. Find: (a) the largest angle; (b) the area; (c) the length of the shortest altitude.
Find the exact value of \( c \) in triangle \( ABC \) where \( a = 4 \), \( b = 6 \) and \( C = 120^\circ \).
In triangle \( ABC \), \( a = 10\text{ cm} \), \( b = 7\text{ cm} \), \( c = 8\text{ cm} \). Find the area of the triangle to 3 s.f.
In triangle \( ABC \), \( a = 5 \), \( A = 30^\circ \), \( B = 45^\circ \). Find the exact value of \( b \).
A regular hexagon has side length 6 cm. Find the length of the longest diagonal.
Two sides of a triangular garden plot measure 5 m and 8 m, meeting at an angle of \( 120^\circ \). Find the length of the third side to 3 s.f.
In triangle \( ABC \), \( AB = 9 \), \( BC = 12 \), \( B = 90^\circ \). Verify using the cosine rule that \( AC = 15 \).
A ship sails 20 km due north, then 15 km on a bearing of \( 070^\circ \). Find the distance and bearing from the starting point.

The \( \textit{circumradius} \) of a triangle is the radius of the unique circle (the \( \textit{circumscribed circle} \)) that passes through all three vertices. The extended sine rule states that for any triangle \( ABC \), \( \frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{c}{\sin C} = 2R \), where \( R \) is the circumradius. If \( a = 10 \) and \( A = 30^\circ \), find \( R \).
Triangle \( ABC \) has \( a = 8 \), \( b = 15 \), \( c = 17 \). Show it is right-angled and find the area.
In triangle \( ABC \), \( A = 50^\circ \), \( B = 70^\circ \), \( a = 12 \). Find: (a) all sides; (b) the area; (c) the shortest altitude.

t2.questionText: Given that \( \sin\theta = \dfrac{3}{5} \) and \( \theta \) is obtuse, find the exact values of \( \cos\theta \) and \( \tan\theta \).
Show that \( \sin^2 x\cos^2 y - \cos^2 x\sin^2 y \equiv \sin^2 x - \sin^2 y \).
Given that \( x \) is acute and \( \sin x = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \), find the exact value of \( \tan x \).
Show that \( (3\sin x + 4\cos x)^2 + (4\sin x - 3\cos x)^2 \equiv 25 \).

(a) Show that \( \sin^2 x - \cos^2 x \equiv 2\sin^2 x - 1 \). 

 

 (b) Hence, or otherwise, solve \( \sin^2 x - \cos^2 x = \dfrac{1}{2} \) for \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \).

(a) Show that \( 2\cos^2\theta + 3\sin\theta - 3 = 0 \) can be written as \( 2\sin^2\theta - 3\sin\theta + 1 = 0 \). 

 

 (b) Hence solve \( 2\cos^2\theta + 3\sin\theta - 3 = 0 \) for \( 0^\circ \leq \theta \leq 360^\circ \).
Express \( \tan x \) in terms of \( \sin x \) and \( \cos x \).
Prove that \( \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x} + \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x} = \dfrac{1}{\sin x \cos x} \).
Given \( \sin x = \dfrac{3}{5} \) and \( x \) is acute, find \( \cos x \) and \( \tan x \).
Prove that \( \cos^4 x - \sin^4 x = \cos^2 x - \sin^2 x \).
Prove that \( (\sin x + \cos x)^2 = 1 + 2\sin x \cos x \).
Given \( \tan x = \dfrac{5}{12} \) and \( x \) is acute, find \( \sin x \) and \( \cos x \).
Prove that \( \dfrac{\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x}{\sin x - \cos x} = \sin x + \cos x \).
Prove that \( \tan x + \dfrac{1}{\tan x} = \dfrac{1}{\sin x \cos x} \).
Simplify \( \dfrac{1 + \tan^2 x}{1 + \cot^2 x} \) where \( \cot x = \dfrac{1}{\tan x} \).
Prove that \( \dfrac{1 - \cos x}{\sin x} = \dfrac{\sin x}{1 + \cos x} \).
Prove that \( \dfrac{\cos x}{1 - \tan x} + \dfrac{\sin x}{1 - \cot x} = \sin x + \cos x \).

t3.questionText: State the period, amplitude, and the coordinates of the maximum point in the interval \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \) for the graph of \( y = \sin x \).
State the period, amplitude, and the coordinates where \( y = \cos x \) crosses the \( x \)-axis in the interval \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \).
State the period of \( y = \tan x \) and give the equations of the two asymptotes in the interval \( 0^\circ < x < 360^\circ \).
State the coordinates of the \( y \)-intercept and the minimum point of \( y = \cos x \) in the interval \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \).
State all the values of \( x \) in the interval \( -360^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \) where the graph of \( y = \sin x \) crosses the \( x \)-axis.
Describe the transformation that maps \( y = \sin x \) onto \( y = \sin x + 2 \). State the maximum and minimum values of \( y = \sin x + 2 \).
Describe the transformation that maps \( y = \cos x \) onto \( y = \cos x - 4 \). State the range of \( y = \cos x - 4 \).
On the same axes, sketch the graphs of \( y = \cos x \) and \( y = \cos x + 3 \) for \( -360^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \). Label the \( y \)-intercepts of both curves.
Describe the transformation that maps \( y = \sin x \) onto \( y = \sin(x - 30^\circ) \). State the new \( x \)-intercepts in the interval \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \).
Describe the transformation that maps \( y = \cos x \) onto \( y = \cos(x + 90^\circ) \). What is the \( y \)-intercept of \( y = \cos(x + 90^\circ) \)?

On the same axes, sketch \( y = -\sin x \) and \( y = \sin(-x) \) for \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \). State how the two graphs compare and explain why, by referring to the symmetry of \( y = \sin x \).

On the same axes, sketch \( y = \cos(-x) \) and \( y = -\cos x \) for \( -180^\circ \leq x \leq 180^\circ \). Use your sketches to verify graphically that \( \cos(-x) \equiv \cos x \) but \( -\cos x \not\equiv \cos x \).
Sketch \( y = \tan(-x) \) on \( -180^\circ \leq x \leq 180^\circ \), showing all asymptotes and \( x \)-intercepts. Explain how your sketch confirms that \( \tan(-x) \equiv -\tan x \).

The curve \( y = f(x) \) is \( y = \sin x \). Describe, in order, a sequence of transformations that maps \( y = f(x) \) onto \( y = \tfrac{1}{2}\sin(3x) + 2 \). State the range of the final curve and its period.
By sketching \( y = 2\sin x \) and \( y = 1 \) on the same axes, find all values of \( x \) in \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \) for which the two graphs intersect. Give exact answers.
Sketch the graph of \( y = 1 - 2\cos x \) for \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \). State the range of the function and find the exact \( x \)-coordinates where the curve crosses the \( x \)-axis.

State the locations of the first four vertical asymptotes of \( y = \tan(2x) \) in the interval \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \). Compare your answer to the asymptotes of \( y = \tan x \) on the same interval.

The curve \( y = a\cos(bx) + c \) has maximum value 4, minimum value \( -2 \), and period \( 120^\circ \). Given that \( a, b, c \) are positive, find their values and sketch the curve for \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \).

Sketch the graph of \( y = \sin\left(x + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) \) for \( 0 \leq x \leq 2\pi \) (radians). State the phase shift, the range, and the \( x \)-values at which the curve crosses the \( x \)-axis.
Find the range of \( y = 5 - 3\sin(2x) \) and determine the \( x \)-values in \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \) at which the maximum and minimum values are attained.
By sketching a suitable graph, find the number of solutions of the equation \( \sin x = 0.4 \) in the interval \( 0 \leq x \leq 4\pi \). State the solutions to 3 significant figures.

The depth of water in metres at a harbour entrance is modelled by \( d(t) = 5 + 3\cos\!\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{6}\right) \), where \( t \) is the number of hours after midnight. (a) State the maximum and minimum depth. (b) Find the time of the first low tide after midnight. (c) State the period of the tide.
A curve has equation \( y = \cos(3x + 60^\circ) \). (a) State its period. (b) Find the three smallest positive values of \( x \) for which \( y = 0 \).

A sinusoidal curve has amplitude 4 and minimum value 0. The curve passes through the points \( (0^\circ, 4) \) and \( (45^\circ, 8) \) and is rising at \( x = 0 \). Find an equation for the curve in the form \( y = a\sin(bx) + d \), giving the values of \( a \), \( b \) and \( d \).

A curve has equation \( y = a\cos\!\big(b(x - c)\big) + d \). Its maximum value is 7, its minimum value is \( -1 \), its period is \( 240^\circ \), and it attains its maximum at \( x = 30^\circ \). Find the values of \( a \), \( b \), \( c \), and \( d \) and sketch the curve on \( [0^\circ, 360^\circ] \).
Find the set of values of \( k \) for which the equation \( 2\cos x + 1 = k \) has exactly two solutions in the interval \( 0^\circ < x < 360^\circ \). Use a sketch to justify your answer.

A curve has equation \( y = \sin(bx) \) where \( b \) is a positive constant. The smallest positive value of \( x \) for which \( y = 0 \) is \( x = 60^\circ \). Find the value of \( b \) and state the period of the curve.
Sketch the graph of \( y = -2\sin(2x) + 1 \) on the interval \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \). State the period, amplitude, range, and find all four \( x \)-intercepts in this interval.

Sketch the graph of \( y = 2\tan(x + 30^\circ) \) on the interval \( -150^\circ \leq x \leq 150^\circ \). State the equations of the asymptotes in this interval and the coordinates of the \( x \)-intercept and the \( y \)-intercept.

A curve has equation \( y = a\cos(bx) + c \), where \( a > 0 \) and \( b > 0 \). Its maximum value is 5, its minimum value is \( -3 \), and its first minimum for \( x > 0 \) occurs at \( x = 90^\circ \). Find the values of \( a \), \( b \) and \( c \).

Starting with \( y = \cos x \), the following transformations are applied in this order:

(i) reflection in the \( x \)-axis,
(ii) horizontal stretch with scale factor 2,
(iii) translation by \( -1 \) in the \( y \)-direction.

Write down the equation of the resulting curve and sketch it on \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 720^\circ \), marking the coordinates of all maxima, minima and the \( y \)-intercept.

Show, by sketching \( y = \cos(x - 90^\circ) \) and \( y = \sin x \) on the same axes for \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \), that the two curves are identical.

Explain the result by describing how \( y = \cos x \) is transformed to give \( y = \cos(x - 90^\circ) \), and verify the identity at \( x = 30^\circ \) and \( x = 210^\circ \).

A sound wave is modelled by \( y = \sin(880\pi t) \), where \( t \) is time in seconds and \( y \) is the displacement (arbitrary units).

(a) State the period of the wave, in seconds.

(b) Hence find the frequency, in hertz (Hz).

(c) Sketch one complete cycle of the wave, starting from \( t = 0 \).

(a) Using the graph of \( y = \sin x \), state all values of \( x \) in \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 720^\circ \) at which the curve has a turning point, and classify each as a maximum or minimum.

(b) Repeat for \( y = -\cos\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}x\right) \) on the same interval.

Sketch \( y = \tan\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}x\right) \) for \( -360^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \).

State the equations of all asymptotes, the coordinates of all \( x \)-intercepts in the interval, and the period. Compare the period with that of \( y = \tan x \).

A curve has equation \( y = a\cos(bx) + c \), where \( a > 0 \) and \( b > 0 \). It has period \( 360^\circ \), and on \( [0^\circ, 360^\circ] \) its maximum value is \( 5 \) occurring at \( x = 0^\circ \), and its minimum value is \( -1 \) occurring at \( x = 180^\circ \).

Find \( a \), \( b \) and \( c \), and sketch the curve on \( [0^\circ, 360^\circ] \).

Sketch \( y = \cos(x + 120^\circ) \) for \( -180^\circ \leq x \leq 180^\circ \).

State the coordinates of the \( y \)-intercept, all \( x \)-intercepts, the maximum point and the minimum point in this interval.

Use the graph of \( y = \cos x \) for \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \) to explain graphically why \( \cos(360^\circ - x) = \cos x \) for all real \( x \).

Verify the identity by direct calculation at \( x = 60^\circ \) and \( x = 120^\circ \).

On the same axes, sketch \( y = \cos(360^\circ - x) \) to confirm that it lies exactly on top of \( y = \cos x \).

A curve has equation \( y = a\sin(bx) \), where \( a > 0 \) and \( b > 0 \). Its range is \( -3 \leq y \leq 3 \), and the distance between two consecutive \( x \)-intercepts is \( 60^\circ \).

Find \( a \) and \( b \) and sketch the curve for \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \).

The curve \( y = 2\cos(2x) + 1 \) is defined for \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \).

(a) State the range of the function.

(b) Show, by considering the equation, that the curve crosses the \( x \)-axis exactly four times in this interval, and find the exact values of those \( x \)-coordinates.

(c) Sketch the curve, indicating the \( x \)-intercepts and the \( y \)-intercept.

Sketch \( y = \sin x + 2 \) for \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \). State the range.

For what values of \( x \) in \( [0^\circ, 360^\circ] \) is \( \sin x > \cos x \)?
