Sketch \( y = \sin x \) and \( y = \sin 2x \) on the same axes for \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \). How many points of intersection are there?
State the range of \( y = 3 - 2\sin x \).
Find the period and asymptotes of \( y = \tan(x - 45^\circ) \) for \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \).
Sketch \( y = 3\sin(2x) \) for \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \). State the amplitude, the period, the range, and the coordinates of all \( x \)-intercepts in this interval.

Sketch \( y = \cos(x + 90^\circ) \) for \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \) and explain, using graph transformations, why this curve is identical to \( y = -\sin x \). Verify your result by checking the value at \( x = 0^\circ \) and \( x = 90^\circ \).
The graph of \( y = \sin x \) is stretched vertically by factor 4 and translated 2 units down. Write the equation.
For \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \), how many solutions does \( 2\sin 3x = 1 \) have?
Sketch \( y = 1 + \tan x \) for \( -90^\circ < x < 90^\circ \). State where it crosses the axes.
The graph of \( y = a\cos(bx) + c \) has maximum 5, minimum -1 and period \( 90^\circ \). Find \( a \), \( b \) and \( c \).
Sketch \( y = \sin x \) and \( y = \cos x \) on the same axes for \( 0^\circ \leq x \leq 360^\circ \). Find all values of \( x \) where \( \sin x = \cos x \).

v1.questionText:
In triangle \(PQR,\) \( \overrightarrow{PQ} = \mathbf{a} \) and \( \overrightarrow{PR} = \mathbf{b}.\) \(M\) is the midpoint of \(QR\) and the point \(N\) lies on \(PM\) such that \(PN:NM = 2:1.\)

a) Find \( \overrightarrow{PM} \) and \( \overrightarrow{PN} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{a} \) and \( \mathbf{b}.\)

b) Show that the points \(Q,\) \(N\) and the midpoint \(K\) of \(PR\) are collinear, and find the ratio \(QN:NK.\)

For the rectangle \(ABCD,\) \( \overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf{p} \) and \( \overrightarrow{AD} = \mathbf{q}.\) The point \(E\) lies on \(AB\) with \(AE:EB = 1:3\) and the point \(F\) lies on \(DC\) with \(DF:FC = 3:1.\)

a) Find \( \overrightarrow{AE},\) \( \overrightarrow{AF} \) and \( \overrightarrow{EF} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{p} \) and \( \mathbf{q}.\)

b) The diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect at \(X,\) and the line \(EF\) crosses \(AC\) at \(Y.\) Show that \(AY:YC = 1:1\) — i.e. \(Y\) is the centre \(X\) of the rectangle.

\(WXYZ\) is any quadrilateral with \( \overrightarrow{WX} = \mathbf{a},\) \( \overrightarrow{XY} = \mathbf{b} \) and \( \overrightarrow{YZ} = \mathbf{c}.\) Let \(P,\) \(Q,\) \(R,\) \(S\) be the midpoints of \(WX,\) \(XY,\) \(YZ\) and \(ZW\) respectively (Varignon's configuration).

a) Find \( \overrightarrow{WZ},\) and hence \( \overrightarrow{SZ} \) and \( \overrightarrow{SW},\) in terms of \( \mathbf{a},\mathbf{b},\mathbf{c}.\)

b) Show that \(PQRS\) is a parallelogram by proving \( \overrightarrow{PQ} = \overrightarrow{SR}.\)

In the triangle \(XYZ,\) the vector \( \mathbf{p} \) represents \( \overrightarrow{XZ} \) and the vector \( \mathbf{q} \) represents \( \overrightarrow{YX}.\) Express the following in terms of \( \mathbf{p} \) and \( \mathbf{q} :\)

a) \( \overrightarrow{XY} \)

b) \( \overrightarrow{YZ} \)

c) \( \overrightarrow{ZY} \)

\(ABCD\) is a parallelogram with \( \overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf{m} \) and \( \overrightarrow{BC} = \mathbf{n}.\) The diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect at \(M.\)

a) By writing \(M\) as both \( \overrightarrow{AM}=\lambda\overrightarrow{AC} \) and \( \overrightarrow{BM}=\mu\overrightarrow{BD} \) for scalars \( \lambda,\mu,\) find \( \lambda \) and \( \mu,\) and hence prove that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.

b) The point \(E\) lies on the side \(BC\) with \(BE:EC = 1:2,\) and the line \(AE\) is extended to meet the line \(DC\) at \(F.\) Find \( \overrightarrow{AF} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{m} \) and \( \mathbf{n}.\)

State whether each of the following is a scalar, a vector, or neither.

a) A car travelling north-east at 60 km/h.

b) The temperature of a room is 21°C.

c) An acceleration of 3 m/s² upwards.

d) A mass of 5 kg.

In triangle \(ABC,\) \(M\) is the midpoint of \(BC\) and \(N\) is the midpoint of \(AC.\) The medians \(AM\) and \(BN\) intersect at \(G.\) Take \( \overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf{a} \) and \( \overrightarrow{AC} = \mathbf{b}.\)

a) Find \( \overrightarrow{AM} \) and \( \overrightarrow{BN} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{a} \) and \( \mathbf{b}.\)

b) Writing \( \overrightarrow{AG}=\lambda\overrightarrow{AM} \) and \( \overrightarrow{BG}=\mu\overrightarrow{BN},\) find \( \lambda \) and \( \mu,\) and hence prove that the medians divide each other in the ratio \(2:1.\)

In triangle \(DEF,\) \(J\) is the midpoint of \(ED\) and \(L\) is the midpoint of \(FD.\) \( \overrightarrow{EF} = \mathbf{f} \) and \( \overrightarrow{ED} = \mathbf{d}.\) Prove that \( \overrightarrow{JL} = \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{f}.\)

The non-zero vectors \( \mathbf{a} \) and \( \mathbf{b} \) are non-parallel. Given that \( (3\lambda - 2)\mathbf{a} + (\mu + 1)\mathbf{b} \) is parallel to \( 4\mathbf{a} - 6\mathbf{b},\) and that
\[
\lambda + \mu = 7,
\]
find the values of \( \lambda \) and \( \mu.\)

Group the following into sets of parallel vectors:

\( 3\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b},\quad 6\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b},\quad 2\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b},\quad -4\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b},\quad -9\mathbf{a}-3\mathbf{b},\quad \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a} \)
\(ABCD\) is a parallelogram. \( \overrightarrow{BA} = \mathbf{n} \) and \( \overrightarrow{BD} = \mathbf{m}.\) Find \( \overrightarrow{BC} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{n} \) and \( \mathbf{m}.\)

\( \overrightarrow{XY} = \mathbf{a},\) \( \overrightarrow{XZ} = \mathbf{b}.\) \(P\) is the midpoint of \(YZ\) and \(Q\) is the midpoint of \(XY.\) Show that \( \overrightarrow{PQ} \) is parallel to \( \overrightarrow{XZ}.\)
Given that \( \overrightarrow{TU} = \mathbf{v} - \mathbf{w} \) and \( \overrightarrow{ST} = 2\mathbf{v} + \mathbf{w},\) show that \( \overrightarrow{US} \) is parallel to \( \mathbf{v}.\)

In the rectangle \(ABCD,\) \(E\) is the midpoint of \(AD\) and \(F\) divides \(DC\) in the ratio \(2:1.\) If \( \overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf{b} \) and \( \overrightarrow{AD} = \mathbf{d},\) find:

a) \( \overrightarrow{DF} \)

b) \( \overrightarrow{BE} \)

c) \( \overrightarrow{EF} \)

Given that \( \overrightarrow{XY} = 3\mathbf{a} - 4\mathbf{b} + 2\mathbf{c} \) and \( \overrightarrow{XZ} = \mathbf{a} - 2\mathbf{b} - 2\mathbf{c},\) show that \( \overrightarrow{YZ} \) is parallel to \( \mathbf{a} - \mathbf{b} + 2\mathbf{c}.\)
\( \overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{a},\) \( \overrightarrow{OB} = \mathbf{b},\) \( \overrightarrow{OC} = 3\mathbf{b} - 2\mathbf{a}.\) Show that \(A,\) \(B\) and \(C\) are collinear.
\( \overrightarrow{XY} = \mathbf{t} + \mathbf{u},\) \( \overrightarrow{AY} = -\mathbf{t},\) \( \overrightarrow{AZ} = \mathbf{u}.\) Show that \(X,\) \(Y\) and \(Z\) are collinear.
\( \overrightarrow{AP} = \mathbf{m},\) \( \overrightarrow{AQ} = \mathbf{m} + 2\mathbf{n},\) \( \overrightarrow{AR} = \mathbf{m} + 6\mathbf{n}.\) Show that \(P,\) \(Q\) and \(R\) are collinear.

\( \overrightarrow{PQ} = -(\mathbf{m}+\tfrac{9}{2}\mathbf{n}),\) \( \overrightarrow{PR} = \mathbf{m} - \tfrac{3}{2}\mathbf{n},\) \( \overrightarrow{PS} = 2\mathbf{m}.\) Show that \(Q,\) \(R\) and \(S\) are collinear.

\(ABCD\) is a quadrilateral. \(X\) is the midpoint of the line \(AC.\)
\( \overrightarrow{DA} = \mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b},\) \( \overrightarrow{AB} = 3\mathbf{a}-2\mathbf{b} \) and \( \overrightarrow{XC} = \mathbf{a}.\)
Is \(DXB\) a straight line? Give reasons for your answer.

On a map, a library \(L\) is at \((1, 4)\) and a park \(P\) is at \((5, 2).\) The town hall \(H\) is the point such that \( \overrightarrow{LH} = 2\overrightarrow{LP},\) and a cafe \(C\) lies on segment \(LP\) with \(LC:CP = 3:1.\)

a) Find the coordinates of \(H\) and \(C.\)

b) A new memorial \(M\) is to be placed so that \(LCHM\) forms a parallelogram (with vertices in that order). Find the coordinates of \(M,\) and find \( |\overrightarrow{LM}| \) in surd form.

The points \(A(2, 5)\) and \(B(6, 1)\) lie on a coordinate grid. A third point \( C(t+1,\ 2t-1) \) is variable as the parameter \( t \) changes.

a) Find \( \overrightarrow{AB} \) and \( \overrightarrow{AC} \) in \( \mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j} \) form.

b) Find the value of \( t \) for which \(A,\) \(B\) and \(C\) are collinear, and state the corresponding coordinates of \(C.\)

c) For that value of \( t,\) determine the ratio \(AC:CB\) and state whether \(C\) lies on the segment \(AB\) or on its extension.

Given that \( \mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix}3\\-1\end{pmatrix},\) \( \mathbf{b} = \begin{pmatrix}-2\\4\end{pmatrix},\) and \( \mathbf{c} = \begin{pmatrix}1\\-3\end{pmatrix},\) calculate:

a) \( \mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}+\mathbf{c} \)

b) \( \mathbf{c}-2\mathbf{b} \)

c) \( 3\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{b}+2\mathbf{c} \)

\(C\) has position vector \( -3\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j} \) and \(D\) has position vector \( 5\mathbf{i}-4\mathbf{j}.\)

a) What are the Cartesian coordinates of \(C\) and \(D?\)

b) Write the vectors \( \overrightarrow{CD} \) and \( \overrightarrow{DC} \) in \( \mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j} \) form.

Given that \( \mathbf{p} = \begin{pmatrix}-1\\-2\end{pmatrix},\) \( \mathbf{q} = \begin{pmatrix}3\\-2\end{pmatrix},\) and \( \mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix}-4\\5\end{pmatrix},\) show that \( \mathbf{p}+3\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{r} \) is parallel to \( 4\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j}.\)

In triangle \(OAB,\) \( \overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{a} \) and \( \overrightarrow{OB} = \mathbf{b}.\) \(M\) is the midpoint of \(AB\) and \(N\) is the midpoint of \(OB.\)

a) Find \( \overrightarrow{OM} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{a} \) and \( \mathbf{b}.\)

b) Find \( \overrightarrow{AN} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{a} \) and \( \mathbf{b}.\)

c) Show that \( \overrightarrow{MN} \) is parallel to \( \overrightarrow{OA}.\)

In the diagram, \( \overrightarrow{OB} = 4\mathbf{a},\) \( \overrightarrow{AB} = 2\mathbf{b},\) \( \overrightarrow{BD} = 4\mathbf{a} - \mathbf{b},\) and \( \overrightarrow{DC} = -\tfrac{5}{2}\mathbf{b} - \mathbf{a}.\) Show that \(OAC\) is a straight line.

In a trapezium \(OABC,\) \( \overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{a},\) \( \overrightarrow{OC} = \mathbf{c},\) and \( \overrightarrow{AB} = k\mathbf{c} \) where \(AB\) is parallel to \(OC.\) \(P\) is the midpoint of \(OA\) and \(Q\) is the midpoint of \(BC.\)

Show that \( \overrightarrow{PQ} = \tfrac{1}{2}(1+k)\mathbf{c}.\)

In triangle \(OAB,\) \( \overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf{a} \) and \( \overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf{b}.\) The point \(P\) divides \(OA\) in the ratio \(1:3\) and the point \(Q\) divides \(AB\) in the ratio \(1:1.\)

a) Find \( \overrightarrow{OP} \) and \( \overrightarrow{OQ}.\)

b) Show that \( \overrightarrow{PQ} = \tfrac{1}{4}\mathbf{a}+\tfrac{1}{2}\mathbf{b}.\)

\(OABC\) is a parallelogram. \( \overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{a} \) and \( \overrightarrow{OC} = \mathbf{c}.\) \(M\) is the midpoint of \(AB\) and \(N\) divides \(OC\) in the ratio \(2:1.\)

a) Express \( \overrightarrow{OM} \) and \( \overrightarrow{ON} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{a} \) and \( \mathbf{c}.\)

b) Show that \( \overrightarrow{NM} \) is parallel to \( 6\mathbf{a}-\mathbf{c}.\)

In triangle \(OAB,\) \( \overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{a} \) and \( \overrightarrow{OB} = \mathbf{b}.\) \(M\) is the midpoint of \(AB\) and the point \(P\) lies on \(OM\) extended such that \( \overrightarrow{OP} = \tfrac{3}{2}\overrightarrow{OM}.\) The line \(BP\) meets \(OA\) at \(Q.\)

a) Find \( \overrightarrow{OP} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{a} \) and \( \mathbf{b}.\)

b) Find \( \overrightarrow{OQ},\) and hence find the ratio \(OQ:QA.\)

\(PQRS\) is a parallelogram with \( \overrightarrow{PQ} = \mathbf{u} \) and \( \overrightarrow{PS} = \mathbf{v}.\) \(T\) is the point on side \(QR\) with \(QT:TR = 1:3\) and \(U\) is the point on side \(RS\) with \(RU:US = 2:1.\)

a) Find \( \overrightarrow{PT} \) and \( \overrightarrow{PU} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{u} \) and \( \mathbf{v}.\)

b) The line \(TU\) is extended to meet \(PQ\) extended at the point \(V.\) Find \( \overrightarrow{PV},\) and hence determine the ratio \(PQ:QV.\)
Write \( 3\begin{pmatrix}2\\-1\end{pmatrix} + 2\begin{pmatrix}-4\\5\end{pmatrix} \) as a single column vector.
The position vector of \(A\) is \( 5\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j} \) and the position vector of \(B\) is \( -\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j}.\) Find \( \overrightarrow{AB} \) as a column vector.

\( \mathbf{a} \) and \( \mathbf{b} \) are non-parallel non-zero vectors.

Given that the vector \( (\alpha+2)\mathbf{a} + (\beta-1)\mathbf{b} \) is equal to the vector \( 5\mathbf{a} - (\alpha\beta)\mathbf{b},\) and that the vector \( (\alpha-1)\mathbf{a} + 4\mathbf{b} \) is parallel to \( 3\mathbf{a} - 2\mathbf{b},\) find all possible pairs \( (\alpha, \beta).\)

\(ABCD\) is a rhombus with \( \overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf{p} \) and \( \overrightarrow{AD} = \mathbf{q}.\) The diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) intersect at the centre \(O.\) The point \(E\) lies on \(AC\) with \(AE:EC = 1:3.\)

a) Express \( \overrightarrow{AO},\) \( \overrightarrow{AE} \) and \( \overrightarrow{BE} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{p} \) and \( \mathbf{q}.\)

b) The line \(BE\) is extended to meet \(AD\) (extended if necessary) at \(F.\) By writing \( \overrightarrow{AF}=s\mathbf{q} \) and \( \overrightarrow{BF}=t\overrightarrow{BE},\) find \( s \) and \( t.\)

In triangle \(ABC,\) \(M\) is the midpoint of \(AB\) and \(N\) is the midpoint of \(AC.\) \( \overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf{b} \) and \( \overrightarrow{AC} = \mathbf{c}.\) Show that \( \overrightarrow{MN} = \tfrac{1}{2}\overrightarrow{BC}.\)
Given \( \overrightarrow{OA} = 3\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} \) and \( \overrightarrow{OB} = -\mathbf{i} + 7\mathbf{j},\) find the position vector of the point that divides \(AB\) in the ratio \(1:3.\)
Write \( 4\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j} \) as a column vector, and \( \begin{pmatrix}7\\2\end{pmatrix} \) in \( \mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j} \) form.

In triangle \(OAB,\) \( \overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{a},\) \( \overrightarrow{OB} = \mathbf{b}.\) The point \(P\) divides \(OA\) in the ratio \(2:1\) and \(Q\) divides \(OB\) in the ratio \(2:1.\) Show that \(PQ\) is parallel to \(AB.\)

In the trapezium \(ABCD,\) \(AB\) is parallel to \(DC\) and \(DC = 2AB.\) \( \overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf{p} \) and \( \overrightarrow{AD} = \mathbf{q}.\) Find:

a) \( \overrightarrow{DC} \)

b) \( \overrightarrow{BC} \)

c) \( \overrightarrow{AC} \)
Show that the points \(A,\) \(B\) and \(C\) with position vectors \( \mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j},\) \( 3\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j} \) and \( 5\mathbf{i}+10\mathbf{j} \) are collinear.
Find the vector \( \overrightarrow{AB} \) given \( A = (3, 7) \) and \( B = (-1, 2).\) Write your answer as a column vector.

In triangle \(OAB,\) \( \overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{a} \) and \( \overrightarrow{OB} = \mathbf{b}.\) \(P\) is the point on \(OA\) such that \(OP:PA = 3:1.\) \(Q\) is the point on \(AB\) such that \(AQ:QB = 1:2.\) Find \( \overrightarrow{PQ} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{a} \) and \( \mathbf{b}.\)

Simplify:

a) \( \overrightarrow{AB} + \overrightarrow{BC} + \overrightarrow{CD} \)

b) \( \overrightarrow{PQ} + \overrightarrow{QR} - \overrightarrow{SR} \)

In the hexagon \(ABCDEF,\) \( \overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf{p} \) and \( \overrightarrow{AF} = \mathbf{q}.\) The hexagon is regular. Express \( \overrightarrow{AD} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{p} \) and \( \mathbf{q}.\)
Given \( \overrightarrow{OA} = \begin{pmatrix}4\\1\end{pmatrix} \) and \( \overrightarrow{OB} = \begin{pmatrix}2\\5\end{pmatrix},\) find the position vector of the midpoint of \(AB.\)

\( \overrightarrow{OA} = 2\mathbf{a},\) \( \overrightarrow{OB} = 3\mathbf{b}.\) \(C\) lies on \(AB\) such that \(AC:CB = 2:3.\) Find \( \overrightarrow{OC} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{a} \) and \( \mathbf{b}.\)

Given \( \mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix}5\\-3\end{pmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{b} = \begin{pmatrix}-2\\1\end{pmatrix},\) find scalars \( \lambda \) and \( \mu \) such that
\[
\lambda\mathbf{a}+\mu\mathbf{b} = \begin{pmatrix}4\\-3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Hence find the magnitude \( |\lambda\mathbf{a}+\mu\mathbf{b}| \) in surd form.

In triangle \(OAB,\) \( \overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{a} \) and \( \overrightarrow{OB} = \mathbf{b}.\) A median of a triangle is a line segment from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side. \(G\) is the centroid (intersection of the three medians). Show that \( \overrightarrow{OG} = \tfrac{1}{3}(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}).\)

In the quadrilateral \(ABCD,\) \( \overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf{p} \) and \( \overrightarrow{AD} = \mathbf{q}.\) Given that \( \overrightarrow{BC} = 2\mathbf{q},\) find \( \overrightarrow{AC} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{p} \) and \( \mathbf{q}.\)

The points \(P,\) \(Q\) and \(R\) have position vectors \( \begin{pmatrix}1\\3\end{pmatrix},\) \( \begin{pmatrix}4\\9\end{pmatrix} \) and \( \begin{pmatrix}6\\13\end{pmatrix}.\) Show that \(P,\) \(Q,\) \(R\) are collinear.

\(A\) is at \((1, 5)\) and \( \overrightarrow{AB} = \begin{pmatrix}3\\-2\end{pmatrix}.\)

a) Find the coordinates of \(B\) and the exact magnitude \( |\overrightarrow{AB}|.\)

b) The point \(C\) lies on the line \(AB\) extended beyond \(B\) such that \( |\overrightarrow{AC}| = 3|\overrightarrow{AB}|.\) Find the coordinates of \(C.\)

c) The point \(D\) is the reflection of \(A\) in \(B.\) Find \(D,\) and find a scalar \( \lambda \) such that \( \overrightarrow{AD} = \lambda\overrightarrow{AC}.\) Hence state the ratio \(AD:AC.\)

In the pentagon \(OABCD,\) \( \overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{a},\) \( \overrightarrow{OD} = \mathbf{d} \) and \( \overrightarrow{AB} = \overrightarrow{DC} = \mathbf{d}.\) Find \( \overrightarrow{BC} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{a} \) and \( \mathbf{d}.\)
Given \( \overrightarrow{AB} = 2\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j} \) and \( \overrightarrow{CB} = -3\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j},\) find \( \overrightarrow{AC}.\)

In triangle \(OAB,\) \( \overrightarrow{OA} = 6\mathbf{a} \) and \( \overrightarrow{OB} = 6\mathbf{b}.\) \(M\) is the midpoint of \(OA\) and \(N\) divides \(AB\) in the ratio \(2:1.\) Show that \(O,\) \(N\) and the midpoint of \(MB\) are collinear.

\(ABCD\) is a square with \( \overrightarrow{AB} = \mathbf{p} \) and \( \overrightarrow{AD} = \mathbf{q} \) (so \( |\mathbf{p}|=|\mathbf{q}|=s,\) the side length). \(E\) is the midpoint of \(CD\) and \(F\) divides \(BC\) in the ratio \(1:2\) from \(B.\)

a) Express \( \overrightarrow{AE},\) \( \overrightarrow{AF} \) and \( \overrightarrow{EF} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{p} \) and \( \mathbf{q}.\)

b) Find \( |\overrightarrow{EF}|^2 \) in terms of \( s,\) assuming the square's sides \( \mathbf{p} \) and \( \mathbf{q} \) are perpendicular (so \( \mathbf{p}\cdot\mathbf{q}=0 \) in the standard Y1 working with \( |\mathbf{a}\pm\mathbf{b}|^2 = |\mathbf{a}|^2+|\mathbf{b}|^2 \) when perpendicular).

c) The line \(AF\) is extended to meet line \(DE\) at \(G.\) Find \( \overrightarrow{AG} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{p} \) and \( \mathbf{q}.\)
Find the value of \( k \) such that \( \begin{pmatrix}k\\6\end{pmatrix} \) is parallel to \( \begin{pmatrix}2\\-3\end{pmatrix}.\)

Given \( \overrightarrow{OA} = \begin{pmatrix}2\\-1\end{pmatrix},\) \( \overrightarrow{OB} = \begin{pmatrix}8\\5\end{pmatrix},\) find the point \(P\) on \(AB\) such that \( \overrightarrow{AP} = \tfrac{2}{3}\overrightarrow{AB}.\)

\(OABC\) is a parallelogram. \( \overrightarrow{OA} = \mathbf{a} \) and \( \overrightarrow{OC} = \mathbf{c}.\) \(D\) is the midpoint of \(OA,\) and \(E\) is the midpoint of \(AB.\)

a) Find \( \overrightarrow{OE} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{a} \) and \( \mathbf{c}.\)

b) Show that \(DE\) is parallel to \(OB.\)

v2.questionText:
Find the exact magnitude of the following vectors:

a) \( 5\mathbf{i} + 12\mathbf{j} \)

b) \( 7\mathbf{i} - 24\mathbf{j} \)

c) \( \begin{pmatrix}-3\\4\end{pmatrix} \)

d) \( \begin{pmatrix}8\\-15\end{pmatrix} \)

Find the exact magnitude of the following vectors:

a) \( 2\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} \)

b) \( -4\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} \)

c) \( \begin{pmatrix}1\\-\sqrt{3}\end{pmatrix} \)

d) \( \begin{pmatrix}-5\\-5\end{pmatrix} \)
\( S \) has position vector \( 8\mathbf{i} - 6\mathbf{j} \). Find the exact length of the line from the origin O to the point S.

For each of the following pairs of points, find the distance between them using position vectors:

a) \( (1,\,3) \) and \( (4,\,7) \)

b) \( (-2,\,5) \) and \( (6,\,-1) \)

c) \( (0,\,-3) \) and \( (-5,\,9) \)

For each of the pairs of vectors given below, find the exact magnitude of the resultant when the two vectors are added together.

a) \( \mathbf{a} = 3\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} \) and \( \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} \)

b) \( \mathbf{u} = \begin{pmatrix}5\\-2\end{pmatrix}\text{ \ and \ } \)  \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix}-1\\-4\end{pmatrix} \)

For each of the following vectors, give the unit vector in the same direction.

a) \( 4\mathbf{i} \)

b) \( 3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} \)

c) \( 6\mathbf{i} - 8\mathbf{j} \)

d) \( \begin{pmatrix}-2\\-1\end{pmatrix} \)
\( \overrightarrow{AB} = 2\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j} \) and \( \overrightarrow{BC} = 4\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} \). Find the unit vector in the direction of \( \overrightarrow{AC} \).
Point A has position vector \( 3\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} \) and point B has position vector \( -1\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j} \). Find the unit vector in the direction of \( \overrightarrow{BA} \).

Given that \( |\overrightarrow{PQ}| = \sqrt{29} \) and \( |\overrightarrow{OQ}| = \sqrt{13} \), and \( \overrightarrow{OP} = \begin{pmatrix}3\\5\end{pmatrix} \) and \( \overrightarrow{OQ} = \begin{pmatrix}-2\\b\end{pmatrix}, \) find \( b \).
The vector \( \mathbf{c} \) has the same direction as \( \mathbf{d} = 3\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j} \) and \( |\mathbf{c}| = 20 \). Find \( \mathbf{c} \).

Find the direction of the following vectors to 1 d.p. (measured anticlockwise from the positive \( x \)-axis):

a) \( 5\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} \)

b) \( -3\mathbf{i} + 7\mathbf{j} \)

c) \( \begin{pmatrix}4\\-3\end{pmatrix} \)

d) \( \begin{pmatrix}-6\\-6\end{pmatrix} \)
Find the direction of the vector \( \begin{pmatrix}-4\\-7\end{pmatrix} \) to 2 decimal places.
Given a vector \( \mathbf{v} = a\mathbf{i} + b\mathbf{j} \) with direction \( 30° \) and magnitude \( 8 \), calculate \( a \) and \( b \).
Given a vector \( \mathbf{w} = a\mathbf{i} + b\mathbf{j} \) with direction \( 120° \) and magnitude \( 6 \), calculate \( a \) and \( b \). Give exact answers.

By finding the horizontal and vertical components, express the following vectors in exact \( \mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} \) form:

a) \( \mathbf{a} \) has direction \( 45° \) and magnitude \( \sqrt{2} \).

b) \( \mathbf{b} \) has direction \( 60° \) and magnitude \( \sqrt{7} \).
The vector \( \mathbf{q} = 7\mathbf{i} + y\mathbf{j} \) has direction \( 44° \). Find \( |\mathbf{q}| \) to 2 d.p.
The vector \( \mathbf{v} = x\mathbf{i} - 4\mathbf{j} \) makes an angle of \( 51° \) below the positive \( x \)-axis. Find \( |\mathbf{v}| \) to 2 d.p.

Vector \( \mathbf{s} \) is parallel to \( \mathbf{t} \). Given that \( \mathbf{t} \) has direction \( 60° \) and \( |\mathbf{s}| = \sqrt{38} \), express \( \mathbf{s} \) in exact \( \mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j} \) form.

Find the magnitude and direction of the vector \( \mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b} \), where \( \mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix}-3\\5\end{pmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{b} = \begin{pmatrix}1\\2\end{pmatrix} \). Give the direction to 1 d.p.

Given that \( \mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix}-5\\2\end{pmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{b} = \begin{pmatrix}3\\-1\end{pmatrix}, \) find the magnitude and direction of \( \mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b} \) to one decimal place.

Let \( \mathbf{a} = 2\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} \) and \( \mathbf{b} = -\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} \).

a) Find, to 2 d.p., the angle between \( \mathbf{a} \) and \( \mathbf{b} \).

b) Find the exact value of the scalar \( k \) such that \( \mathbf{a} + k\mathbf{b} \) is perpendicular to \( \mathbf{b} \).

Let \( \mathbf{c} = 4\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} \) and \( \mathbf{d} = -2\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} \).

a) Find the angle between \( \mathbf{c} \) and \( \mathbf{d} \), to 2 d.p.

b) Place \( \mathbf{c} \) and \( \mathbf{d} \) tail-to-tail at the origin \( O \). Show that the exact area of the triangle formed by \( O \) and the tips of \( \mathbf{c} \) and \( \mathbf{d} \) is \( 5 \) square units.

Find, to 2 d.p., the angles between the following pairs of vectors:

a) \( \mathbf{g} = \begin{pmatrix}5\\-2\end{pmatrix}\text{ and } \)  \( \mathbf{h} = \begin{pmatrix}-1\\-3\end{pmatrix} \)

b) \( \mathbf{e} = \mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j} \) and \( \mathbf{f} = 2\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j} \)

Two boats set off from a harbour. Each boat's velocity (in km/h) is modelled by a vector.

Boat A's velocity: \( \mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix}4\\-1\end{pmatrix} \). Boat B's velocity: \( \mathbf{b} = \begin{pmatrix}1\\5\end{pmatrix} \).

a) Find the angle between the two boats' courses, to 2 d.p.

b) Both boats travel for exactly \( 3 \) hours at their stated velocities. Find the exact distance, in km, between the two boats at the end of those 3 hours.

\( |\overrightarrow{AB}| = 8 \) and \( |\overrightarrow{BC}| = 11 \). The angle between vectors \( \overrightarrow{AB} \) and \( \overrightarrow{BC} \) is \( 115° \).

a) Find \( |\overrightarrow{CA}| \) to 2 d.p.

b) Hence find the interior angle \( \angle ACB \) of triangle \( ABC \) at vertex \( C \), to 2 d.p.

\( |\overrightarrow{EF}| = 3.5 \) and \( |\overrightarrow{EG}| = 4.2 \). The angle between vectors \( \overrightarrow{EF} \) and \( \overrightarrow{EG} \) is \( 28° \).

a) Find \( |\overrightarrow{GF}| \) to 2 d.p.

b) Find the area of triangle \( EFG \), to 2 d.p.

c) Hence find the perpendicular distance from \( G \) to the line \( EF \), to 2 d.p.

A drone's flight is modelled with vectors. First it travels along \( \mathbf{a} = 3\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j} \). Then it turns left along vector \( \mathbf{b} \), at an angle of \( 100° \) to \( \mathbf{a} \). It returns to where it took off along vector \( \mathbf{c} \). Given that \( |\mathbf{b}| = 6\,\mathrm{m} \), find \( |\mathbf{c}| \) to 2 d.p.

The diagram shows a parallelogram \( WXYZ \). \( \overrightarrow{WX} = 3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} \) and \( \overrightarrow{WZ} = 7\mathbf{i} \).

a) Find the angle \( \theta \) at \( W \), to 1 d.p.

b) Hence find the exact area of parallelogram \( WXYZ \).

c) Find the exact length of the diagonal \( WY \).

The quadrilateral ABCD is used to model a plane's flight path as it circles near an airport.
\( \overrightarrow{OA} = 2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j} \), \( \overrightarrow{OB} = 9\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j} \), \( \overrightarrow{OC} = 10\mathbf{i}+8\mathbf{j} \) and \( \overrightarrow{OD} = 3\mathbf{i}+7\mathbf{j} \), where \( \mathbf{i} \) and \( \mathbf{j} \) have a length of \( 1\,\mathrm{km} \).

Calculate, to the nearest \( \mathrm{km} \), the distance the plane travels if it circles twice.

Triangle ABC is shown below with \( A = (1, 2) \), \( B = (5, -1) \), \( C = (-2, 4) \).

a) Find the vectors \( \overrightarrow{AB} \), \( \overrightarrow{BC} \) and \( \overrightarrow{CA} \) in \( \mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j} \) form.

b) Find the lengths of all three sides.

c) Find the angle at vertex A to 1 d.p.
Find the magnitude of \( \begin{pmatrix}6\\-8\end{pmatrix} \).
Find the exact magnitude of \( -\mathbf{i} + 7\mathbf{j} \).
Find the unit vector in the direction of \( \begin{pmatrix}5\\12\end{pmatrix} \).
Points A and B have position vectors \( 3\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} \) and \( 7\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} \). Find the distance AB.
Find the direction of \( 3\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} \), measured anticlockwise from the positive \( x \)-axis.
A vector \( \mathbf{p} \) has magnitude \( 10 \) and direction \( 150° \). Express \( \mathbf{p} \) in exact \( \mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} \) form.
The vector \( \mathbf{r} \) has the same direction as \( 5\mathbf{i} + 12\mathbf{j} \) and magnitude \( 26 \). Find \( \mathbf{r} \).
Given \( \mathbf{a} = \begin{pmatrix}2\\-5\end{pmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{b} = \begin{pmatrix}-1\\3\end{pmatrix}, \) find \( |2\mathbf{a} - 3\mathbf{b}| \).

Point P has position vector \( \begin{pmatrix}1\\4\end{pmatrix}, \) and point Q has position vector \( \begin{pmatrix}a\\-2\end{pmatrix}. \) Given that \( |\overrightarrow{PQ}| = 10 \), find the possible values of \( a \).
Find the direction of \( -5\mathbf{i} - 5\mathbf{j} \) to the nearest degree.
Given \( \overrightarrow{OA} = 2\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j} \) and \( \overrightarrow{OB} = 8\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j} \), find the midpoint \( M \) of \( AB\) as a position vector.
A ship sails from port O on a bearing of \( 060° \) for \( 12\,\mathrm{km} \). Express the displacement as a column vector, giving exact values.

Given \( |\mathbf{a}| = 5 \), \( |\mathbf{b}| = 8 \) and the angle between \( \mathbf{a} \) and \( \mathbf{b} \) is \( 60° \):

a) Find \( |\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}| \) to 2 d.p.

b) Find the angle that \( \mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b} \) makes with \( \mathbf{a} \), to 2 d.p.
Find the angle between \( \begin{pmatrix}1\\0\end{pmatrix} \) and \( \begin{pmatrix}1\\\sqrt{3}\end{pmatrix}. \)
Points \( A(1,\,3) \), \( B(4,\,7) \) and \( C(7,\,3) \) form a triangle. Show that triangle \( ABC \) is isosceles.
The vector \( \mathbf{v} = a\mathbf{i} + b\mathbf{j} \) has magnitude \( 2\sqrt{5} \) and direction \( \tan^{-1}(2) \). Find \( a \) and \( b \).

Two forces act on a particle: \( \mathbf{F}_1 = (6\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{N} \) and \( \mathbf{F}_2 = (-\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{N} \).

a) Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant force \( \mathbf{R} = \mathbf{F}_1+\mathbf{F}_2 \).

b) A third force \( \mathbf{F}_3 \) acts on the particle so that it is in equilibrium. Find \( \mathbf{F}_3 \) in \( \mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j} \) form, its magnitude, and the angle it makes with the positive \( x \)-axis (to 1 d.p.).
A velocity vector has magnitude \( 15\,\mathrm{ms^{-1}} \) and makes an angle of \( 40° \) above the horizontal. Write it in \( \mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} \) form to 2 d.p.

Given \( \overrightarrow{OP} = \begin{pmatrix}3\\-1\end{pmatrix}, \) \( \overrightarrow{OQ} = \begin{pmatrix}-1\\7\end{pmatrix}, \) find the point R such that \( \overrightarrow{OR} = \overrightarrow{OP} + 2\overrightarrow{PQ}. \)
Show that the triangle with vertices \( A(0,\,0) \), \( B(3,\,4) \) and \( C(6,\,0) \) is isosceles and find the angle at \( B \) to 1 d.p.
The vector \( \mathbf{u} = k\mathbf{i} + 2k\mathbf{j} \) has magnitude \( 5\sqrt{5} \). Find \( k \) where \( k > 0 \).
Find the angle between the position vectors of \( A(4,\,3) \) and \( B(-3,\,4) \), measured from the origin.
A hiker walks \( 5\,\mathrm{km} \) on a bearing of \( 030° \) then \( 8\,\mathrm{km} \) on a bearing of \( 120° \). Find the magnitude and bearing of the direct return journey to 1 d.p.
Find the exact distance between the points with position vectors \( 2\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j} \) and \( -4\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j} \).
Given \( |\overrightarrow{PQ}| = 6 \) and \( |\overrightarrow{PR}| = 9 \) and the angle \( QPR = 70° \), find \( |\overrightarrow{QR}| \) to 2 d.p.
Find the unit vector perpendicular to \( 3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} \).

The point \( C \) divides \( AB \) in the ratio \( 2:3 \). Given \( \overrightarrow{OA} = \begin{pmatrix}1\\8\end{pmatrix} \) and \( \overrightarrow{OB} = \begin{pmatrix}11\\3\end{pmatrix} \):

a) Find \( \overrightarrow{OC} \).

b) Find the exact distance \( |OC| \).

c) The line \( OC \) is extended to a point \( D \) such that \( OC : CD = 3 : 2 \). Find \( \overrightarrow{OD} \) and the exact distance \( |CD| \).

A quadrilateral has vertices \( A(0,\,0) \), \( B(5,\,2) \), \( C(7,\,7) \) and \( D(2,\,5) \).

a) Show that \( ABCD \) is a parallelogram.

b) Find the position vector of the centre \( M \) of the parallelogram (the intersection of the diagonals) by computing the midpoints of both diagonals and verifying they coincide.

c) The point \( P \) is the reflection of \( A \) in \( M \). State \( P \) and explain (using vectors) why \( P \) must coincide with \( C \).
Given \( |\mathbf{a}| = 7 \), \( |\mathbf{b}| = 10 \) and \( |\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}| = 13 \), find the angle between \( \mathbf{a} \) and \( \mathbf{b} \) to 1 d.p.
Find the magnitude and direction of \( 8\mathbf{i} - 6\mathbf{j} \).

v3.questionText:
The acceleration of a car is modelled by the vector \( \mathbf{a} = (3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j}) \) ms\(^{-2}\), where \( \mathbf{i} \) is horizontal and \( \mathbf{j} \) is vertical.

a) Calculate the exact magnitude of the acceleration.

b) Find the angle the acceleration makes with the horizontal.

The velocity of a drone is modelled by the vector \( \mathbf{v} = (-5\mathbf{i} + 12\mathbf{j}) \) ms\(^{-1}\), where \( \mathbf{i} \) is due east and \( \mathbf{j} \) is due north.

a) Calculate the exact speed of the drone.

b) Find the bearing on which the drone is travelling, to the nearest degree.

The acceleration of various particles is given by the vectors below. Calculate the exact magnitude of each particle's acceleration.

a) \( \mathbf{a} = (2\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j}) \) ms\(^{-2}\)

b) \( \mathbf{b} = (-3\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j}) \) ms\(^{-2}\)

c) \( \mathbf{c} = (4\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j}) \) ms\(^{-2}\)

d) \( \mathbf{d} = (-\mathbf{i} - 7\mathbf{j}) \) ms\(^{-2}\)

A ball is kicked with velocity \( \mathbf{v} = (8\mathbf{i} + 6\mathbf{j}) \) ms\(^{-1}\), where \( \mathbf{i} \) is horizontal and \( \mathbf{j} \) is vertical (pointing upwards).

a) Calculate the speed of the ball.

b) Find the angle of projection above the horizontal.

A stone is thrown from a cliff. Its velocity is modelled by the vector \( \mathbf{v} = (5\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j}) \) ms\(^{-1}\), where \( \mathbf{i} \) is horizontal and \( \mathbf{j} \) is vertical (pointing upwards).

a) Find the exact speed of the stone.

b) Find the angle the velocity makes below the horizontal.
A ship travels \(120\) km on a bearing of \(060°\). Express the ship's displacement from its starting position as a column vector. Give each component to 2 d.p.
A hiker walks \(8\) km on a bearing of \(230°\). Express the hiker's displacement from the start as a column vector. Give each component to 2 d.p.

A roller coaster is accelerating at \(25\) ms\(^{-2}\) at an angle of \(40°\) below the positive horizontal. Express this acceleration as a vector of the form \( \mathbf{a} = x\mathbf{i} + y\mathbf{j} \). Give values to 2 d.p.

A simple mathematical model of a ball bouncing off the side of a pool table is constructed using vectors. The ball's velocity has vector \( \mathbf{v}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix} \) before it hits the side, and vector \( \mathbf{v}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} \) afterwards. Find the acute angle \( \theta \) between \( \mathbf{v}_1 \) and \( \mathbf{v}_2 \). Give your answer to 2 d.p.
A yacht sails \(50\) km on a bearing of \(315°\). Express the yacht's displacement from its starting position as a column vector. Give each component to 2 d.p.

The velocity of a fish swimming in the horizontal plane is modelled by the vector \( \mathbf{v} = 3t(\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j}) \) ms\(^{-1}\), where \( t \) is the time in seconds.

a) State the fish's velocity after \(2\) seconds.

b) Calculate the fish's exact speed after \(3 \) seconds.

c) Find the angle that \( \mathbf{v} \) makes with \( \mathbf{i} \).

A firework's displacement is modelled by the vector \( \mathbf{s} = 2t^2(-\mathbf{i} + 7\mathbf{j}) \) m, where \( t \) is time in seconds, \( \mathbf{i} \) is horizontal and \( \mathbf{j} \) is vertical (pointing upwards).

a) Find the firework's displacement after 1.5 seconds.

b) Calculate, to 3 s.f., the firework's angle to the horizontal.

The firework explodes after 2.5 seconds.

c) What is the vertical distance from the ground when it goes off?

The position of a boat relative to a harbour is modelled by the vector \( \mathbf{r} = (3t + 1)\mathbf{i} + (t^2 - 4)\mathbf{j} \) km, where \( t \) is the time in hours, \( \mathbf{i} \) is due east and \( \mathbf{j} \) is due north.

a) Find the position of the boat at \( t = 0 \).

b) Find the position of the boat at \( t = 3 \).

c) Calculate the distance of the boat from the harbour at \( t = 3 \).

A toy car moves on a flat surface. Its velocity is modelled by \( \mathbf{v} = (4t\mathbf{i} + (6 - 2t)\mathbf{j}) \) ms\(^{-1}\), where \( t \) is the time in seconds.

a) Find the velocity at \( t = 1 \).

b) At what time is the car moving parallel to \( \mathbf{i} \)?

c) Find the exact speed of the car at \( t = 2 \).

A helicopter's position is modelled by \( \mathbf{r} = (20t)\mathbf{i} + (t^2 + 10t)\mathbf{j} \) m, where \( \mathbf{i} \) is horizontal and \( \mathbf{j} \) is vertical (pointing upwards), and \( t \) is in seconds.

a) Find the height of the helicopter at \( t = 5 \).

b) Find the distance of the helicopter from its starting point at \( t = 5 \).

c) At what time is the helicopter \( 200 \) m above the ground?

An aircraft tries to fly due north at \( 600 \) km/h, but there is a wind from the west at \( 75\) km/h. The aircraft's actual course is modelled by the resultant of these two vectors. Calculate:

a) the actual bearing the plane is flying on, to the nearest degree.

b) the aircraft's resultant speed in km/h (to 2 d.p.).

Two tug boats are pulling a ship with an angle of \(40°\) between them. One tug boat exerts a force of \( 8\) kN and is modelled with vector \( \mathbf{a} \). The other exerts a force of \( 15\) kN and is modelled with vector \( \mathbf{b} \). The resultant force on the ship, \( \mathbf{r} \), is the resultant vector of these two forces. Calculate the size of the resultant force.

Two lumberjacks are pulling ropes attached to a tree stump. The angle between the ropes is \( 100°\). One lumberjack exerts a force of \( 250\) N and the other exerts a force of \(210\) N. The resultant force \( \mathbf{f} \) is modelled by the resultant of these two vectors. Calculate the magnitude of \( \mathbf{f} \).

Ray is attempting to paddle his canoe due north at \(4\) ms\(^{-1}\), but there is a current travelling west at \(3\) ms\(^{-1}\). Ray's actual course is modelled by the resultant of these two vectors. Calculate:

a) the actual bearing Ray is travelling on.

b) Ray's resultant speed in ms\(^{-1}\).

A crate is pulled across a floor by two ropes. The forces in the ropes are modelled by vectors \( \mathbf{F}_1 \) and \( \mathbf{F}_2 \). The magnitude of \( \mathbf{F}_1 \) is 180 N and the magnitude of \( \mathbf{F}_2 \) is 120 N. The angle between the two ropes is 65°. The resultant force is \( \mathbf{R} = \mathbf{F}_1 + \mathbf{F}_2 \). Calculate:

a) the magnitude of the resultant force.

b) the angle the resultant makes with \( \mathbf{F}_1 \).

A park is modelled as a quadrilateral \(EFGH\), with sides given by the following vectors:
\( \overrightarrow{EF} = 2\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} \), \( \overrightarrow{FG} = \mathbf{i} - \frac{1}{2}\mathbf{j} \), \( \overrightarrow{GH} = -\mathbf{i} - \frac{3}{2}\mathbf{j} \) and \( \overrightarrow{HE} = -2\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} \).

Show that the park is a trapezium.

The quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is used to model a garden. The vertices have coordinates \( A(1, 2), B(9, 1), C(7, 7)\) and \( D(2, 8)\) . There is a straight path that crosses the garden. Its start point divides \( \overrightarrow{AB} \) in the ratio \(3:1\), and it ends at the midpoint of \( \overrightarrow{CD} \).

The path is modelled by vector \( \mathbf{p} = \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix}. \)  Calculate \( x \) and \( y \).

The position vectors of the vertices of the parallelogram PQRS are:
\( \overrightarrow{OP} = 2\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} \), \( \overrightarrow{OQ} = 7\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} \), \( \overrightarrow{OR} = 6\mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} \) and \( \overrightarrow{OS} = \mathbf{i} \).

Note: \( O \) is the origin, not a vertex of the parallelogram. \( \overrightarrow{PQ} \) and \( \overrightarrow{SR} \) are opposite sides.

What are the exact lengths of this parallelogram's diagonals?

The routes from Appleton to Bridgford (\( \overrightarrow{AB} \)) and to Crofton (\( \overrightarrow{AC} \)) are modelled by the vectors \( \mathbf{p} \) and \( \mathbf{q} \) respectively. Xena's house lies between Bridgford and Crofton such that her position, \(X\), divides \(BC\) in the ratio \(3:4\).

Find the vector \( \overrightarrow{AX} \) in terms of \( \mathbf{p} \) and \( \mathbf{q} \).

In the diagram below, \(W\) divides \(QR\) in the ratio \( a:b \).

Given that \( \overrightarrow{PW} = \frac{3}{5}\mathbf{s} + \frac{2}{5}\mathbf{t} \), where \( \overrightarrow{PQ} = \mathbf{s} \) and \( \overrightarrow{PR} = \mathbf{t} \), find \( a \) and \( b \).

A swimmer is attempting to swim due east across a river at \( 2 \) ms\(^{-1}\). The river current flows due south at \(1.5\) ms\(^{-1}\). The swimmer's actual motion is modelled by the resultant of these two vectors.

a) Find the swimmer's resultant speed.

b) Find the bearing on which the swimmer actually travels, to the nearest degree.

A field is modelled as a parallelogram \(ABCD\), where \( \overrightarrow{AB} = 5\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} \) and \( \overrightarrow{AD} = \mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} \). All units are in metres.

a) Find \( \overrightarrow{AC} \).

b) Find the exact length of the diagonal \(AC\).

c) Find the exact length of the diagonal \(BD\).

A kayaker tries to paddle due east at \(5\) ms\(^{-1}\) across a river. The current flows at \(2\) ms\(^{-1}\) on a bearing of \(200°\). The kayaker's actual velocity is modelled by the resultant of these two vectors. Find:

a) the resultant speed of the kayaker (to 2 d.p.).

b) the bearing on which the kayaker actually travels (to the nearest degree).

A particle's displacement from the origin at time \( t \) seconds is modelled by \( \mathbf{s} = (t^2 - 4t)\mathbf{i} + (2t + 1)\mathbf{j} \) m.

a) Find the displacement at \( t = 0 \).

b) At what time does the particle cross the \(j\)-axis (i.e. when is the \(i\)-component zero)?

c) Find the exact distance of the particle from the origin at \( t = 5 \).

Three forces act on a particle. The forces are modelled by the vectors \( \mathbf{F}_1 = (4\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j}) \) N, \( \mathbf{F}_2 = (-2\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j}) \) N and \( \mathbf{F}_3 = (a\mathbf{i} + b\mathbf{j}) \) N.

The particle is in equilibrium.

a) Find the values of \( a \) and \( b \).

b) Calculate the exact magnitude of \( \mathbf{F}_3 \).

y1f1.questionText: Find the weight of an object of mass \(5\) kg. Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\).
A resultant force of \(24\) N acts on an object of mass \(6\) kg. Find the acceleration of the object.
Two forces of \(15\) N and \(8\) N act on a particle in the same direction along a straight line. Find the resultant force.
Two forces act on a particle along a straight line: \(20\) N to the right and \(12\) N to the left. Find the resultant force and state its direction.
A book of mass \(2\) kg rests on a horizontal table. State the two forces acting on the book and their magnitudes. Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\).
A particle of mass \(3\) kg hangs in equilibrium from a light inextensible string. Find the tension in the string. Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\).
A resultant force of \(45\) N produces an acceleration of \(5\) m/s\(^2\) on an object. Find the mass of the object.

A crate of mass \(10\) kg sits on a horizontal floor. A vertical downward force of \(18\) N is applied to the top of the crate. Find the normal reaction force exerted by the floor on the crate. Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\).

A car of mass \(1200\) kg travels along a straight horizontal road. The engine provides a driving force of \(3000\) N and the total resistance to motion is \(600\) N. Find the acceleration of the car.

A car of mass \(800\) kg is travelling at constant speed along a horizontal road. The driving force is \(500\) N. The driver removes their foot from the accelerator so that only the resistance force acts. Find the deceleration of the car.
A person of mass \(70\) kg stands on scales in a lift that accelerates upward at \(1.5\) m/s\(^2\). Find the reading on the scales. Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\).
A person of mass \(60\) kg stands on scales in a lift that decelerates at \(2\) m/s\(^2\) while moving upward. Find the reading on the scales. Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\).
A particle of mass \(4\) kg is placed on a smooth plane inclined at \(30°\) to the horizontal. Find the acceleration of the particle down the plane. Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\).
A force of \(50\) N acts at \(40°\) above the horizontal. Find the horizontal and vertical components of the force. Give your answers to 3 significant figures.
Two perpendicular forces of \(6\) N and \(8\) N act on a particle. Find the magnitude of the resultant force and the angle it makes with the \(8\) N force.

A particle is in equilibrium under three forces: a weight of \(20\) N acting vertically downward, a horizontal force \(P\), and a force \(T\) acting at \(60°\) above the horizontal. By resolving horizontally and vertically, find \(P\) and \(T\). Give answers to 3 significant figures.

A car of mass \(1500\) kg is travelling at \(20\) m/s when the driver applies the brakes. The braking force is \(4500\) N and the resistance to motion is \(750\) N. Find the deceleration of the car and the distance it travels before stopping.

A lorry of mass \(5000\) kg travels along a horizontal road against a constant resistance of \(2000\) N. (a) Find the driving force when the lorry moves at constant speed. (b) Find the driving force required to produce an acceleration of \(0.6\) m/s\(^2\).

A box of mass \(5\) kg is placed on a rough plane inclined at \(30°\) to the horizontal. The friction force acting on the box is \(10\) N up the plane. Find the acceleration of the box down the plane. Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\).
A particle of mass \(8\) kg is pulled along a rough horizontal surface by a horizontal force of \(30\) N. The friction force is \(14\) N. Find the acceleration of the particle.

A particle of mass \(6\) kg is on a smooth plane inclined at \(45°\) to the horizontal. Find (a) the acceleration of the particle down the plane and (b) the normal reaction force. Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\).
A particle of mass \(10\) kg rests on a smooth horizontal surface. A force of \(40\) N is applied to the particle at an angle of \(25°\) above the horizontal. Find the acceleration of the particle.

A van of mass \(2000\) kg accelerates from rest at \(1.2\) m/s\(^2\) on a horizontal road against a constant resistance of \(800\) N. (a) Find the driving force during the acceleration. (b) The van then reaches a constant speed. State the driving force at constant speed.
A box of mass \(12\) kg rests in equilibrium on a rough plane inclined at \(20°\) to the horizontal. Find the friction force and the normal reaction. Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\).

A particle of mass \(m\) kg is on a smooth plane inclined at angle \(\alpha\) to the horizontal. A force \(P\) N acts on the particle up the plane, causing it to accelerate at \(a\) m/s\(^2\) up the plane. Show that \(P = m(a + g\sin\alpha)\).

A particle of mass \(m\) kg slides down a rough plane inclined at angle \(\theta\) to the horizontal. The friction force acting on the particle is \(F\) N up the plane. Show that the acceleration of the particle is \(g\sin\theta - \dfrac{F}{m}\).

Two forces of magnitudes \(10\) N and \(7\) N act on a particle. The angle between the two forces is \(60°\). Find the magnitude and direction of the resultant force. Give your answers to 3 significant figures.

A particle of weight \(30\) N is held in equilibrium by two strings. One string is horizontal and has tension \(T_1\). The other string makes an angle of \(50°\) with the vertical and has tension \(T_2\). Find \(T_1\) and \(T_2\). Give answers to 3 significant figures.

Two boxes, A of mass \(3\) kg and B of mass \(5\) kg, are connected by a light inextensible string on a smooth horizontal surface. A horizontal force of \(32\) N is applied to box B in the direction from A to B. Find (a) the acceleration of the system and (b) the tension in the string.

A particle of mass \(5\) kg is on a rough horizontal surface. A force of \(40\) N is applied at \(30°\) above the horizontal. The friction force is \(12\) N. Find (a) the acceleration of the particle and (b) the normal reaction. Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\).

A particle of mass \(8\) kg is on a rough plane inclined at \(25°\) to the horizontal. A force of \(50\) N acts up the plane. The friction force is \(6\) N acting down the plane. Find (a) the acceleration of the particle and (b) the normal reaction. Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\).

A person of mass \(m\) kg stands on scales in a lift. The lift accelerates downward at \(a\) m/s\(^2\), where \(a < g\). Show that the reading on the scales is \(m(g - a)\) N. State the condition under which the scales would read zero and interpret this physically.

Two particles, P of mass \(4\) kg and Q of mass \(6\) kg, are connected by a light inextensible string on a rough horizontal surface. The friction force on P is \(8\) N and the friction force on Q is \(12\) N. A horizontal force of \(50\) N is applied to Q in the direction away from P. Find (a) the acceleration of the system and (b) the tension in the string.
Two forces, each of magnitude \(F\) N, act on a particle with an angle of \(2\alpha\) between them, where \(0 < \alpha < 90°\). Show that the magnitude of the resultant is \(2F\cos\alpha\).

A particle of weight \(W\) N is held in equilibrium by two light inextensible strings. One string makes an angle \(\alpha\) with the vertical and has tension \(T_1\). The other makes an angle \(\beta\) with the vertical and has tension \(T_2\). By resolving horizontally and vertically, show that \(T_1 = \dfrac{W\sin\beta}{\sin(\alpha + \beta)}\).

A particle of mass \(m\) kg slides down a rough plane inclined at angle \(\theta\) to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between the particle and the plane is \(\mu\). Show that the acceleration of the particle down the plane is \(g(\sin\theta - \mu\cos\theta)\).

A box of mass \(15\) kg is on a rough plane inclined at \(35°\) to the horizontal. A force \(P\) N acts on the box up the plane. The friction force is \(20\) N. Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\). (a) When \(P = 120\) N, find the acceleration of the box up the plane. (b) Find the value of \(P\) for which the box is in equilibrium. (c) If \(P\) is removed, determine whether the box remains in equilibrium or slides. Justify your answer.

A particle of mass \(4\) kg is on a rough horizontal surface. A force of magnitude \(P\) N is applied at angle \(\theta\) above the horizontal, where \(\sin\theta = 0.6\) and \(\cos\theta = 0.8\). The friction force is \(9\) N and the particle accelerates at \(2\) m/s\(^2\) horizontally. (a) Find \(P\). (b) Find the normal reaction. Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\).

A boat of mass \(600\) kg moves in a straight line on a lake. The engine provides a constant driving force of \(1800\) N. The resistance to motion is \(R\) N. (a) Given that the boat accelerates from rest to \(12\) m/s over a distance of \(120\) m, find the acceleration and hence find \(R\). (b) The boat then travels at a constant speed \(V\) m/s. State the value of \(V\). (c) The engine is then switched off. Assuming the same resistance \(R\) continues to act, find the deceleration of the boat. (d) Find the distance the boat travels from the moment the engine is switched off until it comes to rest.

A particle of mass \(3\) kg is held at rest on a rough plane inclined at \(40°\) to the horizontal. A horizontal force of magnitude \(H\) N is applied to the particle. Take \(g = 9.8\) m/s\(^2\). (a) By resolving along and perpendicular to the plane, show that the normal reaction is \(R = 3g\cos 40° + H\sin 40°\). (b) Given that the friction force is \(5\) N and the particle is on the point of sliding up the plane, find \(H\). (c) Find the normal reaction for the value of \(H\) found in part (b).

y1f2.questionText: A book of mass \(2\) kg rests on a horizontal table. State the magnitude and direction of (a) the weight of the book and (b) the normal reaction force exerted by the table on the book. Identify the action-reaction pair according to Newton's third law.
A particle of mass \(5\) kg hangs in equilibrium from a light inextensible string attached to a ceiling. Find the tension in the string.

Two particles \(A\) and \(B\), of masses \(3\) kg and \(2\) kg respectively, are connected by a light inextensible string on a smooth horizontal surface. A horizontal force of \(25\) N is applied to \(A\) in the direction \(A\) to \(B\). Find (a) the acceleration of the system and (b) the tension in the string.

Two particles of masses \(4\) kg and \(6\) kg are connected by a light inextensible string that passes over a smooth fixed pulley. The system is released from rest. Find the acceleration of the system.
Two particles of masses \(3\) kg and \(7\) kg are connected by a light inextensible string that passes over a smooth fixed pulley. The system is released from rest. Find the tension in the string.
A car tows a trailer at a constant speed along a straight horizontal road. The resistance to motion of the trailer is \(400\) N. Find the tension in the towbar.
A box of mass \(8\) kg rests on a smooth horizontal table. A vertical string attached to the top of the box exerts an upward pull of \(20\) N. Find the normal reaction of the table on the box.

A particle \(A\) of mass \(4\) kg is suspended from a ceiling by a light inextensible string. A second particle \(B\) of mass \(3\) kg is suspended from \(A\) by another light inextensible string. The system hangs in equilibrium. Find the tension in each string.

Two particles \(P\) and \(Q\), of masses \(3\) kg and \(5\) kg respectively, are connected by a light inextensible string that passes over a smooth fixed pulley. The system is released from rest. Find (a) the acceleration and (b) the tension in the string.

A particle \(A\) of mass \(4\) kg rests on a smooth horizontal table. It is connected by a light inextensible string that passes over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table to a particle \(B\) of mass \(6\) kg hanging freely. The system is released from rest. Find (a) the acceleration and (b) the tension in the string.

A car of mass \(1200\) kg tows a trailer of mass \(400\) kg along a straight horizontal road. The driving force of the car's engine is \(3200\) N. The resistances to motion are \(600\) N on the car and \(200\) N on the trailer. Find (a) the acceleration and (b) the tension in the towbar.

A car of mass \(1000\) kg tows a trailer of mass \(500\) kg along a straight horizontal road at \(20\) m/s. The driver applies the brakes, producing a braking force of \(3000\) N on the car. The resistance to motion is \(400\) N on the car and \(200\) N on the trailer. Find (a) the deceleration of the system and (b) the force in the towbar, stating whether it is a tension or a thrust.

A particle \(A\) of mass \(2\) kg is placed on a smooth plane inclined at \(30°\) to the horizontal. It is connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth pulley at the top of the plane to a particle \(B\) of mass \(3\) kg hanging freely on the other side. The system is released from rest. Find (a) the acceleration and (b) the tension in the string.

Two particles \(P\) and \(Q\), of masses \(5\) kg and \(3\) kg respectively, are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth pulley at the top of a double inclined plane. The plane on which \(P\) rests makes an angle of \(30°\) with the horizontal and the plane on which \(Q\) rests makes an angle of \(45°\) with the horizontal. Both planes are smooth. Find the acceleration of the system and the tension in the string.

A car of mass \(1200\) kg tows a trailer of mass \(800\) kg along a straight horizontal road. The resistance to motion is \(500\) N on the car and \(300\) N on the trailer. The car accelerates from rest at \(0.5\) m/s\(^2\) until it reaches \(15\) m/s, then travels at constant speed. Find (a) the driving force during the acceleration phase and (b) the tension in the towbar during the constant speed phase.

Two particles of masses \(2\) kg and \(8\) kg are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth fixed pulley. The system is released from rest. After \(2\) seconds the string breaks. Find (a) the speed of the particles when the string breaks and (b) the further distance the \(2\) kg particle travels upward after the string breaks.

A car of mass \(900\) kg tows a trailer of mass \(600\) kg along a horizontal road. The resistance to motion is \(300\) N on the car and \(200\) N on the trailer. Find the force in the towbar and state whether it is a tension or a thrust when (a) the system accelerates at \(0.4\) m/s\(^2\) and (b) the system decelerates at \(1.5\) m/s\(^2\) with no engine force.

A person of mass \(70\) kg stands on scales in a lift. Find the reading on the scales (apparent weight) when the lift (a) accelerates upward at \(1.2\) m/s\(^2\) and (b) decelerates while going up at \(0.8\) m/s\(^2\).

Particle \(A\) of mass \(3\) kg lies on a smooth horizontal table, \(1.5\) m from the edge. It is connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table to particle \(B\) of mass \(2\) kg hanging freely, \(0.8\) m above the floor. The system is released from rest. Find (a) the acceleration and (b) the speed at which \(B\) hits the floor.

Two particles of masses \(4\) kg and \(6\) kg are connected by a light inextensible string over a smooth pulley. They are released from rest with each particle \(2\) m from the pulley. Find (a) the acceleration, (b) the tension, and (c) the time taken for the heavier particle to descend \(1\) m.

A car of mass \(1000\) kg tows a trailer of mass \(500\) kg along a horizontal road. The resistance to motion is \(300\) N on the car and \(150\) N on the trailer. The engine produces a driving force of \(2250\) N. (a) Find the acceleration. The car then removes the driving force and applies brakes, producing a braking force of \(1500\) N on the car only (resistances remain). (b) Find the deceleration and the force in the towbar during braking.

A particle \(A\) of mass \(4\) kg lies on a smooth plane inclined at \(40°\) to the horizontal. A light inextensible string connects \(A\) over a smooth pulley at the top of the plane to a particle \(B\) of mass \(5\) kg hanging vertically. The system is released from rest. Find the acceleration and the tension in the string.

Two particles \(P\) (\(3\) kg) and \(Q\) (\(5\) kg) are connected by a light inextensible string over a smooth pulley. Initially \(Q\) is \(1.2\) m above the ground and \(P\) is on the ground. The system is released from rest. Find (a) the acceleration, (b) the speed at which \(P\) leaves the ground. (c) After \(Q\) hits the ground, describe the motion of \(P\).

A particle \(A\) of mass \(5\) kg lies on a smooth horizontal table, \(2\) m from the pulley at the edge. A light inextensible string passes over the pulley and connects to a particle \(B\) of mass \(3\) kg hanging freely. The system is released from rest. Find how long it takes for \(A\) to reach the edge of the table.

Two particles of masses \(M\) and \(m\) (where \(M > m\)) are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth fixed pulley. The system is released from rest. Show that the acceleration of the system is \(\dfrac{(M - m)g}{M + m}\).

Two particles of masses \(M\) and \(m\) (where \(M > m\)) are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth fixed pulley. Show that the tension in the string is \(\dfrac{2Mmg}{M + m}\).

Two particles of masses \(m\) and \(3m\) are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth fixed pulley. The system is released from rest. Show that the acceleration is \(\dfrac{g}{2}\) and find the tension in terms of \(m\) and \(g\).

A particle \(A\) of mass \(2\) kg lies on a rough horizontal table. The friction force between \(A\) and the table is \(5\) N. A light inextensible string connects \(A\) over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table to a particle \(B\) of mass \(3\) kg hanging freely. The system is released from rest. Find the acceleration and the tension in the string.

A particle \(A\) of mass \(2m\) on a rough horizontal table is connected by a light inextensible string over a smooth pulley to a particle \(B\) of mass \(3m\) hanging freely. The friction force on \(A\) is \(F\). Show that the acceleration of the system is \(\dfrac{3mg - F}{5m}\).

Three particles \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) of masses \(2\) kg, \(3\) kg, and \(5\) kg respectively are connected in a line by two light inextensible strings on a smooth horizontal surface. A horizontal force of \(40\) N is applied to \(C\) in the direction of the line \(A\text{-}B\text{-}C\). Find (a) the acceleration, (b) the tension \(T_1\) in the string between \(A\) and \(B\), and (c) the tension \(T_2\) in the string between \(B\) and \(C\).

A particle \(A\) of mass \(4\) kg is placed on a rough plane inclined at \(30°\) to the horizontal. The friction force on \(A\) is \(6\) N. A light inextensible string connects \(A\) over a smooth pulley at the top of the plane to a particle \(B\) of mass \(5\) kg hanging freely. The system is released from rest. Find the acceleration and the tension in the string.

A particle \(P\) of mass \(2\) kg lies on a smooth plane inclined at angle \(\theta\) to the horizontal, where \(\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}\). A light inextensible string connects \(P\) over a smooth pulley at the top of the plane to a particle \(Q\) of mass \(1\) kg hanging freely. (a) Determine which direction the system moves. (b) Find the acceleration. (c) Show that the tension is \(\dfrac{16g}{15}\).

Three particles \(A\), \(B\), and \(C\) of masses \(1\) kg, \(2\) kg, and \(3\) kg respectively hang in a vertical line connected by two light inextensible strings, with \(A\) at the top attached to a fixed support, \(B\) in the middle, and \(C\) at the bottom. The support is then removed and the system falls freely. Find the tension in each string immediately after the support is removed.

A particle \(A\) of mass \(3\) kg rests on a smooth horizontal table, \(4\) m from the edge. A light inextensible string passes over a smooth pulley at the edge and connects to a particle \(B\) of mass \(2\) kg, hanging \(1.5\) m above the ground. The system is released from rest. (a) Find the acceleration. (b) Find the speed when \(B\) hits the ground. (c) Describe the subsequent motion of \(A\). (d) Find the total distance \(A\) travels before stopping at the edge of the table.

A car of mass \(M\) tows a trailer of mass \(m\) along a horizontal road with a driving force \(D\). The resistance to motion on each vehicle is proportional to its mass, with total resistance \(R\). Show that the tension in the towbar is \(\dfrac{mD}{M + m}\).

A particle \(P\) of mass \(4\) kg lies on a rough plane inclined at \(30°\) to the horizontal. A light inextensible string connects \(P\) over a smooth pulley at the top to a particle \(Q\) of mass \(3\) kg on a smooth plane inclined at \(45°\) on the other side. The friction force on \(P\) is \(4\) N. (a) Determine which direction the system moves. (b) Find the acceleration. (c) Find the tension.

Particles \(P\) (\(2\) kg) and \(Q\) (\(5\) kg) are connected by a light inextensible string over a smooth fixed pulley. Initially both particles are \(3\) m above the ground. The system is released from rest. (a) Find the acceleration. (b) Find the speed at which \(Q\) hits the ground. (c) Find the greatest height reached by \(P\) above the ground. (d) Find the total time from release until \(P\) hits the ground.

A particle \(A\) of mass \(m\) lies on a rough horizontal table. A light inextensible string connects \(A\) over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table to a particle \(B\) of mass \(2m\) hanging freely. The friction force on \(A\) is \(F\). The system is released from rest. (a) Show that the acceleration is \(\dfrac{2mg - F}{3m}\). (b) Show that the tension is \(\dfrac{m(2mg + 2F)}{3m} = \dfrac{2m g + 2F}{3}\). (c) State the condition for the system to move.

A particle \(A\) of mass \(m\) lies on a smooth plane inclined at angle \(\alpha\) to the horizontal. A light inextensible string passes over a smooth pulley at the top of the plane and connects \(A\) to a particle \(B\) of mass \(M\) hanging freely (where \(M > m\sin\alpha\)). (a) Show that the acceleration is \(\dfrac{(M - m\sin\alpha)g}{M + m}\). (b) Show that the tension is \(\dfrac{Mmg(1 + \sin\alpha)}{M + m}\). (c) Verify that when \(\alpha = 90°\), the results reduce to the standard Atwood machine formulas.

Particle \(A\) of mass \(4\) kg lies on a rough horizontal table, \(5\) m from the edge. The friction force on \(A\) is \(8\) N. A light inextensible string passes over a smooth pulley at the edge and connects to particle \(B\) of mass \(6\) kg, hanging \(2\) m above the floor. The system is released from rest. (a) Show that the acceleration is \(5.08\) m/s\(^2\). (b) Find the speed when \(B\) hits the floor. (c) After \(B\) hits the floor, the string goes slack. Find how much further \(A\) travels before coming to rest. (d) Does \(A\) reach the edge of the table?

y1ht1.questionText: Define the null hypothesis, \(H_0\), in the context of a hypothesis test.
Define the alternative hypothesis, \(H_1\), in the context of a hypothesis test.
A coin is suspected of being biased towards heads. State suitable null and alternative hypotheses for a test of this claim, defining any parameters you use.
Define the significance level of a hypothesis test.
Explain what it means to carry out a hypothesis test at the 5% significance level.
Explain the difference between a one-tailed test and a two-tailed test.

A teacher believes that a new teaching method has changed the proportion of students passing an exam, but is unsure whether it has increased or decreased. State whether this test is one-tailed or two-tailed, and justify your answer.
Define the term 'test statistic' in the context of a hypothesis test.
Explain what it means to (a) reject \(H_0\), and (b) not reject \(H_0\).

A board-game player suspects that a six-sided die is biased so that it lands on 6 less often than expected. Let \(p\) be the probability of rolling a 6. Write down suitable hypotheses \(H_0\) and \(H_1\) for a test of this claim.

A manufacturer claims that 10% of the light bulbs it produces are defective. An inspector suspects the true proportion is higher than 10%. She tests a random sample of 30 light bulbs. (a) State suitable hypotheses for this test, defining any parameters used. (b) State whether this is a one-tailed or two-tailed test, giving a reason.

A supermarket claims that 30% of its customers use self-checkout. A researcher wants to test whether the true proportion differs from 30%. (a) Write down suitable hypotheses. (b) State whether the test is one-tailed or two-tailed. (c) The researcher uses a 5% significance level. State what this means in context.
Explain why, in a hypothesis test, we test \(H_0\) rather than trying to prove \(H_1\) directly.

A hypothesis test is carried out with \(H_0 : p = 0.2\) and \(H_1 : p > 0.2\), where \(p\) is the proportion of faulty items in a production line. The test results in \(H_0\) being rejected at the 5% significance level. Write a conclusion in context.
In a hypothesis test at the 5% significance level, the p-value is found to be 0.032. State, with a reason, the conclusion of the test.
In a hypothesis test at the 1% significance level, the p-value is found to be 0.038. State, with a reason, the conclusion of the test.
Define a Type I error in the context of a hypothesis test.

A company claims that 25% of its customers are repeat buyers. A test is carried out at the 5% significance level with \(H_0 : p = 0.25\) and \(H_1 : p > 0.25\). (a) Describe, in context, what a Type I error would mean. (b) State the probability of a Type I error.

A doctor claims that a new drug is effective for more than 60% of patients. A hypothesis test is carried out at the 5% significance level with \(H_0 : p = 0.6\) and \(H_1 : p > 0.6\). The test does not reject \(H_0\). Write a conclusion in context.

For each of the following scenarios, state whether \(H_1\) should use \(>\), \(<\), or \(\neq\). (a) A farmer suspects that fewer than 40% of his apple trees are affected by a disease. (b) A company wants to test whether a new process has changed the defect rate from the historical rate of 8%.
A student writes: 'The test shows that we accept \(H_0\).' Explain why this statement is incorrect and write a corrected version.

A hypothesis test is carried out and the p-value is found to be 0.03. (a) State the conclusion at the 5% significance level. (b) State the conclusion at the 1% significance level. (c) Explain why the conclusions differ.

A charity claims that 45% of adults donate to charity each year. A researcher believes the true proportion is lower. She surveys a random sample of 50 adults. (a) Define the parameter \(p\) in context. (b) State \(H_0\) and \(H_1\). (c) Identify the test statistic.

A weather forecaster claims that the probability of rain on any given day in April is 0.35. A meteorologist tests this at the 5% level with \(H_0 : p = 0.35\) and \(H_1 : p > 0.35\). The p-value is 0.012. Write the conclusion of the test in context.

A machine fills packets of cereal so that the probability of a packet being underweight is 0.05. After maintenance, the factory manager wants to test whether this probability has changed. (a) State \(H_0\) and \(H_1\), defining \(p\). (b) State whether the test is one-tailed or two-tailed, giving a reason. (c) The test is to be carried out at the 10% significance level. For a two-tailed test, explain how the significance level is used.

A test is carried out at the 2% significance level to determine whether a coin is biased towards tails, using \(H_0 : p = 0.5\) and \(H_1 : p < 0.5\), where \(p\) is the probability of heads. (a) Describe what a Type I error would mean in this context. (b) State \(P(\text{Type I error})\). (c) Explain why a smaller significance level reduces the chance of a Type I error.

A pharmaceutical company tests whether a new vaccine is effective for more than 70% of patients. The hypotheses are \(H_0 : p = 0.7\) and \(H_1 : p > 0.7\). The p-value from the test is 0.047. (a) At the 5% significance level, state the conclusion. (b) At the 1% significance level, state the conclusion. (c) Explain what the p-value of 0.047 represents.

Before an election, a political party claimed that more than 50% of voters would support them. A polling organisation surveys 100 randomly selected voters. (a) State suitable hypotheses for a test of the party's claim. (b) Of the 100 voters surveyed, 57 say they support the party. State the test statistic. (c) The p-value for this test is 0.097. At the 5% significance level, state the conclusion in context.

A spinner has five equal sections numbered 1 to 5. A player suspects that the spinner is biased so that it lands on 5 more often than it should. She spins it 40 times and it lands on 5 a total of 14 times. A hypothesis test is carried out at the 5% significance level and the p-value is found to be 0.0194. (a) State \(H_0\) and \(H_1\), defining \(p\). (b) State whether this is a one-tailed or two-tailed test. (c) State the test statistic. (d) Write a conclusion in context. (e) State what a Type I error would mean in this context.

Explain the relationship between the significance level of a hypothesis test and the probability of making a Type I error. In your answer, explain why choosing a very small significance level is not always desirable.
A test at the 5% significance level rejects \(H_0\). A student concludes: 'This proves that \(H_1\) is true.' Explain why this conclusion is not correct.
Discuss the trade-off between Type I and Type II errors when choosing the significance level for a hypothesis test. Use an example involving a medical test to illustrate your answer.

A hypothesis test is carried out on the same data at both the 5% and 1% significance levels. The hypotheses are \(H_0 : p = 0.3\) and \(H_1 : p > 0.3\). At the 5% level, \(H_0\) is rejected, but at the 1% level, \(H_0\) is not rejected. (a) What can you deduce about the p-value? (b) Explain why the two tests produce different conclusions. (c) Which conclusion should a researcher report, and why?

A student is testing whether a coin is fair. She flips it 20 times and gets 14 heads. She writes the following:

\(H_0 : p = 0.7\), \(H_1 : p = 0.5\)

Identify and correct all errors in the student's hypothesis test setup.

In a hypothesis test, the significance level is \(\alpha\). Explain why the probability of a Type I error is equal to \(\alpha\). You may assume that the test statistic has a known distribution under \(H_0\).

A tennis player claims that she wins 65% of her service games. Her coach suspects the true proportion is lower. Over a season, the coach records the outcomes of 50 randomly selected service games and finds that she won 27 of them. The coach carries out a hypothesis test at the 5% significance level and obtains a p-value of 0.041. (a) Define the parameter \(p\) in context. (b) State \(H_0\) and \(H_1\). (c) State whether the test is one-tailed or two-tailed. (d) State the test statistic. (e) Write the conclusion in context. (f) State the probability of a Type I error and describe what it would mean in context.

A standard treatment for a condition is effective for 40% of patients. A new treatment is developed and a doctor wants to test whether it is more effective. 80 patients are given the new treatment and 39 respond positively. A hypothesis test is carried out at the 10% significance level and the p-value is 0.0699. (a) State \(H_0\) and \(H_1\), defining \(p\). (b) State the test statistic. (c) Write the conclusion in context. (d) The doctor repeats the test at the 5% significance level. Without further calculation, state the conclusion and give a reason. (e) Describe what a Type I error would mean in this context and state its probability when testing at the 10% level.

A student carries out a hypothesis test with \(H_0 : p = 0.5\) and \(H_1 : p \neq 0.5\) at the 5% significance level. The p-value is 0.062. The student writes:

'Since 0.062 > 0.05, we accept \(H_0\). This proves the coin is fair.'

Identify and explain all the errors in the student's conclusion.

An ecologist believes that 20% of a particular species of bird nests in urban areas. After a change in land use, she suspects the proportion may have changed. She surveys 60 nesting sites and finds that 18 are in urban areas. A hypothesis test at the 5% significance level gives a p-value of 0.0735. (a) State \(H_0\) and \(H_1\), defining \(p\). (b) Explain why a two-tailed test is appropriate. (c) State the test statistic. (d) Write the conclusion in context. (e) State \(P(\text{Type I error})\) and explain its meaning. (f) If the ecologist repeated the test at the 10% significance level, state, with a reason, whether the conclusion would change.

A factory produces bolts and the historical defect rate is 5%. After installing new machinery, the quality manager wants to test whether the defect rate has decreased. A random sample of 100 bolts is taken and 2 are found to be defective. A hypothesis test at the 5% significance level gives a p-value of 0.118. (a) State \(H_0\) and \(H_1\), defining \(p\). (b) State whether this is a one-tailed or two-tailed test. (c) State the test statistic. (d) Write the conclusion in context. (e) The quality manager says: 'Since we did not reject \(H_0\), the defect rate is definitely still 5%.' Explain why this statement is incorrect. (f) If the significance level were changed to 10%, and the p-value remained 0.118, would the conclusion change? Justify your answer.

y1ht2.questionText: A manufacturer claims that 30% of items produced are defective. In a random sample of 10 items, only 1 is found to be defective. Under \(H_0: p = 0.3\), calculate \(P(X \le 1)\) where \(X \sim B(10, 0.3)\). Give your answer to 4 decimal places.

A shop owner believes that 40% of customers buy a particular product. In a random sample of 8 customers, none buy the product. Test at the 5% significance level whether there is evidence that the proportion is less than 0.4. State \(H_0\), \(H_1\), calculate the relevant probability, and state your conclusion.

A teacher claims that 20% of students pass a difficult test. After extra tuition, 5 out of 6 students pass. Test at the 5% significance level whether there is evidence that the pass rate has increased. Calculate \(P(X \ge 5)\) where \(X \sim B(6, 0.2)\).
A coin is tossed 10 times and 8 heads are observed. Test at the 5% significance level whether the coin is biased towards heads. State your hypotheses clearly.

Under \(H_0: p = 0.5\), a fair coin is tossed 5 times and 0 heads are observed. Calculate \(P(X = 0)\) where \(X \sim B(5, 0.5)\) and state whether this is significant at the 5% level for a one-tailed test (\(H_1: p < 0.5\)).

It is claimed that 10% of a population are left-handed. In a random sample of 7 people, 4 are left-handed. Test at the 5% significance level whether the proportion of left-handed people is greater than 10%. Calculate \(P(X \ge 4)\) where \(X \sim B(7, 0.1)\).

A company claims that 50% of its products are rated 'excellent' by customers. In a sample of 8 products, only 1 is rated 'excellent'. Test at the 5% significance level whether the proportion rated 'excellent' is less than 50%. Calculate \(P(X \le 1)\) where \(X \sim B(8, 0.5)\).

A farmer claims that 25% of his hens lay eggs every day. A sample of 6 hens is taken, and none lay an egg on a given day. Test at the 5% level whether the proportion is less than 25%. Calculate \(P(X = 0)\) where \(X \sim B(6, 0.25)\).
A coin is tossed 6 times and all 6 tosses result in heads. Test at the 1% significance level whether the coin is biased towards heads.

A driving school claims a 60% first-time pass rate. In a sample of 5 students, only 1 passes first time. Test at the 5% significance level whether the pass rate is lower than claimed. Calculate \(P(X \le 1)\) where \(X \sim B(5, 0.6)\).

A seed company claims that 80% of its seeds germinate. A gardener plants 20 seeds and only 12 germinate. She wishes to test whether the germination rate is lower than claimed. Using the cumulative binomial table, \(P(X \le 12) = 0.0321\) where \(X \sim B(20, 0.8)\). Carry out the test at the 5% significance level.

A company receives complaints about 5% of its deliveries. After a change in their delivery process, 4 out of 20 deliveries receive complaints. Test at the 5% significance level whether the complaint rate has increased. You are given that \(P(X \ge 4) = 0.0159\) where \(X \sim B(20, 0.05)\).

A doctor believes that a drug is effective for 70% of patients. In a clinical trial, 8 out of 15 patients respond to the drug. Test at the 5% significance level whether the drug is less effective than claimed. You are given \(P(X \le 8) = 0.1311\) where \(X \sim B(15, 0.7)\).

A factory produces light bulbs with a claimed defect rate of 10%. In a sample of 20 bulbs, none are defective. Test at the 1% significance level whether the defect rate is lower than claimed. You are given \(P(X = 0) = 0.1216\) where \(X \sim B(20, 0.1)\).
A coin is tossed 10 times and 9 heads are obtained. Test at the 5% significance level whether the coin is biased (in either direction). State your hypotheses and show your working.

A manufacturer claims that 30% of items produced are premium quality. A quality controller inspects 20 items and finds that 10 are premium quality.
