A multiple-choice test has 40 questions, each with 5 options. A student guesses every answer at random. Let \(X\) be the number of correct answers. (a) Find \(E(X)\). (b) Find \(\text{Var}(X)\). (c) Interpret \(E(X)\) in context.

A basketball player has a free-throw success rate of 0.72. She takes 25 free throws during a game. Let \(X\) be the number of successful free throws. Assuming \(X \sim B(25, 0.72)\), find the mean and standard deviation of \(X\).

A biologist models the number of marked fish recaptured in a sample of 60 fish as \(X \sim B(60, 0.1)\). (a) Find the mean and standard deviation of \(X\). (b) In the sample, 12 marked fish were recaptured. By comparing with the model, comment on whether this observation is unusual.
A random variable \(X \sim B(n, p)\). Given that \(E(X) = 12\) and \(\text{Var}(X) = 9.6\), find the values of \(n\) and \(p\).

A medical screening test is given to 300 patients. The probability that any individual patient tests positive is 0.03, and the number of positive results is modelled as \(X \sim B(300, 0.03)\). (a) Find \(E(X)\) and \(\text{Var}(X)\). (b) State two assumptions needed for this binomial model and comment on whether each is reasonable in this context.

A football team has a 0.6 probability of winning any given match, independently of other matches. Over a season of 38 matches, let \(X\) be the number of wins. (a) Find the mean and standard deviation of \(X\). (b) The team actually won 30 matches. Determine how many standard deviations this is from the mean and comment on the model.
A random variable \(X \sim B(n, p)\). Given that \(E(X) = 15\) and the standard deviation of \(X\) is 3, find \(n\) and \(p\).

An online retailer believes that 22% of website visitors make a purchase. Over a day, 150 visitors are recorded and 45 make a purchase. The retailer models the number of purchases as \(X \sim B(150, 0.22)\). (a) Find \(E(X)\) and \(\sigma\). (b) Determine whether the observed value of 45 is consistent with the model.
A random variable \(X \sim B(n, p)\). Given that \(E(X) = 18\) and \(\text{Var}(X) = 3.6\), find the values of \(n\) and \(p\).

A wildlife researcher surveys 200 quadrats in a meadow. She believes each quadrat has a 0.35 probability of containing a rare wildflower, independently of other quadrats. (a) Find the mean and standard deviation of the number of quadrats containing the wildflower. (b) She finds the wildflower in 84 quadrats. Assess whether her model is appropriate. (c) Suggest a reason why the independence assumption might not hold.
A random variable \(X \sim B(n, p)\). Given that \(E(X) = 20\) and the standard deviation of \(X\) is 4, find \(n\) and \(p\).

A hospital screens 250 newborns for a genetic condition. The condition has a known prevalence of 0.06. Let \(X\) be the number of newborns who test positive. (a) Assuming \(X \sim B(250, 0.06)\), find \(E(X)\), \(\text{Var}(X)\) and \(\sigma\). (b) Over many months, the hospital records an average of 15.5 positive results per 250 babies, with a variance of 13.95. By comparing \(\frac{\text{Var}(X)}{E(X)}\) for both the model and the data, assess whether the binomial model is appropriate.

A call centre receives calls, and the probability that any given call results in a sale is \(p\), independently of other calls. On a day when 80 calls are received, the number of sales is modelled as \(X \sim B(80, p)\). (a) Given that \(E(X) = 20\), find \(p\) and \(\text{Var}(X)\). (b) Find the standard deviation of \(X\) and interpret it in context. (c) Over 50 working days, the call centre records an average of 80 calls per day. The total number of sales over the 50 days is 1160. A manager claims this is evidence that the true probability of a sale has increased above 0.25. By calculating the expected total sales and comparing with the observation, evaluate the manager's claim.

y2am1.questionText: Prove by contradiction that \( \sqrt{2} \) is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that \( \sqrt{3} \) is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that \( \sqrt{5} \) is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that \( \sqrt{6} \) is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that \( \sqrt{7} \) is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that \( \sqrt{8} \) is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that \( \sqrt{10} \) is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that \( \sqrt{\tfrac{1}{2}} \) is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that \( \sqrt{\tfrac{2}{3}} \) is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that \( \sqrt{\tfrac{3}{5}} \) is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that \( \sqrt[3]{2} \) is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that \( \sqrt{2} + 1 \) is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that \( \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{3} \) is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that \( 3 + \sqrt{5} \) is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that if \( n^2 \) is even, then \( n \) is even.
Prove by contradiction that if \( n^2 \) is odd, then \( n \) is odd.
Prove by contradiction that if \( n^3 \) is even, then \( n \) is even.
Prove by contradiction that if \( n^2 \) is divisible by 3, then \( n \) is divisible by 3.
Prove by contradiction that if \( n^2 \) is divisible by 5, then \( n \) is divisible by 5.
Prove by contradiction that if \( 3n + 2 \) is odd, then \( n \) is odd.
Prove by contradiction that if \( 5n - 1 \) is even, then \( n \) is odd.
Prove by contradiction that if \( pq \) is odd (\( p, q \in \mathbb{Z} \)), then both \( p \) and \( q \) are odd.
Prove by contradiction that there is no greatest even integer.
Prove by contradiction (Euclid's argument) that there are infinitely many prime numbers.
Prove by contradiction that there is no smallest positive rational number.
Prove by contradiction that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that the product of a non-zero rational and an irrational is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that there are no integers \( x, y \) satisfying \( x^2 - y^2 = 10 \).
Prove by contradiction that \( \log_2 3 \) is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that \( \log_2 5 \) is irrational.
Prove by contradiction that \( (1 + \sqrt 2)^2 \) is irrational.

y2am2.questionText: Write \( 2 - \dfrac{1}{x + 1} \) as a single fraction in its simplest form.

y2am3.questionText: Express \( \dfrac{x^2 + 2}{(x-1)(x+1)} \) in partial fractions (note it is improper: first divide).

y2am4.questionText: Express \( \dfrac{11x^2 - 14x + 4}{(x-2)(2x-1)^2} \) as a sum of partial fractions.

y2am5.questionText: Use algebraic division to show that \( 2x^3 + 5x^2 - 2x - 5 = (2x + 5)(x^2 - 1) \), hence factorise fully.
Divide \( x^3 + x^2 + x - 2 \) by \( (x-1) \), stating the quotient and remainder.
Given that \( (x - 1) \) is a factor, factorise \( x^3 - 6x^2 + 11x - 6 \) completely.
Given that \( (x + 2) \) is a factor, factorise \( x^3 + x^2 - 4x - 4 \) completely.
Given that \( (x - 3) \) is a factor, factorise \( x^3 - 2x^2 - 5x + 6 \) completely.
Given that \( (x + 1) \) is a factor, factorise \( x^3 - 7x - 6 \) completely.
Given that \( (x + 3) \) is a factor, factorise \( 2x^3 + 5x^2 - 9x - 18 \) completely.
Given that \( (x - 2) \) is a factor, factorise \( 3x^3 - 7x^2 + 4 \) completely.
Divide \( x^4 + 2x^3 - 7x^2 - 8x + 12 \) by \( (x - 2) \), then factorise the quotient to fully factorise the quartic.
Divide \( x^4 - 16 \) by \( (x - 2) \), and hence factorise \( x^4 - 16 \) completely.
Use algebraic division to express \( \dfrac{x^3 + 2x^2 + 3}{x + 1} \) in the form \( ax^2 + bx + c + \dfrac{r}{x+1} \).
Express \( \dfrac{2x^3 + x^2 - x + 4}{x^2 + 1} \) in the form \( ax + b + \dfrac{cx + d}{x^2+1} \).

y2be1.questionText: Expand \( (1+x)^{-2} \) up to and including the term in \( x^3 \), stating the range of validity.
Expand \( (1+x)^{-1} \) up to and including the term in \( x^2 \), stating the range of validity.
Expand \( (1+x)^{-1} \) up to and including the term in \( x^4 \).
State the coefficient of \( x^5 \) in the expansion of \( (1+x)^{-1} \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{-2} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \).
Find the coefficient of \( x^6 \) in the expansion of \( (1+x)^{-2} \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{-3} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{-3} \) up to the term in \( x^4 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{-4} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{-4} \) up to the term in \( x^4 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{-5} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \).
Find the coefficient of \( x^3 \) in \( (1+x)^{-5} \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{1/2} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \), stating the validity.
Expand \( (1+x)^{1/2} \) up to the term in \( x^4 \).
Find the coefficient of \( x^2 \) in the expansion of \( (1+x)^{1/2} \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{-1/2} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{-1/2} \) up to the term in \( x^4 \).
Find the coefficient of \( x^3 \) in the expansion of \( (1+x)^{-1/2} \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{3/2} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{3/2} \) up to the term in \( x^4 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{-3/2} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{-3/2} \) up to the term in \( x^4 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{5/2} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{1/3} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{1/3} \) up to the term in \( x^4 \).
Find the coefficient of \( x^2 \) in \( (1+x)^{1/3} \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{-1/3} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{-1/3} \) up to the term in \( x^4 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{2/3} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{2/3} \) up to the term in \( x^4 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{-2/3} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{4/3} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{-4/3} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{1/4} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \).
Expand \( (1+x)^{3/4} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \).
State the range of values of \( x \) for which the binomial expansion of \( (1+x)^{-3} \) is valid.
State the range of values of \( x \) for which the binomial expansion of \( (1+x)^{1/2} \) is valid.
Use the binomial expansion of \( (1+x)^{1/2} \) up to the term in \( x^3 \) with \( x = 0.1 \) to estimate \( \sqrt{1.1} \) to 4 d.p.
Use the expansion of \( (1+x)^{-1/2} \) up to \( x^3 \) with \( x = 0.2 \) to estimate \( 1/\sqrt{1.2} \).
The coefficient of \( x^2 \) in the binomial expansion of \( (1+x)^n \) is 10. Given that \( n > 0 \), find the value of \( n \).

y2be2.questionText: Expand \( (4 + 3x)^{1/2} \) up to and including the term in \( x^2 \), stating the range of \( x \) for which the expansion is valid.
Expand \( (2+x)^{-1} \) up to and including the term in \( x^3 \), stating the range of validity.
Expand \( (2-x)^{-1} \) up to and including \( x^3 \).
Expand \( (3+x)^{-1} \) up to the term in \( x^3 \).
Expand \( (3-x)^{-1} \) up to the term in \( x^3 \).
Expand \( (4+x)^{-1} \) up to the term in \( x^3 \).
Find the coefficient of \( x^3 \) in the expansion of \( (2+x)^{-1} \).
Find the coefficient of \( x^4 \) in \( (1+2x)^{-2} \).
Find the coefficient of \( x^3 \) in \( (4+x)^{1/2} \).
Using the first three terms of the binomial expansion of \( (4+x)^{1/2} \), estimate \( \sqrt{4.1} \) to 4 d.p.
Use the first three terms of the binomial expansion of \( (9+x)^{1/2} \) with \( x = 0.2 \) to estimate \( \sqrt{9.2} \).
Use the first three terms of the expansion of \( (8+x)^{1/3} \) with \( x=0.5 \) to estimate \( \sqrt[3]{8.5} \).
State the range of values of \( x \) for which the expansion of \( (4 + 3x)^{1/2} \) as a binomial series converges.
State the range of \( x \) for which the expansion of \( (9+2x)^{-1/2} \) is valid.
Rewrite \( \sqrt{9+x} \) in the form \( 3(1+u)^{1/2} \) for a suitable \( u \), and state the range of validity.
Rewrite \( (4+3x)^{-1} \) in the form \( \tfrac{1}{4}(1+u)^{-1} \) and state the validity.
The binomial expansion of \( (4+bx)^{1/2} \) has the coefficient of \(x\) equal to 1. Find \(b\).
In the binomial expansion of \( (a+x)^{-1} \), the coefficient of \( x^2 \) is \( \tfrac{1}{64} \). Given \( a > 0 \), find \( a \).

y2be3.questionText: Express \( \dfrac{3x + 5}{(1 - x)(1 + 2x)} \) in partial fractions, then use the binomial theorem to find the expansion up to the term in \( x^2 \), stating the range of validity.
Express \( \dfrac{4x-1}{(1-x)(1-2x)} \) in partial fractions, then expand as a series in powers of \( x \) up to and including the term in \( x^2 \).
Express \( \dfrac{5x+1}{(1-x)(1+3x)} \) in partial fractions and hence expand up to \( x^2 \).
Express \( \dfrac{7x+2}{(1+x)(1+2x)} \) in partial fractions and hence expand up to \( x^2 \).
Express \( \dfrac{3}{(1-x)(1-2x)} \) in partial fractions and expand up to \( x^2 \).
Express \( \dfrac{4}{(1-x)(1+3x)} \) in partial fractions and expand up to \( x^2 \).
Expand \( \dfrac{8}{(1-x)(1+x)} \) as a series in \( x \) up to \( x^2 \).
Express \( \dfrac{x+4}{(1-x)(1+2x)} \) in partial fractions and hence expand up to \( x^2 \).
Express \( \dfrac{x}{(1+x)(1-2x)} \) in partial fractions and expand up to \( x^2 \).
Expand \( \dfrac{2}{(1+x)(1-x)} \) as a power series in \( x \) up to \( x^2 \).
Expand \( \dfrac{x+5}{(1-3x)(1+x)} \) as a power series in \( x \) up to \( x^2 \).
Express \( \dfrac{2x+7}{(1+2x)(1-x)} \) as a power series up to \( x^2 \).
Express \( \dfrac{3}{(1-x)(1+x)} \) as a power series up to \( x^4 \).
For a series expansion of \( \dfrac{1}{(1-x)(1-2x)} \), state the range of \( x \) for which the expansion is valid.
State the range of \( x \) for which the series expansion of \( \dfrac{1}{(1+x)(1-3x)} \) is valid.
State the range of \( x \) for which the series expansion of \( \dfrac{1}{(2-x)(1+4x)} \) is valid.
Find the coefficient of \( x^2 \) in the expansion of \( \dfrac{3}{(1-x)(1-2x)} \).
Find the coefficient of \( x^2 \) in \( \dfrac{4}{(1-x)(1+3x)} \).
Find the coefficient of \( x \) in the expansion of \( \dfrac{7x+2}{(1+x)(1+2x)} \).
Find the coefficient of \( x^2 \) in \( \dfrac{5x+1}{(1-x)(1+3x)} \).
Find constants \( A \) and \( B \) such that \( \dfrac{1 + 3x}{(1-x)(1+x)} = \dfrac{A}{1-x} + \dfrac{B}{1+x} \).
Given \( \dfrac{4}{(1-x)(1+3x)} \equiv \dfrac{A}{1-x} + \dfrac{B}{1+3x} \), find the coefficient of \( x^3 \) in its power-series expansion.
Find the coefficient of \( x^3 \) in the expansion of \( \dfrac{x}{(1+x)(1-2x)} \).
Use the expansion of \( \dfrac{3}{(1-x)(1-2x)} \) up to the term in \( x^2 \) (result: \( 3 + 9x + 21x^2 \)) with \( x = 0.1 \) to estimate \( \dfrac{3}{0.72} \).
A power-series expansion of \( \dfrac{5x+1}{(1-x)(1+3x)} \) has been computed. Deduce for what range of \( x \) this expansion converges.

y2bn.questionText: State the four conditions that must be satisfied for a random variable \(X\) to be modelled by a binomial distribution \(X\sim B(n,p)\).
A random variable \(X\) follows the distribution \(X\sim B(8,\,0.25)\). Find \(P(X=2)\), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.

A machine produces components and each component is independently defective with probability \(0.05\). A random sample of \(12\) components is taken and \(X\) is the number that are defective. Find \(P(X=1)\), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.

A fair six-sided die is rolled \(20\) times and \(X\) is the number of times a six is obtained. Explain why \(X\) can be modelled by a binomial distribution, referring to the four binomial assumptions, and state the distribution of \(X\).
A random variable \(X\) follows the distribution \(X\sim B(20,\,0.1)\). Find the expected value \(E(X)\).
A fair six-sided die is rolled \(6\) times. Let \(X\) be the number of sixes obtained, so \(X\sim B\!\left(6,\,\tfrac{1}{6}\right)\). Find \(P(X=2)\), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.

In a large population, \(30\%\) of people own a pet. A random sample of \(10\) people is taken and \(X\) is the number who own a pet, so \(X\sim B(10,\,0.3)\). Find \(P(X=3)\), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.
A random variable \(X\) follows the distribution \(X\sim B(7,\,0.4)\). Find \(P(X=0)\), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.

Each day, the probability that a particular bus is late is \(0.2\), independently of other days. Over a period of \(15\) days, let \(X\) be the number of days the bus is late, so \(X\sim B(15,\,0.2)\). Find the expected number of days the bus is late.

In a genetics experiment each offspring independently displays a recessive trait with probability \(\tfrac{1}{3}\). A sample of \(9\) offspring is observed and \(X\) is the number displaying the trait, so \(X\sim B\!\left(9,\,\tfrac{1}{3}\right)\). Find \(P(X=4)\), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.
A fair coin is tossed \(5\) times and \(X\) is the number of heads obtained, so \(X\sim B(5,\,0.5)\). Find \(P(X=2)\), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.
The random variable \(X \sim B(9,\, 0.2)\). Find \(P(X = 3)\), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.
In a large town, 45% of households own a pet. A random sample of 7 households is selected. Find the probability that exactly 4 of them own a pet, giving your answer to 4 decimal places.
The random variable \(X \sim B(8,\, 0.2)\). Find \(P(X = 0)\), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.
The random variable \(X \sim B(6,\, 0.65)\). Find \(P(X = 6)\), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.
The random variable \(X \sim B(40,\, 0.35)\). Find \(E(X)\).
The random variable \(X \sim B(50,\, 0.2)\). Find \(\mathrm{Var}(X)\).
A biased coin has probability \(0.06\) of landing on its edge. The coin is flipped 200 times, with each flip independent. Find the expected number of times the coin lands on its edge.
A netball player scores from each independent shot with probability 0.75. She takes 7 shots. Find the probability that she scores exactly 5 of them, giving your answer to 4 decimal places.
The random variable \(X \sim B(60,\, 0.15)\). Find \(E(X)\) and \(\mathrm{Var}(X)\).

A student claims that the number of red cars among the next 20 cars passing a fixed point can be modelled by a binomial distribution. State two assumptions that must be made for this model to be valid.

A spinner lands on green with probability 0.7 on each independent spin. It is spun 5 times and \(X\) is the number of times it lands on green. State the values of \(n\) and \(p\), and find the probability that it lands on green on all 5 spins, giving your answer to 4 decimal places.

A spinner is designed so that the probability of landing on green on any spin is \( 0.3 \). The spinner is spun \( 15 \) times. Let \( X \) denote the number of times it lands on green, so \( X \sim B(15, 0.3) \). Find the probability that the spinner lands on green at most \( 5 \) times.

In a certain town, \( 40\% \) of households recycle their glass. A random sample of \( 20 \) households is taken. Let \( X \) be the number that recycle their glass, so \( X \sim B(20, 0.4) \). Find the probability that at least \( 8 \) of the households recycle their glass.

A quiz has \( 12 \) multiple-choice questions, each with \( 4 \) equally likely options. A student guesses every answer. Let \( X \) be the number of correct answers, so \( X \sim B(12, 0.25) \). Find the probability that the student answers between \( 4 \) and \( 7 \) questions correctly, inclusive.

A machine fills bottles, and the probability that any bottle is underfilled is \( 0.05 \). A random sample of \( 18 \) bottles is checked. Let \( X \) be the number of underfilled bottles, so \( X \sim B(18, 0.05) \). Find the probability that at least one bottle is underfilled.

A factory finds that \( 10\% \) of the microchips it produces are defective. A batch of \( 25 \) microchips is inspected. Let \( X \) be the number of defective microchips, so \( X \sim B(25, 0.1) \). Find the probability that more than \( 3 \) microchips are defective.

A seed supplier states that \( 20\% \) of a certain type of seed fail to germinate. A gardener plants \( 30 \) of these seeds. Let \( X \) be the number that fail to germinate, so \( X \sim B(30, 0.2) \). Find the probability that fewer than \( 4 \) seeds fail to germinate.

A darts player hits the bullseye with probability \( 0.15 \) on each independent throw. He takes \( 40 \) throws. Let \( X \) be the number of bullseyes, so \( X \sim B(40, 0.15) \). Find the mean and the variance of \( X \).

A telesales operator finds that \( 36\% \) of calls result in a sale. In a shift she makes \( 50 \) independent calls. Let \( X \) be the number of sales, so \( X \sim B(50, 0.36) \). Find the standard deviation of \( X \), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.

A website finds that \( 4\% \) of visitors click on a particular advert. On a given day there are \( 200 \) independent visitors. Let \( X \) be the number who click on the advert, so \( X \sim B(200, 0.04) \). Find the expected number of visitors who click on the advert.

A basketball player makes each free throw independently with probability \( 0.45 \). She takes \( 16 \) free throws. Let \( X \) be the number she makes, so \( X \sim B(16, 0.45) \). Find the probability that she makes between \( 6 \) and \( 9 \) free throws, inclusive.

A train company finds that each of its trains arrives on time with probability \( 0.6 \), independently. On a route there are \( 14 \) trains in a day. Let \( X \) be the number that arrive on time, so \( X \sim B(14, 0.6) \). Find the probability that at most \( 10 \) trains arrive on time.

A new medical test gives a false positive with probability \( 0.08 \) for healthy people. A group of \( 22 \) healthy people is tested independently. Let \( X \) be the number of false positives, so \( X \sim B(22, 0.08) \). Find the probability that there is at least one false positive.

A fairground game is won with probability \( 0.25 \) on each independent attempt. A player has \( 60 \) attempts. Let \( X \) be the number of wins, so \( X \sim B(60, 0.25) \). Find the standard deviation of \( X \), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.
A fair coin is tossed \( 10 \) times. Let \( X \) be the number of heads obtained, so \( X \sim B(10, 0.5) \). Find the probability of obtaining more than \( 7 \) heads.

A machine produces electronic components, and each component is independently defective with probability \( 0.05 \). A quality-control inspector takes a random sample of \( 20 \) components. Let \( X \) be the number of defective components in the sample, so that \( X \sim \mathrm{B}(20, 0.05) \). Find the probability that the sample contains at least \( 2 \) defective components.

A basketball player has probability \( 0.7 \) of scoring with each free throw, and successive throws are independent. In a practice session she takes \( 12 \) free throws. Let \( X \) be the number she scores, so \( X \sim \mathrm{B}(12, 0.7) \). Find the probability that she scores at least \( 10 \) of the \( 12 \) free throws.

A biologist plants \( 15 \) seeds of a particular species. Each seed germinates independently with probability \( 0.8 \). Let \( X \) be the number of seeds that germinate, so \( X \sim \mathrm{B}(15, 0.8) \). Find the probability that between \( 11 \) and \( 13 \) seeds inclusive germinate.

In a production line, \( 10\% \) of items have a minor cosmetic flaw, independently of one another. A batch of \( 25 \) items is inspected. Let \( X \) be the number of flawed items, so \( X \sim \mathrm{B}(25, 0.1) \). Find the probability that between \( 2 \) and \( 5 \) items inclusive are flawed.
The random variable \( X \sim \mathrm{B}(18, 0.35) \). Find the mode of \( X \), that is the most likely value of \( X \).

A fair-ish spinner lands on red with probability \( 0.25 \) on each spin, independently. The spinner is spun \( 30 \) times, and \( X \) is the number of reds, so \( X \sim \mathrm{B}(30, 0.25) \). Find the most likely number of reds.
The random variable \( X \sim \mathrm{B}(11, 0.5) \). (a) Evaluate \( (n+1)p \) and explain what it tells you about the mode. (b) Hence find the mode(s) of \( X \).

In a large population, \( 2\% \) of items are defective. A random sample of \( n \) items is taken, and items are defective independently. Using \( P(X \ge 1) = 1 - P(X = 0) \), find the smallest sample size \( n \) for which the probability of obtaining at least one defective item exceeds \( 0.99 \).

A type of lightbulb has probability \( 0.15 \) of being faulty, independently of other bulbs. A shopkeeper wants the probability of finding at least one faulty bulb in a random sample of \( n \) bulbs to be greater than \( 0.95 \). Using \( P(X \ge 1) = 1 - P(X = 0) \), find the smallest such \( n \).

A call centre receives \( 200 \) calls in a shift, and each call independently results in a complaint with probability \( 0.03 \). Let \( X \) be the number of complaints, so \( X \sim \mathrm{B}(200, 0.03) \). Find \( \mathrm{E}(X) \) and \( \mathrm{Var}(X) \), and interpret \( \mathrm{E}(X) \) in context.

In a quiz, a student answers \( 40 \) independent multiple-choice questions, each correct with probability \( 0.65 \). Let \( X \) be the number answered correctly, so \( X \sim \mathrm{B}(40, 0.65) \). (a) Find \( \mathrm{E}(X) \) and \( \mathrm{Var}(X) \). (b) Find the standard deviation of \( X \) and comment on the spread relative to the mean.

A doctor models the number of patients in a family of \( 5 \) who catch a particular contagious illness during an outbreak as \( X \sim \mathrm{B}(5, p) \), where \( p \) is the probability an individual catches it. Comment, with reasons, on whether the binomial distribution is likely to be an appropriate model in this situation.

A coach models the number of successful penalties a player scores out of their next \( 20 \) attempts as \( X \sim \mathrm{B}(20, p) \), assuming a fixed success probability \( p \). The attempts are taken over a whole season, during which the player receives extra coaching and gradually improves. Comment, with reasons, on whether the binomial distribution is an appropriate model here.

A particular fault occurs independently in each component produced by a machine with probability \( 0.05 \). A random sample of \( n \) components is taken and \( X \) denotes the number of faulty components, so \( X \sim B(n, 0.05) \). Find the least value of \( n \) for which \( P(X \ge 1) \ge 0.99 \).

Each email received by a help desk is, independently, a complaint with probability \( 0.1 \). In a batch of \( n \) emails let \( X \) be the number of complaints, so \( X \sim B(n, 0.1) \). Find the least value of \( n \) for which the probability that the batch contains at least one complaint is at least \( 0.999 \).

A fair six-sided die is rolled \( n \) times. Let \( X \) be the number of sixes obtained, so \( X \sim B\!\left(n, \tfrac{1}{6}\right) \). Find the least number of rolls \( n \) for which the probability of obtaining at least one six is at least \( 0.95 \).
The random variable \( X \sim B(20, 0.15) \). Find \( P(X = 2 \mid X \ge 1) \), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.
The random variable \( X \sim B(12, 0.25) \). Find \( P(X = 3 \mid X \ge 2) \), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.
The independent random variables \( A \sim B(10, 0.3) \) and \( B \sim B(8, 0.4) \) are observed. Find the probability that \( A = 2 \) and \( B = 3 \), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.
The random variable \( X \sim B(15, p) \), where \( 0 < p < 0.5 \). Given that \( P(X = 0) = 0.0352 \), find the value of \( p \).
The random variable \( X \sim B(8, 0.2) \). Show that \( P(X \ge 1) = 0.8322 \), correct to 4 decimal places.

Each day a production line makes 5 items, and each item is, independently, defective with probability \( 0.1 \). A day is called a 'bad day' if at least one of that day's items is defective. Assuming days are independent, find the probability that, over a period of 7 days, exactly 2 are bad days. Give your answer to 4 decimal places.
The random variable \( X \sim B(n, 0.2) \). Given that \( P(X = 0) = 0.0687 \) correct to 4 decimal places, find the value of \( n \).

The independent random variables \( A \sim B(6, 0.5) \) and \( B \sim B(5, 0.3) \) are observed. Event \( S \) occurs if \( A \ge 4 \), and event \( T \) occurs if \( B \ge 2 \). Find the probability that at least one of the events \( S \) and \( T \) occurs, giving your answer to 4 decimal places.

A teacher records whether each of the 30 students in a class passes a driving theory test on their first attempt. She wishes to model the number of students who pass, \( X \), using a binomial distribution \( X\sim B(30,p) \). State the assumptions required for this binomial model to be valid, and discuss whether each assumption is likely to hold in this context.

A market researcher stops 20 people leaving a single supermarket and asks each whether they own a loyalty card for that supermarket. Let \( Y \) be the number who say 'yes'. The researcher models \( Y\sim B(20,0.6) \). Give two reasons why the binomial model may be unrealistic in this situation, referring to the binomial conditions.

Each time a particular machine is switched on there is a probability of \( 0.2 \) that it jams. The machine is switched on \( n \) times, and the switch-ons may be assumed independent. Find the least value of \( n \) for which the probability that the machine jams at least once exceeds \( 0.99 \).
The random variable \( X\sim B(10,0.3) \). Find \( P(X\geq 3 \mid X\geq 1) \), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.

A factory produces electronic components; each component is faulty independently with probability \( 0.05 \). Components are packed into boxes of \( 8 \). (a) Find the probability that a randomly chosen box contains at least one faulty component. (b) A crate contains \( 4 \) such boxes. Find the probability that at least one of the boxes in the crate contains at least one faulty component. Give each answer to 4 decimal places.
The random variable \( X\sim B(12,0.25) \). (a) Find \( P(X=3) \), giving your answer to 4 decimal places. (b) Hence find \( P(X=3 \mid X\leq 3) \), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.
The random variable \( X\sim B(n,p) \) has mean \( 8 \) and variance \( 4.8 \). Find the values of \( n \) and \( p \).

In a large batch of seeds, the number that germinate out of a tray, \( G \), is modelled by \( G\sim B(n,p) \). The mean number that germinate is \( 4.5 \) and the variance is \( 3.15 \). Find \( n \) and \( p \), and state how many seeds are sown in each tray.

A biased spinner lands on red with probability \( 0.15 \) on each spin. The spinner is spun \( n \) times, with the spins independent. Find the least number of spins required so that the probability of obtaining at least one red is greater than \( 0.95 \).

A basketball player attempts \( 15 \) free throws. The number scored, \( S \), is modelled by \( S\sim B(15,0.4) \). (a) State one assumption needed for this model, and comment on whether it is reasonable here. (b) Given that the player scores at least \( 5 \) throws, find the probability that she scores at least \( 8 \). Give your answer to 4 decimal places.

An archer hits the bullseye on each shot with probability \( 0.1 \), independently of other shots. (a) Find the least number of shots she must take so that the probability of hitting the bullseye at least once is greater than \( 0.9 \). (b) Hence, if she takes this number of shots, find the expected number of bullseyes.

y2cp.questionText: For two events \( A \) and \( B \), \( P(A\cap B)=0.18 \) and \( P(B)=0.45 \). Find \( P(A\mid B) \).
Events \( C \) and \( D \) satisfy \( P(C\cap D)=\tfrac{3}{20} \) and \( P(D)=\tfrac{1}{2} \). Find \( P(C\mid D) \).
Given that \( P(A)=0.37 \), write down the value of \( P(A') \).
Events \( A \) and \( B \) have \( P(A)=0.5 \), \( P(B)=0.4 \) and \( P(A\cap B)=0.15 \). Find \( P(A\cup B) \).

The two-way table shows the favourite drink and year group of 50 students.

| | Tea | Coffee | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Year 12 | 8 | 12 | 20 |
| Year 13 | 18 | 12 | 30 |
| Total | 26 | 24 | 50 |

A student is chosen at random. Find \( P(\text{Year 12} \cap \text{Tea}) \).

Using the same table of 50 students:

| | Tea | Coffee | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Year 12 | 8 | 12 | 20 |
| Year 13 | 18 | 12 | 30 |
| Total | 26 | 24 | 50 |

A student is chosen at random. Find \( P(\text{Coffee}) \).

The two-way table shows whether 80 people own a pet and whether they live in a flat or a house.

| | Pet | No pet | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Flat | 9 | 21 | 30 |
| House | 35 | 15 | 50 |
| Total | 44 | 36 | 80 |

A person is chosen at random. Given that they live in a house, find the probability that they own a pet.

Using the same pet/housing table:

| | Pet | No pet | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Flat | 9 | 21 | 30 |
| House | 35 | 15 | 50 |
| Total | 44 | 36 | 80 |

Given that a randomly chosen person owns a pet, find the probability that they live in a flat.

A single card is drawn from a standard pack of 52 cards. Let \( A \) be the event "the card is a King" and \( B \) be the event "the card is a Queen". State whether \( A \) and \( B \) are mutually exclusive, giving a reason.

A fair six-sided die is rolled once. Let \( A \) be the event "the score is even" and \( B \) be the event "the score is greater than 4". Determine whether \( A \) and \( B \) are mutually exclusive, giving a reason.
Events \( A \) and \( B \) are mutually exclusive with \( P(A) = 0.3 \) and \( P(B) = 0.45 \). Find \( P(A \cup B) \).
For events \( A \) and \( B \), \( P(A) = 0.5 \), \( P(B) = 0.4 \) and \( P(A \cap B) = 0.2 \). Find \( P(A \cup B) \).

(a) Predict the reaction time for a person aged \( 25 \). (b) Comment on the reliability of using this model to predict the reaction time of a person aged \( 70 \).

For each of the following pairs of variables, state whether you would expect the product moment correlation coefficient \( r \) to be positive or negative, giving a brief reason.

(b) A person's height and their shoe size.

y2cr.questionText: House-price data for years \( x \) is coded using \( p = \dfrac{x - 2000}{5} \). The regression line of \( y \) (mean price, \(\pounds\)0,000s) on \( p \) is \( y = 12 - 2p \). (b) Determine the constants and write down the model. (c) Predict \( y \) when \( x = 7 \).

y2cr.questionText: The period \( T \) seconds of a pendulum is modelled by \( T = a L^{n} \), where \( L \) is its length in metres. A plot of \( \log T \) (base 10) against \( \log L \) is linear with gradient \( 2 \) and intercept \( 0.602 \). (Although physics predicts \( n=\tfrac12 \), use the experimental fit.) (a) Find \( a \) and \( n \) and write the model. (b) Predict \( T \) when \( L = 2.5 \) m. (c) The experiment only used lengths between \( 0.5 \) m and \( 3 \) m; comment on predicting \( T \) for \( L = 20 \) m.

Two variables are coded as \( p = \dfrac{x - 10}{2} \) and \( q = \dfrac{y - 100}{5} \). The least-squares regression line of \( q \) on \( p \) is \( q = 2 + 4p \). (a) Find the regression line of \( y \) on \( x \). (b) Estimate \( y \) when \( x = 12 \).

A biologist suspects the count \( y \) over time \( x \) follows either \( y = a x^{n} \) or \( y = k b^{x} \). The correlation for \( \log y \) against \( \log x \) is \( 0.973 \), while for \( \log y \) against \( x \) it is \( 1.000 \). The fitted line of \( \log y \) (base 10) on \( x \) is \( \log y = 0.699 + 0.301x \). (a) State which model fits better and justify. (b) Find \( k \) and \( b \) and write down the model. (c) Predict \( y \) when \( x = 6 \).

A kiosk records the maximum daily temperature \( t \) (\(^{\circ}\)C) and the number of ice creams sold \( s \) on 7 days:

| \( t \) (\(^{\circ}\)C) | 16 | 18 | 20 | 22 | 24 | 26 | 28 |

(a) Interpret the value of \( r \) in this context. (b) Use the line to estimate sales when \( t = 25 \) and when \( t = 35 \); for each, state whether it is interpolation or extrapolation and comment on the reliability. (c) A student claims the data shows that higher temperature *causes* higher sales. Comment, suggesting one possible confounding factor.

y2cr.questionText:
For a sample of 6 adults, height \( h \) (cm) and weight \( w \) (kg) are recorded:

| \( h \) (cm) | 150 | 158 | 165 | 172 | 180 | 188 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \( w \) (kg) | 48 | 55 | 61 | 68 | 77 | 86 |

It is given that \( S_{hh} = 988.8 \), \( S_{ww} = 994.8 \) and \( S_{hw} = 989.8 \).
(a) Show that the product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = 0.998 \) to 3 significant figures. (b) Find the equation of the regression line of \( w \) on \( h \), giving coefficients to 3 significant figures. (c) Show that the line predicts a weight of \( 67.0 \) kg for a height of 170 cm, and state whether this is a reliable estimate.

The value \( V \) (\(\pounds\)) of a car is modelled by \( V = A b^{t} \), where \( t \) is its age in years. Data are recorded:

| \( t \) | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \( V \) | 18000 | 14040 | 10951 | 8542 | 6663 | 5197 |

Taking logarithms (base 10), the regression line of \( \log_{10} V \) on \( t \) is \( \log_{10} V = 4.26 - 0.108t \).
(a) Show that \( V = A b^{t} \) gives a linear relationship between \( \log_{10} V \) and \( t \). (b) Use the line to find \( A \) and \( b \) to 3 significant figures, and interpret \( b \). (c) Show that the model predicts a value of about \( \pounds 4090 \) when \( t = 6 \), and explain why a prediction at \( t = 12 \) would be unreliable.

A teacher records revision time \( x \) (hours) and test score \( y \) (out of 100) for 7 students:

| \( x \) (h) | 2 | 4 | 5 | 7 | 8 | 10 | 12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \( y \) | 31 | 40 | 46 | 55 | 58 | 70 | 79 |

The regression line of \( y \) on \( x \) is \( y = 21.2 + 4.81x \) with \( r = 0.999 \).
(a) Interpret the gradient in context. (b) Predict the score for a student who revises for 20 hours, and explain why this prediction should be treated with caution. (c) A newspaper concludes 'revising more guarantees a higher mark.' Critique this claim, referring to causation and to one limitation of the data.

Eight plots of land are studied; \( x \) is the amount of fertiliser (kg) and \( y \) is the yield (tonnes). Seven plots follow the data below, and an eighth plot recorded \( (8, 2) \):

| \( y \) | 3 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 9 | 11 | 12 |

For the seven plotted points, \( r = 0.998 \) and the regression line of \( y \) on \( x \) is \( y = 1.64 + 1.52x \).
(a) State, with a reason, whether the point \( (8, 2) \) is an outlier. (b) Describe the effect of including \( (8, 2) \) on the value of \( r \) and on the gradient of the regression line. (c) Recommend, with justification, whether the eighth plot should be included before reporting results.

y2cr.questionText:
The population \( P \) (thousands) of a town is modelled by \( P = A b^{t} \), where \( t \) is years after 2020:

| \( t \) | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \( P \) | 50.0 | 67.5 | 91.1 | 123 | 166 | 224 |

Taking logs base 10, the regression line of \( \log_{10} P \) on \( t \) is \( \log_{10} P = 1.70 + 0.130t \), with \( r = 1.00 \).
(a) Explain why the high value of \( r \) for the log-linear data supports an exponential model rather than a linear one. (b) Find \( A \) and \( b \) to 3 significant figures. (c) Show that the model predicts a population of about \( 302 \) thousand in 2026, and comment on the reliability of predicting the 2040 population.

A company records weekly advertising spend \( x \) (\(\pounds\) thousand) and sales \( y \) (\(\pounds\) thousand):

| \( x \) | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \( y \) | 12 | 17 | 21 | 26 | 30 | 35 |

Given \( S_{xx} = 17.5 \), \( S_{xy} = 79.5 \) and \( S_{yy} = 361.5 \):
(a) Show that the regression line of \( y \) on \( x \) is \( y = 7.60 + 4.54x \). (b) Show that this line predicts sales of \( \pounds 28000 \) when \( \pounds 4500 \) is spent on advertising, and state whether this is interpolation or extrapolation. (c) Find \( r \) to 3 significant figures and interpret it.

For a simple pendulum the period \( T \) (s) is thought to depend on length \( L \) (m) via a power model \( T = aL^{n} \). Measurements give:

| \( L \) (m) | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \( T \) (s) | 2.00 | 2.83 | 4.00 | 5.66 | 8.00 |

(a) Show that \( T = aL^{n} \) can be written as a linear relationship between \( \log_{10} T \) and \( \log_{10} L \). (b) The regression line of \( \log_{10} T \) on \( \log_{10} L \) is \( \log_{10} T = 0.301 + 0.500\log_{10} L \). Use it to find \( a \) and \( n \) to 3 significant figures. (c) Hence show the model gives \( T \approx 2.00\sqrt{L} \), and use it to show that \( L = 9 \) m gives \( T = 6.00 \) s. State whether this is interpolation or extrapolation.

Global mean temperature anomaly \( y \) (\(^{\circ}\)C) is recorded against year, coded as \( x \):

| year | 1960 | 1970 | 1980 | 1990 | 2000 | 2010 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \( y \) | 0.02 | 0.05 | 0.18 | 0.35 | 0.55 | 0.72 |

The regression line of \( y \) on (year) is \( y = -29.0 + 0.0148(\text{year}) \) and \( r = 0.982 \).
(a) Interpret \( r \) and the gradient in context. (b) Use the line to estimate the anomaly in 2020, stating whether it is interpolation or extrapolation, and comment on reliability. (c) A commentator says the model 'proves' that the passage of time causes warming. Explain why the regression cannot establish this, and suggest a more plausible underlying cause.

A culture of bacteria has count \( N \) at time \( t \) hours, modelled by \( N = A b^{t} \):

Find and classify the stationary point of \( y = x^2 + \tfrac{1}{x} \) for \(x>0\).
Classify the stationary point of \( y = e^x - x \).
Find and classify stationary points of \( y = x^3 + 3x^2 - 9x + 5 \).
Classify the stationary points of \( y = x^2 e^{-x} \).
Classify the stationary point of \( y = \tfrac{\ln x}{x} \) for \(x>0\).
A particle's displacement is \( s = t^3 - 6t^2 \). Find its acceleration at \(t = 3\).
A particle moves so that \( s = 4\sin 2t \). Find its acceleration at \( t = 0 \).
Show that \( s = A\cos(\omega t) \) satisfies \( s'' + \omega^2 s = 0 \).
Classify the stationary points of \( y = -x^3 + 3x^2 \).
Analyse the concavity and find inflection points of \( y = x + \sin x \) on \([0, 2\pi]\).
Find the point of inflection of \( y = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2 \).
State the difference between a stationary point and a point of inflection.
Find and classify stationary points of \( y = 3x^4 - 4x^3 \).
Classify the stationary point of \( y = (x-2)^3 \).
A sheet of card \(12\times 12\) has squares of side \(x\) removed from each corner, then folded into a box. Find the value of \(x\) that maximises volume.
A closed cylinder has volume \( 1000 \) cm³. Find the radius that minimises its surface area.
Classify stationary points of \( y = x^3 - 6x \).
Find \( \tfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} \) for \( y = \cos^2 x \).
Find and classify stationary points of \( y = x^4 + 4x^3 - 2 \).
Find the minimum value of \( y = x^2 + \tfrac{16}{x} \) for \(x>0\).
Find and classify the stationary points of \( y = x^5 - 5x \).
Find \( \tfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} \) for \( y = e^x\sin x \).
Find \( \tfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} \) for \( y = (2x+1)^5 \).
Find the second derivative of \( y = \sin x + \sin 2x \).
Find \( \tfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} \) for \( y = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}} \).
Find \( \tfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} \) for \( y = \ln(x^2+1) \).
Find and classify stationary points of \( y = x^3 - 2x^2 - x + 2 \).
For \(y = x^3 + x\), determine the intervals on which the function is increasing.
On what intervals within \([0, 2\pi)\) is \( y = \sin x \) concave up?
State the second-derivative test for classifying stationary points.

y2df10.questionText: The side of a cube is increasing at a rate of \(0.2\) cm/s. Find the rate at which the volume is increasing when the side length is \(5\) cm.
The radius of a circle is increasing at \(2\) cm/s. Find the rate at which its area is increasing when \(r = 5\) cm.
The radius of a circle is increasing at \(3\) cm/s. Find the rate at which its circumference is increasing.
A circle's area is increasing at \(50\pi\) cm²/s. Find the rate at which its radius is increasing when \(r=5\) cm.
A circular pond is evaporating so that its radius decreases at \(0.5\) cm/s. Find the rate at which its area is decreasing when \(r=10\) cm.
The radius of a sphere is increasing at \(3\) cm/s. Find the rate at which the volume is increasing when \(r=4\) cm.
The radius of a sphere is increasing at \(0.5\) cm/s. Find the rate at which the surface area is increasing when \(r=3\) cm.
A spherical balloon is inflated at \(100\pi\) cm³/s. Find the rate of change of radius when \(r=5\) cm.
A spherical balloon is inflated at \(400\pi\) cm³/s. Find the rate at which its surface area is increasing when \(r=10\) cm.
The side of a cube is increasing at \(0.4\) cm/s. Find the rate at which the surface area is increasing when \(x=6\) cm.
The side of a square is increasing at \(2\) cm/s. Find the rate of increase of the perimeter.
The side of a square is increasing at \(3\) cm/s. Find the rate of increase of area when side is \(4\) cm.
A cube's volume is increasing at \(48\) cm³/s. Find the rate of change of the side length when \(x = 4\) cm.
A cylinder with fixed height \(10\) cm has its radius increasing at \(0.5\) cm/s. Find the rate of change of volume when \(r=3\) cm.
A cylinder of fixed radius \(4\) cm has its height increasing at \(2\) cm/s. Find the rate of volume change.
Water is poured into a cone (apex down) at \(10\) cm³/s. The cone has radius-to-height ratio \(1:2\). Find the rate at which the water level rises when \(h = 4\) cm.
Water flows into a cone at \(2\) cm³/s. The cone has \(r:h = 1:3\). Find \(dh/dt\) when \(h=6\) cm.
Water drains from a cylinder of radius \(10\) cm at \(5\pi\) cm³/s. Find the rate of decrease of water depth.
A \(10\) m ladder leans against a wall. The top slides down at \(0.2\) m/s. Find the rate at which the foot moves away when the foot is \(6\) m from the wall.
A \(5\) m ladder leans against a wall. The top slides down at \(0.3\) m/s. Find \(dx/dt\) when foot is \(3\) m away.
Oil spreads in a circular patch with radius increasing at \(4\) cm/min. Find the rate of increase of area when \(r=50\) cm.
A particle's displacement is \( s = 3t^2 - t^3 \). Find its velocity at \(t=2\).
A particle's displacement is \( s = 2t^3 - 5t^2 \). Find its acceleration at \(t = 3\).
A rectangle has length increasing at \(2\) cm/s and width at \(3\) cm/s. Find the rate of change of area when length = 10, width = 6 cm.
A sphere's surface area is decreasing at \(16\pi\) cm²/s. Find the rate of change of radius when \(r = 4\) cm.
An ice cube melts uniformly so that its surface area decreases at \(12\) cm²/s. Find the rate of change of volume when the side is \(5\) cm.
A particle's displacement is \( s = t e^{-t} \). Find its velocity at \(t = 1\).
A ball's height above ground is \( h = 20t - 5t^2 \). Find its velocity at \(t=1\).
For \( h = 20t - 5t^2 \), find the maximum height reached.
A lamp-post is \(5\) m tall. A \(2\) m tall person walks away from it at \(1\) m/s. Find the rate at which the tip of their shadow moves.
A lamp is \(6\) m tall; a \(1.5\) m person walks away at \(2\) m/s. Find the rate at which the shadow length increases.
An equilateral triangle has side length increasing at \(1\) cm/s. Find the rate of change of area when the side is \(4\) cm.
A sector has angle \(\pi/3\) rad and radius increasing at \(1\) cm/s. Find the rate of area change when \(r=6\) cm.
A sector has fixed radius \(10\) cm and angle increasing at \(\pi/12\) rad/s. Find the rate of area change.
A rectangle has area \(60\) cm² (fixed). Width increases at \(2\) cm/s. Find the rate of change of length when width = 4 cm.
An ice cube melts so its volume decreases at \(6\) cm³/s. Find \(dx/dt\) when \(x = 3\) cm.
A boat is \(3\) km from a straight shore, pulled along a rope at \(2\) km/h. Find the rate of change of the angle \(\theta\) between the rope and shore when the rope is 5 km long.
Gas obeys \(PV = 100\). Pressure increases at \(4\) Pa/s. Find \(dV/dt\) when \(V = 20\).
A hemispherical bowl has radius increasing at \(0.2\) cm/s. Find the rate of change of its volume when \(r = 3\) cm.
A cooling object's temperature satisfies \( T = 80e^{-0.1t} + 20 \). Find \(dT/dt\) when \(T = 60\).
A population satisfies \( P = 100e^{0.05t} \). Find \(dP/dt\) when \(P = 200\).
A sample satisfies \( N = 500 e^{-0.02t} \). Find \(dN/dt\) in terms of \(N\).
An equilateral triangle has area increasing at \(3\sqrt{3}\) cm²/s. Find \(ds/dt\) when \(s = 6\) cm.
A ball falls so that \(s = 5t^2\). Find its velocity at \(t=2\) s.
A cylinder has \(r=3\) cm increasing at \(0.2\) cm/s, and height \(h=5\) cm increasing at \(0.5\) cm/s. Find \(dV/dt\).
Water fills a cone (apex down) with semi-vertical angle \(\tan^{-1}(1/2)\). Find \(dV/dh\) when \(h = 4\) cm.
A stone drops into water and creates a circular ripple whose radius grows at \(0.5\) m/s. Find the rate of area change when \(r=3\) m.
A sphere is expanding so that its volume doubles every \(5\) s. Find the rate of volume change when \(V = 100\) cm³.
A cloud mass \(m\) grows according to \( m = 2e^{0.3t} \). Find \(dm/dt\) when \(m = 8\).
A spherical snowball melts so that \(dV/dt = -k\cdot S\) for positive constant \(k\). Show \(dr/dt\) is constant.
A square pyramid has height \(h\) fixed at 6 and base side \(x\) increasing at \(0.5\) cm/s. Find rate of volume change when \(x = 4\).
A rectangle has fixed perimeter \(40\) cm. Its width increases at \(2\) cm/s. Find the rate of area change when \(w = 8\).
Water flows into a cylindrical tank of radius \(2\) m at \(4\pi\) m³/min. Find the rate at which water level rises.
Boat A moves north at \(15\) km/h, Boat B moves east from same starting point at \(20\) km/h. Find rate of separation when both have travelled \(1\) hour.
A right triangle has legs \(a\) and \(b\). \(a\) increases at 1 cm/s, \(b\) decreases at 2 cm/s. Find the rate of change of the hypotenuse when \(a=3, b=4\).
Coffee temperature \( T = 20 + 60e^{-0.1t} \). Find \(dT/dt\) at \(t=10\).
A bacterial culture has size \( N = 50\cdot 2^{t/3} \). Find \(dN/dt\) at \(t=0\).
Write the rate of change of circle area \(A = \pi r^2\) in terms of \(dr/dt\).
Write \(dV/dt\) for a sphere in terms of \(r\) and \(dr/dt\).
A tray's temperature \(T = 180 - 160e^{-0.2t}\). Find \(dT/dt\) at \(t=0\).
A ship sails north at \(5\) km/h. A receiver on shore is \(2\) km east of the starting point. Find rate at which the straight-line distance between them changes at \(t=1\) h.
A bar's length varies with temperature: \(L = 100 + 0.01T\). If \(T\) increases at \(2\) °C/min, find \(dL/dt\).
Water fills a rectangular trough (\(1\) m wide, \(3\) m long) at \(6\) litres/min. Find the rate at which water depth rises. (\(1\) L = \(0.001\) m³.)
A kite is rising vertically at \(2\) m/s; horizontal distance from observer is fixed at \(100\) m. Find the rate at which the string length changes when string = \(150\) m.

A plane flies horizontally at \(500\) km/h at altitude \(5\) km. Find the rate at which its distance from an observer on the ground is increasing when the plane is directly \(12\) km (horizontal) from the observer.
Charge on a capacitor: \( Q = 5 e^{-0.1t} \) coulombs. Find the current \(i = -dQ/dt\) at \(t=10\) s.
Sand pours at \(30\) cm³/s onto a cone-shaped pile whose height always equals the base radius. Find \(dh/dt\) when \(h=10\) cm.
A lighthouse beacon \(1\) km from shore revolves at \(\pi\) rad/s. Find the speed at which the light hits a point on the shore \(2\) km from the lighthouse's closest point.
A tree's height \(h = 20 - 18e^{-0.1t}\) m. Find \(dh/dt\) when \(h = 10\).
Water pours into a cone (apex down) at \(4\) cm³/s. Cone has semi-vertical angle \(\tan^{-1}(1/4)\). Find the rate at which the water's surface area changes when \(h = 8\) cm.
State the chain-rule identity linking \(\tfrac{dQ}{dt}\), \(\tfrac{dQ}{dx}\) and \(\tfrac{dx}{dt}\).

y2fg1.questionText: Sketch \( y = |2x - 3| - 4 \); state the vertex, both x-intercepts and the y-intercept.
Sketch \( y = 5 - |x| \); state the vertex (which is a maximum), the x-intercepts, the y-intercept and the range.
Sketch \( y = |x - 1| - 3 \); state the vertex, x-intercepts, y-intercept and the range.
Sketch \( y = 4 - |x + 2| \); state the maximum point, the x-intercepts, the y-intercept and the range.
Sketch \( y = |2x + 1| - 5 \); state the vertex, both x-intercepts and the y-intercept.
Sketch \( y = 2|x - 3| - 4 \); state the vertex, both x-intercepts and the y-intercept.
Sketch \( y = 8 - 2|x + 1| \); state the maximum, x-intercepts, y-intercept and range.
Sketch \( y = |x - 5| + 2 \); state the vertex, y-intercept and range. Explain why the graph has no x-intercepts.
Sketch \( y = |2x^2 - 8| \); state the x-intercepts, the y-intercept and the coordinates of the local maximum.
Sketch \( y = |x^2 - 6x + 8| \); state the x-intercepts, the y-intercept and the coordinates of the local maximum between them.
Sketch \( y = |2x^2 - 5x - 3| \); state x-intercepts, y-intercept and the local maximum between the x-intercepts.
Sketch \( y = |16 - x^2| \); state intercepts and the coordinates of the local maximum.
State the range of \( y = |x^2 - 4| - 3 \) for \( x \in \mathbb{R} \).
State the range of \( y = |x^2 - 4x + 5| - 2 \) for \( x \in \mathbb{R} \).
State the range of \( y = 2 - |x^2 - 6x + 5| \) for \( x \in \mathbb{R} \).
Find the values of \(k\) for which \( |x^2 - 6x + 8| = k \) has exactly 4 distinct real solutions.
Find the value of \(k\) for which \( |x^2 - 4x + 3| = k \) has exactly 3 distinct real solutions.
Find the minimum value of \( f(x) = x^2 + 2|x - 2| \), and the value of \(x\) where it occurs.
State the range of \( y = |2x - 1| - 3 \) for \( x \in \mathbb{R} \).
Find the number of distinct real solutions of \( 2x^2 = |2x - 3| \), giving the solutions exactly.
By sketching \( y = x^2 - 2 \) and \( y = |x + 1| \) on the same axes, find the values of \(x\) for which \( x^2 - 2 \ge |x + 1| \), giving exact answers.
Find the points of intersection of \( y = x^2 - 1 \) and \( y = |2x - 3| \), giving exact answers.
State the number of distinct real solutions to \( x^2 - 4|x| + 3 = 0 \), and list them.
For what values of \(k\) does \( |x^2 - 6x + 5| = k \) have (a) 4 solutions, (b) 3 solutions, (c) 2 solutions, (d) no solutions?
How many distinct real solutions does \( x^2 + |x| = |2x - 1| \) have? Find them exactly.
Sketch \( y = |x^2 - 4x - 5| \); state the intercepts and the coordinates of the local maximum between the x-intercepts.

y2fg2.questionText: The diagram shows a curve. State, with a reason, whether the curve represents a function of \(x\).
Does the graph shown (a sideways parabola \(x = y^2\)) represent a function of \(x\)? Justify your answer.
The diagram shows the circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 9\). Explain why this does not define \(y\) as a function of \(x\).
The diagram shows \(y = \sqrt{9 - x^2}\). State, with a reason, whether this is a function.
Does the cubic curve \(y = x^3 - 3x\) define \(y\) as a function of \(x\)? Justify your answer.

The diagram shows a relation in which the input \(x = 2\) is mapped to both \(y = 1\) and \(y = 3\). State why this relation is not a function and explain what single change to the diagram would make it one.
The diagram shows the V-shaped graph \(y = |x|\). State whether this is a function.
Sketch \(f(x) = 2x - 3\) on the domain \(-1 \le x \le 4\). State the range.
Sketch \(f(x) = 5 - x\) on \(0 \le x \le 5\). State the range.
Sketch \(f(x) = x^2 + 2\) on \(-3 \le x \le 3\). State the range.
Sketch \(f(x) = x^2 + 4x + 5\) on \(-3 \le x \le 1\). State the range.
Sketch \(f(x) = 6 - x^2\) on \(-2 \le x \le 3\). State the range.
Sketch \(f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 8\) on \(0 \le x \le 5\). State the range.
Sketch \(f(x) = \sin x\) for \(0 \le x \le \pi\). State the range.
Sketch \(f(x) = \cos x\) for \(0^\circ \le x \le 360^\circ\). State the range.
Sketch \(f(x) = 2\sin x + 1\) on \(0 \le x \le 2\pi\) and state the range.
Sketch \(f(x) = |x - 2|\) on \(-1 \le x \le 5\) and state the range.
Sketch the piecewise function \(f(x) = \begin{cases} x & 0 \le x < 3 \\ 6 - x & 3 \le x \le 6 \end{cases}\) and state the range.
Sketch \(f(x) = e^x\) for \(0 \le x \le \ln 5\). State the range.
The diagram shows the graph of \(y = 3x + 1\). State the domain and the range.
The graph shows \(f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 5\). State the domain and the range.
The graph shows \(f(x) = \dfrac{x + 2}{x + 1}\) for \(x \ge 0\). State the range.
The graph shows \(f(x) = \sqrt{x + 4}\). State the domain and the range.
The graph shows \(f(x) = 4 - |x|\). State the largest domain (in \(\mathbb R\)) for which \(f(x) \ge 0\), and the range on this domain.
The graph shows \(f(x) = \sqrt{16 - x^2}\) for \(a \le x \le b\). State the values of \(a\) and \(b\), and the range.
The graph shows \(f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x^2 + 1}\). State the range.
The graph shows \(f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x - 3}\) drawn over the domain \(x > a\). State the value of \(a\).
The graph shows \(f(x) = \sqrt{x - 5}\) drawn over the domain \(x \ge a\). State \(a\) and the range.
The graph shows \(f(x) = \sqrt{25 - x^2}\) for \(a \le x \le b\). Find \(a\) and \(b\), and state the range.
The graph shows \(f(x) = \ln(x + 2)\) drawn over the domain \(x > a\). State \(a\) and the range.
The graph shows \(f(x) = \sqrt{(x-1)(x-4)}\) drawn over its natural domain. State the domain and the range.
The graph shows \(f(x) = \sqrt{x^2 - 4}\). State the domain and the range.
\(h(x) = \sqrt{x + 3}\), \(x \in \mathbb R\). Give a restricted domain that makes \(h\) a (real-valued) function.
\(k : x \mapsto \tan x\), \(x \in \mathbb R\). Give an example of a single-interval domain on which \(k\) is a function.
\(m(x) = \dfrac{1}{x^2 - 9}\). What is the largest bounded single-interval domain on which \(m\) is a function?
The mapping \(x \mapsto \pm \sqrt{x}\) takes \(x = 4\) to both \(2\) and \(-2\). Suggest a restriction that turns this into a function.
\(f(x) = x^2\), \(x \in \mathbb R\). State a restricted domain on which \(f\) is one-to-one.
\(f(x) = \sin x\). Give a restricted domain on which \(f\) is one-to-one and its range is still \([-1, 1]\).
\(f(x) = \cos x\). Give a domain on which \(f\) is one-to-one and the range is \([-1, 1]\).
Find the range of \(f(x) = 2x + 5\) on \(-3 \le x \le 4\).
Find the range of \(f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 1\) on \(-1 \le x \le 5\).
Find the range of \(f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 1\) on \(3 \le x \le 8\).
Find the range of \(f(x) = e^x\) on \(-1 \le x \le 3\). Give exact endpoints.
Find the range of \(f(x) = \ln x\) on \(e \le x \le e^3\).
Find the range of \(f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x}\) on \(1 \le x \le 4\).
Find the range of \(f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x}\) on \(-2 \le x \le -1\).
Find the range of \(f(x) = \sqrt{x - 1}\) on \(1 \le x \le 10\).
Find the range of \(f(x) = \sin x\) on \(\tfrac{\pi}{6} \le x \le \tfrac{5\pi}{6}\).
Find the range of \(f(x) = 3\cos x - 1\) on \(0 \le x \le \pi\).
Find the range of \(f(x) = |x^2 - 4|\) on \(-3 \le x \le 3\).
Classify \(f(x) = 2x + 1\), \(x \in \mathbb R\), as one-to-one or many-to-one.
Classify \(f(x) = x^2\), \(x \in \mathbb R\), as one-to-one or many-to-one. Justify.
Classify \(f(x) = x^2\), \(x \ge 0\), as one-to-one or many-to-one.
Classify \(f(x) = x^3\), \(x \in \mathbb R\).
Classify \(f(x) = \sin x\) on \(\mathbb R\), and again on \([-\tfrac{\pi}{2}, \tfrac{\pi}{2}]\).
Classify \(f(x) = e^x\), \(x \in \mathbb R\).
Classify \(f(x) = |x|\), \(x \in \mathbb R\).
Classify \(f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x}\), \(x \ne 0\).
Given \(f(x) = 3x - 2\), find \(x\) such that \(f(x) = 19\).
Given \(f(x) = x^2 - 4\), find the values of \(x\) for which \(f(x) = 12\).
\(f : x \mapsto 2x^2 + 1\), \(x \ge 0\). Find \(x\) when \(f(x) = 51\).
\(f(x) = x^2 + bx + c\) has vertex at \((3, -4)\). Find \(b\) and \(c\).
\(f(x) = \dfrac{ax + b}{x + 1}\) has horizontal asymptote \(y = 2\) and passes through \((0, 3)\). Find \(a\) and \(b\).
Is \(f(x) = x^4 - 3x^2\) even, odd, or neither?
Is \(f(x) = x^3 - 4x\) even, odd, or neither?
Is \(f(x) = 2x + 1\) even, odd, or neither?
State the largest closed domain for \(f(x) = x^2\) so that the range is \([0, 9]\).
Determine whether \(f(x) = x^2\), \(x \in \mathbb R\) has an inverse. If not, give a restricted domain on which it does.

The diagram shows \(y = (x - 2)^2 - 1\). (a) Explain why \(f\) has no inverse on its natural domain \(\mathbb R\). (b) State the largest domain \(x \ge k\) on which \(f\) is one-to-one, and find \(f^{-1}\) on this domain.

y2fg3.questionText: \( f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x} \) \((x \ne 0)\) and \( g(x) = 2x + 5 \), \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( gf(x) = 6 \).
\( f(x) = 2x + 1 \) and \( g(x) = 3x - 4 \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 23 \).
\( f(x) = x^2 \) and \( g(x) = x + 5 \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 9 \).
Given \( f(x) = x^2 \) and \( g(x) = \sqrt{x} \) for \(x \ge 0\), find \( fg(x) \) and \( gf(x) \).
\( f(x) = x^2 \), \(x \in \mathbb R\), and \( g(x) = \dfrac{x}{x - 3} \) \((x \ne 3)\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 4 \).
\( f(x) = x^2 + 1 \) and \( g(x) = 3x - 2 \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 50 \).
\( f(x) = \dfrac{x^2}{16} \) and \( g(x) = 2x \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 5 \).
\( f(x) = \sin x \) and \( g(x) = 2x - \tfrac{\pi}{3} \). Solve \( fg(x) = \tfrac{1}{2} \) on the interval \( 0 \le x \le \pi \).
\( f(x) = 3x \) and \( g(x) = x - 1 \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( gf(x) = 14 \).
\( f(x) = x + 3 \) and \( g(x) = 2x \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 11 \).
\( f(x) = 4x - 3 \) and \( g(x) = x + 2 \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 9 \).
\( f(x) = x^2 \) and \( g(x) = x - 1 \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( gf(x) = 24 \).
\( f(x) = 2x + 1 \), \(x \in \mathbb R\), and \( g(x) = \sqrt{x} \) \((x \ge 0)\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 17 \).
\( f(x) = \log_{10} x \) \((x > 0)\) and \( g(x) = 3 - x \), \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 0 \).
\( f(x) = 2^x \) and \( g(x) = x^2 + 2x \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 8 \).
\( f(x) = 3x^3 \) and \( g(x) = 2x \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = gf(x) \).
\( f(x) = \dfrac{7}{3 - x} \) \((x \ne 3)\) and \( g(x) = x^2 + 3 \), \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = -14 \).
\( f(x) = 3x - 4 \) and \( g(x) = 2x + 5 \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( gf(x) = 6 \).
\( f(x) = ax + b \) with \(a > 0\). Given that \( ff(x) = 9x + 4 \) for all real \(x\), find the values of \(a\) and \(b\).
If \( f(x) = x^2 \), find \( ff(x) \).
\( f(x) = (x + 1)^2 \) and \( g(x) = 3x \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 16 \).
\( f(x) = \sqrt{x + 2} \) \((x \ge -2)\) and \( g(x) = x^2 - 1 \), \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 3 \).

\( f : x \mapsto x^2 + b \) and \( g : x \mapsto b - 3x \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\) (\(b\) is a constant). Given that \( gf(2) = -8 \), find the value of \( b \) and hence the value of \( fg(2) \).
\( f(x) = 2x \) and \( g(x) = x + 7 \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 20 \).
\( f(x) = x - 4 \) and \( g(x) = 5x \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( gf(x) = 25 \).
\( f(x) = x^2 \) and \( g(x) = 2x \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 36 \).
\( f(x) = 2x + 1 \) and \( g(x) = ax - 3 \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\) (\(a\) is a constant). Given that \( fg(x) = gf(x) \) for all real \(x\), find the value of \( a \).
\( f(x) = ax + 1 \) and \( g(x) = bx + 2 \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\) (\(a, b\) constants). Given \( fg(1) = 9 \) and \( gf(1) = 8 \), find all possible pairs \((a, b)\).
\( f(x) = e^x \) and \( g(x) = x^2 - 5 \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 1 \).
\( f(x) = x + 1 \) and \( g(x) = x^2 - 3 \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Find all values of \(x\) for which \( fg(x) = gf(x) \).
\( f(x) = x^2 + 1 \) with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve \( ff(x) = 5 \).
\( f(x) = \ln x \) \((x > 0)\) and \( g(x) = e^x - k \), where \(k\) is a constant. Given that \( fg(1) = 0 \), find \(k\), and hence solve \( fg(x) = \ln 5 \).
\( f(x) = ax + b \) and \( g(x) = x + c \), where \(a, b, c\) are constants with \(c \ne 0\). Find all values of \(a\) such that \( fg(x) = gf(x) \) holds for every real \(x\).
\( f(x) = \sqrt{x + a} \), with \(a\) a constant, and \( g(x) = x^2 - 1 \) for \(x \ge 0\). Given that \( fg(0) = 1 \), find \(a\), and state the largest possible domain of \( fg \).
\( f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x - 1} \) \((x \ne 1)\) and \( g(x) = 2x + a \), where \(a\) is a constant. Given \( fg(0) = \tfrac{1}{3} \), find \(a\), and hence solve \( fg(x) = -1 \).
\( f(x) = 3x + 1 \) and \( g(x) = x - 2 \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( gf(x) = 5 \).
\( f(x) = x - 1 \) and \( g(x) = 2x \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 7 \).
\( f(x) = x + 2 \) and \( g(x) = x^2 \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( gf(x) = 16 \).
Evaluate \( ff(2) \) where \( f(x) = 3x - 1 \).
\( f(x) = ax + b \) and \( g(x) = x^2 \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\) (\(a, b\) constants). Given that \( fg(2) = 7 \) and \( fg(-1) = 1 \), find the values of \(a\) and \(b\).
\( f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x} \) \((x \ne 0)\) and \( g(x) = x^2 - 1 \), \(x \in \mathbb R\). Find the largest possible domain and the range of \( fg(x) \).
\( f(x) = e^x \), \(x \in \mathbb R\), and \( g(x) = ax \), where \(a\) is a constant. Given that \( fg(2) = e^6 \), find \(a\), and hence solve \( gf(x) = 12 \). Give your answer in exact form.
\( f(x) = \sqrt{x} \) \((x \ge 0)\) and \( g(x) = x^2 + a \), where \(a\) is a constant. Given \( fg(2) = 3 \), find \(a\), and state the range of \( fg \) on \(x \in \mathbb R\).
\( f(x) = \sqrt{x + 3} \) \((x \ge -3)\) and \( g(x) = x^2 - 2 \) \((x \ge 0)\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 4 \).
\( f(x) = \ln x \) \((x > 0)\) and \( g(x) = x^2 \) \((x > 0)\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = 6 \).
\( f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x - 2} \) \((x \ne 2)\) and \( g(x) = x + 5 \), \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = \tfrac{1}{4} \).
With \( f(x) = 2x + 1 \) and \( g(x) = x^2 \), show that \( fg(x) \ne gf(x) \) as functions.
If \(f(x) = x + a\) and \(g(x) = x + b\), show that \(fg = gf\).

\( f(x) = \ln x \) \((x > 0)\) and \( g(x) = x - k \), \(x \in \mathbb R\), where \(k\) is a constant. Given that the natural domain of \( fg \) is \(x > 3\), find \(k\), and then solve \( fg(x) = \ln 2 \).
\( f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x} \) \((x \ne 0)\) and \( g(x) = x + 1 \), \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve \( fg(x) + gf(x) = 3 \), giving your answer in exact form.
\( f : x \mapsto \sqrt{x} \) \((x \ge 0)\) and \( g : x \mapsto \dfrac{1}{x - 1} \) \((x > 1)\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = \tfrac{1}{2} \) and state the range of \( fg(x) \).
For \(f(x) = 3x\) and \(g(x) = 2x - 1\), find \(fg(x)\) and \(gf(x)\).
\( f(x) = ax + b \) and \( g(x) = bx + a \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\) (\(a, b\) constants). Find all conditions on \(a\) and \(b\) such that \( fg(x) = gf(x) \) holds for every real \(x\).
For \(f(x) = \tfrac{1}{x+1}\) \((x \ne -1)\) and \(g(x) = x^2\), find \(fg(x)\) and state its domain.
\( f(x) = 2x + 3 \), \(x \in \mathbb R\). Solve \( fff(x) = ff(x) \).

\( f(x) = (x + a)^2 \), \(x \in \mathbb R\), and \( g(x) = x - 1 \), where \(a\) is a constant. Given that the minimum value of \( fg(x) \) is 0 and is attained at \(x = 3\), find \(a\), and hence solve \( fg(x) = 4 \).
\( f(x) = \log_3 x \) \((x > 0)\) and \( g(x) = x^2 + ax \), where \(a\) is a constant. Given that \( fg(3) = 3 \), find \(a\), and hence solve \( fg(x) = 2 \).
\( f(x) = \cos x \) and \( g(x) = 2x + \tfrac{\pi}{3} \). Solve \( fg(x) = -\tfrac{1}{2} \) on the interval \(0 \le x \le \pi\).
If \( f(x) = x + 1 \), find \( f^5(x) \) (the function composed with itself five times).
With \( f(x) = x + 1 \) and \( g(x) = 2x - 3 \), solve \(fg(x) = 5\).
\( f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x} \) \((x \ne 0)\) and \( g(x) = x^2 - 4 \), \(x \in \mathbb R\). Find the largest possible domain and the range of \( fg(x) \).
Give an example of two functions \(f, g\) where \(fg \ne gf\), and demonstrate that they differ.
Explain the notation \( (f \circ g)(x) \).
Is composition of functions associative? State the identity.
\( f(x) = x^2 - 1 \) and \( g(x) = \sqrt{x} \) \((x \ge 0)\). Solve the equation \( fg(x) = gf(x) \), stating any domain restrictions.
\( f(x) = 3x + 2 \) and \( g(x) = ax + b \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\) (\(a, b\) constants). Given that \( fg(x) = 6x + 5 \) for all \(x\), find the values of \(a\) and \(b\).
If \(f(x) = 1 - x\), find \(ff(x)\) and comment on the result.
\( f(x) = ax^2 + bx \) and \( g(x) = x - 1 \), both with \(x \in \mathbb R\) (\(a, b\) constants). Given \( fg(2) = 0 \) and \( fg(3) = 18 \), find the values of \(a\) and \(b\).

\( f(x) = x^2 - 3 \), \(x \in \mathbb R\), and \( g(x) = \dfrac{1}{x - k} \) \((x \ne k)\), where \(k\) is a constant. Given that \( gf(2) = 1 \), find \(k\), and hence solve the equation \( gf(x) = -1 \).
Explain why \(fg(x)\) might not be defined for some \(x\), giving a concrete example.

y2fg4.questionText: The function \( h \) is defined by \( h(x) = 2x^2 - 7, \; x \in \mathbb{R}, \; x \ge 0 \).  (a) Find \( h^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.  (b) Evaluate \( h^{-1}(43) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 2x + 3, \; x \in \mathbb{R} \). Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = ax + b, \; x \in \mathbb{R} \), where \( a \) and \( b \) are constants. It is given that \( f(2) = 1 \) and \( f(5) = 13 \).  (a) Find the values of \( a \) and \( b \).  (b) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.  (c) Solve the equation \( f(x) = f^{-1}(x) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 4 - x, \; x \in \mathbb{R} \).  (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.  (b) State what your answer to part (a) tells you about the function \( f \).

The functions \( f \) and \( g \) are defined by \( f(x) = 3x - 2, \; x \in \mathbb{R} \) and \( g(x) = \tfrac{1}{2}x + 5, \; x \in \mathbb{R} \).  (a) Find the composite function \( gf(x) \), simplifying your answer.  (b) Find \( (gf)^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.  (c) Verify that \( (gf)^{-1}(x) = f^{-1}g^{-1}(x) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{x}{2} - 3, \; x \in \mathbb{R} \).  (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.  (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(0) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 7 - 3x, \; x \in \mathbb{R} \).  (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.  (b) Solve the equation \( f(x) = f^{-1}(x) \).  (c) Hence write down the coordinates of the point where the graphs of \( y = f(x) \) and \( y = f^{-1}(x) \) intersect, and explain why this point lies on the line \( y = x \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{2x + 1}{3}, \; x \in \mathbb{R} \). Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 6 - 2x, \; x \in \mathbb{R}, \; 1 \le x \le 4 \).  (a) Find the range of \( f \).  (b) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.  (c) Explain why \( f^{-1} \) exists for this function.
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{1}{2}x + 4, \; x \in \mathbb{R} \).  (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.  (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(10) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = x^2, \; x \in \mathbb{R}, \; x \ge 0 \). Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = x^2 + 3 \), \( x \ge 0 \). Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = x^2 - 8x + 22 \), \( x \ge 4 \).  (a) Express \( f(x) \) in the form \( (x - a)^2 + b \).  (b) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.  (c) Solve the equation \( f^{-1}(x) = 9 \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = (x + 2)^2 - 5 \), \( x \ge -2 \).  (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.  (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(11) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 3x^2 + 1 \), \( x \ge 0 \). Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 5 \), \( x \ge 2 \).  (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.  (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(10) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 2x^2 + 4x + 3 \), \( x \ge -1 \).  (a) Express \( f(x) \) in the form \( a(x + b)^2 + c \).  (b) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 10 \), \( x \ge 3 \).  (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.  (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(5) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 20 - x^2 - 6x \), \( x \ge -3 \).  (a) Express \( f(x) \) in the form \( a - (x + b)^2 \).  (b) Explain why \( f \) has an inverse on this domain.  (c) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.  (d) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(4) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = x^2 - kx + 12 \), \( x \ge 3 \), where \( k \) is a constant. Given that the graph of \( y = f(x) \) has its minimum point at \( x = 3 \):  (a) Show that \( k = 6 \), and write \( f(x) \) in completed-square form.  (b) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.  (c) Solve the equation \( f^{-1}(x) = 7 \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 1 - (x - 3)^2 \), \( x \ge 3 \).  (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.  (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(-8) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{1}{x} \), \( x \ne 0 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Hence explain what is special about the function \( f \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{3x + 2}{x - 4} \), \( x \ne 4 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(5) \). (c) Solve the equation \( f(x) = f^{-1}(x) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{ax + 1}{x - 2} \), \( x \ne 2 \), where \( a \) is a constant. Given that \( f^{-1}(3) = 7 \): (a) show that \( a = 2 \). (b) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (c) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(0) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{x + 1}{x - 2} \), \( x \ne 2 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(3) \). (c) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(-1) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{3x}{x - 1} \), \( x \ne 1 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(6) \). (c) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(2) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{2x - 1}{x + 3} \), \( x \ne -3 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(1) \). (c) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(0) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{x}{x + 2} \), \( x \ne -2 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}\!\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right) \). (c) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(2) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{5 - x}{x} \), \( x \ne 0 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(4) \). (c) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(0) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{4x + 5}{x - 2} \), \( x \ne 2 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(9) \). (c) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(5) \).

The functions \( f \) and \( g \) are defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{3}{2x - 1} \), \( x \ne \tfrac{1}{2} \), and \( g(x) = x + 1 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(3) \). (c) Solve the equation \( f^{-1}(x) = g(x) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{x + 4}{x - 1} \), \( x \ne 1 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Hence state what is special about \( f \). (c) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(3) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{1 - x}{1 + x} \), \( x \ne -1 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Hence state what is special about \( f \). (c) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(2) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{2x}{3 - x} \), \( x \ne 3 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(4) \). (c) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(-6) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \tfrac{x - 3}{2x + 1} \), \( x \ne -\tfrac{1}{2} \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(-3) \). (c) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(0) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = e^x \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \). Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = e^{2x} \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(1) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 4e^{3x} - 5 \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \). (a) State the range of \( f \). (b) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (c) Solve the equation \( f^{-1}(x) = 0 \), giving your answer exactly.
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \ln(x + 1) \), \( x > -1 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(0) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 3\ln(2x - 1) + 4 \), \( x > \tfrac{1}{2} \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(4) \). (c) State, with a reason, the value of \( ff^{-1}(10) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \sqrt{x} + 3 \), \( x \ge 0 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(7) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \sqrt{3x - 6} + 2 \), \( x \ge 2 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Hence solve the equation \( f(x) = f^{-1}(x) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 5^x \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(25) \).

The functions \( f \) and \( g \) are defined by \( f(x) = e^{x} + 2 \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \), and \( g(x) = \ln(x - 1) \), \( x > 1 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range. (b) Find an expression for the composite function \( gf(x) \), and state its range. (c) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(e^2 + 2) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 2x - 5 \), \( x \ge 0 \). (a) State the range of \( f \). (b) Hence state the domain and range of \( f^{-1} \), justifying your answer.
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = x^2 + 2 \), \( x \ge 0 \). State the domain and range of \( f^{-1} \), explaining your reasoning.

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 11 \), \( x \ge 3 \). (a) Express \( f(x) \) in the form \( (x - a)^2 + b \). (b) State the range of \( f \). (c) Hence find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain and range.
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \ln x \), \( x > 0 \). (a) State the range of \( f \). (b) Hence state the domain and range of \( f^{-1} \), and write down \( f^{-1}(x) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = e^x + 1 \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \). State the domain and range of \( f^{-1} \), justifying your answer.

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \dfrac{2x + 1}{x - 3} \), \( x > 3 \). (a) Show that \( f(x) \) can be written as \( 2 + \dfrac{7}{x - 3} \). (b) Hence determine the range of \( f \). (c) State the domain and range of \( f^{-1} \), giving full justification.
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 1 - x \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \). (a) Show that \( f \) is self-inverse. (b) State what this tells you about the graph of \( y = f(x) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \dfrac{x}{x - 1} \), \( x \ne 1 \). (a) Show that \( f \) is self-inverse. (b) Hence write down the value of \( f^{-1}(4) \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x} \), \( x \ne 0 \). Show that \( f \) is self-inverse.
