The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \dfrac{x + 1}{x - 1} \), \( x \ne 1 \). (a) Determine whether \( f \) is self-inverse. (b) Hence, or otherwise, solve the equation \( f(x) = x \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \dfrac{ax + b}{cx - a} \), where \( a, b, c \) are constants with \( c \ne 0 \) and \( a^2 + bc \ne 0 \). (a) Show that \( f \) is self-inverse for all such \( a, b, c \). (b) State, in terms of \( a \) and \( c \), the value of \( x \) that must be excluded from the domain.
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = c - x \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \), where \( c \) is a constant. Show that \( f \) is self-inverse for every value of \( c \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 2 - x \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \). Determine whether \( f \) is self-inverse, justifying your answer.

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 2x + 3 \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \), stating its domain. (b) Verify that \( f(f^{-1}(x)) = x \) for all \( x \in \mathbb{R} \). (c) Explain what part (b) tells you about the relationship between \( f \) and \( f^{-1} \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \dfrac{3x + 4}{x - 2} \), \( x \in \mathbb{R}, \; x \neq 2 \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \) and state the value of \(x\) that must be excluded from its domain. (b) By substituting your expression for \( f^{-1}(x) \) into \( f \), verify in full algebraic detail that \( f(f^{-1}(x)) = x \). (c) State, with a reason, what your answer to (a) reveals about \( f \).
The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = e^x \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \). (a) Write down \( f^{-1}(x) \) and state its domain. (b) Verify that \( f(f^{-1}(x)) = x \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \dfrac{2x - 1}{x + 3} \), \( x \in \mathbb{R}, \; x \neq -3 \). (a) Show that \( f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{3x + 1}{2 - x} \), \( x \neq 2 \). (b) Verify, showing all algebra, that \( f(f^{-1}(x)) = x \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = ax + 3 \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \), where \(a\) is a constant. (a) Given that \( f^{-1}(5) = 2 \), find the value of \(a\). (b) Using your value of \(a\), write down \( f^{-1}(x) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = \dfrac{kx + 2}{x - k} \), \( x \in \mathbb{R}, \; x \neq k \), where \(k\) is a constant. (a) Show that \( f \) is self-inverse for every real value of \(k\). (b) Hence write down \( f^{-1}(x) \), and state the geometrical relationship between the graph of \( y = f(x) \) and the line \( y = x \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = ax + b \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \), where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants. It is given that \( f^{-1}(7) = 1 \) and \( f^{-1}(-5) = -2 \). (a) By forming two equations, find the values of \(a\) and \(b\). (b) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \). (c) Verify that \( f(f^{-1}(x)) = x \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 2x - 4 \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \). (b) On the same set of axes, sketch the graphs of \( y = f(x) \) and \( y = f^{-1}(x) \), marking the points where each graph crosses the coordinate axes. (c) State the geometrical transformation that maps the graph of \( y = f(x) \) onto the graph of \( y = f^{-1}(x) \).

The point \( (3, 7) \) lies on the graph of \( y = f(x) \), where \( f \) is a one-to-one function. (a) Write down the value of \( f^{-1}(7) \). (b) State the coordinates of the corresponding point on the graph of \( y = f^{-1}(x) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 2x - 3 \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \). (b) Sketch \( y = f(x) \) and \( y = f^{-1}(x) \) on the same axes, together with the line \( y = x \). (c) Explain how your diagram shows there is exactly one solution to \( f(x) = f^{-1}(x) \). (d) Solve \( f(x) = f^{-1}(x) \).

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = x^2 - 6x + 11 \). (a) Express \( f(x) \) in the form \( (x - p)^2 + q \), and hence explain why \( f \) is not one-to-one on \( \mathbb{R} \). (b) The domain of \( f \) is now restricted to \( x \geq 3 \). Find \( f^{-1}(x) \) and state its domain. (c) Evaluate \( f^{-1}(6) \), and verify your answer by showing that \( f \) maps it to \( 6 \).

The functions \( f \) and \( f^{-1} \) are both increasing. (a) Explain why any point of intersection of the graphs of \( y = f(x) \) and \( y = f^{-1}(x) \) must lie on the line \( y = x \). (b) Hence state the equation that must be solved to find such intersections.

The function \( f \) is defined by \( f(x) = 3x - 4 \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \). (a) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \). (b) Find the coordinates of the point where the graph of \( y = f(x) \) meets the graph of \( y = f^{-1}(x) \). (c) Verify your answer by checking it satisfies both \( y = f(x) \) and \( y = f^{-1}(x) \).

The functions \( f \) and \( g \) are defined by \( f(x) = 2x + 1 \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \) and \( g(x) = x - 3 \), \( x \in \mathbb{R} \). (a) Find \( fg(x) \) and hence find \( (fg)^{-1}(x) \). (b) Find \( f^{-1}(x) \) and \( g^{-1}(x) \), and hence find \( g^{-1}f^{-1}(x) \). (c) Verify that \( (fg)^{-1}(x) = g^{-1}f^{-1}(x) \), and explain why the order of \(f^{-1}\) and \(g^{-1}\) is reversed.

y2fg5.questionText: \( f(x) = x^2 - 4 \). On the same axes, sketch \( y = |f(x)| \) and \( y = f(|x|) \), labelling intercepts with the axes.
Sketch \( y = |x - 3| \), stating the vertex and intercepts.
Sketch \( y = |2x + 1| \), stating the vertex and y-intercept.
Sketch \( y = |(x - 1)^2 - 4| \); label vertex, peak, intercepts.
Given \( f(x) = x - 3 \), sketch \( y = f(|x|) \).
Sketch \( y = f(|x|) \) where \( f(x) = x^3 \).
Sketch \( y = f(|x|) \) where \( f(x) = x^2 - 2x \).
Sketch \( y = f(|x|) \) where \( f(x) = e^x \).
Sketch \( y = f(|x|) \) where \( f(x) = \ln x \).
Sketch \( y = f(|x|) \) where \( f(x) = \sin x \) on \(-2\pi \le x \le 2\pi\).
Explain when \( |f(x)| \) and \( f(|x|) \) produce the same graph.
Compare \( |f(x)| \) and \( f(|x|) \) for \( f(x) = x^2 - 1 \).
Compare \( |f(x)| \) and \( f(|x|) \) for \( f(x) = x - 1 \).
Compare \( |f(x)| \) and \( f(|x|) \) for \( f(x) = x^3 \).
By considering the graph of \( y = |x^2 - 4| \), find the number of solutions of \( |x^2 - 4| = 3 \).
For \( y = |x^2 - 4| \), state the number of solutions of \( |x^2 - 4| = k \) in terms of \(k \ge 0\).
State the range of \( y = |\sin x| \) on \(\mathbb R\).
For \( f(x) = 2x - 5 \) with domain \(x \ge 0\), state the range of \( f(|x|) \) on \(\mathbb R\).
The graph of \( y = f(x) \) crosses the x-axis at \(-2, 1, 3\). Describe the x-intercepts of \(y = |f(x)|\).
If \(f\) is odd with \(f(0) = 0\), describe the graph of \(y = f(|x|)\).
On the graph of \(y = f(x)\), where does \(|f(x)| = f(x)\)?
Sketch \( y = |x^2 - 4x| \); label intercepts and peak.
Sketch \( y = |2 - x^2| \), labelling intercepts and peak.
The graph of \(y = f(x)\) has min \((3, -5)\) and roots at \(x = 1, 5\). Describe \(y = |f(x)|\).
For what value of \(k \ge 0\) does \( |x^2 - 2x - 3| = k \) have exactly 3 solutions?
For what values of \(k\) does \(|x^2 - 4| = k\) have exactly 4 real roots?
\( f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x, & x \ge 1 \\ x + 1, & x < 1 \end{cases}\). Sketch \( y = f(|x|) \).
If \( f(0) = -7 \), find the y-intercept of \(y = |f(x)|\) and \(y = f(|x|)\).
Describe in words the transformation from \(y = f(x)\) to \(y = |f(x)|\).
Describe the transformation from \(y = f(x)\) to \(y = f(|x|)\).
Sketch \( y = |x| - |x - 2| \) as a piecewise linear function.
Sketch \( y = |x + 1| + |x - 1| \) and state its minimum.
Sketch \(y = |4 - 2x|\); state the vertex and y-intercept.
Sketch \(y = |x^3 + 1|\); give the x-intercept and explain the kink.
Sketch \(y = |x^2 + 4x + 5|\); does the modulus change the graph?
Write \(y = |3 - x| + |x|\) as a piecewise linear function.
For what values of \(k\) does \(|x^2 - 6x + 5| = k\) have exactly 4 solutions?
A cubic \(f(x)\) has roots at \(-2, 1, 3\) and turns at \((-1, 4)\) and \((2, -2)\). Describe the graph of \(y = |f(x)|\).
A graph is symmetric about the y-axis and the original \(f\) was \(f(x) = x - 2\). Is this \(|f(x)|\) or \(f(|x|)\)?
A graph has a V-shape with vertex at \((3, 0)\) (the root of \(f(x) = x - 3\)). Is it \(|f(x)|\) or \(f(|x|)\)?
Find the number of real solutions of \(|x^2 - 9| = x\).
If \(|f(x)| = f(x)\) for all \(x\) in some interval, what can you say about \(f\) on that interval?
Find the number of real solutions of \(|x^2 - 4x + 3| = x\).
Find the area between \(y = |x|\) and the x-axis on \([-3, 3]\).
Find the area between \(y = |x - 2|\) and the x-axis on \([0, 5]\).
Find the area bounded by \(y = 4 - |x|\) and the x-axis.
If \(f(x) = x^3 - 3x\), how many turning points does \(y = |f(x)|\) have on \([-2, 2]\)?
Sketch \(y = |\ln x|\) and state the y-intercept (if any).
How does the graph of \(y = |f(x) + 3|\) differ from \(y = |f(x)|\)?
Is \(|f(x)| + 3\) the same as \(|f(x) + 3|\)? Give an example, and characterise the values of \(f(x)\) for which they differ.
Find \(a\) so that \(y = |x - a|\) passes through \((3, 5)\).
Find \(b\) so that \(y = |2x + b|\) has its vertex at \((3, 0)\).
Find \(c\) so that \(y = |x| + c\) has range \(y \ge 3\).
Find \(k\) so that \(y = k - |x|\) has y-intercept 7.
Find integer values of \(k\) for which \(|x^2 - 4| = k\) has exactly 2 solutions.

Find \(k\) so that the line \(y = 2x - 1\) passes through the vertex of \(y = |x| + k\). (For every real \(k\) the line already meets the V at exactly one point, since its slope 2 exceeds the slopes \(\pm 1\) of the two branches — so no smooth tangency is possible; the only distinguished contact is at the corner.)

y2fg6.questionText: The curve \( y = f(x) \) has a single maximum point at \((4, -2)\). The curve is mapped onto \( y = 3f(2x - 6) + 5 \). (a) Express \( 2x - 6 \) in the form \( 2(x - a) \) and hence list the four transformations in the order they must be applied. (b) Determine the coordinates of the image of the maximum point, stating whether it remains a maximum.
Describe the transformation from \(y = f(x)\) to \(y = f(x) + 5\).
Describe the transformation from \(y = f(x)\) to \(y = f(x - 2)\).
Describe the transformation from \(y = f(x)\) to \(y = 3f(x)\).

A function \( g \) is obtained from \( f \) by the rule \( g(x) = f\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}x + 4\right) \). It is found that \( g \) has a root at \( x = -2 \) and a root at \( x = 6 \). (a) Write \( \tfrac{1}{2}x + 4 \) in the form \( \tfrac{1}{2}(x + b) \) and describe the transformation from \( y = f(x) \) to \( y = g(x) \) as an ordered sequence. (b) Hence find the \( x \)-coordinates of the corresponding roots of \( y = f(x) \).
Describe \(y = f(x) \to y = -f(x)\).
Describe \(y = f(x) \to y = f(-x)\).

The curve \( y = f(x) \) passes through \((0, 6)\) and has a minimum at \((-1, -4)\). It is transformed to \( y = -2f(x) + 1 \). (a) Describe the three transformations in the order they must be applied, and explain why the order of the vertical stretch and the reflection does not affect the result here. (b) Find the image of the minimum point and the image of \((0, 6)\), stating the nature of the first image point.
Describe the transformation \(y = f(x) \to y = \tfrac{1}{2}f(x + 3)\).
Describe \(y = f(x) \to y = -f(x - 2) + 4\).
Describe \(y = f(x) \to y = f(2x - 4)\). [Hint: factorise.]

The curve \( C \) has equation \( y = f(x) \). \( C \) maps to the curve with equation \( y = f(3x + 12) \). (a) By writing \( 3x + 12 \) in the form \( 3(x + a) \), give a valid pair of transformations in order: a horizontal stretch followed by a translation. (b) A different student instead applies a translation first and then the horizontal stretch (scale factor \( \tfrac13 \)), and obtains the same curve \( y = f(3x + 12) \). State the translation that student must use, and explain why it differs from the answer to part (a).
Describe \(y = f(\tfrac{x}{2} - 1)\) as a sequence from \(y = f(x)\).
Describe the transformation \(y = f(x) \to y = 3f(x) + 2\).

The point \((6, 8)\) lies on \( y = f(x) \). A curve \( y = g(x) \) is the image of \( y = f(x) \) under, in order, a translation right \(5\), a vertical stretch of scale factor \( \tfrac14 \), and a reflection in the \( x \)-axis. (a) Write \( g(x) \) in terms of \( f \). (b) Find the image of \((6, 8)\). (c) The curve \( y = g(x) \) is now translated up \(2\) to give \( y = h(x) \). State \( h(x) \) in terms of \( f \) and find the image of \((6, 8)\) on \( y = h(x) \).
Describe \(y = 5 - f(x)\).
Describe the transformation to \(y = f(1 - x)\).
Describe \(y = -2f(-x)\).
Describe \(y = f(\tfrac{1}{3}x) - 2\).
\((2, 3)\) lies on \(y = f(x)\). Find its image on \(y = f(x) + 4\).

The points \((2, 3)\) and \((8, 3)\) both lie on \( y = f(x) \) and are the only points of \( f \) with \( y \)-coordinate \(3\). The same two points, in the same order, lie on \( y = f(ax + b) \) at \((1, 3)\) and \((4, 3)\) respectively. (a) Form two equations in \(a\) and \(b\) and solve them. (b) Hence describe the single sequence of transformations from \( y = f(x) \) to \( y = f(ax + b) \), with the steps in order.
\((2, 3)\) lies on \(y = f(x)\). Find its image on \(y = 2f(x)\).
\((-1, 4)\) lies on \(y = f(x)\). Find its image on \(y = f(2x)\).
\((3, -1)\) lies on \(y = f(x)\). Image on \(y = -f(x)\).

The point \((3, -1)\) lies on \( y = f(x) \). (a) Find the image of \((3, -1)\) on \( y = f(-x) \), then on \( y = -f(-x) \), and finally on \( y = -f(-x) + 4 \), showing each stage. (b) The combined transformation \( y = -f(-x) + 4 \) can be described as a single rotation followed by a translation. State the rotation (centre and angle) and the translation.
\((2, 5)\) lies on \(y = f(x)\). Find its image on \(y = 3f(x - 1) + 2\).
\((-2, 4)\) lies on \(y = f(x)\). Find its image on \(y = \tfrac{1}{2}f(x + 3) - 1\).
\((1, 1)\) lies on \(y = f(x)\). Find its image on \(y = f(2x - 4)\).

The curve \( y = f(x) \) has a maximum at \((2, 9)\) and a minimum at \((6, 1)\). The curve is transformed to \( y = 5 - 2f\!\left(\tfrac12 x + 1\right) \). (a) Write \( \tfrac12 x + 1 \) as \( \tfrac12(x + c) \) and list every transformation in the order applied. (b) Find the images of both stationary points, stating the nature of each image. (c) Find the vertical distance between the two image points.
Start with \(y = x^2\). Stretch vertically ×2 then translate up 1. Write the equation.
Start with \(y = \sin x\); apply a horizontal stretch scale factor 2. Write the new equation.
Start with \(y = e^x\); translate right 2, then reflect in the x-axis.

The curve \( y = \ln x \) is transformed, in order, by: a translation right \(2\), a vertical stretch of scale factor \(3\), and a reflection in the \( y \)-axis. (a) Determine the equation of the resulting curve, simplifying the argument of the logarithm. (b) State the equation of the vertical asymptote of the final curve and the exact coordinates of its \( x \)-axis intercept.
Start with \(y = \tfrac{1}{x}\); translate right 2, then up 3.
Start with \(y = x^2\); apply horizontal stretch scale factor \(\tfrac{1}{3}\), then down 4.

A curve has equation \( y = a\cos\big(b(x - c)\big) + d \), where \(a > 0\), \(b > 0\) and \(0 \le c < \tfrac{\pi}{2}\). It is obtained from \( y = \cos x \) and has period \( \pi \), a maximum value of \(7\), a minimum value of \(-1\), and a maximum point at \( x = \tfrac{\pi}{6} \). (a) Determine the values of \(a\), \(b\), \(c\) and \(d\). (b) Describe, in order, the four transformations that map \( y = \cos x \) onto this curve.
Transform \(y = x^2\) so its vertex is at \((3, -2)\).
Transform \(y = x^3\) by translating up so it passes through \((0, 5)\).
Transform \(y = e^x\) by horizontal stretch factor \(\tfrac{1}{2}\), then up 1.

The curve \(y = x^2\) is transformed by the following chain, in order: a translation by \(\begin{pmatrix} -2 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}\), then a stretch parallel to the \(y\)-axis by scale factor \(3\), then a translation by \(\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -5 \end{pmatrix}\). (a) Find the equation of the final curve in the form \(y = a(x + b)^2 + c\). (b) State the coordinates of the vertex of the final curve. (c) A student performs the same three transformations but applies the \(y\)-stretch last instead of in the middle. Show that this changes the equation, and give the new equation.
(a) Start with \(y = f(x)\); stretch horizontally ×\(\tfrac{1}{2}\) then translate right 4. (b) Reverse order. Compare.
Apply to \(y = x^2\): (a) reflect in x-axis then up 4, (b) up 4 then reflect. Compare.
Describe the transformations from \(y = x^2\) to \(y = (x + 3)^2 - 5\).
Describe the transformations from \(y = \sin x\) to \(y = 2\sin(3x)\).

The curve \(C\) has equation \(y = 2e^{3x - 6} - 1\). (a) By writing \(3x - 6 = 3(x - 2)\), describe fully the sequence of three single transformations that maps \(y = e^x\) onto \(C\), giving them in a valid order. (b) Hence find the exact coordinates of the point where \(C\) crosses the \(x\)-axis. (c) State the equation of the horizontal asymptote of \(C\).
Describe \(y = \tfrac{1}{x} \to y = \tfrac{2}{x} + 1\).
Describe \(y = x^2 \to y = 4 - (x - 1)^2\).

The curve \(y = \cos x\) is mapped onto the curve \(y = g(x)\) by, in order: a stretch parallel to the \(x\)-axis by scale factor \(\tfrac{1}{2}\), then a reflection in the \(x\)-axis, then a translation by \(\begin{pmatrix} \frac{\pi}{4} \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}\). (a) Find \(g(x)\) in the form \(-\cos(a x + b)\), stating \(a\) and \(b\). (b) Show that \(g(x)\) can also be written as \(\cos(2x - \tfrac{\pi}{4})\), and explain which trig identity makes the reflection 'disappear'. (c) State the smallest positive value of \(x\) at which \(g(x)\) attains its maximum value.
Describe \(y = \sqrt x \to y = \sqrt{2x} + 1\).
\(y = 2f(x + 3) - 1\) passes through \((0, 5)\). Find \(f(3)\).
\(y = f(2x - 4)\) passes through \((3, 7)\). What point does \(y = f(x)\) pass through?
\(f(4) = 10\). Find the value of \(3f(x - 1) + 2\) at \(x = 5\).
The graph \(y = f(x)\) has a max at \((5, 8)\). The graph \(y = af(x - 2) - 3\) has max at \((7, 9)\). Find \(a\).
Describe \(y = x^2 \to y = (x - 2)^2 + 3\) and state the vertex.
Describe \(y = x^2 \to y = -\tfrac{1}{2}(x + 1)^2 + 4\).

The function \(y = f(x)\) has a single maximum point at \((-4, 6)\) and a single minimum point at \((2, -3)\). The curve \(y = h(x)\) is obtained from \(y = f(x)\) by the transformation \(h(x) = 2 - 3f\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}x + 1\right)\). (a) By writing \(\tfrac{1}{2}x + 1 = \tfrac{1}{2}(x + 2)\), describe the full sequence of transformations mapping \(f\) to \(h\). (b) Find the coordinates of the image of the point \((-4, 6)\) on \(y = h(x)\), stating whether it is a maximum or minimum of \(h\). (c) Find the coordinates of the image of \((2, -3)\) on \(y = h(x)\).
\(y = f(x)\) has roots at \(x = -1, 2, 4\). Roots of \(y = f(x - 3)\)?
\(y = f(x)\) has roots at \(-2, 4\). Roots of \(y = f(2x)\)?

A curve \(C\) is obtained from \(y = \tfrac{1}{x}\) by applying, in order: a stretch parallel to the \(x\)-axis by scale factor \(\tfrac{1}{2}\), then a translation by \(\begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}\), then a translation by \(\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}\). (a) Show that \(C\) has equation \(y = \dfrac{1}{2x - 6} - 4\). (b) State the equations of the two asymptotes of \(C\). (c) Find the exact coordinates of both intercepts of \(C\) with the coordinate axes.
Asymptote of \(y = e^{x - 1} - 4\)?
\(y = f(x)\) passes through \((0, 0)\). Find two transformations so the new graph passes through \((1, 2)\).
Find \(a, b, c\) so that \(y = a(x - b)^2 + c\) has vertex at \((3, -4)\) and passes through \((5, 0)\).
Apply (i) horizontal stretch factor 3 then (ii) up 4 to \((1, 2)\).
Apply to \((-2, 5)\): reflect in y-axis, vertical stretch ×\(\tfrac{1}{2}\), then left 3.
Find \(k\) so that \(y = f(x - k)\) passes through the origin, given \(f(5) = 0\).

The curve \(y = \tan x\) is transformed to the curve \(y = g(x)\) where \(g(x) = \tan\!\left(2x + \tfrac{\pi}{3}\right) - 1\). (a) By writing the argument in the form \(2\left(x + \tfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\), describe fully the sequence of three transformations mapping \(y = \tan x\) onto \(y = g(x)\). (b) State the period of \(y = g(x)\). (c) The vertical asymptote of \(y = \tan x\) nearest to \(x = 0\) on the positive side is \(x = \tfrac{\pi}{2}\). Find the image of this asymptote on \(y = g(x)\), and hence write down the smallest positive \(x\)-coordinate of an asymptote of \(g\).
Start with \(y = \ln x\); apply horizontal stretch factor 2, then reflect in x-axis, then up 1. Write the equation.
The line \(y = x\) is transformed by \(y = f(x) \to y = 2f(x - 1) + 3\). Find the new equation.
\(y = x^2\) is transformed by \(y = f(x) \to y = f(2x) - 3\). Find the new equation.
A parabola has vertex \((-2, 5)\) and passes through \((0, 1)\). Express as a transformation of \(y = x^2\).
\((2, -3)\) lies on \(y = f(x)\). Image on \(y = f(x) - 4\)?
Image of \((2, 4)\) on \(y = -f(x)\)?

The point \(P(6, -8)\) lies on the curve \(y = f(x)\). (a) The point \(P\) is mapped to the point \(Q(-3, 12)\) under the transformation \(y = a\,f(bx)\). Find the values of the constants \(a\) and \(b\). (b) Using these values of \(a\) and \(b\), the curve \(y = a\,f(bx)\) is then translated by \(\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}\). Find the image of \(P\) on this final curve. (c) The point \(R\) on \(y = f(x)\) is mapped to \((10, 0)\) on \(y = a\,f(bx)\). Find the coordinates of \(R\).
Image of \((2, 3)\) on \(y = f(\tfrac{x}{3})\)?
Describe \(y = f(x + 3) - 5\).

A curve has equation \(y = g(x)\). After the transformation \(y = 4 - 2\,g(x - 3)\) is applied, the resulting curve passes through the point \((7, -6)\) and has a minimum point at \((1, 4)\). (a) Find the coordinates of the point on the original curve \(y = g(x)\) that maps to \((7, -6)\). (b) The minimum point of \(y = 4 - 2g(x-3)\) is at \((1, 4)\). Find the coordinates of the corresponding stationary point on \(y = g(x)\), and state whether it is a maximum or a minimum. (c) Explain why the transformation turns a maximum of \(g\) into a minimum of the new curve.
Describe \(y = f(-x - 2)\) as a sequence of transformations from \(f(x)\).
Describe \(y = 2f(3(x + 1))\).
Start with \(y = \sin x\); stretch vertically ×4 then translate left \(\tfrac{\pi}{2}\). Write the equation.
Stretch \(y = x^2\) horizontally by factor 2. New equation?
State the vertex of \(y = -(x - 2)^2 + 5\) and the transformations from \(y = x^2\).

The curve \(C\) has equation \(y = 3\sin\!\left(4x - \tfrac{\pi}{2}\right) + 1\). (a) By writing the argument as \(4\left(x - \tfrac{\pi}{8}\right)\), describe the sequence of four transformations mapping \(y = \sin x\) onto \(C\). (b) State the period and the exact maximum and minimum values of \(y\) on \(C\). (c) Find the smallest positive value of \(x\) at which \(C\) attains its maximum value.
State the amplitude and period of \(y = 3\cos(\tfrac{x}{2})\).
Max of \(\cos x\) is at \((0, 1)\). Find the image of this max on \(y = 2\cos(x - \pi)\).
Translate \(y = 2^x\) up so it passes through \((3, 8)\) — state the equation. (No vertical stretch.)

A curve \(C\) is obtained from \(y = \ln x\) by the following chain of transformations, in order: a stretch parallel to the \(x\)-axis by scale factor \(\tfrac{1}{3}\), then a translation by \(\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}\), then a vertical stretch by scale factor \(2\), then a translation by \(\begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}\). (a) Find the equation of \(C\), simplifying the argument of the logarithm. (b) State the equation of the vertical asymptote of \(C\). (c) Find the exact \(x\)-coordinate of the point where \(C\) crosses the \(x\)-axis.
Describe \(y = e^{-x} + 4\) from \(y = e^x\).
\((0, 1)\) on \(y = e^x\). Find its image on \(y = e^{x - 2} + 3\).
Find the asymptotes of \(y = \tfrac{2}{x - 3} + 1\).
A transformation of \(y = \tfrac{1}{x}\) has asymptotes \(x = -2, y = 5\) and passes through \((0, 4)\). Find the equation.

The function \(f\) has range \([2, 7]\). (a) State the range of \(y = 3 - 2f\big(\tfrac{1}{2}x\big)\), justifying which transformations affect the range. (b) The curve \(y = f(x)\) has a single maximum at the point \((4, 7)\). State the coordinates of the corresponding turning point on \(y = 3 - 2f\big(\tfrac{1}{2}x\big)\) and say whether it is a maximum or a minimum.
\(f\) has min \(-1\). Min of \(y = 2f(x) + 5\)?
\(f\) has range \([-4, 6]\). Range of \(y = f(3x) - 1\)?
Period of \(y = \sin(3x - \pi)\)?

The function \(f\) has exactly three roots, at \(x = 1\), \(x = 3\) and \(x = 5\), and \(f(0) = 12\). (a) By writing the argument in the form \(f(a(x-b))\), find all roots of \(y = f(2x - 4)\). (b) Find all roots of \(y = 3f(2x - 4)\) and state its \(y\)-intercept. (c) Explain why \(y = f(2x-4) + 1\) need not have the same number of roots as \(f\).
\(f\) has turning point \((2, -1)\). Turning point of \(y = 2f(x - 3) + 4\)?
\(f(3) = 4\). Find \(a\) so \(y = af(x)\) passes through \((3, 10)\).
\(f\) has minimum value \(-3\). Find \(k\) so \(y = f(x) + k\) touches the x-axis.

Starting from \(y = x^2\), the following transformations are applied in order: (i) a translation by \(\binom{3}{0}\), (ii) a vertical stretch by factor \(2\), (iii) a reflection in the \(x\)-axis, (iv) a translation by \(\binom{0}{5}\). (a) Find the equation of the resulting curve in the form \(y = a(x-h)^2 + k\). (b) State the coordinates of its vertex and whether it is a maximum or minimum. (c) Show that performing (ii) and (iii) in the opposite order gives the same final curve, but performing (i) after (iv) does not.
If \(g(x) = 2f(x - 3)\), express \(g^{-1}(x)\) in terms of \(f^{-1}\).
Find \(a, b > 0\) so that \(y = a\sin(bx)\) has amplitude 5 and period \(\pi\).
Apply to \(y = \sqrt x\): reflect in y-axis then stretch vertically ×3. Equation?
\(y = \ln x\) is transformed to \(y = 2\ln(x + 1) - 3\). At which x does the transformed curve cross the x-axis?
Explain the difference between \(y = 2f(x)\) and \(y = f(2x)\), using a specific max point of \(f\) at \((2, 3)\).
Image of \((a, b)\) on \(y = f(-x) + 5\)?
Describe the mapping \((x, y) \to (2x - 1, \tfrac{y + 3}{2})\) in terms of transformations of \(y = f(x)\).

The function \(f\) has domain \([-2, 6]\) and range \([0, 9]\). Define \(g(x) = 4 - f(3 - 2x)\). (a) By writing the argument as \(f\big(-2(x - \tfrac{3}{2})\big)\), describe fully the sequence of transformations mapping \(f\) to \(g\). (b) Find the domain and range of \(g\). (c) The point \((6, 9)\) lies on \(y = f(x)\). Find its image on \(y = g(x)\).
A transformation of \(y = x^2\) has vertex \((2, -3)\) and passes through \((0, 5)\). State the equation.
Determine \(b, c\) for \(y = (x + b)^2 + c\) given its minimum is at \((-2, -9)\). Verify it passes through \((1, 0)\).
Find amplitude, period, and reflection for \(y = -2\sin(\tfrac{\pi x}{3})\).
\(f\) has maximum \((1, 5)\). What kind of turning point is this on \(y = -f(x)\)?

The curve \(y = f(x)\) has a horizontal asymptote \(y = 2\) and a vertical asymptote \(x = -1\), and passes through \((0, 5)\). The curve \(y = g(x)\) is obtained by reflecting \(y = f(x)\) in the \(x\)-axis, then stretching vertically by factor \(3\), then translating by \(\binom{-4}{1}\). (a) Write \(g\) in terms of \(f\). (b) State the equations of both asymptotes of \(y = g(x)\). (c) Find the \(y\)-coordinate of the point on \(y = g(x)\) whose \(x\)-coordinate is \(-4\).
\(f\) has vertical asymptote \(x = 3\). Asymptote of \(y = f(2x)\)?
Apply: reflect in x-axis, stretch y ×4, shift left 2, shift up 3. Image of origin?
Describe \(y = 2(x - 1)^2 + 3\) from \(y = x^2\).

A curve has equation \(y = 2 - (3 - x)^3\). (a) Show that this curve can be obtained from \(y = x^3\) by a sequence of transformations, describing each fully and in the correct order. (b) A student claims that the curve is the image of \(y = x^3\) under a reflection in the point \((3, 2)\). By considering the image of a general point \((t,\, t^3)\) on \(y = x^3\), determine whether the student is correct. (c) State the coordinates of the point of inflection of \(y = 2 - (3 - x)^3\).
\(y = f(x) = \sqrt x\) is shifted right 4 then stretched ×3 vertically. Equation?
Describe the transformations needed to go from \(y = x^2\) to each of: (a) \(y = (x - 1)^2\), (b) \(y = x^2 + 3\), (c) \(y = 2x^2\), (d) \(y = -x^2\).
Horizontal asymptote of \(y = -e^x + 7\)?

The function \(f\) has roots at \(x = -1\) and \(x = 3\) only, a maximum point at \((1, 8)\), and \(f(0) = 6\). The curve \(y = g(x)\) is defined by \(g(x) = 5 f\big(\tfrac{1}{2}x + 1\big) - 10\). (a) Find the roots of \(y = g(x)\). (b) Find the coordinates and nature of the turning point of \(y = g(x)\). (c) Determine the \(y\)-intercept of \(y = g(x)\).
If \(f\) has roots at \(x = -1, 3\), what are the roots of \(y = f(\tfrac{x}{2})\)?
\(f\) has y-intercept 2 and x-intercept \(-4\). Find the y-intercept of \(y = f(x + 3)\).

The function \(f\) satisfies \(f(0) = 5\), \(f(2) = -3\) and \(f(-6) = 11\). The curve \(y = h(x)\) is obtained from \(y = f(x)\) by a horizontal stretch of factor \(\tfrac{1}{2}\), then a translation \(3\) units to the right, then a reflection in the \(x\)-axis, then a translation \(4\) units up. (a) Express \(h(x)\) in terms of \(f\). (b) Find the \(y\)-intercept of \(y = h(x)\). (c) Find \(h(1)\) and \(h(4)\), or explain why a value cannot be found.
A curve is \(y = x^2\) reflected in the x-axis and shifted so its vertex is at \((3, 7)\). Write its equation.
Describe \(y = \sin(x - \pi) + 2\) from \(y = \sin x\).
Using \(\sin(x + \pi) = -\sin x\), describe two equivalent ways to go from \(y = \sin x\) to \(y = \sin(x + \pi)\).

The point \((4, 9)\) lies on \(y = f(x)\). The curve \(y = f(x)\) is transformed, in order, by: (i) a horizontal stretch of scale factor \(2\), (ii) a vertical stretch of scale factor \(\tfrac{1}{3}\), (iii) a translation \(7\) units up. Find the image of \((4, 9)\) on the resulting curve.
Describe the single transformation mapping \(y = x^2\) to \(y = 4x^2\).

(a) Show that the curve \(y = -8(x - 1)^3 + 5\) can be obtained from \(y = x^3\) by a sequence of transformations, describing each transformation fully and in order. (b) The same curve can be reached by first applying a horizontal transformation (a stretch followed by a translation) and then a vertical translation only. Find the horizontal stretch factor \(k\), the horizontal translation, and the vertical translation, and explain why a reflection is not separately needed. (c) State the coordinates of the point on the curve corresponding to the point \((2, 8)\) on \(y = x^3\).
\(y = x^3\) passes through \((2, 8)\). Image on \(y = (x - 1)^3 + 2\)?
\(y = x^3\) has inflection at origin. Inflection of \(y = (x + 5)^3 - 4\)?

A parabola \(C\) is the image of \(y = x^2\) under an unknown combination of one vertical stretch (factor \(a > 0\)) and one translation by \(\binom{p}{q}\). It is known that \(C\) passes through the points \((1, 5)\), \((3, 5)\) and \((2, 1)\). (a) Use the symmetry of the two equal \(y\)-values to find the horizontal translation \(p\). (b) Hence find the vertical stretch factor \(a\) and the vertical translation \(q\), and write the equation of \(C\) in the form \(y = a(x - p)^2 + q\). (c) State the single transformation that maps \(C\) back onto \(y = x^2\) if the translation is undone first.
Describe a sequence of transformations that maps \(y = \sin x\) to \(y = \cos 2x\).
Simplify \(y = -\cos(x + \pi)\) in terms of \(\cos x\).
Apply to \(y = f(x)\): up 2, then stretch y ×3. Find \(y\)-value when \(f(x) = 4\).
Apply to \(y = f(x)\): stretch y ×3, then up 2. \(y\)-value when \(f(x) = 4\)?
Show that two successive reflections in the y-axis give the identity.
Apply to \(y = f(x)\): translate right 3, then reflect in y-axis. Write the resulting equation.

y2fg7.questionText: Solve, and state the solution set, the inequality \( |x^2 - 2x + 3| \ge 2x - 1 \).
Find the set of values of \(x\) for which \( |x^2 - 5x + 4| \le 4 - x \).
Solve the inequality \( |x^2 + 2x - 8| > x + 4 \), giving your answer as a union of intervals.
Solve the inequality \( |x^2 - 4x + 5| < 3x - 5 \), giving your answer as an interval.
Solve the equation \( |x^2 - x - 6| = 4 - 2x \), giving exact answers.
Find the set of values of \(x\) for which \( |x^2 + x - 6| \ge x + 2 \), giving exact answers.
Solve the inequality \( |x^2 - 4| < x + 2 \), giving your answer as an interval.
Solve the equation \( |x^2 - 3x + 1| = x \), giving exact answers.
Find the set of values of \(x\) for which \( |x^2 + 2x - 3| \ge 2x + 6 \).
Solve \( |x^2 - 4x + 3| \ge 2x - 1 \), giving the solution set in surd form.
Find the set of values of \(x\) for which \( |x^2 + 2x + 5| < 3x + 1 \).
Solve \( |x^2 - 5x + 6| \le 2x \), stating the full solution set.
Solve \( |x^2 - 6x + 10| > 4 \), giving the answer in surd form.
Solve \( |x^2 - x - 6| = x + 3 \), giving all real solutions in exact form.
Find the set of values of \(x\) for which \( |x^2 + x + 1| > 2x + 3 \).
Solve \( |x^2 - 2x - 8| \le |x + 2| \), stating the full solution set.
Solve \( |x^2 - 3x| \ge 4 - x \), giving the solution set in surd form.
Solve \( |x^2 - 4x + 1| \le 4 \). Give your answer as an interval in exact form.
For what values of \(k\) does \( |x - 1| = kx \) have exactly one solution (for \(k > 0\))?
For \(k \ge 0\), state the number of real solutions of \( |x^2 - 4| = k \).
The curve \(y = |x^2 - 2x|\) meets the line \(y = k\) at exactly 3 points. Find \(k\).
Find the set of values of \(x\) for which \( |x^2 - 6x + 10| \ge 2x - 5 \).
Find all real numbers whose distance from 5 is 3, by solving a modulus equation.
Solve \(|x - 2| + |x - 6| = 4\) and give a geometric interpretation.
Solve \( |x^2 - x - 6| > x + 2 \). Give the full solution set.
Sketch \(y = |2x - 1|\) and \(y = x\) and solve \(|2x - 1| > x\).
For what \(k\) does \(|x - 3| = k\) have exactly 2 real solutions?
For what value of \(k\) does \(|x^2 - 1| = k\) have exactly 3 real solutions?
For what values of \(k\) does \(|2x - 3| = 2x + k\) have exactly 2 real solutions?
For \(a < b\), describe the solutions of \(|x - a| + |x - b| = b - a\).
Find the set of values of \(x\) such that \( |2x^2 - 3x - 2| \le x + 4 \).
Prove that for all real \(x, y\): \(|x + y| \le |x| + |y|\).
Find the set of values of \(x\) for which \( |x^2 - 5x + 7| \ge 1 \).
Solve \( |x^2 + x - 6| = |2x - 1| \). Give your answers in exact form.
Find the set of values of \(x\) for which \( |x^2 - 4x + 5| < 2 \).
Solve \( |x^2 - 2x - 3| > 2x + 2 \). Give the full solution set.
Solve \(|x^2 - 4x + 5| > 2x - 7\), giving the full solution set.
Find the set of values of \(x\) for which \(|x^2 - 6x + 8| \le 3\).
Find the set of values of \(x\) for which \(|x^2 - 2x - 1| \le x + 1\).
Find the set of values of \(x\) for which \(|x^2 - 4x| \ge 5 - 2x\).
For \(k = 5\), how many real solutions does \(|x^2 - 9| = k\) have?
Find \(k\) such that \(|x^2 - 4| = k\) has exactly 3 solutions.
Solve \(|x^2 - 4x + 5| \le 2x - 3\), giving your solution set in interval form.
Find the set of values of \(x\) for which \(|x^2 - 5x + 4| > x - 1\).
Solve \(|x^2 - 3x - 4| \le x + 1\), giving your full solution set.
Solve \(|x^2 - x - 6| = x + 2\), listing every solution.
Find all integer values of \(a\) so \(|x - a| < 3\) has exactly 5 integer solutions.
Express the solution of \(|x - 5| \ge 2\) in interval notation.
Find the set of values of \(x\) for which \(|x^2 - 2x - 3| \ge |2x - 1|\).
Prove the reverse triangle inequality \(|x - y| \ge ||x| - |y||\).
Find the set of real numbers \(x\) satisfying \(|x^2 - 4x + 7| > 2x + 1\).
Write an equation for "the distance between \(x\) and \(-5\) is 8."
Sketch \(y = |x - 2|\) and \(y = 3x\) on the same axes, and use the sketch to solve \(|x - 2| = 3x\).
Find \(k\) so that \(|x + 2| + |x - 2| = k\) holds for all \(x \in [-2, 2]\) but not outside.
Prove: if \(|a - b| < \epsilon\) and \(|b - c| < \epsilon\), then \(|a - c| < 2\epsilon\).

y2hc.questionText: A scientist collects bivariate data on \( n \) pairs of observations and wants to test whether there is correlation between the two variables. Using the population correlation coefficient \( \rho \), write down the null hypothesis \( H_0 \) and the alternative hypothesis \( H_1 \) for this test.

A researcher believes that as the number of hours of revision increases, exam marks tend to increase, suggesting positive correlation. Using the population correlation coefficient \( \rho \), write down the null hypothesis \( H_0 \) and the alternative hypothesis \( H_1 \) for a test of this belief.

An economist suspects that as the price of an item increases, the quantity sold tends to decrease, suggesting negative correlation. Using the population correlation coefficient \( \rho \), write down the null hypothesis \( H_0 \) and the alternative hypothesis \( H_1 \) for a test of this suspicion.

A student investigates whether there is some correlation between daily temperature and ice-cream sales. State whether a hypothesis test of this claim should be one-tailed or two-tailed, and write down the alternative hypothesis \( H_1 \) in terms of \( \rho \).

A gardener wants to test whether there is positive correlation between the amount of fertiliser used and plant height. State whether a hypothesis test of this claim should be one-tailed or two-tailed, and write down the alternative hypothesis \( H_1 \) in terms of \( \rho \).

A test uses \( H_0: \rho = 0 \) and \( H_1: \rho > 0 \) at the \( 5\% \) significance level. The sample gives a PMCC of \( r = 0.62 \) and the critical value from tables is \( 0.497 \). Compare \( r \) with the critical value and state the conclusion of the test.

A test uses \( H_0: \rho = 0 \) and \( H_1: \rho < 0 \) at the \( 5\% \) significance level. The sample gives a PMCC of \( r = -0.58 \) and the critical value from tables is \( -0.532 \). Compare \( r \) with the critical value and state the conclusion of the test.

A test uses \( H_0: \rho = 0 \) and \( H_1: \rho > 0 \) at the \( 5\% \) significance level. The sample gives a PMCC of \( r = 0.41 \) and the critical value from tables is \( 0.549 \). Compare \( r \) with the critical value and state the conclusion of the test.

A two-tailed test uses \( H_0: \rho = 0 \) and \( H_1: \rho \neq 0 \). The sample gives a PMCC of \( r = 0.71 \) and the critical value from tables is \( 0.632 \). By comparing \( |r| \) with the critical value, state the conclusion of the test.

A two-tailed test uses \( H_0: \rho = 0 \) and \( H_1: \rho \neq 0 \). The sample gives a PMCC of \( r = -0.39 \) and the critical value from tables is \( 0.468 \). By comparing \( |r| \) with the critical value, state the conclusion of the test.

A test uses \( H_0: \rho = 0 \) and \( H_1: \rho < 0 \) at the \( 5\% \) significance level. The sample gives a PMCC of \( r = -0.44 \) and the critical value from tables is \( -0.521 \). Compare \( r \) with the critical value and state the conclusion of the test.

A test of \( H_0: \rho = 0 \) against \( H_1: \rho > 0 \) uses the \( 5\% \) significance level. For the sample size used, the critical value is given as \( 0.4973 \). The observed product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = 0.582 \). State whether the result is significant and which hypothesis is accepted.

A test of \( H_0: \rho = 0 \) against \( H_1: \rho > 0 \) is carried out at the \( 1\% \) significance level. For the sample size used, the critical value is given as \( 0.6581 \). The observed product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = 0.514 \). State whether the result is significant and which hypothesis is retained.

A test of \( H_0: \rho = 0 \) against \( H_1: \rho < 0 \) uses the \( 5\% \) significance level. For the sample size used, the critical value is given as \( -0.5494 \). The observed product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = -0.612 \). State whether the result is significant and which hypothesis is accepted.

A test of \( H_0: \rho = 0 \) against \( H_1: \rho < 0 \) is carried out at the \( 2.5\% \) significance level. For the sample size used, the critical value is given as \( -0.6319 \). The observed product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = -0.488 \). State whether the result is significant and which hypothesis is retained.

A test of \( H_0: \rho = 0 \) against \( H_1: \rho \ne 0 \) uses the \( 5\% \) significance level. For the sample size used, the critical value is given as \( 0.6664 \). The observed product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = -0.701 \). By comparing \( |r| \) with the critical value, state whether the result is significant.

A test of \( H_0: \rho = 0 \) against \( H_1: \rho \ne 0 \) is carried out at the \( 2\% \) significance level. For the sample size used, the critical value is given as \( 0.7155 \). The observed product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = 0.642 \). By comparing \( |r| \) with the critical value, state whether the result is significant.
For a set of bivariate data the product moment correlation coefficient is found to be \( r = 0.03 \). State what this value suggests about the linear correlation between the two variables.
For a set of bivariate data the product moment correlation coefficient is found to be \( r = 0.98 \). State what this value suggests about the linear correlation between the two variables.
For a set of bivariate data the product moment correlation coefficient is found to be \( r = -0.96 \). State what this value suggests about the linear correlation between the two variables.

A one-tailed test of \( H_0: \rho = 0 \) against \( H_1: \rho > 0 \) is to be carried out at the \( 5\% \) significance level. From a table for the relevant sample size, the values \( 0.4973 \) (for \( 5\% \) one-tailed) and \( 0.5760 \) (for \( 2.5\% \) one-tailed) are given. State which critical value should be used for this test.

A two-tailed test of \( H_0: \rho = 0 \) against \( H_1: \rho \ne 0 \) is to be carried out at the \( 5\% \) significance level. From a table for the relevant sample size, the values \( 0.4973 \) (for \( 5\% \) one-tailed) and \( 0.5760 \) (for \( 2.5\% \) one-tailed) are given. State which critical value should be used for this test.

An agricultural scientist records, for \( 12 \) farms, the monthly rainfall (mm) and the crop yield (tonnes per hectare). The product moment correlation coefficient for the sample is found to be \( r = 0.621 \). The scientist believes that higher rainfall is associated with higher yield, and tests this at the \( 5\% \) significance level. For \( n = 12 \) at the \( 5\% \) level (one-tailed), the critical value is \( 0.4973 \). Carry out the test, stating your hypotheses and conclusion clearly.

A used-car dealer records the age (years) and the selling price (\( \pounds \)) of \( 15 \) cars of the same model. The product moment correlation coefficient for the sample is \( r = -0.706 \). The dealer believes that older cars sell for less, and tests this at the \( 5\% \) significance level. For \( n = 15 \) at the \( 5\% \) level (one-tailed), the critical value is \( -0.4409 \). Carry out the test, stating your hypotheses and conclusion clearly.

A teacher records, for \( 10 \) students, the number of hours of revision and the exam score (\%). The product moment correlation coefficient for the sample is \( r = 0.548 \). The teacher believes that more revision is associated with higher scores, and tests this at the \( 5\% \) significance level. For \( n = 10 \) at the \( 5\% \) level (one-tailed), the critical value is \( 0.5494 \). Carry out the test, stating your hypotheses and conclusion clearly.

A kiosk owner records, on \( 8 \) days, the mean daily temperature (\( ^\circ\mathrm{C} \)) and the number of ice creams sold. The product moment correlation coefficient for the sample is \( r = 0.842 \). The owner believes higher temperatures are associated with more sales, and tests this at the \( 1\% \) significance level. For \( n = 8 \) at the \( 1\% \) level (one-tailed), the critical value is \( 0.7887 \). Carry out the test, stating your hypotheses and conclusion clearly.

A geographer records the altitude (m) and the mean annual temperature (\( ^\circ\mathrm{C} \)) at \( 20 \) weather stations. The product moment correlation coefficient for the sample is \( r = -0.391 \). The geographer believes that higher altitude is associated with lower temperature, and tests this at the \( 5\% \) significance level. For \( n = 20 \) at the \( 5\% \) level (one-tailed), the critical value is \( -0.3783 \). Carry out the test, stating your hypotheses and conclusion clearly.

An engineer records, for \( 14 \) days, the hours of sunshine and the energy generated (kWh) by a solar panel. The product moment correlation coefficient for the sample is \( r = 0.512 \). The engineer believes that more sunshine is associated with greater energy output, and tests this at the \( 5\% \) significance level. For \( n = 14 \) at the \( 5\% \) level (one-tailed), the critical value is \( 0.4575 \). Carry out the test, stating your hypotheses and conclusion clearly.

A retailer records the price (\( \pounds \)) and the weekly demand (units) for a product over \( 11 \) weeks. The product moment correlation coefficient for the sample is \( r = -0.498 \). The retailer believes that a higher price is associated with lower demand, and tests this at the \( 5\% \) significance level. For \( n = 11 \) at the \( 5\% \) level (one-tailed), the critical value is \( -0.5214 \). Carry out the test, stating your hypotheses and conclusion clearly.

A botanist records, for \( 9 \) plants, the mass of fertiliser applied (g) and the plant height (cm). The product moment correlation coefficient for the sample is \( r = 0.798 \). The botanist believes that more fertiliser is associated with greater height, and tests this at the \( 1\% \) significance level. For \( n = 9 \) at the \( 1\% \) level (one-tailed), the critical value is \( 0.7498 \). Carry out the test, stating your hypotheses and conclusion clearly.

A motoring journalist records the engine size (litres) and the fuel economy (mpg) of \( 16 \) cars. The product moment correlation coefficient for the sample is \( r = -0.402 \). The journalist believes that a larger engine is associated with worse fuel economy, and tests this at the \( 5\% \) significance level. For \( n = 16 \) at the \( 5\% \) level (one-tailed), the critical value is \( -0.4259 \). Carry out the test, stating your hypotheses and conclusion clearly.

A coach records, for \( 13 \) athletes, the weekly training hours and the \( 5\,\mathrm{km} \) race time (minutes). The product moment correlation coefficient for the sample is \( r = -0.611 \). The coach believes that more training is associated with faster (lower) race times, and tests this at the \( 5\% \) significance level. For \( n = 13 \) at the \( 5\% \) level (one-tailed), the critical value is \( -0.4762 \). Carry out the test, stating your hypotheses and conclusion clearly.

A marketing analyst records, for \( 18 \) months, the advertising spend (\( \pounds000 \)) and the monthly sales (\( \pounds000 \)). The product moment correlation coefficient for the sample is \( r = 0.589 \). The analyst believes that greater advertising spend is associated with higher sales, and tests this at the \( 1\% \) significance level. For \( n = 18 \) at the \( 1\% \) level (one-tailed), the critical value is \( 0.5614 \). Carry out the test, stating your hypotheses and conclusion clearly.

A technician records, on \( 10 \) occasions, the relative humidity (\%) and the time taken for paint to dry (minutes). The product moment correlation coefficient for the sample is \( r = 0.673 \). The technician believes that higher humidity is associated with longer drying times, and tests this at the \( 5\% \) significance level. For \( n = 10 \) at the \( 5\% \) level (one-tailed), the critical value is \( 0.5494 \). Carry out the test, stating your hypotheses and conclusion clearly.

A researcher records, for \( 22 \) teenagers, the daily screen time (hours) and the nightly hours of sleep. The product moment correlation coefficient for the sample is \( r = -0.347 \). The researcher believes that more screen time is associated with less sleep, and tests this at the \( 5\% \) significance level. For \( n = 22 \) at the \( 5\% \) level (one-tailed), the critical value is \( -0.3598 \). Carry out the test, stating your hypotheses and conclusion clearly.

An economist records, for \( 25 \) households, the annual income (\( \pounds000 \)) and the annual savings (\( \pounds000 \)). The product moment correlation coefficient for the sample is \( r = 0.521 \). The economist believes that higher income is associated with higher savings, and tests this at the \( 1\% \) significance level. For \( n = 25 \) at the \( 1\% \) level (one-tailed), the critical value is \( 0.4622 \). Carry out the test, stating your hypotheses and conclusion clearly.

A researcher records the daily maximum temperature \( t \) and the number of cups of hot chocolate \( h \) sold at a cafe for a random sample of \( 12 \) days. The product moment correlation coefficient for the sample is \( r = -0.624 \). The researcher wishes to test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is any (non-zero) correlation between temperature and hot chocolate sales. The two-tailed critical value for \( n = 12 \) at the \( 5\% \) level is \( 0.5760 \). Carry out the test and state your conclusion in context.

A teacher collects the number of hours of sleep \( s \) and a reaction-time score \( w \) for a random sample of \( 15 \) students. The product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = 0.482 \). Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence of any correlation between hours of sleep and reaction-time score. The two-tailed \( 5\% \) critical value for \( n = 15 \) is \( 0.5140 \). State your conclusion in context.

For a random sample of \( 10 \) towns, a planner records the average rainfall \( x \) and the number of outdoor markets per month \( y \). The product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = -0.701 \). Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence of correlation between rainfall and the number of outdoor markets. The two-tailed \( 5\% \) critical value for \( n = 10 \) is \( 0.6319 \). State your conclusion in context.

Over a random sample of \( 20 \) days, a city analyst records the number of ice creams sold \( a \) and the number of recorded sunburn cases \( b \). The product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = 0.553 \). Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence of correlation between ice cream sales and sunburn cases. The two-tailed \( 5\% \) critical value for \( n = 20 \) is \( 0.4438 \). State your conclusion in context, and comment on whether this shows that buying ice creams causes sunburn.

A biologist tests for correlation between two variables using a random sample of \( 18 \) observations at the \( 5\% \) significance level. She wishes to detect correlation in either direction. The one-tailed critical values for \( n = 18 \) are \( 0.3994 \) at the \( 5\% \) level and \( 0.4716 \) at the \( 2.5\% \) level. State, with a reason, which critical value she should use, and write down the critical region for \( r \).

An economist studies the relationship between the unemployment rate \( u \) and a measure of consumer confidence \( c \) over a random sample of \( 25 \) regions. The product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = -0.547 \). Test, at the \( 1\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence of correlation between unemployment and consumer confidence. The two-tailed \( 1\% \) critical value for \( n = 25 \) is \( 0.4869 \). State your conclusion in context.

A student tests for correlation between two variables using a random sample of \( 14 \) paired observations and a two-tailed test at the \( 10\% \) significance level. The relevant one-tailed critical values for \( n = 14 \) are \( 0.4575 \) at the \( 5\% \) level and \( 0.3961 \) at the \( 10\% \) level. State which critical value should be used, with a reason, and write down the critical region for \( r \).

A nutritionist records, for a random sample of \( 16 \) people, the amount of dietary fibre eaten per day \( f \) and a digestive-discomfort score \( d \). The product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = -0.398 \). Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence of correlation between fibre intake and discomfort score. The two-tailed \( 5\% \) critical value for \( n = 16 \) is \( 0.4973 \). State your conclusion in context.

A sports scientist records the resting heart rate \( h \) and a fitness score \( g \) for a random sample of \( 30 \) athletes. The product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = -0.412 \). Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence of correlation between resting heart rate and fitness score. The two-tailed \( 5\% \) critical value for \( n = 30 \) is \( 0.3610 \). State your conclusion in context.

Across a random sample of \( 22 \) countries, a journalist records the number of mobile phones per person \( m \) and the average life expectancy \( l \). The product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = 0.608 \). Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence of correlation between mobile phone ownership and life expectancy. The two-tailed \( 5\% \) critical value for \( n = 22 \) is \( 0.4227 \). State your conclusion in context, and explain why this does not show that owning more phones increases life expectancy.

A researcher will test for correlation between two variables using a random sample of \( 28 \) paired observations, with a two-tailed test at the \( 1\% \) significance level. The one-tailed critical values for \( n = 28 \) are \( 0.4276 \) at the \( 1\% \) level and \( 0.4629 \) at the \( 0.5\% \) level. State, with a reason, which critical value should be used and write down the critical region for \( r \).

A psychologist records, for a random sample of \( 11 \) participants, the daily screen time \( s \) (hours) and a self-reported wellbeing score \( w \). The product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = -0.602 \). Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence of correlation between screen time and wellbeing. The two-tailed \( 5\% \) critical value for \( n = 11 \) is \( 0.6021 \). State your conclusion in context.

A geographer records the altitude \( a \) (metres) and the mean annual temperature \( T \) (°C) at a random sample of \( 13 \) weather stations. The product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = -0.668 \). Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence of correlation between altitude and mean annual temperature. The two-tailed \( 5\% \) critical value for \( n = 13 \) is \( 0.5529 \). State your conclusion in context.

Over one summer, a seaside town records the daily number of ice creams sold and the daily number of people treated for sunburn. The product moment correlation coefficient for the \( n = 30 \) days is \( r = 0.78 \). A one-tailed test of \( H_0:\ \rho = 0 \) against \( H_1:\ \rho > 0 \) at the \( 5\% \) level uses the critical value \( 0.3061 \). The local newspaper reports that 'eating ice cream causes sunburn'. Comment on whether the data support this claim, and explain carefully what the test does and does not show.

A researcher collects data from \( n = 40 \) primary schools on the average shoe size of pupils and their average score on a reading test. She finds \( r = 0.71 \) and, testing \( H_0:\ \rho = 0 \) against \( H_1:\ \rho \neq 0 \) at the \( 5\% \) level with critical value \( 0.3120 \), concludes that 'having bigger feet improves reading ability'. Carry out the test and critique her conclusion, identifying a confounding variable.

Two studies each test \( H_0:\ \rho = 0 \) against \( H_1:\ \rho > 0 \) at the \( 5\% \) level. Study A uses \( n = 10 \) (critical value \( 0.5494 \)) and Study B uses \( n = 50 \) (critical value \( 0.2353 \)). Both observe a sample PMCC of \( r = 0.30 \). Determine the conclusion of each test, and explain how and why the sample size affects the critical value and hence the outcome.

A student writes: 'To make it as hard as possible to wrongly reject \( H_0:\ \rho = 0 \), you should collect a very large sample, because then the critical value is bigger.' A test of \( H_1:\ \rho > 0 \) at the \( 5\% \) level has critical value \( 0.4973 \) when \( n = 12 \) and critical value \( 0.1654 \) when \( n = 100 \). Use these values to explain why the student's reasoning is incorrect, and state the correct effect of increasing \( n \).

A market analyst examines \( n = 200 \) companies and finds the correlation between two financial measures is \( r = 0.18 \). Testing \( H_0:\ \rho = 0 \) against \( H_1:\ \rho \neq 0 \) at the \( 5\% \) level uses the critical value \( 0.1388 \). The analyst reports that the two measures have 'a strong, statistically proven relationship'. Carry out the test and critique this statement, explaining why a significant result need not indicate a strong relationship.

In a study with \( n = 150 \), the correlation between hours of background music and worker productivity is \( r = 0.16 \). A one-tailed test of \( H_0:\ \rho = 0 \) against \( H_1:\ \rho > 0 \) at the \( 5\% \) level uses the critical value \( 0.1348 \). Explain what can and cannot be concluded about the usefulness of background music for predicting productivity.

An agronomist measures the correlation between rainfall and crop yield for \( n = 18 \) regions, obtaining \( r = 0.40 \). She wishes to test at the \( 5\% \) level whether there is positive correlation. For \( n = 18 \) at the \( 5\% \) level, the one-tailed critical value is \( 0.3994 \) and the two-tailed critical value is \( 0.4683 \). Carry out both a one-tailed test (\( H_1:\ \rho > 0 \)) and a two-tailed test (\( H_1:\ \rho \neq 0 \)), and explain why the choice of test changes the conclusion.

A psychologist expected, before collecting any data, that two test scores would be negatively correlated. For \( n = 22 \) participants she finds \( r = -0.38 \). At the \( 5\% \) level the one-tailed critical value is \( 0.3598 \) and the two-tailed critical value is \( 0.4227 \). She runs a two-tailed test, gets a non-significant result, and concludes 'there is no correlation'. Explain why a one-tailed test would have been appropriate here, carry it out, and critique her conclusion.

For a sample of \( n = 25 \) athletes, the correlation between training hours and performance score is \( r = 0.42 \). A two-tailed test of \( H_0:\ \rho = 0 \) against \( H_1:\ \rho \neq 0 \) is considered. The two-tailed critical values are \( 0.3961 \) at the \( 5\% \) level and \( 0.5052 \) at the \( 1\% \) level. Test at both levels, compare the conclusions, and explain why a more demanding significance level can change the outcome.

A geographer tests \( H_0:\ \rho = 0 \) against \( H_1:\ \rho > 0 \) for \( n = 30 \) river sites, finding \( r = 0.55 \). The one-tailed critical values are \( 0.3061 \) at the \( 5\% \) level and \( 0.4226 \) at the \( 1\% \) level. State the conclusion at each level, and explain what it means that the result is significant at the \( 1\% \) level as well as the \( 5\% \) level.

A biologist studies the correlation between a pollutant level and a fish health index across \( n = 16 \) lakes, finding \( r = -0.45 \). She suspected, before collecting data, that higher pollutant levels reduce fish health. The relevant critical values at the \( 5\% \) level are: one-tailed \( 0.4259 \) and two-tailed \( 0.4973 \). Carry out the most appropriate test, state the conclusion, and explain why an inappropriate choice of test (two-tailed) would have changed the conclusion. Comment on what the significant result does and does not establish.

A researcher records, for a random sample of \( 12 \) towns, the number of fast-food outlets \( x \) and the mean adult body mass index \( y \). The product moment correlation coefficient for the sample is \( r = 0.612 \). The critical value for a two-tailed test at the \( 5\% \) significance level with \( n = 12 \) is \( 0.5760 \). (a) State suitable hypotheses for a test of whether there is a correlation between the number of outlets and mean BMI, defining your symbol. (b) Carry out the test at the \( 5\% \) level and state your conclusion in context. (c) The researcher concludes that building fewer outlets would reduce BMI. Comment on this conclusion.

An agronomist studies whether higher rainfall is associated with higher wheat yield. For a random sample of \( 15 \) fields she finds a product moment correlation coefficient of \( r = 0.452 \). For a one-tailed test with \( n = 15 \) the critical values are \( 0.4409 \) at the \( 5\% \) level and \( 0.5923 \) at the \( 1\% \) level. (a) State the hypotheses, justifying your choice of a one-tailed test. (b) Test the claim at both the \( 5\% \) and the \( 1\% \) levels of significance, stating each conclusion in context. (c) Comment on the strength of the evidence given that the result is only just significant at the \( 5\% \) level.

A teacher records the number of hours \( x \) that each of \( 10 \) students spent revising and their test score \( y \). The product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = 0.658 \). The critical value for a two-tailed test at the \( 5\% \) level with \( n = 10 \) is \( 0.6319 \). (a) Test at the \( 5\% \) level whether there is a correlation between revision time and score, stating your conclusion in context. (b) On inspecting the data the teacher notices one student who revised for many hours but scored very poorly, lying far from the pattern of the other points. Explain how removing this point would be likely to affect \( r \) and the outcome of the test, and discuss whether the point should be removed.

For a random sample of \( 20 \) cars, an engineer records engine size \( x \) (litres) and fuel consumption \( y \) (litres per 100 km). The product moment correlation coefficient is \( r = 0.704 \). The car sizes in the sample range from \( 1.0 \) to \( 2.5 \) litres. For a one-tailed test at the \( 1\% \) level with \( n = 20 \) the critical value is \( 0.5155 \). (a) Test, at the \( 1\% \) level, the claim that larger engines have higher fuel consumption, stating your conclusion in context. (b) Using the result, the engineer predicts the fuel consumption of a \( 6.0 \) litre engine. Critique this prediction. (c) State one further assumption that should hold for the PMCC test to be valid here.

A biologist measures, for \( 14 \) ponds, the water temperature \( x \) and the rate of algal growth \( y \). A scatter diagram shows the points rising to a peak and then falling, forming a clear curved pattern. The biologist computes \( r = 0.143 \) and, for a two-tailed test at the \( 5\% \) level with \( n = 14 \), uses the critical value \( 0.5324 \). (a) Carry out the test and state the statistical conclusion. (b) The biologist concludes that temperature and algal growth are unrelated. Explain why this conclusion is unsafe, referring to the scatter diagram. (c) State, with a reason, whether a PMCC test is appropriate for these data.

A psychologist believes that the more hours people spend on social media, the lower their reported sleep quality. For a random sample of \( 18 \) people she finds \( r = -0.461 \). She is unsure whether to use a one-tailed or a two-tailed test. The critical values with \( n = 18 \) are: one-tailed \( 5\% \), \( 0.3994 \); two-tailed \( 5\% \), \( 0.4683 \). (a) State which test is appropriate to her belief and justify your choice. (b) Carry out the appropriate test at the \( 5\% \) level and state your conclusion in context. (c) State what the conclusion would have been had she instead used the other test, and comment.

A health analyst tests whether daily step count \( x \) is correlated with resting heart rate \( y \) for a random sample of \( 25 \) adults, obtaining \( r = -0.396 \). For a two-tailed test with \( n = 25 \) the critical values are \( 0.3961 \) at the \( 5\% \) level and \( 0.5052 \) at the \( 1\% \) level. (a) Carry out the test at the \( 5\% \) level and state your conclusion in context. (b) Interpret the result, given how close \( r \) is to the \( 5\% \) critical value. (c) Explain the effect on your conclusion of testing at the \( 1\% \) level instead.

A journalist surveys visitors leaving a single gym on a Monday morning, recording weekly exercise hours \( x \) and self-reported happiness \( y \) for \( 16 \) people. She finds \( r = 0.589 \). The critical value for a two-tailed test at the \( 5\% \) level with \( n = 16 \) is \( 0.4973 \). (a) Test at the \( 5\% \) level whether there is a correlation, stating your conclusion in context. (b) Give two reasons why the sample may not support a general claim about the population of all adults. (c) The journalist writes that 'exercising more makes people happier'. Explain why the test does not justify this.

An economist examines the relationship between average years of schooling \( x \) and gross domestic product per capita \( y \) for a sample of \( 11 \) countries, finding \( r = 0.553 \). The critical values for a two-tailed test with \( n = 11 \) are \( 0.6021 \) at the \( 5\% \) level and \( 0.7348 \) at the \( 1\% \) level. (a) Test at the \( 5\% \) level and state your conclusion in context. (b) The economist notes that one very wealthy country with relatively low schooling lies far from the other points. Explain how this single country is likely to be affecting \( r \) and the test result. (c) Explain what would happen to your conclusion if the test were carried out at the \( 1\% \) level.

A sports scientist tests whether longer warm-up time \( x \) is associated with faster sprint time \( y \) (so a negative correlation is predicted) for a random sample of \( 22 \) athletes, obtaining \( r = -0.602 \). For a one-tailed test with \( n = 22 \) the critical value at the \( 1\% \) level is \( 0.4921 \). (a) State the hypotheses and justify a one-tailed test. (b) Carry out the test at the \( 1\% \) level and state your conclusion in context. (c) The athletes were all from one elite squad. State, with reasons, two conditions that should hold for the PMCC test to be valid, and comment on whether the sampling supports generalising the result.

Over a sample of \( 13 \) consecutive years, an analyst records a city's annual ice-cream sales \( x \) and the number of drowning incidents \( y \), finding \( r = 0.681 \). The critical values for a two-tailed test with \( n = 13 \) are \( 0.5529 \) at the \( 5\% \) level and \( 0.6835 \) at the \( 1\% \) level. (a) Test at both the \( 5\% \) and \( 1\% \) levels, stating each conclusion in context. (b) The analyst claims ice-cream sales cause drownings. Critique this, suggesting a more plausible explanation. (c) The analyst also predicts drownings for a year with ice-cream sales double the largest in the sample. Comment on this prediction.

y2hm.questionText: A machine fills bags of flour so that the mean mass is stated to be \( 500\,\mathrm{g} \). A supervisor believes the machine has started to overfill the bags, so that the mean mass has increased. Write down the null hypothesis \( H_0 \) and the alternative hypothesis \( H_1 \) for a test of this belief.

The mean lifetime of a brand of battery is stated to be \( 18 \) hours. A consumer group suspects that the true mean lifetime is less than this. Write down the null hypothesis \( H_0 \) and the alternative hypothesis \( H_1 \) for a test of this suspicion.

A component is manufactured to have a mean length of \( 25\,\mathrm{mm} \). An engineer wants to test whether the mean length has changed in either direction. Write down the null hypothesis \( H_0 \) and the alternative hypothesis \( H_1 \) for this test.

A population is modelled by \( X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2) \) with \( \mu = 80 \) and \( \sigma = 6 \). A random sample of \( n = 9 \) observations is taken and the sample mean \( \bar X \) is calculated. Write down the distribution of \( \bar X \).

Under a null hypothesis, \( \bar X \sim N\!\left(100, \dfrac{15^2}{36}\right) \). A sample of size \( n = 36 \) gives a sample mean of \( \bar x = 98 \). Calculate the value of the test statistic \( Z = \dfrac{\bar X - \mu_0}{\sigma/\sqrt{n}} \).

Under a null hypothesis \( \mu_0 = 50 \), the population standard deviation is \( \sigma = 4 \). A random sample of size \( n = 25 \) has sample mean \( \bar x = 51.2 \). Calculate the value of the test statistic \( Z = \dfrac{\bar X - \mu_0}{\sigma/\sqrt{n}} \).

A normal population has standard deviation \( \sigma = 2.5 \). Under \( H_0: \mu = 20 \), a random sample of size \( n = 16 \) gives sample mean \( \bar x = 20.6 \). Calculate the value of the test statistic \( Z = \dfrac{\bar X - \mu_0}{\sigma/\sqrt{n}} \), giving your answer to 3 significant figures.

Under \( H_0: \mu = 5 \), a normal population has \( \sigma = 0.4 \). A random sample of size \( n = 64 \) gives sample mean \( \bar x = 4.85 \). Calculate the test statistic \( Z = \dfrac{\bar X - \mu_0}{\sigma/\sqrt{n}} \) and state which tail the observed value lies in.

A normal population has mean \( \mu = 300 \) and standard deviation \( \sigma = 12 \). A random sample of size \( n = 20 \) is taken. Find \( P(\bar X > 305) \), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.

A normal population has mean \( \mu = 1.5 \) and standard deviation \( \sigma = 0.05 \). A random sample of size \( n = 10 \) is taken. Find \( P(\bar X < 1.48) \), giving your answer to 4 decimal places.

A normal population has variance \( \sigma^2 = 36 \). Under \( H_0: \mu = 70 \), a random sample of size \( n = 9 \) gives sample mean \( \bar x = 73.4 \). Calculate the value of the test statistic \( Z = \dfrac{\bar X - \mu_0}{\sigma/\sqrt{n}} \).

A hypothesis test for the mean of a normal distribution uses \( H_0: \mu = 50 \) and \( H_1: \mu > 50 \) at the 5% significance level. The test statistic is calculated to be \( z = 2.13 \). The critical value for this upper one-tailed test is \( 1.645 \). State, with a reason, whether \( H_0 \) should be rejected.

A hypothesis test for the mean of a normal distribution uses \( H_0: \mu = 200 \) and \( H_1: \mu > 200 \) at the 5% significance level. The test statistic is calculated to be \( z = 1.42 \). The critical value for this upper one-tailed test is \( 1.645 \). State, with a reason, whether \( H_0 \) should be rejected.

A hypothesis test for the mean of a normal distribution uses \( H_0: \mu = 80 \) and \( H_1: \mu < 80 \) at the 5% significance level. The test statistic is calculated to be \( z = -1.80 \). The critical value for this lower one-tailed test is \( -1.645 \). State, with a reason, whether \( H_0 \) should be rejected.

A hypothesis test for the mean of a normal distribution uses \( H_0: \mu = 15 \) and \( H_1: \mu \ne 15 \) at the 5% significance level. The test statistic is calculated to be \( z = 2.45 \). The critical values for this two-tailed test are \( \pm 1.96 \). State, with a reason, whether \( H_0 \) should be rejected.

A hypothesis test for the mean of a normal distribution uses \( H_0: \mu = 120 \) and \( H_1: \mu \ne 120 \) at the 5% significance level. The test statistic is calculated to be \( z = -1.55 \). The critical values for this two-tailed test are \( \pm 1.96 \). State, with a reason, whether \( H_0 \) should be rejected.

A hypothesis test for the mean of a normal distribution uses \( H_0: \mu = 30 \) and \( H_1: \mu > 30 \). The test is carried out at the 5% significance level using the standard normal distribution. Write down the critical value for this test.

A hypothesis test for the mean of a normal distribution uses \( H_0: \mu = 5 \) and \( H_1: \mu > 5 \) at the 1% significance level. The test statistic is calculated to be \( z = 2.50 \). The critical value for this upper one-tailed test is \( 2.326 \). State, with a reason, whether \( H_0 \) should be rejected.

A hypothesis test for the mean of a normal distribution uses \( H_0: \mu = 60 \) and \( H_1: \mu \ne 60 \). The test is carried out at the 5% significance level using the standard normal distribution. Write down the critical values for this test.

A random sample of \( n = 36 \) observations is taken from a normal distribution with population standard deviation \( \sigma = 12 \). For a hypothesis test on the mean, calculate the standard error of the sample mean, \( \dfrac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}} \).

The mean lifetime of a type of battery is stated to be \( 80 \) hours. A consumer group wishes to test whether the mean lifetime has changed. Stating your reason, determine whether this is a one-tailed or a two-tailed test.

A hypothesis test for the mean of a normal distribution uses \( H_0: \mu = 250 \) and \( H_1: \mu < 250 \) at the 5% significance level. The test statistic is calculated to be \( z = -2.05 \). The critical value for this lower one-tailed test is \( -1.645 \). State, with a reason, whether \( H_0 \) should be rejected.

A machine fills bottles with a sports drink. The mass of drink dispensed is normally distributed with standard deviation \( 7.5\,\mathrm{g} \). The machine is set to dispense a mean of \( 500\,\mathrm{g} \). A technician suspects the machine is now over-filling. A random sample of \( 20 \) bottles has a mean mass of \( 503.4\,\mathrm{g} \). Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence that the machine is over-filling.

The lifetimes of a brand of car tyre are normally distributed with mean \( 1200 \) (hundreds of km) and standard deviation \( 80 \) (hundreds of km). After a change of rubber compound, a manager believes the mean lifetime has decreased. A random sample of \( 25 \) tyres has a mean lifetime of \( 1165 \) (hundreds of km). Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence that the mean lifetime has decreased.

The time taken for a commuter to travel to work is normally distributed with standard deviation \( 6 \) minutes. Historically the mean journey time has been \( 34 \) minutes. After a new road layout is introduced, the commuter believes the mean journey time has fallen. Over a random sample of \( 16 \) journeys the mean time is \( 30.5 \) minutes. Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence that the mean journey time has decreased.

A factory produces metal bolts whose lengths are normally distributed with standard deviation \( 0.4\,\mathrm{mm} \). The target mean length is \( 25.0\,\mathrm{mm} \). An engineer suspects the mean length has increased. A random sample of \( 36 \) bolts has a mean length of \( 25.12\,\mathrm{mm} \). Test, at the \( 1\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence that the mean length has increased.

The running time of a brand of rechargeable battery is normally distributed with standard deviation \( 1.5 \) hours and a stated mean of \( 18.0 \) hours. A reviewer claims that the mean running time is actually greater than stated. A random sample of \( 40 \) batteries has a mean running time of \( 18.55 \) hours. Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether the reviewer's claim is supported.

The reaction times of athletes to a starting signal are normally distributed with standard deviation \( 0.040 \) seconds and a mean of \( 0.250 \) seconds. After a new training programme, a coach believes the mean reaction time has decreased. A random sample of \( 50 \) starts has a mean reaction time of \( 0.238 \) seconds. Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence that the mean reaction time has decreased.

A cereal packaging line fills boxes whose contents have mass normally distributed with standard deviation \( 12\,\mathrm{g} \). The nominal mean content is \( 750\,\mathrm{g} \). A consumer group suspects boxes are being under-filled. A random sample of \( 30 \) boxes has a mean content of \( 745\,\mathrm{g} \). Test, at the \( 10\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence that the mean content is below \( 750\,\mathrm{g} \).

A workshop cuts metal rods to a target mean length of \( 100.0\,\mathrm{cm} \). The lengths are normally distributed with standard deviation \( 2.0\,\mathrm{cm} \). A supervisor suspects the rods are being cut too long on average. A random sample of \( 25 \) rods has a mean length of \( 101.0\,\mathrm{cm} \). Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence that the mean length exceeds \( 100.0\,\mathrm{cm} \).

The lifetimes of a type of light bulb are normally distributed with standard deviation \( 150 \) hours and a stated mean of \( 2000 \) hours. A manufacturer believes a redesign has increased the mean lifetime. A random sample of \( 36 \) bulbs has a mean lifetime of \( 2055 \) hours. Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence that the mean lifetime has increased.

The waiting time at a pharmacy counter is normally distributed with standard deviation \( 1.2 \) minutes and a historical mean of \( 8.5 \) minutes. After staffing changes, the manager believes the mean waiting time has fallen. A random sample of \( 45 \) customers has a mean waiting time of \( 8.10 \) minutes. Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence that the mean waiting time has decreased.

A supplier sells bags of sand with mass normally distributed with standard deviation \( 0.6\,\mathrm{kg} \) and a labelled mean of \( 25.0\,\mathrm{kg} \). A retailer suspects the bags are heavier than labelled on average. A random sample of \( 16 \) bags has a mean mass of \( 25.35\,\mathrm{kg} \). Test, at the \( 1\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence that the mean mass exceeds \( 25.0\,\mathrm{kg} \).

The times taken by members of a swimming squad to complete a particular race are normally distributed with standard deviation \( 1.8 \) seconds and a mean of \( 62.0 \) seconds. After a new coaching method, the coach believes the mean time has improved (decreased). A random sample of \( 20 \) swims has a mean time of \( 61.0 \) seconds. Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence that the mean time has decreased.

A factory produces sheets of plastic whose thickness is normally distributed with standard deviation \( 0.05\,\mathrm{mm} \) and a target mean of \( 1.50\,\mathrm{mm} \). An operator suspects the mean thickness has increased. A random sample of \( 40 \) sheets has a mean thickness of \( 1.515\,\mathrm{mm} \). Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence that the mean thickness has increased.

The time to download a large file over a network is normally distributed with standard deviation \( 0.50 \) seconds and a mean of \( 4.20 \) seconds. After an upgrade, an engineer believes the mean download time has decreased. A random sample of \( 25 \) downloads has a mean time of \( 3.95 \) seconds. Test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether there is evidence that the mean download time has decreased.

The mass of cereal in a packet is modelled by a Normal distribution with mean \( \mu\,\mathrm{g} \) and known standard deviation \( 8\,\mathrm{g} \). The packets are designed to contain a mean of \( 500\,\mathrm{g} \). A quality inspector takes a random sample of \( 16 \) packets to test, at the \( 5\% \) significance level, whether the mean mass has increased. Find the critical value of the sample mean \( \bar X \) and hence state the critical region for this test.

A machine fills bottles with a volume of liquid that is Normally distributed with mean \( \mu\,\mathrm{ml} \) and known standard deviation \( 5\,\mathrm{ml} \). The machine is set to deliver a mean of \( 330\,\mathrm{ml} \). A technician suspects the machine is now under-filling and takes a random sample of \( 25 \) bottles.
